name: Canary
summary: A two-line poster headline, 'CANARY TESTS IT.' on a yellow highlight bar, then a long proof sequence of agent transcripts, diffs and replayed failures.

observations.hero: Left-aligned on near-black: a 'Backed by Y Combinator' chip, a grey line '[agent] WRITES YOUR CODE.' whose agent name rolls between Claude, Codex, Cursor and Copilot, then 'CANARY' in yellow and 'TESTS IT.' in black on a yellow bar. Below are one paragraph, a single yellow 'COPY THE PROMPT' button and the mono caption 'One line for your agent.' The bottom edge shows the top of a mock agent window with a floating 'Start Demo' pill.
observations.typography: The measured h1 element is 32px, weight 400, −0.01em tracking, in Archivo Black. The largest display text measures 124px Archivo Black, set in caps. Body text is 17px Archivo with 1.7 line height and a 64ch measure. Nav, eyebrows, buttons and terminal text are in a monospace face; IBM Plex Mono is among the three measured families. Section heads repeat the heavy all-caps display style.
observations.visual_system: The ground is a warm near-black with sparse yellow constellation dots and lines. A single yellow accent carries CTAs, the highlight bar and active tabs. Red and green mark failures, diffs and two of the stats. Surfaces are thin-bordered dark panels, terminal panes, code diffs and a case-file timeline. There are no photographs; the diagrams are a dot sphere of failure paths and an integration fan-in.
observations.page_sequence: Hero → agent demo window (thread + diff) → stats row (10K+ bugs, 12K+ hours, 80%+ fix rate, 55% P0/P1) → 01 Install (3 steps, copyable prompt) → 02 Problem (three points + failure-path sphere) → 03 How it works (4 tabs) → 04 Where it runs (4 tabs) → 05 Integrations diagram → 06 Examples (4 case tabs + case file) → 07 Research (QA-Bench bar chart) → 08 closing CTA → footer.
observations.interaction: I clicked '02 ONE CLICK, TWO RECORDS' in Examples, then on a second load '02 Run' in How it works. Neither tab stayed selected: the How-it-works row advanced on its own from 01 to 03 while I waited. On load the hero agent name rolled between names, stats counted up from 0 when scrolled into view, and the 'Start Demo' pill stayed fixed over the demo. With reducedMotion set to reduce, the running-animation count was 0–1 versus 5 by default. Hero frames taken 2s apart were identical in both modes.
observations.accessibility: Several small mono captions and labels sit at low contrast on near-black: 'One line for your agent.', stat labels and footer column heads. The floating 'Start Demo' pill overlaps the demo window's title text. On mobile, footer links measured 18px tall and the demo message input 22px; the demo's 'Claude Code' tab is clipped at the right edge. No horizontal overflow was measured. Tab rows that advance on their own change content while it is being read.
observations.mobile: The nav collapses to the logo and a hamburger. The display drops to 44px, and the headline wraps to four short lines with the bar still behind 'TESTS IT.' The demo window becomes one tall column, thread above diff. The stats stack vertically, install steps stack, 4-tab rows become 2×2 grids and Examples tabs stack vertically. The integrations fan-in becomes a 2-column chip grid with arrows down to Canary, then Codex. The page grows to 11,532px.

principles: Make the claim evidence itself: replay a real failure as terminal output plus a case file (test, break, root cause, fix) instead of listing features.
When the buyer's tool is the entry point, make the primary CTA something that runs inside that tool (a copyable prompt) rather than a signup form.
Keep one accent colour, use it for action and emphasis only, and reserve red/green for pass/fail meaning.
Number sections like a document (01 / INSTALL … 08 / YOUR MOVE) so a long proof sequence stays navigable.
interpretation.fit: Developer tools where trust comes from seeing a concrete failure caught, such as testing, security or observability. It would be wrong for a non-technical buyer who cannot read diffs or terminal logs.
interpretation.risks: At ten sections and over 9,000px, the page asks for a lot of scrolling before the closing CTA. Self-advancing tabs ignored my clicks, so visitors can lose control of what they read. The heavy all-caps display face is loud on every section head, which flattens the hierarchy. The stats are unsourced on the page.

limitations: On the first exploratory load the page rendered before its styles applied (cream ground, stacked nav, monospace headings). Later loads rendered the dark design, so I treat the first as a load-timing artefact, not a variant.
Could not confirm whether tab clicks are ignored by design or lost to timing; two attempts on different tab rows did not hold.
The 'Start Demo' walkthrough was not started.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Traverse
archetype_note: Unstyled single HTML document in browser-default serif, closer to a text memo than a designed landing page.
summary: The homepage is one unstyled text document: thesis, team size, open roles and an email address, with no navigation, imagery or product surface.

observations.hero: There is no hero in the usual sense. A centred 650px column on white opens with a bold 'Traverse (ʌΛ)' heading, then a one-sentence value statement and two short paragraphs on the company thesis and team. The whole page fits in one 1440×900 screen with empty space below.
observations.typography: Everything is in the browser-default measured family, Times New Roman. The h1 is 24px, weight 700, 0 tracking, 1.4 line height. Body text is 16px with 1.4 line height at about 81ch on desktop. 'Careers' is a smaller bold subhead. Text size never goes above 24px.
observations.visual_system: Black text on a white ground, default blue underlined links and a default grey horizontal rule. The page uses one bulleted list and no colour, imagery, icons, buttons, logo mark or surfaces. The only motif is the '(ʌΛ)' glyph pair after the name.
observations.page_sequence: Name heading → value sentence → thesis paragraph → team paragraph → Careers subhead → hiring paragraph → four-role bullet list → email contact line → horizontal rule → backers line → X link. The measurement record counted 0 sections.
observations.interaction: There was no control to operate: the only interactive elements are a mailto link and an X profile link, and following either would leave the page. Measured animations were 0 on load and after scroll. Reduced-motion loads looked identical, with nothing moving in either mode. The page height equals the viewport, so there is nothing to scroll.
observations.accessibility: Black on white and default link blue give high contrast. Content sits in a semantic order (heading, paragraphs, list). On mobile the two inline links measured 17px tall, below common tap-target sizes. There is no nav landmark or skip structure, but with one screen of content there is little to skip. No horizontal overflow was measured.
observations.mobile: The same document reflows to a 370px column with about 10px side margins, and the line measure falls to about 46ch. Type sizes are unchanged: h1 24px, body 16px. Nothing is hidden or recomposed. The page still fits within one 844px screen.

principles: If the sale happens through a handful of direct relationships, the homepage can be a plain statement of thesis, team size and contact, with nothing in between.
State the operating model in one line ('a small team… a handful of companies at a time') so visitors self-qualify before reaching out.
When there is no product to show, credible backers and a direct email can stand in for product evidence on a recruiting-first page.
interpretation.fit: Early infrastructure or services firms that are hiring and sell through founder-led enterprise relationships. It would be wrong for any self-serve product that needs visitors to understand, try or buy without talking to someone.
interpretation.risks: There is no product evidence, pricing, customer proof or conversion path besides email. The page cannot be told apart from an unstyled placeholder. A visitor arriving from search gets no visual identity or memorable artifact.

limitations: No safe on-page control exists to operate; only outbound links.
Could not tell whether the default-browser styling is deliberate or a missing stylesheet; no stylesheet-loaded fonts were detected.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: 21st
archetype_note: Catalogue storefront: the hero is a filterable shelf of live component previews, not an input/output tool.
summary: The first screen is the catalogue itself: category pills switch rows of live component previews directly under the headline.

observations.hero: On a near-black ground with a deep blue glow, a left-aligned two-line headline reads 'The living library of interfaces'; 'living' is a blue italic serif. A one-line count of '12,000+ crafted React components…' follows. Next comes a '2,000+ Marketing blocks:' label with seven category pills, then a full-bleed row of preview cards (glass blob, AI-tools text hero, line-art figure) that bleeds off both edges.
observations.typography: The h1 measures 64px General Sans, weight 500, −0.022em tracking, 1.1 line height. The largest measured text is 69.1px Averia Serif Libre, which matches the italic serif accent words ('living', 'builders', 'anywhere', 'engineers', 'humans', 'answered'). Body text is 17px General Sans at 1.5 line height and a 52ch measure. ui-monospace is used in code panels. Large later headings set a white lead phrase against a grey continuation.
observations.visual_system: The ground is near-black, with a blue radial glow in the hero and a saturated blue for the Sign up and Browse components buttons. Imagery is the product itself: component preview cards, a code editor, a bookmark list and an author grid with avatars and component counts. The 'Copy the prompt' section breaks palette with three coloured cards: terracotta for Claude Code, blue-violet for Codex, cream-pink for Lovable.
observations.page_sequence: Hero with marketing-block pills and preview row → UI-component pills and second preview row → 'Used by 4,226,417 builders' with enterprise and startup logos → 'Copy the prompt. Paste it anywhere' (3 tool cards) → two panels (real code; save for later) → 'Built by real design engineers' author grid fading out → 'Built by humans / Ready for agents' CTA pair → FAQ (7 items) → footer.
observations.interaction: I clicked the 'Hero sections' pill. The active state moved to it, and the preview row swapped to different cards: an AI-cloud deploy hero, a 'Take a screenshot' hero and the glass blob. On load the cards first showed as empty placeholders, then filled in. On two desktop visits the page turned into a 'Something went wrong' panel once scrolling began. A reduced-motion load rendered normally; first-screen frames 2s apart were identical, though 18 animations were still reported running.
observations.accessibility: Secondary text is grey on dark blue or near-black: pill labels, the grey half of large headings, and author rows that fade toward near-invisible. Category pills are small 13px text. The scroll-triggered error replaced all content, including navigation, with only 'Try again' and 'Go home'. On the stored 390 capture the pill rows are clipped mid-word at the right edge as in-element scrollers; no page-level horizontal overflow was measured.
observations.mobile: Nav links disappear, leaving the logo, Log in and Sign up. The h1 drops to 40px over three lines. Both pill rows become clipped horizontal strips, and each preview row shows about one and a half cards. Logos wrap into rows, the three prompt cards and the two panels stack, and the author grid becomes two columns ending with '…and 700+ design engineers'. The FAQ heading sits above the list. The live mobile load showed the error panel; the layout here is from the stored capture.

principles: If the inventory is the product, put a filter control and real items in the first screen so the first click is already browsing.
Show where the product lands (terminal, agent, builder) with one card per destination tool, so 'works with your stack' becomes concrete.
Give an aggregator a human face by listing contributors with counts; it signals curation and supply depth at once.
Use one contrasting italic serif for a single word per heading as a recurring brand signature, and keep everything else in one sans.
interpretation.fit: Marketplaces, template libraries, asset stores and registries whose catalogue is self-explanatory when shown. It would be wrong for a single-workflow B2B tool, where a shelf of thumbnails would hide the one job it does.
interpretation.risks: The page depends on heavy client rendering with video and canvas. In this inspection it failed into a full-page error on scroll and on mobile load, which removes everything including navigation. Rows of moving previews compete with each other. The grey half-headlines and faded author grid trade legibility for atmosphere.

limitations: The client-side error appeared on every desktop visit after scrolling and on the mobile load; desktop sections below the second preview row were described from the stored full-page capture, not the live page.
Could not verify whether the error is specific to headless Chromium or the proxy environment.
Did not open the FAQ items or any component pages.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Arbital
archetype_note: Live-market ambience page: tickers, flip counters and dot-matrix charts make the trading feed itself the visual system.
summary: Market motion is the brand: a dot-matrix headline over a dotted price chart, with a scrolling ticker and flip counters, ahead of a single 'Start Trading' action.

observations.hero: Centred on a dark navy-to-black ground: the headline 'Trade what's moving.' in dot-matrix letterforms over a faint dotted price chart. Below it sit 'Memes, stocks, and perps in one app.', a blue 'Start Trading' button and 'Backed by Y Combinator'. Trade toasts ('@hannah_ok bought SOL +8.4%') appear at the right. A full-width ticker strip of assets with % changes sits above a three-up row of split-flap counters for volume traded, traded monthly and traders.
observations.typography: The measured h1 element computes to 16px geist, weight 400, 0 tracking. The visible headline is drawn as dot-matrix letters, and GeistPixelCircle is among the measured families. The largest measured text is 52px geist. Body text is 14px geist, 1.6 line height, at about 81ch. The 'Institutional market making.' heading is a high-contrast serif; Playfair Display is among the measured families. Counters use monospaced digits in flip tiles.
observations.visual_system: The ground is dark navy fading to near-black, with one saturated blue for CTAs and highlighted words. Green and red mark price changes. The motifs are dotted fields for the chart, world map and pixel letters, plus ticker chips, token rows, a trade ticket and bento cards with coin icons. A giant outlined 'Arbital' wordmark sits in the footer.
observations.page_sequence: Hero → ticker strip → flip counters → Memes 'Catch them early.' (token list) → split pair: Stocks 'The world's markets. Always OPEN' (dot map) | Perps 'Long it. Short it.' (trade ticket) → 'Everything in one place.' 4-card bento → 'Institutional market making. For everyone.' + Deploy a Strategy + 4 feature cards → FAQ (4) → 'Join 2,500+ traders.' CTA → footer.
observations.interaction: I clicked FAQ item 02 'Are the stocks real stocks?'. Its answer expanded and item 01 collapsed, with the +/× icons swapping. On load the ticker scrolled, trade toasts appeared, the chart backdrop shifted and counter digits flipped; the trader count read 2,620–2,623 across loads. The perps ticket switched from BTC to ETH to SOL between frames. Sections below the counters rendered only after scrolling. Under reduced motion the ticker held still, but the chart backdrop and counters still changed, with 2,118 running animations reported at load.
observations.accessibility: The dot-matrix headline has broken strokes and lower edge contrast than solid text. Small grey caps labels and the muted subcopy under 'Catch them early.' are low contrast on black. Reduced motion does not stop the counters or backdrop. On mobile, footer links measured 16px tall. In the stored full-page captures, about 3,000px below the counters is blank because those sections render only on scroll. No horizontal overflow was measured.
observations.mobile: The nav, X and Discord buttons collapse to a hamburger. The dotted chart moves above the headline instead of behind it, and the largest text drops to 32px. The ticker shows about three chips. The three counters stack vertically. The footer stacks links, socials and legal lines, with a smaller outlined wordmark. Mid-page sections were blank in the stored 390 capture and were not seen live on mobile.

principles: For a product about live data, let a few real-looking feeds (ticker, counters, activity toasts) carry the visual identity instead of illustration.
Give each product line one sentence and one artifact (token list, world map, order ticket) so a multi-market app reads as distinct, concrete choices.
Use a split-flap or monospaced counter for traction numbers so they read as instruments, not marketing claims.
Close with an FAQ that answers custody and 'is it real' questions before the final CTA.
interpretation.fit: Consumer trading, crypto and market-data products, where motion signals liveness and the audience expects tickers. It would be wrong for regulated advice or banking products, where constant motion and gamified toasts undercut a sense of care.
interpretation.risks: Motion runs even under reduced motion, and the headline is set in a less legible dot-matrix form. Content that renders only on scroll leaves full-page captures, previews and some readers with a large blank page. Counters and toasts give no source or time basis for the numbers.

limitations: Mid-page sections at 390 were not observed live; the stored mobile capture shows them blank.
Did not follow 'Start Trading', 'Deploy a Strategy' or any app link.
Could not verify whether ticker, toast and counter values are live data or simulated.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: HeyClicky
summary: The whole homepage is staged as a macOS desktop: a menu-bar nav, scattered .mov windows, folders and stickers around a lowercase wordmark.

observations.hero: A macOS-style menu bar serves as nav: text links left, a logo glyph centred, Wi-Fi, battery and clock icons plus a blue 'get heyclicky' link right. The centred lowercase wordmark h1 and 'an ai buddy that lives on your mac' sit above two pill CTAs, 'download for mac' and 'windows waitlist'. Around them float window-framed video thumbnails labelled as .mov files, folder and trash icons, name-tag stickers and kaomoji, over a dotted grid. A large hello.mov video with 'play video' starts at the fold.
observations.typography: Measured h1 is Inter 88px, weight 500, tracking -0.03em, line-height 1.1, and its text is the product name only; 56px at 390. Body measured Inter 16px/1.5. Geist Mono is the second measured family; a monospaced face appears on a terminal-style student discount card. Headings, buttons, FAQ and footer copy are set in lowercase throughout.
observations.visual_system: Light grey ground with a dotted grid; OS-style window chrome (traffic-light buttons, filename captions) frames videos, notes, testimonials and pricing cards. Glossy blue and grey pill buttons. Accents come from collected objects: folders, a trash can, an old candybar phone, a cartoon character image, coloured 3D staircases. Pricing sits on a full-bleed sky-and-clouds photo; the footer wordmark is built from blue folder icons.
observations.page_sequence: Hero → hello.mov video → three feature sections (finally do the thing; use your screen as context; spawn agents with your voice), each a window-framed video with a dotted waveform and 'heyclicky' speech bubble → 'the dream' founder note in a notes window → feedback: repeated 'they use it everyday' line and tweet-style cards → '25,000+ happy users' bar → pricing on sky → FAQ accordion → footer with folder-icon wordmark.
observations.interaction: Operated the pricing monthly/yearly tab: selecting 'yearly' changed pro from $20 to $16 and max from $100 to $80, added 'save $4/mo' and 'save $20/mo' badges and switched captions to 'billed yearly'. In my normal load, two top-of-page frames 1.5s apart were identical and the page reported 9 running animations. Under reduced motion every video element reported paused at 0s and one animation was still running.
observations.accessibility: Feature body copy is pale grey on the light grey ground. On desktop the floating windows' fullscreen buttons measure 12×12px and unmute buttons 16×16px. At 390 a DOM check found 17 links or buttons under 32px in one dimension, including footer links 24px tall and a 17px demo-video button; no unlabelled links or buttons were found. No horizontal overflow at either width.
observations.mobile: The menu bar drops its text links and status icons, keeping the logo glyph, 'get heyclicky' and an icon button. Most floating windows disappear; a few stickers and folders remain, clipped at the edges. CTAs stack full width, h1 drops to 56px, each feature's text stacks above its video, pricing cards stack, and the footer becomes two columns. Page height grows from 7,767px to 9,004px.

principles: If the product lives inside a familiar operating environment, borrowing that environment's chrome can explain where it runs before any copy does.
Keep one conversion action legible against a busy, collectable field by giving it the strongest colour and the centre of the composition.
Reuse a single framing device (here, window chrome) across video, testimonials and pricing so a dense page still reads as one system.
Put plan toggles next to the price numbers they change, with the saving stated in the card.
interpretation.fit: Suits consumer or prosumer desktop utilities with a playful voice and a founder-led audience. It would be wrong for a compliance or banking product, where faked OS chrome and meme objects would undercut trust.
interpretation.risks: The scattered objects compete with the value proposition, and the h1 carries only the name, so the product claim rests on a small subline. Pale grey body text and tiny window controls trade legibility for atmosphere. '100% free' under the download button sits awkwardly beside $20 and $100 paid tiers lower down.

limitations: The full-page 1440 capture was missing from the input bundle; desktop sequence comes from live viewport captures.
Feature videos and the hello.mov film were not played, so their content was not verified.
User count and testimonials are company statements, not checked.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Atomarine
summary: A full-bleed render of floating platforms with a full-width uppercase claim along the bottom edge makes an unbuilt industrial system feel concrete.

observations.hero: A full-bleed aerial image of floating data-center platforms and a service vessel at sea fills the screen. The uppercase h1 'NUCLEAR DATA CENTERS AT SEA' runs the full content width along the bottom edge, with a yellow-dot label above it and a yellow 'SCROLL TO SEE THE PLATFORM ↓' cue at right. A three-line tagline sits mid-left. The nav holds only the wordmark and a yellow Contact button.
observations.typography: Single measured family, Instrument Sans. Measured h1 80.7px, weight 500, tracking 0, line-height 0.9, set uppercase; 42px with line-height 1.1 at 390, wrapping to two lines. Body measured 14px/1.3. Section heads are mixed-case and medium weight; small uppercase labels with a dot mark each section (THE CONSTRAINT, SCALE, POWER).
observations.visual_system: Alternates near-black navy, white and deep blue grounds. A single yellow accent for buttons, labels and benefit headings. Imagery is photoreal pictures of platforms, ships and a desert data center; abstract dot-field and particle graphics accompany stats; the scale section uses white line drawings of platform layouts. A large outlined wordmark closes the footer.
observations.page_sequence: Hero image → four-stat grid (4X, 1.5 GW, <1.1 PUE, 20–40 YR) with particle graphics → 'AI's bottleneck is access to power' numbered list beside a desert photo → 'Going offshore unlocks unparalleled scalability' with a platform image and four yellow-labelled benefits → 'The campus grows with demand' scroll section with line drawings → 'Gas today, nuclear tomorrow' comparison slider → backer logo strip → embedded YouTube video → 'Get in touch' form → footer.
observations.interaction: Dragged the 'Gas today, nuclear tomorrow' comparison handle left: the divider moved from about 60% to about 15% of the width, so the branded marine-reactor vessel filled most of the frame over the LNG carrier. Section content appeared only after it entered view; captures taken under 0.5s after a scroll step showed blank sections. In the scale section, line drawings and a statement slid horizontally as I scrolled. Under reduced motion the hero video element still reported playback (about 1.5s elapsed).
observations.accessibility: Small grey stat captions on near-black are low contrast. Hero tagline is white text directly over the render with no visible scrim. At 390, the footer email and back-to-top links are 16px tall, and a DOM check found 16 links or buttons with no text, aria-label or title. Contact form fields have visible labels. Measurement record marks the reduced-motion rule as unverified. No horizontal overflow.
observations.mobile: The hero image is recropped to a portrait slice; the h1 drops to 42px and wraps to two lines under the label, losing the full-width edge effect, and the 'scroll to see' cue is gone. Stats become a single column; the constraint list moves above its photo; the four benefits stack under the platform image. Nav keeps wordmark and Contact. In my live 390 scroll most sections stayed blank in captures, while the batch full-page capture shows them.

principles: When the product is physical and not yet built, lead with a render that shows its scale in context and state the category in the headline.
Order the narrative as constraint, answer, scale path, then transition story so a sceptical buyer meets the problem before the claim.
Use a before/after slider when the pitch is a substitution, so the visitor performs the change themselves.
Restrict accent colour to one hue for actions and labels so it survives across dark, white and photographic sections.
interpretation.fit: Suits deep-tech, energy and infrastructure companies selling to investors, operators and partners, where one bold image carries the thesis. It would be wrong for a self-serve software product that needs to show an interface and a sign-up path.
interpretation.risks: Reveal-on-scroll content leaves sections blank to fast scrollers, screenshots and possibly assistive tools. The page shows renders and claims (4X faster, <1.1 PUE) without sourcing on the homepage. A single Contact action and 14px body text limit depth for technical buyers, and the hero video kept playing under reduced motion.

limitations: Embedded YouTube video was not played.
Stat claims and renders are company statements; whether imagery is rendered or photographed was not verified.
Whether reveal sections fail on real mobile devices or only in headless scrolling was not determined.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: AgentPhone
summary: A scripted live phone call with timer, waveform and captions sits directly under the headline, so the product is shown working before it is explained.

observations.hero: A centred 'Backed by Y Combinator' pill, a two-line h1 'Phone numbers for AI Agents' and a two-line subline sit over a black-to-green gradient tiled with outline robot-mascot drawings. Two actions follow: green 'Start building now' and a 'Copy Prompt' pill with an AGENT/MCP/NPM switch. Below, a glass card shows a call bar (+1 (415) 555-0142, timer, mic, mute, hang-up), a waveform with caption bubbles, and a Call/Message toggle. A circular 'talk to the team' badge sits bottom-right.
observations.typography: Measured h1 Alte Haas Grotesk 80px, weight 700, tracking -0.06em, line-height 1; 36px at 390. Body measured Inter Variable Local 14px/1.5 desktop and 16px at 390. JetBrains Mono is measured for code blocks and the AGENT/MCP/NPM switch. Section heads are bold, centred and tightly tracked.
observations.visual_system: Near-black ground with radial green glows; green is the only accent, used for primary buttons, waveforms and active tabs. Surfaces are dark rounded cards with green gradient fills. A robot mascot appears as background tiles, card stickers and footer stickers. Product evidence is drawn UI: country picker, transcription stream, number grid, MCP JSON, chat bubbles, call screens. Partner logos are white monochrome.
observations.page_sequence: Hero with call demo → 'Across the agent ecosystem' logo row → 'How it works' four-step tabs over a UI carousel with arrows → 'Everything in one API' bento (phone identity, transcription, numbers, MCP support) → 'Ways to integrate' language tabs and code block → 'Use cases' cards → FAQ accordion → closing CTA panel repeating hero actions → footer with address, status, SOC 2 badge and mascot stickers.
observations.interaction: Clicked the 'Node' tab in 'Ways to integrate': the green pill moved from Python to Node, the install line changed from 'pip install agentphone' to 'npm install agentphone', and the sample switched to JavaScript with import and await. On load, the call timer advanced (00:40 to 00:43), waveform bars changed and caption text cycled through a scripted conversation. Under reduced motion the same demo kept running: timer 00:24 to 00:32, captions changed.
observations.accessibility: Some captions inside demo cards are small grey text on dark green. The AGENT/MCP/NPM switch buttons are 25px tall and the unmute button 20px at 390. The fixed 'talk to the team' badge overlaps cards and code at 390. Reduced motion does not stop the hero demo. No unlabelled links or buttons found by a DOM check at 390; no horizontal overflow. A reduced-motion screenshot timed out once before succeeding.
observations.mobile: Nav reduces to the wordmark and 'Get Started'. The h1 drops to 36px; both actions become full-width stacked bars. The call card narrows with captions still visible. Logos wrap into rows; How it works becomes a vertical list; bento cards stack one per row. Code blocks keep their size and clip long lines at the right edge. Footer columns stack.

principles: Put a running, believable product moment directly under the headline so an infrastructure API reads as a working thing, not a diagram.
Offer a copy-to-agent or install path beside the primary button when the buyer will hand setup to a coding agent.
Use language tabs that swap install command and sample together so each developer sees one complete path.
Repeat the hero's exact action pair at the end of the page so a convinced reader does not have to scroll back.
interpretation.fit: Suits developer APIs and infrastructure whose output is an event (a call, a message, a webhook) that can be dramatised in a loop. It would be wrong for a product whose value is slow or invisible, such as data residency or audit logging, where a looping fake demo would mislead.
interpretation.risks: The hero demo is scripted and keeps moving under reduced motion. Dense dark-on-green cards and small grey captions cost legibility. The mascot, gradients and bento make the page long (8,663px desktop) before pricing, and code samples clip on phones.

limitations: The hero call demo was not verified as connected to a live service; it appeared scripted.
Partner logos and SOC 2 badge were not independently verified.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Juno
summary: A warm portrait photograph in an inset hero card, then photo-led step cards with chat overlays, frame a health tool as personal support rather than software.

viewports.desktop: 1440 × 900: rendered and measured from batch captures; live visit returned HTTP 502, no control operated

observations.hero: An inset rounded card fills the first screen with a golden-hour photograph of a woman seated on a hillside. A translucent pill nav inside the card holds the logo, five links, 'Example report' and a white 'Download' pill. Bottom-left, a three-line h1, a two-line subline, a white 'Download Juno' pill and an 'HSA/FSA eligible' check mark sit over the photo.
observations.typography: Single measured family, Instrument Sans. Measured h1 64px, weight 500, tracking -0.03em, line-height 1.0; 40px with line-height 1.1 at 390. Body measured 20px/1.4 at desktop and 18px at 390, with a 54-character measure. Section heads are large, light-grey or dark, centred or left-aligned, with no display contrast family.
observations.visual_system: White ground after the photographic hero. Imagery is lifestyle photography of people using phones or resting, with chat-bubble and data overlays ('Headache · logged today', '5h 10m'). Condition categories use soft gradient sky thumbnails. Advisor portraits sit in rounded cards. Buttons are pill-shaped, black or white. Colour comes from photography, not a brand accent.
observations.page_sequence: Hero → institution and press logos (UCL, Forbes, Oxford, Y Combinator) → 'How it works': four-step index at left beside photo cards with bullet lists → 'Built for your condition' list of five condition groups → 'Built with doctors and patients' advisor cards → 'Hear from our community' video testimonial carousel → (seen only at 390) download CTA, reviews, App Store rating, 'Always free' plan list, privacy commitments, FAQ, 'Start with one conversation' closing card, footer with medical disclaimer and crisis line.
observations.interaction: Not operated: both live visits returned HTTP 502 ('upstream request failed'), so no control, scroll or reduced-motion load was performed. The measurement record lists 3 running animations on load and 14 after scroll at 1440, and marks a reduced-motion rule as observed. In the batch desktop capture, a band of roughly 1,700px below the hero rendered blank.
observations.accessibility: Hero subline is white over a bright sky and foliage with no visible scrim. In the batch captures several headings and paragraphs ('Built for your condition', 'Built with doctors and patients') render in very pale grey, some images are grey placeholders, and at 390 two step images show alt text instead of images. At 390 the floating nav pill overlaps advisor content. No horizontal overflow measured.
observations.mobile: Nav collapses to logo and a menu button inside the pill. The hero photo is recropped so the face fills the top half, with text and CTA stacked beneath. Logos shrink to one row. How it works becomes numbered headings each followed by its image and bullets. Advisors form a compact two-column list; community videos scroll horizontally. Page height falls from 14,619px to 7,924px and measured sections from 9 to 8.

principles: For a sensitive consumer category, lead with a human photograph and a plain-language claim before any interface.
Show the product through what a user would say ('My headache is bad today') overlaid on real-life scenes rather than through screenshots.
When the product handles health data, place clinical credibility (advisors, institutions) high on the page and data commitments beside the plan details.
Keep eligibility details such as HSA/FSA directly under the primary button where purchase anxiety is highest.
interpretation.fit: Suits consumer health, wellness and care apps where reassurance and empathy matter more than feature density. It would be wrong for a clinician-facing or enterprise tool, where buyers need workflow, integration and compliance detail up front.
interpretation.risks: The long photographic page depends on lazy-loaded images and reveals that rendered blank, grey or as alt text in captures. Stock-feeling portraits risk reading as generic. The desktop page is very long (14,619px), and the product UI itself is barely shown.

limitations: Live visits on 2026-10-19 returned HTTP 502 twice; no control was operated and reduced motion was not tested live.
The desktop full-page capture stops at 9,000px of 14,619px; later desktop sections were inferred only from the 390 capture.
Blank band, pale text and missing images may be capture artefacts of scroll reveals rather than real-user states.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Imperfect
summary: A torn-paper, cut-out-athlete collage world carries the brand, while the product shows up only as small schedule miniatures inside dark cards.

observations.hero: Split first screen on white: a large three-line headline "For the imperfect ones." bottom left, a short subhead, paragraph and orange "Talk to your coach" pill in the middle column, and a cut-out runner over overlapping torn-paper and translucent colour shapes on the right. A smaller collage and a thin orange line motif bleed off the top-left corner. Nav is a script-style wordmark plus four text links, no nav button.
observations.typography: Display is a rounded geometric sans, measured family Rink: h1 96px, weight 500, line-height 0.9, tracking 0; the final period is set in blue. Body is measured Inter at 18px/1.4 with a 36ch measure in the hero. Families: Inter, Rink, system-ui. Section heads reuse the rounded display face at smaller sizes over small purple uppercase eyebrows. The measured h1 text contains the phrase twice in the DOM.
observations.visual_system: White and pale-grey grounds alternate with a deep navy band and a lilac app band. Saturated orange, mustard, olive, purple and blue appear as torn, textured paper shapes; athlete cut-outs (runner, cyclist, triathlete) sit on blue shadow shapes with hand-drawn orange route lines. Product UI appears only as small diagrams: a week grid with a moved session, a 'Today' card, a goal path, a dot-grid progress counter.
observations.page_sequence: Hero → "Every pro has a coach" with three torn-paper benefit cards → navy "Built for imperfect weeks" 2×2 scenario cards → "Three sports. One coach." (Running, Cycling, Triathlon cards) → two-column FAQ accordion → lilac "Take your coach with you" with QR, store badges and two phone mockups → navy footer.
observations.interaction: Operated the FAQ item "Do I need a watch?": the plus became an ×, aria-expanded went true and a short answer opened below. Nothing moved in the first screen on load. On scroll, the navy scenario cards appeared one after another with their diagrams drawing in; at about 1.5s the fourth card was still faint. With reduced motion, all four cards were fully rendered on arrival and I saw nothing move.
observations.accessibility: Mobile body text measures 12px. Scenario-carousel dots on mobile measure 16×24px. In the static desktop full-page capture the fourth scenario card is empty because it had not yet animated in. FAQ buttons expose aria-expanded. No horizontal overflow measured at either width; no images without alt were found.
observations.mobile: The hero recomposes: collage and runner move above the headline, which drops to 40px on two lines with copy and CTA beneath; nav collapses to a hamburger. Benefit cards stack with alternating offsets. The scenario grid becomes a swipe carousel with four dots, sport cards scroll sideways with the third card cropped at the edge, FAQ becomes one column, and the app band shows store badges without the QR code.

principles: Let one tactile illustration system (here torn paper and cut-out athletes) carry the brand so product screenshots can stay small and diagrammatic.
Explain an adaptive product with before/after scenario cards that show the plan changing, rather than feature lists.
Put the emotional promise in the headline and the literal category in the subhead directly beside it.
When content animates in on scroll, make sure the reduced-motion and static states render every card fully.
interpretation.fit: Suits consumer apps selling a feeling as much as a function: fitness, habits, hobby coaching. Wrong for a product whose buyer needs to see dense UI or data before trusting it, such as an analytics tool.
interpretation.risks: The coach itself (the AI conversation) is never shown at full size, so the product's core interaction is left to imagination. Scroll-entrance cards are empty until triggered, which shows in static captures and possibly for fast scrollers. 12px mobile body text is small for the main explanatory copy.

limitations: Did not open the hamburger menu or the store links; app behaviour not inspected.
Animation count of 55 after scroll comes from the measurement record; I observed only the scenario cards visibly entering.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Applied Electrodynamics
summary: A long scroll-scrubbed canvas sequence of the camera and walls being 'seen through' replaces conventional feature sections entirely.

observations.hero: Near-black page with a rounded hero card holding a dark product render of a box-shaped camera with a striped-ring logo on its face; "A new kind of camera" sits bottom left inside the card. Below: a grey two-line subline ("See through walls, and much more."), a green "Preorder Now" pill and a centred down arrow. Header has the striped-ring wordmark left and "Backed by Y Combinator" plus green "Preorder" pills right.
observations.typography: Single measured family, Söhne, for everything: h1 83.8px, weight 500, line-height 1, tracking -0.025em; body 30px/1.1 with a 72ch measure. Captions pair a white lead phrase with grey continuation in the same size ("See through walls. Map mechanical…"). The wordmark is widely spaced uppercase.
observations.visual_system: Near-black ground throughout with slightly lighter rounded panels. Imagery is a dark product render and wall scenes (ornate wallpaper, a framed painting) with a magenta-purple imaging overlay revealing what is behind the surface. Muted green is the only accent, used for every preorder button. Logo grid uses white marks on dark rounded tiles.
observations.page_sequence: Hero card → scroll-scrubbed product sequence (camera turns, wall scenes with imaging overlay; captions "See through walls.", "Pinpoint issues in no time.", "Keep secure.") → "Built by engineers from Apple, Google, and MIT." → eight-tile logo grid → YC and "250+ patents" paragraph → preorder form → footer of pill links.
observations.interaction: Operated the header "Preorder" link: the page jumped to the preorder form (#waitlist-head). On load only the down arrow pulsed. Scrolling scrubbed the canvas: the camera body turned and the wall scenes and captions changed with scroll position. With reduced motion the arrow kept pulsing and the scroll-scrubbed sequence still moved with scroll; the measurement record lists no reduced-motion rule.
observations.accessibility: Grey secondary text on near-black (subline, second half of captions, "Be first to see through walls.") is noticeably lower contrast. Form fields use placeholders with aria-labels but no visible labels; a fifth unlabelled text input is present in the DOM. One frame showed body text passing under the sticky header pills without a backdrop. In the static full-page capture the sequence area is roughly 4,000px of blank dark space.
observations.mobile: The two header pills stack, with "Backed by" shrinking to the word plus the Y mark. The hero card becomes a tall portrait panel with the h1 at 32px; body drops to 16px. The canvas sequence remains (hero region measures 5,317px). The logo grid becomes two columns, the form stacks under its heading, and footer pills form two columns.

principles: For hardware with a hard-to-believe capability, show the capability happening on a recognisable surface before any claims.
Use one family at one weight and let white versus grey within a sentence do the hierarchy work.
Keep a single accent colour reserved for the purchase action so it is findable at every scroll depth.
If the story lives in a scroll-scrubbed canvas, provide a static fallback for reduced motion and for crawlers or captures.
interpretation.fit: Suits deep-tech hardware with one striking visual demonstration (imaging, sensing, optics). Wrong for a software product with many features or buyers who need specs and pricing up front.
interpretation.risks: Most of the page's information is locked in a canvas that renders blank in static capture and may load slowly; the claims list is three captions long. Reduced motion is not honoured. Credibility rests on logo tiles and a patent count rather than technical detail or images from the device itself that are labelled as such.

limitations: Did not type into or submit the preorder form.
Could not confirm whether the imaging overlays are real device output or illustration.
Canvas frames may have loaded partially during the scroll pass; some frames showed only the black device face.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Oasiz
summary: The whole homepage is one screen: wordmark, App Store badge and an auto-advancing phone carousel set over a pixel-art arcade world.

observations.hero: The root URL redirects to /landing. One screen: a widely tracked "OASIZ" wordmark headline, two lines of tagline ("The ultimate social arcade. Play, remix, and create games with friends!") and an App Store badge on the left; a large phone mockup on the right; a pixel-art island party scene, palms, water and city skyline across the bottom. "Join Discord" and "Sign In" ghost pills top right. A cookie banner overlaps the lower centre.
observations.typography: Display and body are a squared, techno geometric sans, measured family Kodchasan: h1 96px, weight 600, tracking 0.2em, line-height 1; body 14px/1.6. Montserrat also appears among the measured families. Phone slides use spaced uppercase titles (PLAY, REMIX, CREATE, EXPLORE).
observations.visual_system: Blue-to-violet gradient sky with pixel sparkle stars; saturated pixel-art characters, arcade cabinets, tetromino blocks and a skyline. The phone mockup has a cyan rim and dark screen showing real app UI per slide. Footer is near-black with grey link columns.
observations.page_sequence: Single hero screen → footer (Resources, Legal, Company, Social). The measurement record counts zero sections.
observations.interaction: Clicked the fourth carousel dot: the phone switched to the EXPLORE slide. Without input the carousel advanced every few seconds through six slides including Play with friends, Play, Remix, Create and Explore. Nothing else was seen moving. With reduced motion the carousel still advanced on its own.
observations.accessibility: Carousel dots measure 6×6px (active 18×6px) at 390, and I found no pause control for the auto-advancing carousel. Footer links are 20px tall on mobile. The cookie banner covers the lower part of the phone at both widths until dismissed. White tagline text sits on a mid-blue gradient.
observations.mobile: Logo and "Join Discord" disappear, leaving only "Sign In". Wordmark (48px), tagline and App Store badge centre-stack at the top, and the phone mockup fills most of the width below, hiding most of the pixel world. The footer becomes a two-column grid.

principles: When the product lives in an app, a homepage can be just a door: one download action and real screens cycling in a device frame.
Let a carousel of named verbs (play, remix, create) explain a multi-mode product in one slot.
Build the backdrop from the product's own visual language, here pixel-art game assets, so the brand and the content read as one world.
interpretation.fit: Suits consumer mobile apps and games where the store page and the app do the persuading. Wrong for anything needing a web sign-up, pricing, or trust-building copy, such as B2B or paid subscriptions.
interpretation.risks: With no sections there is no explanation of how AI-built games work, no social proof and no Android path. The auto-advancing carousel ignores reduced motion and has tiny dots, and the cookie banner sits on top of the key visual.

limitations: Did not test Sign In, Join Discord or the App Store link.
The full slide list was read from screenshots over time; one slide title was not captured.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Clair Health
summary: A soft-luxury editorial page: high-contrast serif headlines, full-bleed product renders and lifestyle video, with a floating pre-order pill throughout.

observations.hero: After a brief grey-green loading screen with a progress bar, a mauve-to-blush gradient shows a centred two-line serif headline "The first continuous hormone monitor" above a large render of a pearl-and-rose-gold wrist band cropped at the bottom. A frosted pill nav (About, FAQ, Partners, Careers, Ask Clair, white "Pre-order now") floats at top with a faint funding announcement link below; a cream "Pre-order now" pill sits bottom centre.
observations.typography: Display is a high-contrast old-style serif, measured family EB Garamond: h1 96px, weight 400, line-height 1, tracking -0.03em (-0.035em on mobile at 48.8px). Body is measured Geist at 16px/1.2. Families: Geist, EB Garamond, Inter. The "100,000+" stat is set very large in a grey sans.
observations.visual_system: Warm, soft grounds that change per section: mauve, blush, pale sage, orange gradient, cool grey. Imagery is glossy product renders, lifestyle video, clinician portraits on tilted cards with Stanford Medicine marks, and social-post thumbnails. Feature panels switch between green, dark green and red with short messages.
observations.page_sequence: Loader → hero → "Understand your body like never before" video → "For every stage of your life" list with coloured message panel → "The breakdown" (three icons, band render) → "Trained on clinical data from 100,000+ women" → "Developed with leading scientists" cards → video testimonial → tabbed FAQ → founding-member offer and form → "Join 32,000+" social posts and email field → footer "Stay in the loop".
observations.interaction: Clicked the "About & Privacy" FAQ tab: the questions swapped to that set with "Is Clair a medical device?" open. On load a loader ran, then the hero video elements were reported playing. During scroll the life-stage list highlight moved down and the side panel changed colour and message without a click. With reduced motion the hero videos stayed paused and no load animations were reported, but the life-stage list still advanced during scroll.
observations.accessibility: The funding announcement and unselected list and FAQ items are light grey on light grounds, low contrast. On 390 the floating pre-order pill overlaps headings and FAQ text, and the scientist carousel dots measure about 7–8px. Footer nav links are 14px tall on mobile. No horizontal overflow measured.
observations.mobile: Nav becomes logo plus hamburger; the announcement wraps to two lines; the headline sets in two lines at 48.8px; the band render is cropped off both edges. Scientist cards become a one-card carousel with dots, the FAQ tabs compress to small two-line labels, and the offer list and form stack. The floating pre-order pill remains on every screen.

principles: Pair a classical serif display with a neutral sans body to make a medical-adjacent device read as personal and premium rather than clinical.
Translate abstract sensing into concrete daily messages ("Hot flashes likely. Stay cool tonight.") shown in context.
Stack credibility in escalating order: data scale, named clinicians, then a real person on video.
A persistent purchase pill works only if it never covers the copy it floats over; reserve space for it on mobile.
interpretation.fit: Suits consumer health and wellness hardware sold on trust and aspiration. Wrong for a clinical or B2B buyer who needs regulatory status and evidence near the top rather than in a FAQ tab.
interpretation.risks: Long page (about 11,300px) with a loader before the hero adds delay. Several low-contrast greys carry real information. The floating pill covers text on mobile, and the scroll-driven list ignores reduced motion. The medical-device answer sits in the second FAQ tab near the bottom of the page.

limitations: Did not submit any of the pre-order or email forms, play the testimonial with sound, or open Ask Clair.
The provided 1440 full-page capture was truncated at 9,000px; the lower page was checked live.
Could not tell whether the life-stage list advances on a timer or on scroll position.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Sparkles
summary: A cast of hand-drawn shape characters carries the brand, while plain UI mocks below explain how agents turn requests into pull requests.

observations.hero: A 56 px nav (logo, four links, Sign in, Book a demo) sits over a thin 'Backed by Y Combinator' strip. The hero is split: centred serif headline, three-line subcopy, Sign in and Book a demo buttons, 'Free to start' note and greyed trusted-by logos on the left; a grid of thick-outlined coloured shapes with cartoon eyes fills the right half. A consent dialog overlays the lower centre of the first screen.
observations.typography: Headline in measured family Gelica, a soft display serif: h1 60 px, weight 600, line-height 1.0, tracking 0. Section heads reuse it. Body in measured Inter at 18 px / 1.6 with a 64ch measure. UI mocks, chips and footer use the same sans at smaller sizes; tracked uppercase small labels for 'TRUSTED BY' and 'BACKED BY'.
observations.visual_system: Warm off-white ground, near-black text and buttons, hairline borders. Colour comes almost entirely from the illustrated characters (coral, sky blue, ochre, green) with heavy black outlines; the same cast reappears beside the FAQ. Product is shown through flat, low-chrome mocks (browser window, green Slack panel, integration chips). The page closes on a black CTA band, then a saturated green footer with an oversized outlined wordmark.
observations.page_sequence: Hero with character grid → 'Run a coding agent from wherever you work' (Web UI and Slack mocks joined by dotted lines to a 'Your agents' node, then 3,000+ integrations chip cloud) → 'From prompt to pull request' four-step accordion beside a media panel → Pricing (Monthly/Annual toggle, Credits and Enterprise cards) → FAQ accordion beside character illustration → black CTA band → investor grid → green footer.
observations.interaction: Operated the pricing Monthly/Annual toggle. After full load, choosing Annual flipped aria-checked and the Credits card changed from '$50.00 / month, 500 credits every month' to '$500.00 / year, 2 months free, 6,000 credits granted up front'; an earlier click before the page finished loading changed nothing. The first screen did not change across a 1.5 s frame comparison; my probe counted 10 running animations. Under reduced motion: 1 running animation, all video elements paused, but a frame comparison after scrolling still differed.
observations.accessibility: The consent dialog stays fixed over mid-page content at every scroll position until a choice is made; at 390 it covers the hero's Book a demo button. Trusted-by logos are rendered in light grey. Accordion and FAQ buttons expose aria-expanded; the billing toggle uses role=radio. No horizontal overflow measured at either width. Mobile primary buttons are full-width and roughly 40 px tall.
observations.mobile: Nav collapses to logo plus hamburger; the YC strip stays. h1 drops to 48 px and the character grid moves below the stacked full-width Sign in / Book a demo buttons, pushing hero height to 1,043 px. Web UI and Slack mocks stack, the integration chips rewrap, pricing cards and toggle stack, the FAQ character illustration is not visible in the 390 capture, and the investor grid becomes two columns. Page grows from 7,385 to 10,490 px.

principles: Give an abstract product a recurring illustrated cast so the brand is recognisable before the visitor understands the mechanics.
Keep product mocks plain and low-chrome when the brand layer is loud, so the two do not compete.
Explain multiple entry points with one convergence diagram (each surface drawn as a mock, joined to a single agent node) rather than separate feature blocks.
Put the billing toggle's consequence in the card itself (price, period and credits all change) so the choice is legible without footnotes.
interpretation.fit: Suits collaboration tools sold to mixed technical and non-technical teams, where approachability is part of the pitch. It would be wrong for security or compliance infrastructure, where cartoon faces in the hero can read as unserious to a risk-averse buyer.
interpretation.risks: Half the hero is illustration that says nothing about agents, sandboxes or pull requests, so the copy carries all the explanation. Sign in and Book a demo appear as equal pairs repeatedly, leaving no single primary action. The persistent consent dialog sits on content, and the mobile page is long.

limitations: The media panel in 'From prompt to pull request' rendered blank in all captures; its content was not verified.
Reduced-motion behaviour was judged from frame comparisons and animation counts only; I did not identify which element still moved.
Did not interact with the consent dialog, so the page was always seen with it open.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Button Computer
archetype_note: Really a DTC hardware storefront: cinematic video hero over a commerce theme with an on-page buy box.
summary: A full-bleed lifestyle video of the device clipped to a person opens a commerce-template page that ends in a buy box and FAQ.

observations.hero: A tall 136 px white header holds the stacked BUTTON COMPUTER logo left and small uppercase ACCOUNT and CART (0) links right. Below, a full-width video frame shows a woman in a library with the small square device clipped to her collar; the white headline, one-line subcopy and a yellow 'PREORDER NOW' pill sit bottom-left. A 'Backed by Y Combinator / Featured in TechCrunch, WIRED' strip follows directly under the frame.
observations.typography: Measured Poppins for display: h1 44 px, weight 500, line-height 1.2, tracking -0.02em; section heads in the same geometric sans at medium weight, centred statement lines larger. Body in measured DM Sans at 16 px / 1.5, 55ch measure. Small tracked uppercase labels for nav, 'BACKED BY', buttons and buy-box fields.
observations.visual_system: Light grey ground with white rounded cards, dark grey text, a single saturated yellow for the hero pill and subscribe button, and a lavender 'Buy with Shop' button. Imagery is warm, cinematic lifestyle photography and video of the device in use; no product renders on a plain background. Layout alternates image and text cards. Footer is a dark charcoal band.
observations.page_sequence: Video hero → backer and press strip → statement 'You press it to talk to AI…' → Instant productivity (image | text) → statement on privacy → Private by design (text | image) → 'Watch the video' banner → three use cases (car, on the go, home) → Preorder today buy box with gallery → FAQ accordion → Meet the founders with photo → 'Not quite ready?' email signup → footer.
observations.interaction: Operated the FAQ item 'When will my Button ship?'. After full load it expanded to show a one-line shipping answer and the previously open first item collapsed (single-open accordion); a click before load finished did nothing. On load the hero frame changed across a 1.5 s comparison (moving video); no Web Animations were running. With reduced motion the hero frame did not change across the same comparison.
observations.accessibility: Hero text is white over a dark, moving video; legible in captures but contrast depends on the frame. FAQ answers are light grey on near-white. FAQ toggles carry aria-label but exposed no aria-expanded in the DOM probe. Buy box shows a grey 'SOLD OUT' button and 'Out Of Stock' badge beside the hero's 'PREORDER NOW'. Nav links are small uppercase text. No horizontal overflow at either width.
observations.mobile: Header shrinks to 61 px and keeps ACCOUNT and CART. The video crops to a portrait-ish frame with h1 at 25 px over it. Press logos split into two centred rows. Alternating image/text pairs stack image-over-text. The three use cases become a single-item swipe row with dot indicators. Gallery thumbnails move below the main image. Footer 'COMPANY' links collapse into an accordion. Content width measured 270 px.

principles: For a small device, show it worn and in use in the first frame so scale and context land before any spec.
Name the category's main objection (an always-listening AI device) in its own section and again as the first FAQ.
Keep price, availability and refund terms together in one buy box on the homepage when the page's job is to sell.
interpretation.fit: Suits consumer hardware and DTC products where desire and trust are built through lifestyle imagery and a short path to checkout. It would be wrong for a developer tool or API, where the visitor needs to see the interface or code rather than a mood.
interpretation.risks: The hero promise 'PREORDER NOW' meets a sold-out, out-of-stock buy box further down, which reads as a dead end. The device itself is small in the hero frame. The structure follows a generic commerce theme, so the page's identity rests almost entirely on footage and photography.

limitations: One desktop navigation timed out at 45 s before succeeding with a longer wait; load performance was not measured.
Under reduced motion no video element was found by the probe, so I could not tell whether the hero video was paused or not yet loaded.
Did not play the 'Watch the video' content.
Did not verify whether preorder is actually unavailable or whether the sold-out state is a display state.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: CodeWisp
summary: The homepage is the game catalog itself: a showcase slot with leaderboard and rails of user-made games, with no headline or marketing copy.

observations.hero: A sticky 62 px dark nav holds logo, mono uppercase links (PLAY, EXPLORE, DISCUSS, CREATE, MARKETPLACE), a 'Search Game' field, a Discord icon and an outlined lime 'Sign in'. Below a 'Recommended' label, a large game key-art panel sits left and a side panel right with thumbnail strip, game title, creator, description, an all-time leaderboard and a lime-outlined PLAY button; pagination dots underneath. The 'Featured' grid starts within the first screen.
observations.typography: No h1 on the page (measured null). Section labels and game titles in sans; the measured display element is 27.2 px Inter at 1440 and 20 px Geist at 390. Body and metadata in measured Geist Mono at 11 px / 1.8 (creator names, play counts, likes, leaderboard). Families measured: Geist Mono, Geist, Inter.
observations.visual_system: Near-black blue-green ground with a darkened pixel-art village illustration behind the showcase. Colour comes from the games' own thumbnails, which are bright and varied. Accent is a lime/yellow-green used for outlines, the selected thumbnail and PLAY. Cards are thumbnail-over-caption with mono stats; hairline rules extend from section labels.
observations.page_sequence: Recommended showcase with leaderboard → Featured (8 cards) → Hot (8) → Top (8) → Recently Updated (8) → New (8) → footer link columns (Navigate, Account, Resources, Legal, Community). Several games repeat across rails.
observations.interaction: Operated the 'Next showcase game' arrow (it is transparent until the showcase is hovered). The side panel switched from Aether Rush to Cube Jump: selected thumbnail highlight moved, title and creator changed, the second pagination dot became active, and the main art area was dark 1.5 s after the click. A full-screen loading layer intercepted clicks for several seconds after load. Under reduced motion no animations were running and the first screen did not change across a 1.5 s comparison.
observations.accessibility: Body and metadata at 11 px mono, with dim grey text (creator line, lower leaderboard rows) on a dark ground. Showcase arrows are invisible until hover, so not discoverable on touch. Icon buttons carry aria-labels ('Next showcase game', 'Show Cube Jump', 'Random game'). No h1. No horizontal overflow at either width.
observations.mobile: Nav reduces to hamburger, logo and Sign in; the search field is not shown. The showcase stacks key art above the panel, the description shows in full, and the leaderboard lengthens to about fifteen rows. Every rail becomes a single column of full-width cards, so the page grows from 3,432 px to 12,920 px.

principles: When user-made content is the product, let the homepage be the catalog so the first click is play, not sign-up.
Attach live social proof (a leaderboard, play and like counts) to the showcased item rather than to a separate testimonial section.
Use a monospace face for metadata to give a catalog a tool-like texture without changing the display type.
interpretation.fit: Suits UGC platforms, marketplaces and libraries with enough good inventory to sell themselves. It would be wrong for a product without a content library yet, or for a visitor who needs to learn that they can create, since 'build games with AI' is never stated on the page.
interpretation.risks: No headline or value proposition, so a first-time visitor sees a game portal rather than a creation tool. Rails repeat the same games, which makes the catalog look smaller than its length suggests. 11 px mono body, hover-only arrows and a loading layer that blocks input weaken usability, and mobile becomes very long.

limitations: Showcase content varied between loads: one load showed a description and leaderboard, another showed 'No project description yet.' with no leaderboard.
My probe counted 81 running animations a few seconds after navigation while the measurement record reports 0; the early count may come from the loading layer.
Did not play a game or use search.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Drafted
summary: An architectural-sketch hero hands off to feature cards that act out each step of house design with a scripted cursor.

observations.hero: Minimal nav: serif 'Drafted' wordmark left, Learn and a black Sign In right. Centred serif headline, one-line subcopy and a black 'Start Creating' button sit over a pale watercolour/pencil illustration of a floor plan (left) and a farmhouse with trees (right). Grey press logos (Business Insider, TechCrunch, Reviewed) follow, and a row of illustrated house-plan cards with creator names starts at the fold.
observations.typography: Measured DM Serif Display for display: h1 60 px, weight 400, line-height 1.2, tracking 0; section heads in the same high-contrast serif, card titles at small sizes. Body in measured Inter at 14 px / 2.0 with an 86ch measure at 1440. Large serif numerals for the stats band.
observations.visual_system: Warm off-white and parchment ground, near-black text and buttons, beige rounded cards. Hero and closing band use soft, desaturated architectural illustration; plan cards pair painterly house renders with coloured floor plans. Product UI appears as small light mocks (room list, toolbar, materials panel, invite form). A sage-tinted band holds the persona cards.
observations.page_sequence: Sketch hero with plan cards → stats band (users, plans generated, rendered plans) → 'Everything you need…' (furnished plans, exterior renders) → 'The fastest workflow for home design' (five step cards) → Design together → Manage multiple projects → 'Join over 100,000 professionals' persona cards → Explore inspiration (Explore/Remix demo) → illustrated 'Create your first AI house plan for free' CTA → FAQ → guides → large link-directory footer.
observations.interaction: Operated the 'Make a plan your own' chapter control in Explore inspiration: the left rail marker moved from Explore to it and the demo's pill switched from Explore to Remix. On load, hero plan cards changed between captures; step cards showed a cursor adding rooms, a Create button and swapping toolbar selections. After the hero scrolls away a 'Start Creating' button appears centred in the nav. Under reduced motion frames still differed at the top and after scrolling.
observations.accessibility: Hero subcopy and press logos are mid-grey over a pale illustration; stats labels are light grey. Before full load several demo panels rendered empty. The document height equals the viewport and content scrolls inside an inner container. Persona cards are buttons exposing aria-expanded. No horizontal overflow measured. Motion continued under reduced-motion emulation.
observations.mobile: h1 drops to 36 px; the CTA label changes to 'Get Started'; nav keeps Sign In and drops Learn, adding Start Creating after scroll. The illustration shrinks to a faint house behind the CTA, press logos become a horizontally clipped strip, and one plan card shows at a time. Stats reflow to one large figure over two. Step, persona and FAQ blocks become one column; inner scroll height grows from about 8,000 to 11,359 px.

principles: Let each feature card act out its own step with a scripted cursor so the workflow reads without a video or sign-up.
Borrow the domain's own artefact style (pencil plans, watercolour elevations) for the hero to signal craft before any claim.
Promote the primary CTA into the nav once the hero button scrolls out of view.
interpretation.fit: Suits generative tools whose output is visual and step-based (plans, designs, layouts), where watching the steps is the argument. It would be wrong for a product with an invisible output such as an API or back-office automation, where staged UI theatre has nothing concrete to show.
interpretation.risks: Motion continues under reduced-motion emulation. Scrolling inside an inner container rather than the document can break full-page capture, scroll restoration and some assistive and browser scrolling behaviour. Demo panels are blank until scripts load. A 14 px body at an 86ch measure is long for reading, and the footer link directory dominates the page's end.

limitations: The page scrolls inside an inner container, so the measurement record's page_height (900 / 844) and the full-page screenshots cover only the first screen; I scrolled the container separately.
Which elements still moved under reduced motion was judged from frame comparisons, not identified individually.
In two visits the window load event did not fire within 120 s although content rendered; load performance was not measured.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Hotbox
summary: A serif promise flanked by fan-comment chips and outcome pills, then a tabbed DM-to-checkout chat mock that replays the sale per vertical.

observations.hero: Centred stack: pill eyebrow 'The AI system for high-demand drops', two-line serif headline with 'revenue' in rust and underlined by a brush stroke, one-sentence subhead, single 'Book a demo' button. Five tilted fan-question chips on the left and four outcome pills ('Tickets sold', 'Jersey purchased') on the right connect to the headline by thin curved lines. A row of product-category cards with 3D object renders sits along the fold.
observations.typography: Display h1 72px, weight 700, tracking -0.035em, line-height 0.9, measured family Honoka Mincho (a serif); the same serif carries every section headline. Body 19px / 1.5, measured family General Sans, measure about 74ch at desktop. Small caps-spaced sans eyebrows in rust or lime label each section.
observations.visual_system: Warm cream ground with a faint square grid, alternating with near-black espresso bands lit by a rust radial glow. Accents: rust-orange (underline stroke, connector lines, eyebrows) on light, acid lime (progress bar, checkmarks, CTA in footer card) on dark. Imagery is glossy 3D product renders on tilted white cards plus UI mocks: an Instagram-style DM thread, a dashboard, a brand-voice slider card. Wordmark sits on a tan cardboard-textured tag.
observations.page_sequence: Hero with comment chips and outcome pills → category card row → 'From message to order' dark demo (6 vertical tabs + phone chat) → 'The crowd is already telling you what they want' 3 feature cards → 'One system. Three views.' Automate/Measure/Retarget dashboard → 'Less inbox grind' without/with comparison → 'Automatic does not have to mean generic' voice section → FAQ accordion → dark CTA card with oversized wordmark and footer links.
observations.interaction: Clicked the 'Trading cards' tab in 'From message to order': the tab took the rust fill with lime title and the phone mock swapped from a mika.22 jersey conversation to a ryan.rips conversation about a 1/1 card, with the lime progress bar restarting. On load the category card row scrolls sideways and chat bubbles appear in sequence. While scrolling, 'Three views' moved from Automate to Measure. With reduced motion the card row still moved; running animations fell from 15 to 7.
observations.accessibility: Hero comment chips and outcome-pill labels are small (roughly 11-13px) and rotated. Grey body text inside the beige 'Without Hotbox' card is light against its ground. The category card row keeps moving under reduced motion. No horizontal overflow at either width. The header stayed at the top in every desktop scroll capture although the measurement recorded sticky_nav false.
observations.mobile: Header drops to wordmark and 'Login' with no other navigation visible. The desktop eyebrow is replaced by a 'Backed by a16z speedrun' line; comment chips and outcome pills are removed. h1 shrinks to 35.1px over three lines. Category cards stay a horizontal row. The vertical tabs stack above the phone mock, the three views become a horizontal button row, the comparison cards stack, and body drops to 16px at 44ch.

principles: Let one vertical selector drive a single product mock so each buyer segment sees its own worked example without leaving the page.
End the demo on the business outcome (a revenue-added receipt) rather than on interface chrome.
Surround the headline with literal inputs on one side and outcomes on the other so the product's job reads as a transformation before any copy is parsed.
Alternate light editorial bands for claims with dark bands for proof so the reader can tell argument from evidence by colour alone.
interpretation.fit: Suits B2B tools whose value is a conversation or workflow that can be scripted end to end (commerce agents, support automation, sales assistants). Wrong for infrastructure or APIs where the output is not a human-readable exchange.
interpretation.risks: The page is long (about 8,700px) with three separate simulated UIs, so proof repeats rather than deepens. Persistent marquee motion ignores reduced motion. Mobile strips navigation to Login only and drops the input/outcome framing that explains the hero on desktop. Only one CTA (book a demo) exists for every reader.

limitations: Did not open 'Book a demo' or log in; no conversion flow inspected.
Playwright screenshots timed out on this page; captures were taken through the DevTools protocol instead.
Mobile navigation behaviour (menu, sticky header) not operated.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Voltair
archetype_note: Hardware product-render showcase: full-bleed studio renders plus a scroll-driven globe operations sequence.
summary: A full-bleed studio render of the orange VTOL drone carries the first screen; the headline is a short stacked label beside it.

observations.hero: Full-bleed render of an orange-and-white fixed-wing VTOL drone, nose and camera gimbal toward the viewer, on a soft grey studio ground. Bottom-left: US-flag badge 'Engineered, manufactured, and deployed in America', three-line headline 'Drone / Infrastructure / Layer' with 'Layer' in orange, and 'Built for the grid'. Logo mark top-left, dark pill 'Book a Demo' top-right, orange pill 'Plan Your Mission' bottom-right. No navigation links.
observations.typography: No h1 element was measured. Largest display text 84px, measured family Neue June Medium, a wide grotesque set tight. Body 16px with line-height 1.1, measured family Garet Regular, measure about 51ch. Measured family Geist Mono carries bracketed index labels such as '[01 // AIRCRAFT]' and stat captions ('FLIGHT RANGE').
observations.visual_system: White ground for content sections, grey studio renders for hero and a mid-page band, near-black final section with faint map-line texture. One accent: saturated orange (headline words, pill CTAs, index labels, globe markers). Imagery: drone renders, sensor outputs (aerial RGB, false-colour thermal, LiDAR point cloud), a line drawing of the drone on its charging station, and a dotted wireframe globe. Footer ends on a large grey VOLTAIR wordmark.
observations.page_sequence: Render hero → four utility co-op logos → Faraday-1 aircraft: three sensor cards and four stat tiles (85 mi, 135 min, 12 min, <500 ms) → Lighthouse-1 ground station: proactive vs reactive mission lists flanking a line drawing → 'eyes in the sky' line → render band with 'Reserve Pilot Slot' → 'How Voltair Works' globe steps (select mission, deploy VTOL, receive data) → dark CTA 'Autonomous aerial coverage for critical infrastructure.' → contact/navigation footer.
observations.interaction: The page has no tabs, toggles or inputs; only links. Hovered 'Book a Demo': no visible change in the capture. Zero running CSS animations at load and after scroll. On scroll, the Faraday-1 block was caught mid-fade, and the globe section advanced 01 → 02 → 03: region marker, drone with orange beams, then an orange data card that filled with a line-drawn structure. Hero captures 2.5s apart were identical with and without reduced motion.
observations.accessibility: No h1 element in the measurement. White 'Drone Infrastructure' sits partly over the light grey of the render. Content captured mid-fade was very low contrast. Body line-height measured 1.1, tight for multi-line paragraphs. No visible text navigation in the header. No horizontal overflow; mobile scrollWidth matched 390.
observations.mobile: The hero crops to the drone nose and gimbal; the headline drops to 48px and 'Plan Your Mission' becomes a full-width pill under it, with 'Book a Demo' kept top-right. Logos regroup 2×2, sensor cards stack, stat tiles go 2×2, mission lists stack around the line drawing, and the globe steps persist with a narrower globe and the step text below. The footer stacks, moving the wordmark between navigation and the description.

principles: For physical products, let a full-bleed render of the hardware be the hero and keep the headline to a short category label.
Index each product as a numbered system component so a hardware stack reads as one service rather than separate SKUs.
Show the operating model as numbered steps on one pinned visual so buyers see how the service runs, not just what it contains.
Put named customer logos directly under the hero when the buyer is a regulated utility that buys on precedent.
