interpretation.fit: Suits hardware, robotics and defence or utility suppliers whose object is visually distinctive and whose buyers want proof of capability. Wrong for software products with no physical artefact, where a render-led hero would have nothing to show.
interpretation.risks: The first screen names a category ('infrastructure layer') but not the job (inspection data for utilities) until the sensor cards. There is no h1 and no text navigation, which weakens structure for assistive tech and scanning. Repeated 'Plan Your Mission' CTAs with no pricing or spec sheet leave little for a technical evaluator to take away.

limitations: Full-page screenshots were missing from the input bundle; the page was reviewed through live scroll captures instead.
Desktop screenshots timed out and the 390 capture hung in the globe section; mobile frames were taken with WebGL disabled, so mobile canvas rendering may differ from a real device.
No safe in-page control exists; only a hover was performed.
Did not verify whether the globe sequence honours reduced motion while scrolling.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: snag
summary: The homepage is the product: a search bar for where and when, then shelves of real priced sublet listings directly beneath it.

observations.hero: A peach band holds only the lowercase headline 'find sublet in minutes' and a white pill search bar with 'where' (pre-filled New York, clear button), 'when' ('add dates') and a round orange search button. Logo top-left, hamburger top-right; no other navigation. Below the band, the 'popular sublets' row of five listing cards is already visible in the first screen.

All headings and labels are lowercase ('popular sublets', 'best prices', 'list my place'). Listing captions are bold sans in white label boxes stacked over the photos.
observations.visual_system: Peach hero band over a pale cream page; bright orange for logo, search button and nothing else; charcoal footer. Imagery is real phone photos of rooms in tall rounded cards, overlaid with chips (avatar stacks with 'N interested', green '$N cheaper', red 'N saves'), a heart button, a white location/date label, a price pill and a verified host avatar. The host row uses selfie-style portraits with '+$63,281'-style earnings tags.

observations.interaction: Clicked 'add dates': a two-month calendar popover (October and November 2026) opened under the search bar, past dates greyed, overlapping the listing row. 21 animations were running at load and after scroll. In reduced-motion mode the count stayed at 21 and listing photos changed between captures 2.5s apart.
observations.accessibility: Search field labels 'where' and 'when' are small grey text. University logos are pale grey on cream. Listing caption labels sit on varied photos but on solid white boxes. Mobile heart buttons are roughly 32px. Motion on listing photos continued with reduced motion requested. Desktop navigation is hamburger-only. No horizontal overflow.
observations.mobile: An app-install banner ('snag sublets', 'get') takes the top. The h1 changes wording to 'find a sublet' at 40px. The pill search becomes stacked labelled fields with a full-width orange 'search' button. Each listing row becomes a horizontal scroller showing about 1.7 cards; host portraits show two at a time. principles: If the product is search, make the search control the hero and render real inventory immediately below it, so the first screen is already a result.
Give each shelf one social-proof metric (interest, savings, saves) so rows read as ranked answers rather than generic browse.
Rebuild an inline desktop search bar as stacked labelled fields with a full-width action on mobile instead of shrinking it.
Show the supply side's payoff as concrete earnings next to real faces to recruit listers on the same page as renters.
interpretation.fit: Suits two-sided marketplaces with photogenic, location-bound inventory (rentals, events, local services). Wrong for B2B or regulated products where buyers need explanation, credentials or pricing before inventory makes sense.
interpretation.risks: There is almost no explanation of trust or how sublets are verified beyond small check badges, so it leans on the 30,000-students claim. Pre-filled New York may misdirect visitors from other cities. Lowercase-only headings and the missing article in 'find sublet in minutes' read casual. Image motion ignores reduced motion.

limitations: Did not run a search, save a listing or open 'list my place'.
Listings, prices and counts are live inventory and will differ on another visit.
Did not inspect the hamburger menu contents.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

principles: Put the product's real output in the hero as a framed, labelled preview so the claim and the evidence share the first screen.

Use hairline rules, mono labels and a code sample to signal developer-grade infrastructure to a technical buyer without a dark theme.
interpretation.fit: Suits developer-facing AI and media infrastructure where output can be shown live and buyers compare latency, price and SDKs. Wrong for consumer apps, where mono labels, code blocks and spec strips would read as noise.
interpretation.risks: Evidence panels that show 'VIDEO PLACEHOLDER' undercut a page whose whole argument is visual realism. Low-contrast mono labelling makes structure hard to scan. limitations: Did not join the hero avatar call (would request microphone access).

Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Marble
summary: A light, single-accent page that walks each back-of-house job through its own concrete artifact: invoice, purchase-order checklist, prep sheet, schedule grid.

observations.hero: Left column: a three-line headline with 'autonomous' in burnt orange, a two-sentence description, and an orange 'Get a demo' button beside an outlined 'Learn more'. The right half holds a greyscale isometric kitchen illustration with an orange floor line. A row of greyed restaurant-group logos labelled 'Trusted by leading restaurant groups' closes the first screen.
observations.typography: Measured h1 64px, line-height 1.1, weight 300, tracking −0.025em, family Geist; body 17px/1.5 in measured Inter at about 68 characters. Phone h1 40px, body 15px. Nav labels are small tracked uppercase; section eyebrows ('THE PROBLEM', 'THE SOLUTION') are small orange uppercase. Large light-weight headings pair a dark first line with a grey second line ('Reimagine your operation. / Give your team more time for hospitality.').
observations.visual_system: Off-white ground, near-black text, one burnt-orange accent used for buttons, accent words, active tabs and chart highlights. Greyscale isometric illustration; black-and-white photographs on the problem cards; pale grey UI mockups (invoice, prep sheet, demand chart, schedule grid). Contrast bands: a near-black stats band, a full-bleed orange CTA band, and a grey marble-texture band above a dark footer.
observations.page_sequence: Hero + logo row → founders video band with 'Watch the full video' → rotating word list ('Top restaurant brands use Marble for' Inventory Counting, etc.) → 'The old operating stack was broken' with three photo cards → four modules (Inventory, Labor, Finance, Intelligence) → 'Purpose-built tools' four-tab panel → 'Better decisions' four artifact cards → dark stats band → A&W customer story with metrics → Connect / Learn / Compound steps → integrations → orange CTA 'See it in your kitchen next week.' → marble band → footer.
observations.interaction: Clicked tab '03 Agents on autopilot': its label turned orange (aria-selected false→true) and the right panel switched from a vendor-invoice card ($215.24 total) to a four-step 'Purchase order workflow' list. While scrolling, the active tab also changed without clicks (02, then 04). The logo row drifted sideways; the word list highlighted one word at a time; artifact cards went from pale to full contrast. Under reduced motion the logo row stayed still over 2 s and no animations were running.
observations.accessibility: Inactive tab copy and not-yet-revealed card text render very pale grey on off-white. One trust-row logo appeared as a broken image showing alt text 'The'. The founders video has a labelled pause control. No horizontal overflow at 1440 or 390. Phone CTAs are full-width bars roughly 44px tall.
observations.mobile: Nav collapses to wordmark, orange 'Get a demo' and a menu icon. The hero illustration is not shown; both CTAs become full-width stacked bars. Logos become a three-up strip. Modules form a 2×2 grid. The four-tab tools panel is recomposed into stacked sections, each with eyebrow, heading, copy and its own mockup. 'Better decisions' cards stack singly. Measured h1 drops from 64 to 40px.

principles: Give every product capability its own concrete artifact so switching tabs visibly changes the evidence, not only the caption.
State the operator's cost (hours, waste, labour overage) before introducing modules, so each module answers a named loss.
Reserve one accent colour for actions and the single word that carries the claim.
On phones, unroll a tab set into stacked sections rather than shrinking the tab panel.
interpretation.fit: Suits multi-location operations software sold to managers who need to see the documents the system produces. Wrong for a self-serve consumer app where a 16,000px explanatory scroll delays the one action.
interpretation.risks: The page is very long (16,376px measured at desktop). Scroll-driven tab changes compete with clicks. Much secondary copy is pale grey, and the phone first screen has no product image at all. A broken logo undermines the trust row.

limitations: Video elements reported paused in this headless Chromium, so the founders video and any video-driven hero behaviour were not seen playing.
Measurement says no sticky nav, but a floating nav bar appeared at the top of every scrolled desktop frame; the discrepancy was not resolved.
The 390 full-page capture is cut at 12,000px and later sections were not yet revealed; mobile was not operated live.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Gravis Robotics
summary: Full-bleed field footage of an excavator under a two-line bold headline, on a black ground with red used sparingly, lets the machine stand in for the pitch.

observations.hero: A black top bar holds the 'G' mark and six text links (Hardware, Software, About Us, News, Careers, Contact); there is no button. Below, full-width excavator footage under a dark gradient carries a small 'GRAVIS ROBOTICS' label, the centred two-line headline 'Tap your finger / move a mountain', a scroll cue, and a pause button at bottom right.
observations.typography: Measured h1 72px, line-height 1.0, weight 700, tracking 0, family Bahnschrift (a condensed-leaning DIN-style sans); body 22px/1.3 measured Inter at about 45 characters. Phone h1 28px, body 14px. Section titles ('What we do', 'Why Autonomy?', 'Meet the Gravis Rack') use the same bold display face at smaller size; dates and footer labels are small red text.
observations.visual_system: Black ground with white type; red is the only accent (buttons, the active benefit icon, logo-carousel progress line, news dates, footer headings). Imagery is real machinery: aerial and close-up excavator footage, a red-boom photo carousel with rounded corners, a cab photo, a white rendered excavator beside a worker. A dark soil-texture band sits behind the customer logos.
observations.page_sequence: Video hero → 'What we do' copy with red 'Watch the video' button beside an image carousel → 'Why Autonomy?' four-item accordion (Superhuman Productivity, Safety, Predictability, Simplicity) with image panel → 'Meet the Gravis Rack' photo and red 'Explore the Hardware' button → 'Trusted by market leaders' logo marquee on soil texture → 'Latest News' three cards → footer with offices and newsletter field.
observations.interaction: Clicked 'Safety' in 'Why Autonomy?': it was already marked red; after the click a white render of an excavator and a standing worker filled the image panel, which was empty in the pre-click frame. With default motion, the hero footage changed shots between frames 2 s apart (35% of pixels). In one load the headline and logo were absent for 9 s after DOMContentLoaded; after the load event they were present. Under reduced motion the hero held one still frame with headline shown.
observations.accessibility: White headline over footage sits on a darkening gradient. Small red dates and footer labels on black are low contrast. The newsletter email field had no aria-label attribute. The hero has a visible pause control. No horizontal overflow. Large areas rendered as empty black in full-page captures until scrolled into view.
observations.mobile: Nav collapses to the 'G' mark and a menu icon. The hero shortens (measured 664px) and the headline drops to 28px, about 0.39× desktop. The photo carousel shows one image; the logo marquee shows about two logos at a time; news cards stack; the footer stacks with the newsletter button below the field. In the 390 capture the space between the carousel and the logos rendered as plain black.

principles: When the product is a machine doing physical work, let unedited field footage carry the first screen and keep the headline to two short lines.
Use one accent colour only for state and action so the active item reads instantly on a dark ground.
Explain what the product does in one paragraph before showing customer logos and funding news.
interpretation.fit: Suits robotics, hardware and industrial autonomy with real field footage. Wrong for an API or SaaS product with nothing physical to film.
interpretation.risks: The first screen offers no action besides navigation and a scroll cue. Content depends on media and scroll reveals, leaving long black gaps while loading. The phone headline at 28px loses most of its weight. Benefit copy ('Less exposure, more awareness') stays generic next to strong imagery.

limitations: Video elements reported paused to script in this headless Chromium even while hero pixels changed, so playback behaviour is described only from frame differences.
Headline timing varied between loads; visibility depended on load progress over this proxy.
Measurement could not verify a reduced-motion rule; only one reduced-motion load was compared.
The 390 layout was captured, not operated live.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Context.dev
summary: The hero is a working, prefilled request box with five API modes as tabs, framed in saturated blue and wrapped in a dot-matrix motif carried through the page.

observations.hero: An announcement bar sits above a nav with 'Book demo' and a black 'Start for free'. Centred: a 'Backed by Y Combinator' badge, the headline with 'agents' in blue, one-line description, 'Start for free' and a 'Connect Context.dev' dropdown. Below, a thick blue frame holds a search box with mode tabs (Search Web, Scrape, Answer, Map, Brand), a self-typing placeholder query, and a blue submit arrow. Blue dot fields fill both margins.

The second measured family is doto; the demo placeholder and the ASCII-like card illustrations use a dot-matrix face. Section headings set a phrase in blue ('fully loaded.', 'at any scale.', 'what the web knows.').

Dot-matrix motif throughout: margin dot fields, dotted diagrams inside product cards, a giant dotted 'context.dev' wordmark in the footer. Hairline grid frames with corner marks. A dark band for 'Latest updates' and a dark footer.
observations.page_sequence: Hero demo → customer logo strip → 'Give your agent access to the web' with Prompt / MCP / CLI terminal → 2×2 product cards (Search, Scrape, Research, Monitor) → 'Also in the API' chips → 'Every page, fully loaded.' 99.96% stat and request log → tabbed code examples with six language tabs → 'Build on what the web knows' 3×2 use cases → 'Enterprise-grade security' → blue customer-story carousel → dark 'Latest updates' → FAQ with category tabs and 'Ask anything' box → footer.
observations.interaction: Clicked the hero 'Scrape' mode: the tab expanded to 'Scrape Any Page', a tooltip appeared ('Scrape any URL as Markdown, HTML, images, or a screenshot'), 'Search Web' shortened to 'Search', and the placeholder cleared and restarted typing. A click on the 'Python' code tab produced no visible change. The nav stays fixed on scroll. Under reduced motion no animations were running and the dot fields were still, but the placeholder still changed ('latest AI research papers' → 'open source vector databases').
observations.accessibility: Measured body text is 12.6px at desktop. Chip and caption text is light grey. At several scroll positions section copy showed through the fixed nav and overlapped the logo. Hero mode buttons and the search input carry aria-labels; the FAQ 'Ask anything' input had no aria-label attribute. No horizontal overflow.
observations.mobile: Nav collapses to logo and menu icon; the announcement bar stays. The hero drops the demo box and the 'Connect' dropdown, keeping one 'Start for free' with '1,000 free credits. No card required.' Headline breaks to two lines at 40px. Logos sit in a boxed three-up strip; the terminal and product cards stack singly. The 390 capture is blank below about 4,800px.

principles: Put a prefilled, safe request in the first screen and expose the product's verbs as modes of that one input.
Carry one visual motif from hero to footer so a long developer page reads as one system.
Offer the integration paths a developer will ask about (prompt, MCP, CLI, six SDK languages) as tabs near the top rather than on a docs page.
interpretation.fit: Suits developer APIs whose value is visible in a single request and response. Wrong for a non-technical buyer who needs outcomes before parameters.
interpretation.risks: Body copy at 12.6px is small for a ten-section page. The phone hero removes the demo, losing the page's strongest proof where most visitors arrive. Placeholder typing continues under reduced motion. Density is high: many tabs, chips and carousels compete.

limitations: One reduced-motion load failed through the proxy ('upstream request failed') and two succeeded; the paired default-motion load timed out, so default dot-field motion was not sampled side by side.
I did not submit the hero demo, so its output view was not seen.
The 390 full-page capture is blank below about 4,800px; mobile was not operated live.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Elyra
summary: A warm, photographic hero with a large light serif headline sells the guest's feeling first and leaves the reservation product almost entirely off the first screen.

Almost no colour beyond the photographs: white pills on dark, black pills on light, orange only in the YC badge. A small line drawing of a plate and wine glass decorates the word-list section. The hero eyebrow and stat captions are low-contrast grey on dark; inactive list words are pale grey on white. The phone nav 'Book a demo' pill looks about 30px tall. FAQ items are buttons. principles: For a hospitality product, lead with the guest's experience in photography and serif type, then explain the system in the sections below.

interpretation.risks: The product itself is hard to find: the three platform cards rendered as empty white panels in this browser and no interface appears above the fold. limitations: Video elements (four, including the platform-card media) reported paused at 0 s in this headless Chromium, so the platform cards appeared blank; they may show product footage in other browsers.

In one default-motion load the hero headline was also absent for 9 s after DOMContentLoaded; a later default-motion load after the load event showed it, and the reduced-motion load at the same timing did not.

name: Hedge
summary: A full-width two-line headline with a green second clause carries the pitch, backed by a numbered, ledger-like page of broker tools.

Geist Mono is the only other measured family; it carries the uppercase eyebrows, section numbers ('/ 01 · THE DIFFERENCE') and ticker labels. Palette is near-black, one dark green and grey; the only dark tile in the page body is 'Browse all guides' in the coverage grid. CTA with direct line → footer with oversized wordmark.
observations.interaction: Operated the /06 'In their words' tab list: selecting '02 Senior Producer' swapped the large quote and attribution and moved a short underline from 01 to 02. The coverage ticker scrolled continuously on load. While scrolling, a 'Hedge Connector' promo card appeared bottom-left alongside the cookie panel bottom-right. With reducedMotion 'reduce', no running animations were found and the first screen did not change over 1.2s.
observations.accessibility: Mono eyebrows and ticker labels are small and grey on off-white. The cookie panel covers the lower right of the first screen at 1440 and most of the lower half at 390; mid-scroll the promo card covered the lower left at the same time. No horizontal overflow at either width. The header did not stay in view after scrolling down.
observations.mobile: Nav collapses to the wordmark and a circular menu button. The headline rewraps to four lines at 39px with the green clause kept. All card rows and the 12-class coverage grid stack to one column, taking the page from 7,160px to 11,382px. The cookie panel occupies most of the first screen below the buttons.

principles: Split the headline into a plain category clause and a coloured qualifier so the niche reads as the emphasis, then reuse that two-tone device on every section heading.
Number sections like a document ('/01', '/02') when the audience is professional and expects to scan for a specific part.
Turn domain inventory (coverage classes, forms, checklists) into a browsable grid so the homepage doubles as a reference tool for repeat visitors.
A scrolling ticker of covered categories can state breadth without a logo wall when the buyer cares about scope more than social proof.
interpretation.fit: Suits B2B services sold to practitioners who know the jargon (wholesale insurance, lending, logistics brokerage) and judge credibility by specificity. Wrong for a consumer product, where the lack of imagery and the density of trade terms would read as cold.
interpretation.risks: With no imagery, every section looks the same in weight, so the long middle (coverage grid, resources) can blur together. Two simultaneous overlays (cookie panel and promo card) cover content on scroll, and the mobile page grows to over 11,000px because dense grids stack one item per row.

limitations: Measurement record lists the nav height as 777px at 1440, which does not match the visible ~73px header; not relied on.
Did not operate the appetite checker, which links away from the homepage.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

Body measured 16px/1.5 fontMono, 84ch measure (14px/1.6, 49ch at 390). principles: When the product is a desktop app, swap the mobile hero's download button for an 'email me the link' capture instead of a dead-end download.
Show the value of hidden infrastructure by staging a familiar interface (a chat client) and contrasting answers with and without your product.
Put open-source traction (GitHub star count) directly beside the primary CTA when developers are the early audience.
Let one typeface family signal the product's register (monospace for developer tooling) in the hero, then relax to sans and serif for longer reading below.
interpretation.fit: Suits developer tools and local-first infrastructure whose value appears only inside other software. Wrong for a non-technical buyer, for whom a monospaced hero and MCP/REST API vocabulary set the wrong expectations.
interpretation.risks: The page is very long (over 10,000px measured at 1440) and repeats proof in several forms. Mock-ups that look operable but do not respond, as with the with/without toggle in this session, can read as broken. Three type registers on one page weaken the hero's mono signal.

limitations: The with/without toggle produced no visible change in this session; whether it works in other browsers or after other input was not tested.
Live page height at 1440 was 7,599px versus 10,399px in the measurement record, and the live run reached the footer without the FAQ seen in the stored full capture; content may vary between loads.
Stored full-page captures were truncated at 9,000px (1440) and 12,000px (390), so the lower page was reviewed from the live visit only.

Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

observations.visual_system: Cream ground after the dark hero. Warm, desaturated photography: the contract still life, a wood-panelled interior with an armchair, and studio portraits of attorneys on pale grey. Cards are rounded, off-white with soft borders; one pricing tier is inverted to near-black. Client logos sit in individual tiles. Colour beyond cream, brown and black comes only from client logos.
observations.page_sequence: Photo hero with split CTA panel → '500+ startups, scaleups, and enterprises trust General Legal' testimonial masonry + logo tiles → interior photo with 'Expert judgment for every matter' and four numbered steps (Start Today, Priced Up Front, Accessible Expertise, Legal at AI Speed) → 'A new kind of firm...' attorney portrait cards → 'The best lawyers, now on every matter' practice-area card → 'Simple, transparent pricing' four tiers → FAQ → closing CTA and footer.
observations.interaction: Operated FAQ item '4. How does pricing work?': it expanded with a tinted row, the plus became a minus, and an answer with a 'pricing page' link appeared. On scroll, the large 'Expert judgment' line sat over the interior photo while step cards passed; the practice-area labels were at different angles in live and stored captures. The fixed header moved out of view when scrolling down. Nothing visibly moved on the first screen in either normal or reduced-motion loads.
observations.accessibility: Cream text and the outlined 'Start a matter' button sit on a photograph; the right half of the description runs over the lighter document area. Where 'Expert judgment for every matter' crosses the photo, letters darken against the wood, reducing legibility. At 390 the menu icon is two thin lines. The hero image stops about 15px short of the right edge at both widths. No horizontal overflow measured.
observations.mobile: The photo is cropped tighter on the document; headline, description and two full-width stacked buttons fill the lower half, and the panel's explanatory labels are dropped. Testimonials reduce to one card per row, logos to a two-column grid, attorney cards to a horizontal row cut at the edge. The 'Expert judgment' photo-and-steps section does not appear (measured sections 6 vs 7). Pricing tiers stack.

principles: Split the hero CTA into two labelled paths ('talk to us' vs 'start now with a fixed quote') when buyers arrive at different levels of readiness.
Use a still-life of the actual work product (a contract) as hero imagery to signal the service without stock-photo people.
Put real prices on the homepage when the business model's differentiator is pricing; it turns a positioning claim into something checkable.
Show the named experts with credentials early when trust in a new kind of firm depends on who does the work.
interpretation.fit: Suits professional services re-packaged as products (legal, accounting, advisory) where trust, people and pricing transparency matter more than a software UI. Wrong for a self-serve software tool, where atmosphere photography would delay showing what the product does.
interpretation.risks: The photographic mood costs legibility in two places (hero copy over the image, display text over the interior photo). The page is long (12,104px at 1440) and the mobile version silently drops the four-step process section, so phone visitors lose the explanation of how engagement works.

limitations: Measurement record reports a video element, but nothing played on the first screen in this browser; headless Chromium may not support the video format, so hero motion was not verified.
Rotation of the practice-area labels was inferred from two captures; its trigger was not observed.
YC page location field is blank, so no geography evidence is recorded.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Known
archetype_note: Manifesto splash: one centered text poem on black plus an app CTA; a brand poster, not an editorial page.
summary: The homepage is a single centered manifesto on black, a short protest against swiping, ending in one Apply to Join button.
round: Pear portfolio, Pre-seed → Seed (year not shown)

viewports.desktop: 1440 × 900: rendered, scrolled; no in-page control at this width (menu toggle operated at 390)

observations.hero: knowndating.com redirects to known.com. The first screen is pure black with a wordmark top-left, three text links and an outlined Apply to Join pill top-right, and a narrow centered block of short sentences in four stanzas ('Profiles told us nothing...', 'Not a game. Not a job. Not a gamble.'). There is no headline, image or product shot above the fold.
observations.typography: Measured h1 is 16px, weight 500, 0em tracking, family -apple-system, and holds 'Known: your pocket matchmaker, a swipeless dating app'; it is not the visible copy. Largest measured display text is 18px. The manifesto is set as small, centered, regular-weight sans lines with blank-line stanza breaks; body measured 16px / 1.5. The wordmark is a custom lowercase logotype; only -apple-system is in the measured families.
observations.visual_system: Black ground (#000-like) with off-white text; footer shifts to a slightly warm near-black. The bottom CTA is a light grey pill with a metallic sheen. Press logos (Union-Tribune, LA Times, WSJ and more) are dimmed grey. A QR code sits in the desktop footer. A full-viewport video element exists but was paused and not visible in any capture.
observations.page_sequence: Manifesto stanzas → 'This is Known.' → Apply to Join button → 'Available on iOS & Android, featured in' press logos → footer (QR code, Discover / Here / Elsewhere link columns, wordmark, copyright). Measured as one section, 1317px tall at 1440.
observations.interaction: At 390 I operated the hamburger: it became an X and a black panel dropped down with three large links (How it Works, Guidelines, Journal) over the top of the manifesto. With motion on, manifesto lines changed between captures and the 390 full capture shows lines fading in from a blur. In motion mode only three press logos showed, the first cropped at the edge; under reduced motion all lines rendered at once, eight press logos appeared in a static grid, and paired captures were identical.
observations.accessibility: Small grey 'Available on iOS & Android' text and dimmed press logos sit on black at low apparent contrast. The visible manifesto is not the h1; the h1 is a 16px line. Transparent sticky nav lets manifesto text scroll beneath the links. No horizontal overflow measured. Mobile header CTA and hamburger are comfortably sized.
observations.mobile: Nav links collapse into a hamburger and the Apply to Join pill moves beside it. Stanzas rewrap to the same centered column. The footer QR code is replaced by an app icon labeled 'Tap to Install', and link columns go two-up then stack. Page grows to 1601px.

principles: When the product's pitch is a rejection of category norms, a short manifesto can carry the whole first screen without any product imagery.
Pair a single-action page with one CTA repeated in the nav and at the end of the text, so the reader never has to search for the next step.
Swap a desktop QR code for a direct install link on mobile so the download path fits the device.
interpretation.fit: Consumer apps with a clear stance and an application or waitlist gate, where tone matters more than features. Wrong for any B2B or technical product whose buyer needs to see how it works.
interpretation.risks: The page explains almost nothing: no screenshot, no how-it-works, no pricing, and the real h1 is hidden from sight. The line-by-line blur reveal delays reading on load, and the low-contrast grey details may fail contrast checks.

limitations: Could not operate an in-page control at 1440; the only interactive elements were nav links and Apply to Join, which leads to an application flow.
A video element was present but paused; whether it plays under other conditions was not verified.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Prized
summary: A saturated cobalt brand world, with ASCII art, a split-flap board and a giant clock, shows always-on dev boxes as scenes rather than feature lists.

observations.hero: A white YC announcement strip sits above a full-bleed cobalt hero. Left: a three-line light-weight headline, one-line subhead, white 'Create my box' and outlined 'Read the docs' pills, a '$30 of credit. No card.' note, and a black terminal chip with a curl install command and copy button. Right: a large cloud drawn in ASCII characters over a dotted field.
observations.typography: Measured h1 77.4px, weight 300, -0.035em tracking, line-height 1.0, family prizedSans; body 17px / 1.6 prizedSans with an 87ch measure. JetBrains Mono is used for commands, labels and the split-flap board; a 'mockFace' family appears in product mocks. The display reads as a light grotesque with tight tracking.
observations.visual_system: Three grounds alternate: cobalt blue, black, and white rounded cards. Imagery is all typographic: ASCII clouds and laptops, a split-flap departures board, a 24-hour bar chart, a huge 17:58 clock. Pills for CTAs, mono for anything machine-like. Footer ends with an oversized ghosted wordmark and asterisk logo. A floating 'Watch the launch 1:02' video tile sits bottom-right.
observations.page_sequence: YC strip → blue hero → 'New: Sandboxes' strip → black 'Check on it from anywhere' dashboard mock → white '24 hours a day' bar chart → black 'Ports are localhost' split-flap board plus terminal → white card 'Files go both ways' with ASCII laptops → pinned blue 'At six you close the lid' clock scene → 'A clear advantage' table vs Codespaces and Coder → blue 'Your box is two minutes away' CTA → black footer.
observations.interaction: I clicked 'on Windows?' under the install chip: the command changed to 'irm https://prized.dev/install.ps1 | iex' and the caption to 'Windows PowerShell · on macOS or Linux?'. The dashboard mock's filter tabs could not be clicked; an overlay intercepted pointer events. With motion on, the hero ASCII cloud and the split-flap characters changed between captures, and the clock scene stayed pinned across about 1,800px of scroll. Under reduced motion, paired captures at top and mid-page were identical.
observations.accessibility: White text on cobalt reads clearly at display sizes, but small light-blue mono captions ('macOS and Linux') on blue look low-contrast. The copy button is icon-only but exposed an accessible name. Product-mock buttons are present in the DOM but blocked from pointer input. No horizontal overflow measured. Mobile CTA pills are large.
observations.mobile: h1 drops to 34px over four lines; the YC strip shortens to 'Backed by Combinator'; 'Sandboxes' leaves the nav. The ASCII cloud moves below the install chip, which wraps the curl command with a backslash continuation. Sections stack single-column; the comparison table stays tabular. Measured content width 249px; page 9473px with 9 sections.

principles: Turn each product claim into one memorable scene (a clock, a port board, a sync diagram) instead of a feature grid.
Put the real install command in the hero with a copy button and an OS toggle, so a developer can act without leaving the first screen.
Build imagery from the product's own medium, here text characters, so the brand and the subject reinforce each other.
Gate ambient motion on prefers-reduced-motion so the scenes still read when frozen.
interpretation.fit: Developer infrastructure and CLI-first tools whose buyers trust terminal output more than illustrations. Wrong for a regulated enterprise purchase where buyers need security, compliance and integration detail early.
interpretation.risks: Scene-per-section pacing makes a long page (8,845px) with little dense information; the pinned clock scene costs a lot of scroll for one idea. Mock UI that looks clickable but is not may frustrate. Small mono captions on blue risk contrast failures.

limitations: Did not play the launch film or inspect the docs; the hero ASCII cloud's motion was observed only as changes between two captures.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: End Close
summary: A framed split hero pairs a plain reconciliation promise with a live-looking matching table and an 'Agent resolved' toast, then walks the workflow tab by tab.

observations.hero: Redirects to www.endclose.com. A white page with a wordmark, a centered outlined nav pill (Product, Company, Docs) and a violet 'Learn more on a call' button. The hero is a hairline-framed two-column box: left a four-line headline, subhead, violet 'Book a demo' and 'Find out more →'; right a reconciliation table mock (24 / 14 matched / 10 unmatched) with an 'Agent resolved · EXC-004' toast. A four-cell stat row closes the frame. A cookie banner overlays the lower left.
observations.typography: Measured h1 60px, weight 600, 0em tracking, line-height 1.0, family ui-sans-serif (system stack); body 18px / 1.6 with a 45ch measure. Geist Mono is used for amounts, references and the feature-chip cloud. Hierarchy is weight and size only; no display face.
observations.visual_system: White and very light grey bands, hairline borders with small crosshair marks at frame corners, one violet accent for primary buttons, active tab rules and highlighted chips. Imagery is product UI only: tables, a data-source picker modal, a reconciliation overview with record counts. Green/red amounts and status pills come from the mocks. One testimonial card uses a blue gradient panel with a headshot.
observations.page_sequence: Framed hero + stat row → 'From origination to closed books' three tabs (Ingest, Automated matching, AI agents) over a product mock → Sunbound testimonial → 'Everything you need out of the box' four tabs + mono feature-chip cloud → 'Compare us to building in-house or buying a legacy vendor' three-column table → 'Trust your numbers. Stop chasing them.' CTA card → footer with SOC badge.
observations.interaction: I clicked the 'Automated matching' tab: its top rule turned violet and the mock changed from an 'Add a data source' modal to a 'TabaPay vs CRB' reconciliation overview (102,009 of 161,396 reconciled). On scroll the nav re-formed as a centered floating pill holding the logomark, links and CTA. The active tab's rule filled like a progress bar; that fill kept running under reduced motion, while the hero stayed static in both modes.
observations.accessibility: Inactive tab titles and descriptions are light grey on white, a contrast concern. Mono chips are small. The cookie banner covers part of the first screen at both widths. At 390 the word 'reconciliation' extends past the hero frame's right border, though no page-level horizontal overflow was measured. A progress animation continues under reduced motion.
observations.mobile: Nav collapses to a hamburger (measured nav height 0). h1 drops to 48px; the table mock moves below the CTAs and the stat row stacks two-up. Tabs stack vertically, the comparison table becomes stacked per-row blocks, and the page more than doubles to 9387px. The cookie banner covers roughly the lower quarter of the first screen.

principles: Show the exception being resolved, not just the dashboard: a single toast like 'Agent resolved · Duplicate refund' carries the AI claim more credibly than a slogan.
Tie each workflow tab to its own product state so clicking a step changes what the buyer sees.
Use a three-way comparison (you, build in-house, legacy vendor) when the real competitor is the buyer's own engineering team.
Reserve a monospace face for money and identifiers so financial data reads as data.
interpretation.fit: B2B finance, payments ops and other back-office software where buyers want proof of correctness and audit trails. Wrong for a consumer product or anything that needs emotional brand pull over evidence.
interpretation.risks: The layout follows a common B2B SaaS pattern and is visually hard to tell apart from peers. The hero headline breaks its frame on mobile, the cookie banner hides first-screen content, and the tab progress fill ignores reduced motion. The 99.999% claim sits without visible sourcing.

limitations: Whether the workflow tabs auto-advance on their own was not confirmed.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Andera
summary: A centered, lavender-tinted hero hands off to a scroll-pinned walkthrough in which mock audit workpapers fill in and log checks as you scroll.

observations.hero: A lavender announcement bar ('We raised $37M led by Lightspeed...'), then a white nav with six links and an outlined Book a demo. The centered headline 'Audit just got / a whole lot easier' has 'lot easier' in a purple gradient and small selection-handle squares and dots around it. Below: a two-line subhead, a dark 'Book a demo' button, a 'Trusted by audit teams at' logo row, and the top of a 'My Tasks' dashboard mock.
observations.typography: Measured h1 64px, weight 550, -0.01em tracking, line-height 1.1, family Manrope; body 16px / 1.5 Manrope with a 52ch measure. Inter is also present. Section headings repeat a two-tone pattern: dark indigo plus a purple-gradient phrase ('end-to-end.', 'your controls', 'security.').
observations.visual_system: Near-white ground with lavender tints, dark-indigo text and a purple accent. Faint fine-line wave patterns at the hero edges; small rounded pill labels ('Features', 'Explore GRC', 'Security') above each section. Imagery is product UI: task dashboards, a spreadsheet with an audit log, RCM and testing tables, plus concentric rings around a SOC badge and a team photo.
observations.page_sequence: Announcement bar → centered hero + logos → dashboard mock with progress chart → 'Fieldwork automated, end-to-end' pinned three-step (Control Testing, Evidence Gathering, Exception Management) → 'A home for your controls' tabs (RCM, Risks, Dashboard) → 'Focus on risk, not reconciliation' three staggered numbered cards → 'Enterprise-grade security' → 'Give your team their best hours back' CTA → 'We are the industry experts' about + photo → FAQ accordion → footer.
observations.interaction: I clicked the 'Dashboard' tab under 'A home for your controls': the caption changed to 'Track anything and everything...' and the two-table RCM/Testing mock was replaced by an 'Acme Inc' dashboard (58% completed, workload bar, control rows). While scrolling, the features section pinned and its step titles lit in turn. Under reduced motion the hero was static, but audit-log check icons still appeared between captures in the features mock.
observations.accessibility: Several texts are pale lavender-grey on near-white ('Trusted by audit teams at', inactive step titles, card body text), a contrast concern. Measured mobile body text is 12px. The 1440 full-page capture shows a long blank band where the pinned section sits. No horizontal overflow measured. The FAQ uses buttons for questions.
observations.mobile: The announcement bar wraps to two link lines; nav reduces to Book a demo plus a hamburger. h1 drops to 44px and still fits on two lines. Logos wrap to three rows. Tabs, the three numbered cards and the about section stack single-column; the dashboard mock is scaled down rather than recomposed. Measured body text drops to 12px; page 9587px.

principles: Let a pinned scroll section narrate a multi-step workflow, with one step lit at a time and its mock filling in beside it.
Show the work being done (timestamped audit-log lines, 'Control passes with no deviations') rather than a static result when selling automation to auditors.
Repeat one heading device, like a gradient tail phrase, across sections to give a light-ground B2B page a recognizable rhythm.
Answer the buyer's incumbent question (RPA, existing GRC tool) directly in the FAQ.
interpretation.fit: Enterprise compliance, audit and GRC tools sold to professional users who need to see their own artifacts (RCMs, workpapers, exceptions). Wrong for a self-serve product, where a long pinned walkthrough delays the moment of trying it.
interpretation.risks: Pale lavender text costs legibility, and 12px mobile body text is small. The pinned section adds scroll length and renders as empty space in static captures and possibly for crawlers. Some log animation continues under reduced motion. The decorative selection handles around the headline say little about the product.

limitations: The FAQ accordion and the other two pinned feature steps' mocks were not inspected in detail.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Vercel
summary: A two-word category claim beside the brand triangle, then three use-case chapters, each proven by a named customer's live product and one usage number.

observations.hero: Left: a two-line h1 'Agentic Infrastructure' above a black 'Deploy now' pill and an outlined 'Talk to sales' pill. Centre: a solid black triangle with a soft shadow, missing from the measurement's first-screen capture but present in later captures. Right: three short stacked lines saying who it is for. Wide empty margins above and below; a seven-logo customer row (Meta, Blackbox.ai, DoorDash, OpenAI, SpaceX, The Weather Company, Polymarket) closes the first screen.
observations.typography: Measured h1 64px, weight 400, tracking -0.06em, line-height 1.0, family GeistSans; 48px with line-height 1.2 at 390. Body 16px/1.5 GeistSans; measured families GeistSans and Geist Mono. Section headings run near display size with visibly tight tracking and regular weight, so hierarchy comes from size and space, not boldness. Customer stats set the first clause in black and the rest in grey. At 390 the hero subline is set in the mono family (measured body family Geist Mono).
observations.visual_system: Near-white ground, black type, and no accent colour except a blue folded-corner graphic on the Backends card. The only imagery is the triangle mark and greyscale, bottom-faded screenshots of customer products (a Notion AI chat, the Zapier homepage, Mintlify docs). Pill buttons, 1px card borders and large blank areas; no photography, gradients or illustration.
observations.page_sequence: Hero → customer logo row → 'Build agents on infrastructure that thinks like them' (Notion artifact, stat, features) → 'Ship apps that scale from zero to millions instantly' (Zapier) → 'Host platforms that serve every customer' (Mintlify) → 'Recently shipped' (Backends, Agents, Sandbox cards) → 'Built by you, or your agents' CTA (Deploy now, Onboard your agent) → six-column footer link grid.
observations.copy: H1: 'Agentic Infrastructure'. No subhead paragraph; instead three lines: 'For coding agents', 'To ship apps and agents', 'Automated by agents'. Primary button 'Deploy now'; secondary 'Talk to sales'; the header adds 'Get a Demo', 'Log In' and 'Sign Up'. The h1 names the category and the lines name agents and the teams building them as the audience. Each use case carries one customer claim, e.g. 'Zapier serves over 100 million monthly website visits on Vercel.'
observations.interaction: Hovering 'Products' opened a full-width menu of three columns (Agent Stack, Core Platform, Tools) in large type and greyed the page; a click straight after the hover left it closed. Captures 2s apart at the top and mid-page were identical. Customer artifacts appeared during slow scrolling but were blank after instant jumps; the full-page captures are blank from the Mintlify section down. At 390 the logo row moved on its own and the mono subline changed between captures. Under reduced motion the hero was unchanged and artifacts still appeared.
observations.accessibility: No horizontal overflow at either width. At 390, 87 of 91 visible links and buttons were under 44px tall (hero buttons 40px, footer links 24px); the menu button is 44×44 and labelled 'Open menu'. The three Recently shipped card links (/backends, /agents, /sandbox) had no text content or aria-label. Grey second clauses and faded artifact text are lighter than body copy; one footer label computed at about 3.1:1.
observations.mobile: The triangle moves above a centred 48px h1; the three audience lines collapse to one mono line that changed between captures; buttons stretch full width and stack; nav reduces to the triangle and a menu button; the logo row becomes a cropped strip that scrolls by itself. Case studies stack heading → artifact (overlapping cards cropped at the right edge) → stat → features. Page height measured 5557px against 5930px at 1440.

principles: Organise a broad platform by the jobs buyers hire it for, and back each job with one named customer, one number and a four-item feature list.
Let customers' real products be the imagery; a strict monochrome keeps those screenshots reading as evidence rather than decoration.
Replace the subhead paragraph with a short list of who the product is for, placed beside the headline.
interpretation.fit: Suits broad infrastructure or platform companies with recognisable customers and several distinct buyer jobs. Wrong for an early developer tool without marquee customers, where readers need to see the API or a working example before they trust a category claim.
interpretation.risks: The first screen carries no product evidence and the h1 is an abstract category label. The proof depends on artifacts that render only as they scroll into view, so full-page captures and fast scrolls show large empty areas. No code, pricing or deploy flow appears on the page; developers have to click through to evaluate.

limitations: The 390 full-page capture is blank below the second case study, so later mobile sections were not visually inspected.
Whether the hero triangle responds to the pointer was not tested.
Contrast was checked by computed-style sampling only, not a full audit.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Superhuman
summary: A cinematic sky-and-portrait video carries the brand mood while floating product UI cards supply proof, then a sticky-tabbed suite walks through four products.

observations.hero: Full-bleed video of a person in profile against a dusk sky. A centred white headline, a one-line subhead and a dark 'Get Superhuman' button with a purple arrow sit on the sky. Translucent product cards float over the video: a Go chat booking a meeting, a vertical app rail, an inbox list, a doc with an editing toolbar and a 'Tailor this language for executives' chip. A dark pill above the nav asks 'Looking for Superhuman Mail?'. The person differed between captures.
observations.typography: Measured h1 64px, weight 540, tracking 0, line-height 1.0, family Super Sans VF; 32px at 390. Body 18px/1.5 with a 55ch measure at 1440 and 28ch at 390; Super Sans VF is the only measured family. Section and product headlines are large, light-weight dark grey on stone; the wordmark is spaced uppercase. Links are purple, underlined, with a trailing arrow.
observations.visual_system: Two grounds: a photographic sky video with frosted, purple-tinted UI cards, then warm stone with diagonal hatch-pattern gutters, hatched dividers, dashed rules and bordered panels. Product panels pair text with screenshots set on photographic or gradient backdrops. Later come a dark teal brand block with a collage portrait, a pink-and-blue blurred cloud band with faint mono text, and a maroon footer with a giant tonal 'SUPERHUMAN' wordmark.
observations.page_sequence: Mail announcement pill → nav → video hero with floating UI → 'Trusted by the most innovative companies in the world' logo grid → 'Your Superhuman suite' with sticky tabs (Mail, Grammarly, Docs, Go) over four stacked product panels → 'Becoming Superhuman.' brand statement with 'Read our announcement' → 'AI that works everywhere you work' closing band with 'Get Superhuman' → footer.
observations.copy: H1: 'Superpowers, everywhere you work'. Subhead: 'Mail, Docs, and AI that works in every app and tab'. Primary button 'Get Superhuman'. The category is presented as a suite; each product gets a superlative headline ('The most productive email app ever made', 'Everyone's favorite AI writing partner') and four outcome bullets such as 'Save 4 hours every single week'. The audience is anyone working across apps; no role or company size is named.
observations.interaction: Clicking 'Docs' in the suite tabs scrolled the Docs panel up under the sticky tab bar and shaded Docs; the shading also followed scroll position before the click. On load one video was playing and the measurement counted 10 running animations; floating cards and chips shifted while scrolling, and logo-grid cells changed between captures, sometimes blank. With reduced motion the hero video stayed paused on a still frame and one animation on an image in an asset grid kept running.
observations.accessibility: White headline over moving video: estimated from screenshot pixels at about 3.9:1 for the h1 and 3.0:1 for the 26px subhead, varying with the frame. Frosted cards carry small light text over video. At 390 the menu button is 36×36, the wordmark link had no text or aria-label in the DOM scan, and 39 of 44 targets were under 44px tall. No horizontal overflow. The alternate variant noted in limitations had no h1 element.
observations.mobile: The text block stacks above the video; the h1 drops to 32px over two lines; floating UI cards are removed, leaving the portrait. Nav becomes wordmark plus a menu button that opens a full-screen list. The logo grid becomes 3×2. The suite loses its tab bar: products stack, each with its screenshot below the bullets, and 'Get the suite' moves under the heading. Page height grows from 6446px to 8505px.

principles: Layer real product UI fragments over an emotional full-bleed scene so mood and proof are read in the same glance.
For a multi-product suite, put a sticky tab bar over stacked chapters so it both navigates and shows where the reader is.
Give every product chapter the same structure (headline, one sentence, learn-more link, four outcome bullets, screenshot) so several products read as one system.
interpretation.fit: Suits prosumer or team productivity suites selling an outcome such as time saved across several products. Wrong for developer or infrastructure products whose buyers need technical specifics rather than atmosphere.
interpretation.risks: Headline contrast depends on the video frame, and the hero leans on video that some browsers and capture tools will not play. Two homepage variants were served on the same day, so first impressions differ by visitor. Four products and superlative claims compete for one button, and the outcome bullets have no supporting evidence on the page.

limitations: Two of four fresh desktop loads served a different variant: a dark hero, 'Save 4+ hours each week with Superhuman Mail', with an auto-advancing Mail/Go/Docs list and no h1. This record describes the variant that matches the measurement record.
Desktop product-panel images were blank in the full-page capture and appeared only during the live scroll.
The measurement record lists the reduced-motion rule as unverified; reduced-motion behaviour here comes from one load.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Plain
summary: A centred two-tone promise, then four feature chapters that each pair a wide product video with three close-up UI fragments, ending in a 29-minute onboarding ladder.

viewports.desktop: 1440 × 900: rendered, scrolled; no control could be operated (see limitations)
viewports.mobile: 390 × 844: rendered and measured; menu toggle operated

observations.hero: Centred on white: a two-line h1 with the first line bright green and the second near-black, a two-line subhead, and two square-cornered mono buttons ('BOOK A DEMO' filled green, 'START A TRIAL' outlined). Below sits a wide pale-green panel framed by solid and dashed green curves that holds a product video, with a full-width logo strip across it at the fold. A dark green bar above the nav promotes Ari; a cookie prompt covered the lower right.
observations.typography: Measured h1 80px, weight 400, tracking -0.02em, line-height 1.0, family ABC Favorit Regular; 46px at 390. Body 18px/1.3 with a 73ch measure at 1440, 20px at 390. Measured families ABC Favorit Regular and Medium, Roboto and Geist Mono. Mono uppercase is reserved for buttons, eyebrows ('HUNDREDS OF FAST-MOVING TEAMS RELY ON PLAIN'), chapter pills (AGENTS, WORKFLOWS) and 'DISCOVER …' links.
observations.visual_system: White ground alternating with deep forest-green bands with rounded top corners; one bright green accent for buttons, links, icons and line-art. Pale green panels with green curves frame product media; warm off-white cards hold small UI fragments (an if/else rule, an agent reply, 'Create Linear Ticket', auto-triage labels). Dotted vertical lines connect sections. A maroon Granola case-study card breaks the green palette.
observations.page_sequence: Ari bar → nav → centred hero → product panel and logo strip → second logo row → 'Tools add [icon] distance.' problem → dark 'Meet a new approach: Support Infrastructure' with six capability cards → Agents → Workflows → Sidekick → Insights chapters → dark 'Speed, meet power.' comparison rows → 'Take their word for it' testimonials → 'Here's what you can do in 29 mins and 59 secs' (5/15/29 mins) → security → closing CTA → footer.
observations.copy: H1: 'Build support your own way'. Subhead: Plain is AI support infrastructure that lets B2B teams build anything, no-code or all-code. Primary button 'BOOK A DEMO'; secondary 'START A TRIAL', with 'START FOR FREE' in the closing CTA. The page names the category 'Support Infrastructure' and the audience 'B2B teams', frames the problem as 'Tools add distance.', and addresses comparison shoppers directly ('Here's why, and when, we win').
observations.interaction: No tabs, toggles, carousels or demo inputs were found in a scan of buttons, tabs and pointer-cursor elements. The header 'Product' dropdown, built as a link, did not open on hover or click, and the floating chat launcher sat under the cookie prompt. Product media are videos that did not play here. Captures 2s apart at top and mid-page were identical with and without reduced motion; the measurement counted 2 animations at 1440 and 50 on load, 143 after scroll at 390. At 390 the menu opened as a full-screen accordion.
observations.accessibility: The accent green (computed rgb 26,211,121) on white is about 2.0:1, used for the first h1 line and 'START A TRIAL'; light text on the green 'BOOK A DEMO' is about 1.9:1, as is 'START FOR FREE' on pale green. At 390 the menu toggle is a 24×24 element exposed as neither button nor link, the logo link had no name, 11 of 15 targets were under 24px tall, and the chat bubble overlapped 'BOOK A DEMO' in the open menu. No horizontal overflow.
observations.mobile: The h1 stays centred at 46px; buttons stretch and stack; the announcement shortens to 'Your new autonomous support agent'. The hero panel shows product UI (a webhook ticket thread with an 'Ask a follow up' composer). The problem line's single Slack icon becomes a row of app icons with a 999+ badge; the dark section heading overlays a monitor photo; capability cards and chapters stack (pill → media → headline → text). Page height grows from 12,155px to 16,328px.

principles: Under each wide product view, add three close-up fragments of real states (a routing rule, an agent reply, a created ticket) so every feature claim has something concrete to point at.
Name the pain in a short visual phrase before introducing the new category.
Turn onboarding claims into a time ladder (5, 15, 29 minutes) with specific tasks at each step.
Reserve a mono uppercase voice for actions and labels so navigation cues never blend into prose.
interpretation.fit: Suits B2B workflow software sold against incumbents, where buyers want to see mechanics, routing and integrations. Wrong for a single-action consumer product, where twelve thousand pixels of repeated chapters would bury the one thing to do.
interpretation.risks: The brand green fails text contrast on the h1, buttons and links. Wide product proof depends on videos that this browser could not play, leaving the static fragments to carry the evidence alone. Four identical chapter templates flatten priority, and the page is very long on both widths.

limitations: No desktop control could be operated: the page has no tabs, toggles, carousels or demo inputs, and the header dropdown and chat launcher did not respond in headless Chromium.
Product videos did not play in this Chromium build (it reports no H.264 support; WebM sources never loaded), so their content was not seen at 1440.
Contrast values come from computed styles or screenshot pixels, not a full audit.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Harvey
summary: A serif declaration with a full-width product dashboard directly beneath, then a buyer split, an auto-advancing product accordion and a stack of enterprise proof.

observations.hero: Split first screen under a black funding announcement bar: a two-line serif h1 on the left; on the right a one-sentence trust claim and a square black 'Request a Demo' button. Directly below, a full-width rounded panel with a dark painterly texture frames a large product screenshot, 'Whitford Lane's Command Center', with usage charts. The nav repeats 'Request a Demo' beside 'Login'.
observations.typography: Measured h1 72px, weight 400, tracking -0.012em, line-height 1.0, family HarveySerifFont; 48px/1.1 at 390. Body 14px/1.3, family HarveySansFont, 43ch measure at 1440. The serif sets the h1, several section heads, the testimonial quote, video-card titles and the stat numerals; the sans sets 'Product Innovation for the Best Legal Minds', labels and body. The product UI itself uses the serif for page titles.
observations.visual_system: Off-white upper page that turns near-black from the client videos onward. Product screenshots sit on dark green-grey painterly textures; law-firm logos are greyscale. Square-cornered black buttons, thin rules between accordion items and stats, a portrait photo for the testimonial, and no accent colour outside the product UI.
observations.page_sequence: Funding bar → nav → split hero → full-width product screenshot → '3,500+ Legal Organizations Build on Harvey' logo grid → 'One Platform for Legal Work' (For Law Firms / For In-House cards) → 'Introducing Harvey II' with video → 'Product Innovation for the Best Legal Minds' accordion and product panel → three-slide testimonial carousel → 'Real Impact for Real Clients' video cards → stats → 'Enterprise-Grade Security and Controls' certifications → 'Unlock Professional Class AI for Your Organization' CTA → footer.
observations.copy: H1: 'Build a Frontier Legal Organization'. Subhead: the world's top law firms and in-house legal teams trust Harvey with their highest-stakes work. Primary button 'Request a Demo', repeated in the nav, hero, Harvey II block and closing band; no trial or pricing path appears. Audiences are named explicitly (law firms, in-house teams), and scale is asserted with numbers (3,500+ organizations, 200,000+ professionals, 80+ AmLaw 100 firms) and the funding headline.
observations.interaction: The Product Innovation list auto-advances, with a growing progress line and a 'Pause auto-advance' button; it had reached Spaces on arrival. Clicking 'Vault' set aria-expanded to true, expanded its description and 'Learn More', collapsed Spaces, and swapped the right panel from a 'Project Titan — Acme Co' space to a 'Create a vault' file-source dialog. Product images were semi-transparent in some scroll captures and blank after instant jumps. With reduced motion the progress line did not change across captures 2s apart; in the normal run it did.
observations.accessibility: Accordion buttons expose aria-expanded, and auto-advance has a labelled pause button. Inactive accordion labels are light grey on off-white. At 390 the menu button is 24×25px, the funding announcement becomes an 18px-tall scrolling ticker link, 43 of 97 targets were under 24px tall, and the hero dashboard's text becomes too small to read. No horizontal overflow at either width.
observations.mobile: The announcement becomes a scrolling ticker; nav reduces to the wordmark and a menu button that opens a black full-screen overlay with large serif items and 'Request a Demo' / 'Login' buttons. The h1 wraps to three lines at 48px above the subhead, button and a shrunken dashboard. Logos form three columns; buyer cards stack; the accordion becomes every item expanded with its image; client videos stack as dark tiles showing an 'H' placeholder. Page height grows to 14,611px.

principles: Put a real, detailed product screen at full width directly under the headline so the first scroll lands on product rather than marketing.
Split readers by buyer type early (law firm or in-house) before the feature tour begins.
If a feature list auto-advances, sync it to a product panel, show progress, and give it a pause control.
Use the serif for claims and numbers and the sans for explanation and UI, so voice and evidence stay visually distinct.
interpretation.fit: Suits vertical enterprise software sold to conservative, high-stakes professional buyers who look for peers, numbers and certifications. Wrong for a self-serve or early-stage product: without logos, usage figures and certifications the proof stack has nothing to stand on.
interpretation.risks: Much of the persuasion is accumulated enterprise proof (funding, logos, AmLaw counts, certifications) that a young company cannot copy. A single demo-request path excludes evaluators who want to try the product. Dense dashboards become illegible at 390, and the page runs to 14,611px on a phone.

limitations: No 1440 full-page screenshot was in the bundle; the desktop sequence comes from the live slow scroll.
Client case-study videos were not played; the 390 capture shows placeholder tiles in their place.
Whether reduced motion fully stops auto-advance was inferred from two captures 2s apart.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Dia
summary: An oversized serif wordmark on a yellow scene outranks a modest h1, then numbered steps show finished artifacts Dia produces, with the waitlist button always on screen.

observations.hero: Saturated yellow, blurred foliage-like ground. A floating white pill nav (logo, What's New, Apps, Security) sits top centre over a one-line white serif h1. Below, an oversized white serif 'DIA' wordmark with swash terminals is half-hidden behind a cream macOS-style browser window showing a tab sidebar and an 'Ask anything…' field. A cream arc cuts across the bottom, holding a wide black 'Join the Waitlist' button and 'Available for macOS and Windows'.
observations.typography: Measured h1 38.8px, weight 500, tracking -0.04em, line-height 1.1, family Exposure VAR (a serif); 28px at 390, where the measured largest text is 48px in ABC Oracle. The 'DIA' wordmark is far larger than the h1. Body 14px/1.4 ABC Oracle at 1440, 16px/1.5 at 390; measured families ABC Oracle, ABC Oracle Triple, ABC Favorit Mono and Exposure VAR. Section heads use the serif; feature cards use spaced uppercase pills; privacy toggles use mono and the footer mono uppercase.
observations.visual_system: Warm yellow hero, then cream for the rest of the page. Product evidence is shown as finished artifacts in framed, shadowed browser windows: a 'Friday Brief' with a landscape painting, a pale-blue 'Sarah's Week Recap', a chat summary. Bento cards with thin rounded borders, a dotted-border privacy box with a lock and On/Off chips, and the cream arc reused as a persistent bottom bar. The footer carries a circular Browser Company seal.
observations.page_sequence: Pill nav → h1 → DIA wordmark and browser window → Join the Waitlist → 'Dia reads between the tabs' (01 Start your day two steps ahead, 02 Synthesis you'll actually use, 03 Find the answer without hunting it down, each with an artifact) → 'Built for how you actually work' bento (Profiles, Live Work, Better Meetings, Splits, Decks, Organized Tabs) → 'Privacy first with you in control' → 'Ready for a better day?' with Join the Waitlist → mono footer.
observations.copy: H1: 'More than a browser. A better workday.' There is no subhead; the only supporting line is 'Available for macOS and Windows'. Primary button 'Join the Waitlist'; with a phone user agent it read 'Send download link'. The page names the category as a browser and immediately reframes it as a workday outcome; section copy addresses people juggling work, freelance and personal contexts, and names 'Dia for Work' for teams.
observations.interaction: Clicking '02 Synthesis you'll actually use' scrolled the page so the 'Sarah's Week Recap' artifact sat beside the list, expanded 02's description with a left rule, and greyed 01 and 03; the active step also followed scroll position. After the hero, a sticky bottom arc with 'Join the Waitlist' and a top-right waitlist pill stayed on screen. The four video elements never loaded a source, and captures 2s apart at top and mid-page were identical; reduced motion looked the same, with all content visible.
observations.accessibility: White serif h1 on yellow estimated at about 2.2:1 from screenshot pixels. Inactive step titles and footer links are light grey on cream. The sticky bottom bar covers roughly the lowest 100px of the viewport throughout. At 390 the menu toggle measured 16×16px and a tap on it timed out; 19 of 29 targets were under 24px tall. No horizontal overflow at either width.
observations.mobile: The pill nav becomes a full-width bar with the 'Dia' wordmark and a '+' button. The h1 wraps to two lines; the wordmark and window scale down, and the waitlist button moves below the yellow arc at full width. The numbered steps recompose into artifact-then-caption pairs with no side list; the bento becomes one column; privacy chips are cropped at both edges; the footer becomes two mono columns.

principles: Show what the product produces (a morning brief, a weekly recap, an answer) as finished artifacts rather than the interface mid-task.
When the name is the asset, let the wordmark be the display type and keep the h1 to one supporting line.
Keep a single conversion action persistent during long storytelling, and adapt its label to the visitor's device.
On phones, recompose a scroll-linked side list into artifact-then-caption pairs instead of shrinking it.
interpretation.fit: Suits consumer or prosumer software with a distinctive brand and one action such as a waitlist or download. Wrong for B2B infrastructure or regulated buyers who need pricing, integrations, security detail and a sales path.
interpretation.risks: White text on yellow fails contrast, and the sticky bar permanently costs viewport height. The hero window is decorative (an empty 'Ask anything' field), so the first screen sells mood over capability. A waitlist-only action with no pricing leaves evaluators nothing to try immediately.

limitations: Hero and feature-card videos did not load in this Chromium build, so their content was not seen.
The 'Dia reads between the tabs' heading appeared clipped in the measurement full-page capture but rendered fully in the live visit.
The main button label differed by user agent; other device-specific differences were not explored.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Cursor
summary: Small, quiet type defers to staged product windows—agent queue, CLI, Slack, phone—set on painted landscapes, so the product's working state carries the pitch.

observations.hero: A thin nav, then a left-aligned two-line h1 and two pill buttons (dark download, light 'Request a demo →'); no subhead. Below, a full-width beige panel holds a 'Cursor Desktop' window mock—agent task sidebar ('In progress', 'Ready for review'), chat pane, browser or editor pane—overlapped by a 'Cursor CLI' window, set over a painted landscape. The demo fills the lower half of the first screen.
observations.typography: Measured h1 26px/1.3, weight 400, tracking -0.012em, CursorGothic—small for a hero; 24.4px at 390. Measured body 17.3px/1.3 EB Garamond; the only serif visible is inside the hero's mock 'Acme Labs' page, while section copy is a grotesque like the h1. berkeleyMono and system-ui are also measured; CLI text is monospace. Section heads pair a dark lead sentence with a grey continuation. The largest type is the closing 'Try Cursor now.'
observations.visual_system: Warm off-white ground with slightly darker beige panels and borderless cards; near-black pill buttons; orange reserved for text links ('Learn about cloud agents →'). Every feature panel pairs copy with a macOS-style window (traffic-light dots) floating over a painted landscape. Customer logos sit in eight grey tiles. Two photographs (code on monitors, a team at a whiteboard); otherwise all imagery is product UI.
observations.page_sequence: Hero (h1, CTAs, desktop + CLI demo) → logo tiles 'Trusted every day by teams that build world-class software' → four alternating feature panels (agents turn ideas into code → works autonomously, in parallel → in every tool: terminal, Slack, GitHub, with a curl install line → hand work to AI teammates) → 'The new way to build software.' six named testimonials → 'Stay on the frontier' three cards → dated changelog → research-team photo panel → recent blog highlights → 'Try Cursor now.' → footer with theme toggle.
observations.copy: h1: 'Cursor is your coding agent for building ambitious software.' No hero subhead. The primary button is platform-specific: 'Download for Linux' in the measurement capture, 'Download for macOS' in the live visit, 'Get started →' at 390. The category is named directly ('coding agent'); audience is implied by 'teams that build world-class software' and the enterprise card's 'Trusted by over half of the Fortune 500'.
observations.interaction: Clicked the 'presence.ts' file tab in the first feature panel's editor mock: only a hover state appeared (a close ×); the panel stayed on feature-prd.md. Frame pairs 1–1.5 s apart at the top and eight scroll positions showed no visible change. Demo windows (Slack, CLI, phone repo list) were empty when scrolled into view live but filled in the measurement capture, and the hero showed a different task state in each capture. Reduced motion: sampled frames still.
observations.accessibility: Grey continuation sentences and grey card metadata sit on beige at visibly reduced contrast. Demo windows are built from real DOM controls: four icon-only buttons in them have no accessible name and two textareas are labelled only by placeholder. 30 visible controls at 390 are under 24px in one dimension, mostly inside demos (model pickers ~19px tall). No horizontal overflow at either width (measured). A cookie banner covers the lower first screen in the measurement captures.
observations.mobile: Nav reduces to logo, 'Sign in' and a menu icon; the two hero buttons become one 'Get started →'. The hero demo keeps desktop scale and is cropped by its frame's right edge. Logo tiles become 4×2; feature panels stack copy above demo; testimonials drop from six to three; frontier cards stack; changelog and blog rows become horizontal strips with the next card cut off at the edge; footer goes to two columns.

principles: Let the product carry the hero: a modest headline and two buttons leave room for a large, realistic working-state window above the fold.
Use one staging device—an app window over the same painted backdrop—in every feature section so varied demos read as one system.
Split each section head into a dark claim and a grey elaboration to get headline and subhead in one typographic block.
Match the primary download button to the visitor's platform so the first action needs no choice.
interpretation.fit: Suits products whose interface is the proof—editors, agent consoles, developer tools—sold to audiences who recognise the UI. Wrong for back-end or abstract products (a payments API, a compliance engine) where a window mock shows nothing a visitor can read.
interpretation.risks: A 26px h1 gives the category claim little weight, so the page leans on brand recognition. Demo windows are dense small-text UI, unreadable when cropped at 390, and their filled state depends on timing—early viewers can see empty windows. Grey secondary text on beige lowers contrast, and tabs that look clickable do nothing.

limitations: The live visit rendered without the painted backdrops and some card images; visual-system notes rely on the measurement captures.
A second desktop load returned HTTP 502 and was stopped as instructed; observations use the first live visit.
Could not establish when or how the demo windows fill with content; no motion appeared in 1–1.5 s frame pairs.
Cookie banner and platform-specific button label varied between captures.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Railway
summary: An illustrated night-sky railway world—track rail, departure board, 'All Aboard'—wraps scripted product-canvas demos, so infrastructure reads as calm rather than technical.

observations.hero: Under a dark nav, an inset rounded panel holds an illustrated night sky with stars and pink-lit clouds. Centered: serif h1, one-line subhead, a purple 'Deploy →' and a dark 'Agents' button. Beneath sits a large product window ('New Project' dialog, later a service canvas) with a stage bar—Deploy, Network, Scale, Monitor, Evolve—over painted mountains and a bullet train; a 6×2 logo grid closes the panel.
observations.typography: Measured h1 54px/1.1, weight 500, tracking -0.036em, IBM Plex Serif (40px, -0.049em at 390). Section heads use the same serif as two-line sentence-case statements ('Deploy anything / without the complexity'). Measured body 18px/1.6 Inter at a 56ch measure. JetBrains Mono and SF Mono are also measured; the stats board uses wide-spaced monospace characters in split-flap tiles.
observations.visual_system: Near-black navy ground with large rounded panels tinted per chapter (navy, teal-grey, maroon). Each chapter carries a coloured pill label (grey 'Build and deploy', green 'Network and connect', orange 'Scale and grow'). A vertical track line with train-car icons runs down the left edge between chapters. Imagery is product UI—service-graph canvas, metrics dashboard, environment stacks—plus the illustrated sky, mountains and a perspective grid floor at the close.
observations.page_sequence: Hero panel (h1, CTAs, staged product window, logos) → Build and deploy (canvas mock, three features, 'Alternative to' logos) → Network and connect → Scale and grow → Monitor and observe (metrics dashboard) → Evolve and collaborate (environment stacks) → 'Trusted by the best in business' three customer quotes → '…and loved by developers' social posts → 'deploys per month (and counting)' split-flap stats board → 'A better future is now boarding' with 'All Aboard' → footer with Featured cards and a Compare column.
