observations.copy: h1: 'Ship software peacefully'. Subhead: 'With the all-in-one intelligent cloud provider', with 'intelligent' underlined. Primary button 'Deploy →', secondary 'Agents'; the nav adds 'Book a demo'. The category is named as 'cloud provider'. Competitors are named through each chapter's 'Alternative to' logos and the footer's Compare column (Heroku, Render, Fly.io, Vercel). Proof uses counts ('220.4M+ deploys per month', 'Join 2M+ developers').
observations.interaction: Clicked 'Evolve' in the hero's stage bar: no visible change within 2 s (an earlier attempt timed out waiting for the bar to settle). The bar advanced on its own—'Network' and 'Scale' were highlighted at different times as the window switched scenes. Section canvases rebuilt with new project names; a pointer opened a dropdown in the dashboard mock; the stats heading read '0+' in a live frame ('220.4M+' in the measurement capture) and the split-flap board filled in from blank tiles. Reduced motion: sampled frames still.
observations.accessibility: Grey body text on navy and small grey 'Alternative to' logos are low-contrast. The nav's sign-in and demo links render as grey placeholder blocks for the first seconds. A full-width cookie notice appears at the bottom after a few seconds. At 390 the split-flap board clips labels and digits ('DEPLOYMENT', '220,433,48') inside its frame; no page-level overflow measured. Footer text links measure ~20px tall at 1440.
observations.mobile: Nav collapses to logo and a menu icon. The hero drops the product window: serif h1 (40px), subhead, two buttons, then a 2×3 logo grid inside the sky panel. Each chapter becomes a stacked card—label, serif head, a reduced canvas thumbnail, features listed vertically. Customer quotes stack; developer posts become a sideways card row; the stats board crops at both edges. Page grows to 13,351px (measured).

principles: Build one metaphor into the structure—progress rail, departure board, boarding call—so brand elements also mark navigation and proof.
Give every feature chapter the same frame (label, statement, live-looking demo, three features, 'alternative to' row) so a long page stays scannable.
Name the incumbents you replace in line so evaluators can map the product to tools they already use.
Animate product mocks to show state changes (build, alert, scale), but make each resting frame meaningful on its own.
interpretation.fit: Suits developer infrastructure in a crowded category where tone ('peacefully') is the differentiator and the team can fund custom illustration. Wrong for products sold through risk-averse procurement—core banking, healthcare records—where whimsy can undercut the seriousness buyers expect.
interpretation.risks: Illustration and staged demos load late: early frames show a flat panel, an empty dialog and placeholder nav. The mobile hero removes the product entirely, leaving only the slogan. Chapter demos move on their own, so a reader can miss the state being explained, and the stage bar looks interactive but did not respond.

limitations: The hero stage-bar control did not respond in two attempts; could not confirm whether it is meant to be interactive.
Full-page captures stop at 9,000px (desktop) and 12,000px (mobile); the page end was seen only in live frames.
The live mobile visit did not scroll past the hero; mobile notes rely on the measurement capture.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Figma
summary: The hero sets a four-word h1, a stacked collage of finished design work and one oversized black button side by side, letting outputs stand in for the tool.

observations.hero: Three zones on a white first screen: the h1 set left over three lines, a centred collage of overlapping artifacts (a phone audio-player UI with a bird photo, an orange chat card, photos), and a large black 'Get started' button on the right. The nav carries 'Log in', 'Contact sales' and a black 'Get started for free'. A pale-blue Config banner with its own button pins to the viewport bottom a few seconds after load.
observations.typography: One family carries the page: measured h1 56px/1.0, weight 400, tracking -0.022em, figmaSans (36px, -0.035em at 390). Measured body 30px/1.2 figmaSans—the large intro paragraphs. figmaMono is the only other measured family. Headings never go bold; hierarchy comes from size and a black-then-grey split within one sentence pair. The closing 'Get started' bar sets display-size type inside the button.
observations.visual_system: White ground, black text, black buttons; colour comes almost entirely from product media—illustration, type specimens, photos and UI—in a staggered tile grid with round play buttons. Hairline dividers and wide blank space separate sections. The only tinted surface is the pale-blue Config banner with a black, distorted wordmark. The footer flips to black.
observations.page_sequence: Hero (h1, artifact collage, Get started) → 'Move fast in the right direction on an AI-native canvas' with 'Your built-in creative collaborator' → 'One workspace for your entire product development process' with media and design/build links → 'Powerfully expressive. Incredibly precise.' staggered media grid → 'Start with design context. Build with consistency.' (Figma Make) → 'The products you love are designed in Figma' quote, 95% stat, logo marquee → 'Ideas no longer have to wait their turn' full-width Get started → template carousel → black footer.
observations.copy: h1: 'The full-stack creative canvas'. Section lines name the audience as teams working with agents ('Teammates and AI agents work in the same space with shared context'; 'Made so your whole team can go from WIP to ship, together'). Primary buttons: 'Get started' (hero, closing bar) and 'Get started for free' (nav). Proof is one statistic, '95% of the Fortune 500 uses Figma', beside one named quote.
observations.interaction: Clicked the template carousel's 'Next slide' arrow: the counter changed from '1 of 10' to '2 of 10' and the card row shifted one card left. The hero collage held still across ~7 s; the Config banner appeared at the viewport bottom; the logo marquee scrolled sideways, with a pause button at its end. Video tiles showed a 'Player error' overlay in this Chromium. At one scroll step the page re-flowed and the scroll position jumped back ~740px. Reduced motion: frames still, no animations reported running.
observations.accessibility: Grey continuation sentences on white are lighter than the lead but large (30px measured). The fixed Config banner covers the bottom ~90px of the viewport at 1440 and a taller stacked block at 390 until dismissed. At 390, inline 'Explore …' links measure ~22px tall. The logo marquee has a visible pause control and a skip link is present. No horizontal overflow at either width (measured).
observations.mobile: Nav keeps the logo, a black 'Get started for free' button and a menu icon. The hero stacks: h1 (36px) → artifact collage at reduced width → centred 'Get started'. The Config banner becomes a stacked block with a full-width 'Read more'. The media grid drops to two staggered columns; quote, stat and template sections stack; footer link groups run as one long list.

principles: Show what customers make with the tool rather than the tool's chrome when the output is more persuasive than the interface.
Use one typeface and carry hierarchy with size and a black/grey value split, so a restrained page frames colourful media.
Give the one action that matters unusual physical scale—a hero button rivalling the h1, a full-width closing bar.
Pair one strong statistic with one named quote instead of a wall of testimonials.
interpretation.fit: Suits visual and creative products with varied, attractive output—design, video, presentation and site builders. Wrong for infrastructure, security or compliance tools whose output is invisible and whose buyers need mechanism and evidence.
interpretation.risks: The argument depends on video tiles: when playback fails the page shows error overlays and blank slots. The h1 is abstract and does not tell a newcomer what the product does. A persistent promotional banner competes with the primary button and covers content on both widths.

limitations: Video tiles failed to play in headless Chromium ('Player error'), so their motion and content could not be seen.
Full-page captures contain large blank areas where media had not rendered; those sections were checked only in live frames.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Clerk
summary: A tabbed showcase of Clerk's own drop-in components—sign-up form, sign-in card, profile panel—sits directly under a heavy h1, so the shipped UI is the pitch.

observations.hero: A black announcement bar ('Clerk raises $50m Series C') sits above a floating rounded nav. Left: a heavy two-line h1 and one-line subhead. Right: a 'Build with agents' tab holding a copyable prompt. Below, a full-width panel with four product tabs (User Authentication, Multi-tenancy, Enterprise Authentication, Agent Authentication) shows a crisp 'Create your account' card between faded sign-in and profile cards, with sub-tabs underneath. No hero button; Sign in and Sign up sit in the nav.
observations.typography: Measured h1 56px/1.1, weight 700, tracking -0.035em, family geistNumbers (32px, weight 600, -0.015em at 390)—a tight, heavy grotesque. Measured body 11px ui-sans-serif at 1440 and 16px geistNumbers at 390. soehneMono and Inter are also measured; the agent prompt is set in a monospace. Section heads are bold and short ('Auth that keeps evolving', 'Subscription billing, without the headache') under small coloured eyebrow labels.
observations.visual_system: Light grey and white sections alternate with near-black bands whose top and bottom edges are cut into chamfered trapezoids. The dark band holds a bento grid of feature cards with soft rendered grey illustrations (code-entry slots, fingerprint, phone, profile card). Accent colour is limited to purple and cyan eyebrows and small dots. Product components appear as white cards with soft shadows and blue-violet glows; framework and integration logos sit as outline icons in a hairline grid.
observations.page_sequence: Announcement bar → hero (h1, agent prompt, tabbed component demo) → customer logos → dark 'Auth that keeps evolving' bento of 11 features → 'Everything your B2B SaaS needs' (roles, auto-join, invitations, organization components) → 'Subscription billing, without the headache' with a pricing-table mock → dark split 'Build with SDKs for modern frameworks' / 'Integrate with the tools you love' → 'Trusted around the world' with a Supabase CEO quote and a wall of developer posts → footer.
observations.copy: h1: 'Everything you need for authentication'. Subhead: 'More than APIs. The complete user layer for modern apps.' There is no hero button; the first offered action is copying 'Add Clerk auth to my app: clerk.com/SKILL.md', then per-section links such as 'Explore user authentication ▸'. The category is named directly; the audience is developers building B2B SaaS, with pricing language in proof ('Free for your first 50,000 monthly retained users').
observations.interaction: Clicked the 'Multi-tenancy' tab in the hero demo: it took a hover highlight but the panel stayed on User Authentication through ~2 s. The hero demo did not change across ~8 s at the top; the measurement capture shows a pointer graphic and a typed 'c' in its email field. Nav Sign in/Sign up appeared a few seconds after load. On scroll, a soft glow behind the billing mock shifted hue; with reduced motion that glow still shifted and nothing else was seen moving.
observations.accessibility: Faded side cards in the hero demo and grey card text are low-contrast. At 390 a floating round chat button overlaps the demo card, and the tab label 'Enterprise Authenticati…' and the agent prompt are truncated. No horizontal overflow at either width (measured). In the desktop DOM check all 81 visible controls had accessible names; 46 were under 24px in one dimension, mostly nav and footer text links.
observations.mobile: The floating nav keeps logo, Sign in, Sign up and a menu icon. The hero stacks h1 → subhead → truncated agent prompt → tabs as a 2×2 grid → only the central 'Create your account' card, with sub-tabs cut off at the right. Logos become 2×2. The bento becomes one column; the billing mock shows one plan with the next peeking; framework and integration grids stack. Page grows from 7,187px to 13,378px (measured).

principles: If the product is UI, show the real components in context before any feature list.
Offer an agent-ready install prompt beside the headline when buyers increasingly start integrations through coding agents.
Gather a broad feature set into one dark bento band with a single illustration style, so breadth reads as one system.
Mark chapter changes on a long page with contrasting bands and a distinctive edge shape.
interpretation.fit: Suits developer products that ship visible UI—authentication, payments, chat or form widgets—where component quality is a buying reason. Wrong for back-end-only infrastructure with no UI to show, where a component showcase would have to be invented.
interpretation.risks: No hero button: the strongest call is a copy-to-clipboard prompt plus nav links, which can stall non-developer evaluators. The hero demo depends on tab state and timing; when it does not respond, the first screen is a static form. Faded side cards and small grey text lower contrast.

limitations: The live mobile visit and a verification reload returned HTTP 502 and were stopped; mobile notes come from the measurement captures.
Could not confirm whether the hero tabs switch for real users; the one click produced only a hover highlight.
The hero demo's pointer and typing were seen only in the measurement capture, not live.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Neon
summary: Numbered, mono-labelled chapters of two-tone sentence headlines on black carry a backend-platform argument, switching to a mint ground with marker highlights for the architecture story.

observations.hero: An announcement bar ('Neon now has realtime…') tops a black nav with Discord, a GitHub star count, Log in and Sign up. The upper two-thirds is a field of glowing vertical green, blue and white bar clusters. Lower left: a monospace line 'NEON IS PART OF THE DATABRICKS PLATFORM', a two-line h1 with a dotted underline under 'Lakebase', and white 'Get started' plus outline 'Read the docs' pills. A divider and a scrolling logo row close the screen.
observations.typography: Measured h1 56px/1.1, weight 400, tracking -0.04em, Inter (32px at 390). Measured body 18px/1.3 Inter at a narrow 29ch measure. GeistMono is the other measured family; uppercase labels, the large outline-grey chapter numerals ('01', '02', '03') and terminal-style blocks are monospace. Section heads are one paragraph—a white lead sentence, then a grey continuation—with the first line indented.
observations.visual_system: Pure black ground for the first half, with green as the main accent and small red triangles marking chapter labels. Mid-page the ground switches to pale mint, where key phrases get green marker highlights. Surfaces are hairline-bordered dark cards and stat tiles (100K+, 70%, 20M+, 3M+); uppercase labels such as 'WHERE STARTUPS START' sit on dark-green bars. Charts are pixel and bar grids; the closing panel at 390 shows a grey wireframe mountain.
observations.page_sequence: Hero → logo marquee → 01 Build your backend (five product cards: Lakebase Postgres, Authentication, Compute, Storage, AI Gateway) → 02 Operate it with agents (three points + agent chat panel) → 03 Scale your app and agent (startups, agent platforms, Fortune 500 tiers with stats and a quote) → mint manifesto with side index (Lakebase Architecture, Advanced Autoscaling, Built by Databricks) → autoscaling chart toggle → 'Backed by giants' stats → usage-based pricing cards → 'The world's most advanced backend platform.' CTAs → footer.
observations.copy: h1: 'The backend for apps and agents, built to scale on Lakebase Postgres.' No separate subhead; the Databricks line above the h1 supplies the reassurance. Primary button 'Get started', secondary 'Read the docs'; the close adds a copyable '$ npx neon init'. The audience is named as apps and agents, then segmented into startups, agent platforms and the Fortune 500 in chapter 03.
observations.interaction: Clicked 'Save costs' in the autoscaling toggle: it took the pressed state and the chart changed from a split 'Without Neon' (red spike, 'Resource limit reached… Outage triggered') vs 'With Neon' ('Autoscaling active', '+4 vCPU') view to one chart with a '4 vCPU/16 GB RAM… Savings estimation 80%' callout. The logo row scrolled continuously; the chapter-02 agent panel shifted between frames; the hero bars held still across ~7 s. Reduced motion: the logo row stopped; sampled frames still.
observations.accessibility: Grey continuation sentences and small grey card copy on black are low-contrast. The Databricks label link measures 10px tall at 390. Broken-image placeholders are visible in captures (announcement bar, Storage card, Databricks logo); the live check found 4 broken images at 1440 and 2 at 390. Large black voids sit between chapter-03 items at 1440. No horizontal overflow (measured); footer legal links are ~15px tall at 390.
observations.mobile: Announcement text truncates with an ellipsis; nav becomes logo plus menu. The hero bar field shrinks to a band above the h1; buttons stay side by side. Chapters keep the numeral above the two-tone sentence; the five product cards become a sideways strip with the next card peeking; the agent panel moves below the text and shows a prompt and 'Thinking…'. Pricing cards and stats stack; the closing panel puts the wireframe mountain above full-width buttons.

principles: Number the chapters and label them in monospace so a long technical page reads as a sequence, not a feature dump.
Write each section head as one sentence pair—bright claim, grey elaboration—so the point lands before any card.
Use a two-state toggle on one chart to show both buyer motives (avoid outages, save costs) with the same data.
Place the backing or ownership signal above the h1 when it answers the buyer's first risk question.
interpretation.fit: Suits developer infrastructure with a clear technical claim and buyers who read docs before talking to sales. Wrong for consumer or design-led products, where the restraint and long grey-on-black text would feel cold and slow.
interpretation.risks: Much of the page depends on late-loading media: captures show black voids, broken-image icons and blank card illustrations, which undercuts a reliability pitch. Grey text on black lowers contrast. The h1 packs two audiences and a product name into 13 words.

limitations: Several images failed to load in this browser; whether they render for real visitors was not verified.
The desktop full-page capture stops at 9,000px; the lower page was seen in live frames only.
The closing wireframe mountain was seen only at 390; the matching desktop area was empty in live frames.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: ElevenLabs
summary: A quiet split hero hands the first screen to a tabbed sampler of playable voice orbs, and three product families (Creative, Agents, API) organize the whole page.

observations.hero: A slim announcement bar ('Meet Eleven v4, our most emotive model yet.' plus Discover) sits above a non-sticky nav. The hero splits: two-line h1 with black 'Sign up' and outlined 'Contact sales' pills on the left, a three-line subhead on the right. Below, a wide rounded grey panel with three tabs (ElevenCreative, ElevenAgents, ElevenAPI) holds a carousel of gradient voice orbs with play buttons, captions (Characters, Narration, Conversational), prev/next arrows and a row of product sub-tabs that falls below the fold.
observations.typography: Measured h1 48px, weight 300, line-height 1.1, tracking -0.02em, family Waldenburg; 36px at 390. Section heads repeat the light, large sans treatment, each under a small grey eyebrow (ElevenCreative, ElevenAgents, ElevenAPI). Body 15px Inter, line-height 1.5, about 50ch measure. Geist Mono is in the measured family list and the API code samples are set in a monospace.
observations.visual_system: Off-white ground, light grey rounded panels, pill buttons in black or white outline. Colour comes almost entirely from imagery: blurred gradient orbs for voices, noise-textured gradient cards (orange-red, blue-grey), gradient news thumbnails and photo case-study cards. Hairline rails and rules with small tick marks frame each section. Product proof is two app-dashboard screenshots, chat bubbles, a line chart and code cards; the Safety section uses thin line-drawn wireframe figures.
observations.page_sequence: Announcement → nav → split hero → tabbed voice sampler → 18-logo wall → 'Two platforms built on the same research foundation' with two app screenshots → ElevenCreative (editor demo, speech demo, four capability cards, customer tabs) → ElevenAgents (chat demo, analytics chart, three cards, customer tabs) → ElevenAPI (text to speech, speech to text, music, each with code) → impact stories (Creative/Agents toggle, photo cards) → research timeline and posts → 'Safety, built in' → Latest updates → 'AI Communication Platform' CTA band → footer with a column per product family.
observations.copy: H1: 'Bringing technology to life'. The subhead names three audiences (enterprises, creators, developers) and maps them to ElevenAgents (customer experience), ElevenCreative (content creation) and 'the leading AI voice generator'. Primary button: 'Sign up' (secondary 'Contact sales'). Section heads are plain capability statements ('Deploy agents that talk, type, and take action'); the closing band names the category 'AI Communication Platform' with 'Talk to sales' and 'Create an AI agent'.
observations.interaction: Operated: the ElevenAgents hero tab. In four attempts it took a grey hover fill and one run reported aria-selected=true, but the panel still showed the ElevenCreative orb carousel up to 10 s later; no content swap was seen. Two first-screen captures 1.5 s apart were identical and no running CSS/WAAPI animations were reported at 1440. A 'Voice chat' floating button appeared bottom-right after load. Reduced motion: top and mid-page captures were static; the measurement records a reduced-motion rule.
observations.accessibility: Inactive orb captions and card descriptions are light grey on pale grey panels (low contrast). A 'Skip to content' link exists. At 390 the nav 'Sign up' is 78×36, the menu 36×36 and the announcement arrow 28×28; hero buttons and tabs are 44px tall. No unlabeled buttons or images without alt were found. The measurement flags horizontal overflow at 390; the live load reported document width 390 with body overflow-x hidden, while the sub-tab strip extends to about 794px and code samples are cut off at the right edge.
observations.mobile: The nav collapses to 'Sign up' plus a menu; the announcement shortens to 'Introducing Eleven v4'. The hero stacks h1 (36px), subhead, then side-by-side buttons. Tabs shorten to Creative/Agents/API and the product sub-tabs move above the orbs as a sideways-scrolling pill strip, with one large orb and partial neighbours. The logo wall becomes two columns; app screenshots stack under their labels; bento cards go single-column; code samples keep their width and clip.

principles: When one company sells distinct product families to different buyers, put a family switcher inside the hero so each audience finds its path before the long scroll.
For a product whose output can be sampled, make samples (here, playable voice previews) the first-screen artifact instead of a feature list.
Mirror the business structure everywhere: the same three families should organize hero tabs, section order, eyebrow labels and footer columns.
Keep display type light and quiet when imagery supplies the colour and emotion, so the two do not compete.
interpretation.fit: Suits multi-product AI or platform companies with distinct creator, enterprise and developer buyers and an output that can be sampled (audio, images, generated media). Wrong for a single-purpose developer tool, where three tabs and a 10,000px tour would bury one clear job.
interpretation.risks: The hero sampler is heavy: in a loaded headless session screenshots timed out and the tab switch never visibly completed, so the first interaction may feel unresponsive on weak devices. Grey secondary text is faint. The page runs about 10,800px at 1440 and 15,800px at 390, with much content behind tabs that scanners will not open. The light 48px h1 is easily outweighed by the sampler below it.

limitations: The ElevenAgents tab never visibly switched panels in four automated attempts (one run reported aria-selected=true); tab content is not described.
Voice previews were not played; audio quality was not assessed.
The 1440 full-page capture stops at 9,000px of a 10,822px page; the closing band and footer were seen only in live scroll captures.
The headless session was heavily loaded and several screenshots timed out, so load-time motion may be under-observed.
The measurement's horizontal-overflow flag at 390 disagrees with the live document-width check.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.
Selected as a maintainer pick; no public design recognition was found and recorded.

name: Pitch
archetype_note: Hybrid: prompt-box entrance inside an oversized-type brand scene, followed by a conventional SaaS feature tour.
summary: A 180px headline over a purple scene of blurred slide templates, with an AI prompt box directly beneath it as the first action.

observations.hero: A lavender announcement bar ('Pitch's MCP & API are here') sits over a saturated purple scene of blurred, scattered slide-template thumbnails. The h1 fills the centre in two huge white lines. Directly under it is a white prompt box pre-filled 'Generate a sales presentation for a digital marketplace' with '+', 'Prompts' and a pale 'Generate' button, then a two-line subhead. Nav: logo, five items, white 'Log in' pill and lime 'Sign up'; the desktop hero has no separate signup button.
observations.typography: Measured h1 180px, weight 700, line-height 0.8, tracking -0.04em, family Mark Pro Bold (a heavy geometric sans); 82px at 390. Body 18px Eina 03 Regular, line-height 1.6, about 49ch measure; 14px on mobile. Section heads are bold sans in black or violet; eyebrows ('WHY PITCH', 'THE PAYOFF', 'HOW TO', 'TOOLKIT') are uppercase in a typewriter-style face not named in the measured families. Stats use very large violet numerals.
observations.visual_system: Two grounds alternate: saturated purple/violet (hero, Solutions, Templates, FAQ) and white (features, stats, steps, toolkit). Accents are lime green (Sign up, Get a demo, a quote card) and lavender cards. Imagery is product UI on violet gradient tiles with collaborator cursors and name tags, real slide templates, and portrait testimonial cards. A giant ghosted 'Let's Pitch' sits behind the FAQ. Icons are thin violet line glyphs.
observations.page_sequence: Announcement → nav → hero (h1, prompt box, subhead) → customer logo strip → 'Pitch is your presentation workspace' with four feature rows → 'The payoff' stats (4M+, 150+, 5H+) → 'From first draft to closed deal' numbered steps ((01) Create …) → testimonial wall → 'A complete presentation toolkit' bento (AI Agent, Slide editor, Viewer analytics, Pitch rooms, Brand library …) → 'Generate slides from your existing stack' → Solutions with four audience tabs → Templates (150+) category list → FAQ ('Not just another slide tool') → footer.
observations.copy: H1: 'Create slides that win.' Subhead: 'From prompt to presentation, 4M+ teams create and deliver winning slides together in Pitch.' The desktop hero's action is the prompt box's 'Generate'; the nav and mobile hero use 'Sign up' / 'Sign up for free' and 'Get a demo'. The page title and a section head call it a 'presentation workspace'; the audience is 'teams' and, in Solutions, software companies, creative agencies, leading brands and freelance designers.
observations.interaction: Operated: the 'Creative agencies' tab in Solutions. The underline moved from 'Software companies', the heading changed from 'Ramp your sales engine' to 'Win more pitches' with agency copy, and the image slot was blank about 2 s later. On scroll the h1 left the hero while the prompt box stayed, nav links faded leaving Log in/Sign up pinned, and the full nav returned over purple sections. Fast scrolling produced long blank viewports. With reduced motion a viewport about 3,600px down was still blank across two captures; the measurement found no reduced-motion rule.
observations.accessibility: The white subhead over a light-lavender gradient is low contrast, more so once scrolling lightens the hero. Inactive Solutions tabs are dim lavender on deep purple. The 'Generate' button is pale violet with white text. At 390 the hero buttons are 44px tall and the logo link 30px. The 390 DOM query found no unlabeled buttons or images without alt, and no horizontal overflow (matching the measurement).
observations.mobile: The h1 drops to 82px and breaks into three centred lines. In the measurement capture the prompt box is an empty frosted panel, and two buttons, 'Sign up for free' and lime 'Get a demo', appear in the hero instead. The nav becomes logo plus a round menu button. Feature rows stack image over text; stats sit in two columns; testimonials and Solutions tabs run off the right edge as sideways rows; toolkit cards stack.

principles: If the product starts from a prompt, put the input directly under the headline so the first action is using the product rather than signing up.
One oversized, tightly leaded headline can carry brand identity on its own if it stays at four or five words that still fit a phone screen.
Introduce audience tabs after the general tour, once visitors know what the product does, so each segment sees tailored proof without a fork at the top.
interpretation.fit: Suits AI-assisted creative tools with a single-prompt starting point and a strong visual brand (decks, documents, design generators). Wrong for compliance-heavy or infrastructure buyers who need specifics and evidence before a playful prompt.
interpretation.risks: Scroll-gated reveals leave blank screens on fast scrolling and stayed blank under reduced motion, with no reduced-motion rule found. Light text on lavender loses contrast. Desktop leads with 'Generate' while mobile leads with signup buttons and an empty-looking prompt panel, so the first action differs by breakpoint. The page is long (about 14,350px at 1440).

limitations: No 1440 full-page capture was supplied; the desktop sequence comes from live scroll captures, several of which were blank until sections revealed.
The prompt was not submitted, so generated output was not observed.
Two video elements did not play in headless Chromium; their motion is unverified.
The live 390 load rendered mostly blank in a loaded session; mobile observations rely on the measurement captures.
The typeface of the uppercase eyebrow labels is not in the measured family list.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Mintlify
summary: A serif headline beside a realistic docs-site mockup, with live agent-traffic counters reframing documentation as infrastructure for AI agents.

observations.hero: Left column: a bordered chip 'Agent traffic' with a green monospace percentage and chevron, a three-line h1, a grey subhead with bolded audience words, then black 'Get started' and outlined 'Sign up with Google'. Right and below: a large mockup of a Mintlify docs site (sidebar, API Reference tabs, Quickstart Guide cards) bleeding off the right edge, crossed by sweeping green-to-lime thread lines in the measurement capture. A floating 'Ask assistant' button sits bottom-right. Sticky nav: logo, three menus, Pricing, 'Sign in', black 'Contact sales'.
observations.typography: Measured h1 50px, weight 400, line-height 1.0, tracking -0.04em, family arizonaFlare (a serif); 40px at 390. The serif returns only in the closing CTA; other section heads are two-tone sans statements, a black first sentence and a grey second. Body 14px inter, line-height 1.4, about 45ch measure. paperMono is in the measured families, and the counters ('Agent traffic', ticker values) are monospaced.
observations.visual_system: White ground with thin vertical rails framing the content and short green bars beside section heads. The signature motif is bundles of thin green/lime/teal lines sweeping through the hero, bento cards and closing band. The product appears as pale, green-tinted docs UI. Bento cards are warm off-white with small UI fragments (role list, agent cursors, AI-tool icons). Colour arrives in customer cards: Anthropic orange, Coinbase blue, HubSpot salmon, gradient startup art. Buttons are square-cornered black or white.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → hero (counter chip, serif h1, buttons, docs mockup) → logo grid ('Join 20,000+ of the world's most ambitious companies building for agents') → 'Agents at work today' ticker → knowledge-platform bento (six cards) → 'Powering businesses of all sizes' enterprise story carousel → 'Built to scale with the agent web' with stats (300M+, 2B+, 99.99%) → 'Enabling the next generation of startups' carousel → testimonial grid → Latest updates → closing CTA 'The knowledge platform built for agents' → footer with status pill and theme switch.
observations.copy: H1: 'The intelligent documentation platform'. Subhead: 'Self-updating documentation for startups, enterprises, and agents', with the three audiences bolded. Primary button: 'Get started' (also 'Sign up with Google'; nav 'Contact sales'). The page recasts docs as agent infrastructure: 'Agent traffic' counter, 'Agents at work today', 'Trusted by teams building for agents', and a closing 'knowledge platform built for agents'. Proof splits into 'For enterprises' and 'For startups' buttons.
observations.interaction: Operated: 'Next customer story' in the enterprise carousel. The Anthropic card slid left and dimmed, a Coinbase card ('How Coinbase became agent-ready with Mintlify', +50x, 12+) took focus, a HubSpot card peeked at right, and the previous arrow became active. Two first-screen captures 1.5 s apart showed no visible change although 7 running animations (3 infinite) were reported. The 'Agent traffic' figure differed between loads. Reduced motion: the first screen was static and 5 animations still reported running.
observations.accessibility: Grey second-clause headings and grey body text sit lighter than the black lead text. The disabled previous arrow is nearly invisible. The floating 'Ask assistant' button overlaps content at bottom-right at both widths. A 'Pause testimonials' control sits above the testimonial grid. At 390 the menu button is 38×38 and hero buttons 42px tall; no unlabeled buttons, images without alt, or horizontal overflow were found.
observations.mobile: The nav collapses to logo and menu. The hero stacks chip, 40px h1, subhead and two buttons; the docs mockup shrinks and crops off the right edge. The logo grid becomes two columns (the logos shown differed between captures). Bento cards go single-column, each keeping its line motif. Stats stack vertically. Story carousels show one card with the next peeking, arrows under the heading.

principles: When the product publishes something, show that published artifact (here a docs page) beside the headline instead of an abstract illustration.
Back a new positioning claim with a live-looking number in the hero and a ticker below it, so the claim reads as measured rather than asserted.
Split proof by buyer size with separate carousels and segment buttons ('For enterprises', 'For startups') instead of one mixed logo wall.
One serif headline inside an otherwise sans system can carry the brand voice without slowing scanning.
interpretation.fit: Suits developer and B2B tools that sell to both startups and enterprises, especially when the output can be shown as a screenshot. Wrong for a product with few customers yet: most of this page's length is named-customer proof.
interpretation.risks: Much of the scroll is customer proof; the bento cards explain capabilities with one-line labels and abstract fragments, and several rendered empty in the full-page capture. Counters invite scrutiny without a visible source. The floating assistant button covers content, and the two-tone grey headings weaken contrast.

limitations: The hero line graphic seen in the measurement capture had not drawn in either live load within about 4 s, so its motion was not observed.
Several bento cards rendered empty in the 1440 full-page capture; their final content was only partly seen.
Counter values (agent traffic, ticker, stats) were not checked against any source.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Ramp
category: Fintech: corporate cards and spend management
summary: A value-equation headline with inline email capture sits beside a celebrity photo and a self-cycling product UI, backed by live 'agents at work' counters.

observations.hero: A black announcement bar ('Ramp raises $1.85B…') tops a sticky nav with 'Sign in', lime 'See a demo' and black 'Get started'. Left: a small uppercase label with a changing percentage, the one-line h1, a grey subhead, and an email field joined to a lime 'Get started for free' button. Right: a cut-out photo of two men holding skateboards, handwritten name scribbles and a caption popup. Below, a wide panel shows animated product UI, and an 'Agents at work today' ticker runs along the bottom of the first screen.
observations.typography: Measured h1 64px, weight 400, line-height 1.0, tracking 0, family Lausanne; 40px at 390, where it breaks into two lines. Body 13px Lausanne, line-height 1.5 (12px on mobile). Lausanne is the only measured family, so hierarchy comes from size and colour: section heads pair a black sentence with a grey continuation ('One platform for all of finance. Agents for every workflow, working 24/7.'), and small uppercase labels mark counters.
observations.visual_system: White ground with a faint dot grid behind the hero; black and grey text; a single acid lime accent on primary buttons, the skateboards and highlights. Surfaces are light grey rounded panels holding dense, realistic product UI (invoices, forecasts, policy documents, integration icons). Photography mixes the celebrity cut-out with office scenes and testimonial portraits; a dotted globe illustrates global spend. The footer is near-black with long regulatory disclosures.
observations.page_sequence: Announcement → sticky nav → hero (label, h1, email capture, photo and caption, animated UI, ticker) → logo grid with customer stat → 'One platform for all of finance' module cards (cards and expenses, procure to pay, accounting, banking, integrations) → 'See recommendations for your business' AI input → 'Systems that never spoke' scroll story → 'Built on the intelligence of 85k+ finance teams' → Stack, customer-video and policy-agent sections with quotes → 'Scale the team. Shrink the paperwork.' → 'We've got the receipts' testimonials → repeated h1 with email capture → dark footer.
observations.copy: H1: 'Time is money. Save both.' Subhead: 'Cards, expenses, bill payments, and banking* – in the blink of AI', listing the modules with a footnoted asterisk. Primary button: 'Get started for free' beside a work-email field (nav adds 'See a demo'). The category is 'One platform for all of finance'; the audience is 'finance teams' and '85,000 of the world's most ambitious companies'. The closing block repeats the h1 and form.
observations.interaction: Operated: the close button on the hero caption popup; the popup disappeared, exposing a 'Forecast' screen and a 'Bills' phone panel. On load the UI panel cycled through screens (invoice matching went from 'MATCHING TO P.O.' to 'MATCHED'; reporting and forecast views appeared), and ticker and percentage values changed. Sections revealed late on scroll; reaching the footer opened a 'Stay up to date' newsletter modal. With reduced motion the first screen was static, but the product panel was still empty and the ticker absent about 4 s after load.
observations.accessibility: Grey continuation text in headings and 13px body copy are on the light side. The caption popup covers part of the product panel; at 390 the popup and the bottom ticker overlap the photo. At 390 a 16×16 control with no text or aria-label sits at the top of the page; the email field and button are 42–43px tall and full-width. No images without alt and no horizontal overflow were found. An unrequested modal appears at the end of the page.
observations.mobile: The announcement wraps to two lines and the nav becomes logo plus a 40×40 menu. The h1 breaks into two lines; email field and lime button stack full-width. The photo and popup move below the form, with the ticker over the bottom of the first screen, followed by a cropped product composite with a Ramp card. The logo grid becomes three columns; module cards stack; testimonials scroll sideways.

principles: Compress the value proposition into a short equation-style headline, put the email field in the hero, and repeat the identical headline and form at the end.
Let one panel cycle through real product screens so a multi-module product shows breadth without asking the visitor to click tabs.
Label running counters ('agents at work today', share of payments processed) so an AI claim reads as concrete activity.
If a pop-culture image is used for attention, keep its caption dismissible and out of the way of the product proof.
interpretation.fit: Suits broad B2B platforms with self-serve signup and a mature product UI to show (fintech, finance operations, HR). Wrong for an early product without real screens or customers: the page depends on dense UI, logos and named customer quotes.
interpretation.risks: The first screen stacks many elements (announcement, counter label, form, celebrity photo, caption, animated UI, ticker) that compete for attention. Under reduced motion the product panel was empty rather than showing a static frame. Long scroll-driven sections rendered blank in captures, and the end-of-page modal interrupts. 13px body text is small for a page about 14,500px long.

limitations: No 1440 full-page capture was supplied; the desktop sequence comes from live scroll captures.
Three autoplay videos did not play in headless Chromium; their content and motion are unverified.
The 'Systems that never spoke' scroll story and several logo tiles and cards rendered blank in captures, so their content is not described.
The email and recommendation inputs were not typed into or submitted.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Browserbase
category: Developer infrastructure: cloud browsers for AI agents
summary: Dithered pixel-art landscapes and orange highlight-block headings give an invisible browser-infrastructure API its own world, with an interactive ecosystem diagram explaining the product.

observations.hero: A sticky white nav (orange 'B' logo, five links, 'Log in', 'Sign up', black 'Get a demo') sits above a framed hero panel: pale blue dotted ground with a dithered pixel-art mountain range in orange, yellow, green and black. The heading is centred in two orange highlight blocks with white text, followed by a two-line subhead and two pills, black 'Get API key' and pale 'Setup for agents' with a copy icon. The logo-row heading shows below the panel within the first screen.
observations.typography: No h1 exists; the hero heading is an h2. Measured display 45px, family gtPlanar (a geometric sans), dropping to 21px at 390; body 20px in 'plain', line-height 1.2 (16px on mobile). gtStandardMono is in the measured families; uppercase monospaced labels ('TRY FOR FREE ▶', 'GET STARTED ▶', 'HUMAN YEARS BROWSING THE WEB') and highlighted keywords ('BRIDGE', 'AI', 'DIGITAL WORLD') are set in a monospace. Key phrases are orange inside black headings.
observations.visual_system: White ground divided by thin blue-grey blueprint rules and column rails. Orange is the brand colour: logo, headline highlight blocks, accent words and a full-bleed orange footer with a giant 'B'. Dithered pixel-art landscapes and a pixel computer supply the imagery. Some headings and stat cards sit on pastel highlight blocks (yellow, blue, pink). Use cases are pale-blue line sketches of UI: cursors, a sign-in form, a CAPTCHA, a hotel price card.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → pixel-landscape hero → logo row ('10,000+ companies building beyond the API') → 'See what agents can do on the web' (Search API, Fetch API, Browser-as-a-Service) → 'Use the whole web like it's an API' with bullet list and pixel computer → eight use-case cards → interactive ecosystem diagram → 'Zero setup. Real results.' three steps → CTA band ('100% of the web at production scale.') → 'Don't use the web. Scale it.' with mountain and '10,000+ years saved' → 'Trusted by' counter cards → orange footer.
observations.copy: Hero heading: 'Give your agents access to the whole web.' Subhead: 'Browserbase makes the web as reliable and programmable as APIs'. Primary button: 'Get API key' (secondary 'Setup for agents'; nav 'Get a demo'). The audience is builders of AI agents: headings address 'your agents' and claim 'Anything you can do in a browser, your agent can too.' Use-case cards end in monospaced 'GET STARTED ▶' links.
observations.interaction: Operated: the 'Extract structured web data' tab on the ecosystem diagram. The highlighted arc moved round the ring, the centre title changed from 'Research at web scale', a different set of capability chips lit up, the right-hand output switched from browser windows ('Running 128 browsers…') to a code panel with a JSON skeleton, and the left source tiles changed. Two first-screen captures 1.5 s apart were identical. Counters showed placeholder zeros ('000,000') in captures. Reduced motion: no visible change; the measurement records a reduced-motion rule.
observations.accessibility: The hero heading is an h2 and no h1 was found. White text on orange highlight blocks and orange accent words on white are the main contrast risks. At 390 the menu icon is 24×24, hero pills 39px tall and logo tiles 153×44; a skip link exists. Several media areas rendered as large blank gaps, and counters read '000,000' or '00,000+' when captured. No unlabeled buttons, images without alt, or horizontal overflow were found at 390.
observations.mobile: The hero heading shrinks to 21px highlight blocks; the pills stack vertically and the landscape compresses into a short strip. Logos become a two-column grid with play triangles. The API list, use-case cards and three steps stack single-column with tall blank media slots between them. The pixel computer moves under its text. The 'Don't use the web' mountain does not appear in the capture. The footer reflows to two link columns with the large 'B' at the bottom.

principles: An infrastructure product with no interface to show can own a recognisable look by applying one illustration technique consistently across hero, diagrams and step cards.
Make the architecture diagram switchable by job (research, extraction, form filling, testing) so each scenario lights up the capabilities and output it uses.
Give the hero one action per audience: an API key for developers and a setup action aimed at agents.
Monospaced micro-labels and highlight blocks can give a developer page texture without adding more imagery.
interpretation.fit: Suits API and infrastructure products for developers and AI builders, where the product is invisible and identity must come from art direction. Wrong for buyers who must see an interface or dashboard before purchase, such as finance or HR software.
interpretation.risks: With no h1 the main claim is weaker for assistive technology and search. The imagery is decorative and says little about how the API works until the diagram section. In automated captures counters showed zeros and media slots were blank, which reads as broken if animations or videos fail. White text on bright orange blocks is a contrast risk.

limitations: No h1 exists, so typography cites the measured display size rather than h1 metrics.
Four video elements (three with autoplay) did not play in headless Chromium; several media areas were blank and their content is unverified.
Counter values appeared as placeholders in captures; final figures were not verified.
The first reduced-motion and 390 live loads timed out on navigation and were rerun once.
'Setup for agents' was not clicked; what it copies is unverified.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Attio
summary: A centred one-line category claim over a live-typing CRM workspace, then a sticky five-step rail walks the revenue lifecycle through dense product panels.

observations.hero: A black announcement bar and white nav sit above a centred stack: a pill link ('GTM lessons from Elena Verna and more'), a one-line h1, a two-line grey subhead, and an outlined 'Talk to sales' beside a dark 'Start for free'. Below, a macOS-style frame of the Attio workspace (Basepoint sidebar, Home, a prompt box) begins inside the first screen and continues past the fold.
observations.typography: Measured h1 64px, weight 600, line-height 1, tracking −0.02em, family interDisplay; body 18px inter at 1.3 line-height, about 48ch. Section headings are two-tone: a black clause followed by a mid-grey clause at the same size. Measured families also include JetBrains Mono and tiemposText; the only serif I saw is the large testimonial quote. Phone h1 40px, tracking −0.01em, body 15px.
observations.visual_system: White ground with a faint lavender wash under the hero and hairline vertical rules framing the content column. Product UI (tables, kanban, workflow nodes, charts, email drafts) is the main imagery. Mid-page the ground turns near-black: a spectral arc behind 'Universal Context™', a wireframe funnel with dots, integration icon tiles, an isometric SDK diagram. Small tinted pill labels ('Platform', 'Signals', 'Changelog') head sections. The measurement record flags a dark background and a canvas.
observations.page_sequence: Hero + workspace frame → 10-logo grid → 'The intelligent system that never sleeps' with a sticky five-step rail (Build pipeline → Retain and expand) beside product panels → 'Live from day one' self-building record → dark 'Universal Context™' + five-claim strip → Signals → Connectivity icon row → 'SDK. API. MCP.' → serif testimonial on a dotted ground → 'Run at any scale' stats → tabbed customer stories → changelog cards → dark 'Agentic revenue runs on Attio.' CTA → footer.
observations.copy: H1: 'Welcome to agentic revenue.' Subhead: Attio is the platform that builds pipeline, advances deals and grows accounts around the clock. Primary button 'Start for free' (secondary 'Talk to sales'). The category is named as CRM ('The only CRM with Universal Context™'; page title 'The CRM for agentic revenue'); the audience is sales and revenue teams ('Free your reps to sell', 'For the people who own the number').
observations.interaction: Clicked the 'Railway' tab in Customer stories: aria-pressed became true, the tab cell shaded, and the panel swapped from '83% faster lead triage' (Granola, billboard photo) to '100% adoption, no admin' (Railway, team photo). On load the hero workspace typed 'How do I win my deal with GreenLeaf' and then switched to a deal view and a companies table showing 'AI is thinking…'. On scroll the rail highlight moved down the five steps. With reduced motion set, the hero demo still advanced between captures.
observations.accessibility: Grey second clauses of headings and grey subheads are noticeably lighter than the black text on white. Phone: 'Dismiss banner' 32×32px, menu button 36×36px, 'Talk to sales' 36px tall, email field and 'Send me a demo' 40px tall; four links or buttons with no text or label were counted. No horizontal overflow at 1440 or 390. A cookie card covers the bottom-left corner until dismissed.
observations.mobile: H1 drops to 40px over two centred lines. The hero buttons become an email field, a full-width 'Send me a demo' button and a 'Talk to sales →' link. The workspace frame is cropped at the right edge. The sticky rail becomes a horizontally scrolling tab strip (Build pipeline, Convert leads, Run sales motion…) with product tables running off-screen. A 'Stay ahead of GTM' email block sits before the final CTA; the footer stacks to two columns. Measured sections: 9.

principles: Back the category claim in the first screen with a working-looking product session rather than an illustration.
Walk a multi-stage workflow with a sticky step rail: one short claim per step, one dense, realistic product panel beside it.
Use two-tone headlines (statement in full black, elaboration in grey) to carry a long proposition without a separate subhead.
interpretation.fit: Suits horizontal B2B software whose value spans several workflow stages and whose interface is presentable at close range. Wrong for a single-action product or an unfinished UI, where the rail would expose thin or repetitive screens.
interpretation.risks: At about 17,600px and eight-plus chapters the story is long and the platform message repeats; grey heading clauses trade contrast for rhythm; the hero demo keeps running under reduced motion; on phones the rail's tables are cropped and hard to read.

limitations: Did not accept or dismiss the cookie card, so it covers part of several captures.
Hero and section demos change over time; captures show different states and the full demo sequence was not verified.
No control was operated at 390 wide; mobile is described from captures and measurements.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Granola
summary: A large serif promise beside a typing meeting-note mock, then one named note recurs before, during and after a meeting inside lime and charcoal brand bands.

observations.hero: Left column: a 'New · Granola for Apple Watch' pill, a four-line serif h1, a two-line sans subhead, a dark olive 'Download for free ↓' pill and a platform line ('Available for macOS, Windows, iOS, Android'). Right: a 'Q3 GTM sync' note window with traffic-light dots over collage-style art panels, overlapped by a phone-shaped call window and a 'Transcribing' pill.
observations.typography: Measured h1 86.4px, weight 400, line-height 0.9, tracking −0.02em, family quadrant (a serif in the captures); body 16px melange (a sans) at 1.5, about 50ch. The serif recurs in section heads, mock note titles and testimonial quotes; sans carries UI text and body. 'For the doers' is set near full content width. Phone h1 48px; body stays 16px.
observations.visual_system: White ground with near-black text. Brand colour is a dark olive button plus lime-yellow panels and charcoal bands. Imagery mixes macOS-style app windows, call video tiles, halftone and abstract collage art, and landscape photos behind feature mocks. Full-width bands separate chapters (charcoal logos, lime 'Perfect meeting memory', charcoal testimonials, warm grey MCP). The footer ends in a giant Granola wordmark.
observations.page_sequence: Hero → 'Effortless notes, enhanced instantly.' with three proof rows → oversized 'For the doers' → charcoal 'Trusted by teams we admire' logo grid → 'Granola helps you before, during and after your meetings.' three-step stepper with panels → lime 'Perfect meeting memory' chat box → charcoal testimonials → 'Works everywhere you do, how you do' five feature rows → 'Use your meeting notes anywhere' MCP connector → 'Unlimited meeting notes for free' card CTA → footer with wordmark.
observations.copy: H1: 'The AI notepad for back-to-back meetings'. Subhead: 'Notes, actions and memory. Without a meeting bot.' Primary button 'Download for free' (nav adds 'Talk to sales'). The category is in the h1 ('AI notepad'); the audience is people in stacked meetings ('For the doers', 'Helping busy people through busy days'), and the no-bot difference recurs ('Humans in the room, not bots').
observations.interaction: Clicked 'After the meeting' in the stepper: the page scrolled about 1,770px to the 'Post-meeting admin, done' panel, the label turned dark with an underline, and the panel showed 'List actions', 'Write follow-up email' and 'Draft project plan'. On load the hero note typed text, showed an 'Enhancing notes' state, and the call tiles changed faces. With reduced motion set, the note still typed and showed 'Enhancing notes' between captures.
observations.accessibility: Inactive stepper labels and the platform line are light grey on white. In several live captures the nav download pill rendered as an empty grey bar with no text; at 390, a 112×40px link with no text was found and four unlabelled controls were counted. The 'New' pill link is 32px tall on phone. No horizontal overflow at either width.
observations.mobile: H1 drops to 48px, left-aligned over four lines; the full 'Download for free' button stays in the first screen and the note mock moves below it, with the art panels cropped to its edges. The nav collapses to a 'Download' pill and a menu icon. Feature rows and testimonials stack to one column; measured sections drop to 10 and page height to 12,192px.

principles: Carry one named sample artifact (a specific meeting note) through every workflow stage so the visitor follows one story instead of a feature list.
Put the main objection-killer in the subhead ('Without a meeting bot') and repeat it in the feature rows.
Let one characterful display serif and one saturated accent hold the brand, and keep product UI in a plain sans so the two never compete.
interpretation.fit: Suits single-purpose productivity tools with a clear before/during/after and a desktop UI worth showing. Wrong for multi-product platforms, or buyers who need architecture and compliance detail before anything else.
interpretation.risks: Much of the meaning sits in images and video; when they had not loaded, sections showed empty frames and an unlabelled nav button. The hero demo ignores reduced motion. The 86px serif h1 takes four lines and pushes the platform line toward the fold.

limitations: On the live visit several images, videos, partner logos and the nav download label loaded late or not at all; imagery is described from the measurement capture.
Did not dismiss the cookie dialog that appeared over the hero.
No control was operated at 390 wide.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Modal
summary: A one-line dark-mode platform claim over a self-assembling green dot-matrix cube, then a sticky product rail and numbered line diagrams for each infrastructure capability.

observations.hero: A bright green announcement bar ('Series D: $1B in annualized run rate…'), then a dark nav with 'Log in' and a light 'Sign up' pill. Centred: a one-line h1 with 'production AI' in green, a two-line grey subhead, a light 'Get started' pill and a dark 'Contact us' pill. A glowing green dot-matrix cube fills the rest of the screen; a 'Trusted by the world's leading AI teams' logo strip follows just below the fold.
observations.typography: Measured h1 45px, weight 500, line-height 1.1, tracking −0.01em, family ABC Diatype; body 18px ABC Diatype at 1.3, about 47ch. One sans family does display and body; DM Mono is the only other measured family (the small '$30 / month free compute' line looks monospaced). The h1 is small relative to the canvas under it. Phone h1 37px, body 17px.
observations.visual_system: Near-black ground with one bright green accent for the logo, the headline phrase and small section-label icons. Imagery is abstract: a dot-matrix cube canvas, a dotted world map, three numbered thin-line diagrams with coloured nodes, and dark dashboard cards (audit logs, container chart, live GPU usage). Customer proof switches to a warm light-grey ground with a scattered geometric icon field and grey logo tiles.
observations.page_sequence: Announcement bar → hero with cube canvas → logo strip → 'Container infrastructure that won't box you in' with sticky rail (Inference, Training, Sandboxes, Functions) beside four product panels → 'Infrastructure reimagined…' three numbered diagrams → 'Capacity that scales with your ambition' world map + four capabilities → 'Production-ready from day one' dashboard cards → light customer carousel + eight logo tiles → 'Latest updates' three posts → 'Ship your first app in minutes' CTA → footer.
observations.copy: H1: 'The platform for production AI'. Subhead: cloud infrastructure for teams that develop, train and serve AI applications at scale. Primary button 'Get started' (secondary 'Contact us'; nav 'Sign up'). The category is cloud or container infrastructure; the audience is AI teams ('Trusted by the world's leading AI teams'). The closing CTA adds a concrete offer: '$30 / month free compute'.
observations.interaction: Clicked 'Next customer story': the card changed from a DoorDash quote with a red-accented icon field to a Cognition quote with a blue-accented field. On load, successive captures showed a small cluster of green dots growing into the full cube. In my scroll captures the rail highlight stayed on 'Inference' while later panels were in view. With reduced motion the cube rendered complete and three captures 1.5s apart were identical.
observations.accessibility: Secondary text is small and mid-grey on near-black (feature descriptions, footer links). Desktop carousel arrows are 32×32px. Phone: menu button 32×32px, 'Get started' and 'Contact us' 36px tall; no unlabelled controls counted; no horizontal overflow at either width.
observations.mobile: H1 drops to 37px and wraps to two centred lines, 'production AI' on the second; the cube stays below the buttons and the logo strip peeks at the bottom. The sticky rail is removed: each product becomes a stacked section headed by its icon label (Inference, Training…). Diagrams, capabilities and dashboards stack singly; the footer becomes a two-column link list. Page height rises to 14,611px.

principles: For a multi-product platform, give every product the same anatomy (one claim, three capabilities, one link) behind a sticky product selector.
Explain infrastructure that has no natural screenshot with numbered, monochrome line diagrams rather than stock illustration.
Keep the hero to one short line with a single accent-coloured phrase and let one abstract motif carry the brand.
Change the ground colour when the page moves from capability to customer proof so the evidence reads as its own chapter.
interpretation.fit: Suits developer and infrastructure platforms whose buyers already know the category and want breadth, reliability and proof. Wrong for a new category that needs the first screen to explain what the product does.
interpretation.risks: The hero says little beyond the category and the cube is decorative rather than explanatory; no code or product UI appears above the fold; grey-on-black secondary text is low in contrast; canvas and loaded media leave empty frames when slow.

limitations: Product-panel media were empty dark rectangles in live captures but filled in the measurement capture; their animated states were not verified.
The customer carousel arrows only became available after scrolling the whole page once; the carousel's autoplay behaviour, if any, was not checked.
No control was operated at 390 wide.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Sierra
summary: Full-bleed moving imagery of human moments carries a two-line outcome promise and an agent-conversation bubble, deferring product UI until after a 30-logo wall.

observations.hero: A blue announcement bar ('Sierra Summit 2026 Recap…'), then a white nav with green logo, 'Sign in' and a green 'Learn more' pill. Below, full-bleed moving imagery of a sleeping baby on a parent's shoulder; the two-line white h1 and a white 'Learn more' pill sit at lower left, and a frosted chat bubble at right shows one line of an agent–customer exchange. In the measurement first-screen captures the h1 and bubble had not yet appeared.
observations.typography: Measured h1 65px, weight 400, line-height 1.1, tracking −0.02em, family gtAmerica; body 16px gtAmerica at 1.5. gtAmerica is the only measured family: hierarchy comes from size alone, with display kept at weight 400. Section heads are centred; card titles sit white on gradients. Phone h1 32px, body 14px.
observations.visual_system: White ground, deep green for logo and buttons, a blue announcement bar. Hero imagery is warm, documentary-style moving pictures of people (the measurement record finds a canvas, not a video element). Desktop logos form a grey wall of 30, five per row. Feature cards use saturated diagonal gradients (olive, blue, mauve, rust) with faint white icons. Product sections switch to pale blue-grey UI cards, entered through a dotted-ground transition; compliance badges and a light grey footer close.
observations.page_sequence: Announcement bar → moving-image hero → 'Leading brands succeed with Sierra' + 'Customer stories' button + 30-logo wall → 'Standout customer experiences. Stronger growth.' one wide and three gradient cards → 'The results speak for themselves' four quotes → 'The agent-building agent' (Ghostwriter Build/Optimize UI) → 'Use AI to improve your AI' (Insights, four cards) → 'Turn conversations into outcomes' (Horizon, four cards) → 'Trust and reliability' nine badges → 'Discover what Sierra can do for you' CTA → footer.
observations.copy: H1: 'Better outcomes. Built on Sierra.' No hero subhead. Every primary button reads 'Learn more' (nav, hero, closing CTA). The hero names neither category nor product; it emerges in card copy ('Build powerful AI agents quickly', 'The agent-building agent') and the Product menu ('The leading conversational AI platform for businesses'). The audience is enterprise brands ('Leading brands succeed with Sierra', 'the great companies of the world').
observations.interaction: Opened the 'Product' nav menu: aria-expanded became true, the item gained a pale green pill, and a white panel appeared with Build / Orchestrate / Optimize / Scale columns (Ghostwriter, Agent Studio, Horizon, Context Engine, Explorer, Insights, Channels, Trust and reliability). Meanwhile the hero imagery changed scene (baby → man on a phone) and the bubble text changed. On load the bubble alternated agent and customer lines. With reduced motion the hero was static: three captures were identical.
observations.accessibility: White h1 and bubble text sit directly on moving imagery; on phone the h1 overlays a light blue sweater area. Phone: header 'Learn more' 32px tall, hero 'Learn more' 40px tall, announcement link 15px tall; no unlabelled controls counted; no overflow at either width. The cookie card overlaps the hero's lower-left corner.
observations.mobile: H1 drops to 32px at left over a tighter crop of the imagery; no chat bubble was visible in the phone first screen. The logo wall becomes three columns in brand colours instead of grey. Feature cards stack and gain '+' expand buttons; testimonials stack; product cards become sideways rows with the next card peeking at the right edge. Footer columns stack to two.

principles: When the buyer's outcome is emotional, open on imagery of the end customer and overlay a short product exchange to tie the scene to the software.
Place a large, quiet logo wall directly after the hero when trust, not comprehension, is the first hurdle.
Tag each product chapter with a small named pill (Ghostwriter, Insights, Horizon) so a broad platform reads as distinct tools.
interpretation.fit: Suits enterprise platforms selling outcomes to executives, with recognisable logos to show. Wrong for self-serve or developer products, where visitors must see what the product does before they will talk to sales.
interpretation.risks: The hero names neither product nor category and offers only 'Learn more', so meaning depends on the imagery and later sections; text-over-imagery contrast varies frame to frame; first-screen text arrived late in one capture; product UI does not appear until about 4,900px down.

limitations: The measurement record reports sticky_nav false and a 700px nav height, but the announcement bar and nav stayed pinned in every scroll capture; the measurement may have read a different element.
Only a few scenes of the hero imagery were seen; its full sequence was not verified.
Did not accept the cookie banner. No control was operated at 390 wide.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Excalidraw
summary: The editor's own hand-drawn idiom (handwritten words, doodles, cursor tags, an editor screenshot) becomes the brand, with a free, no-account start repeated throughout.

observations.hero: Pale mint-white ground scattered with pastel doodles and collaborator cursor tags ('brocketdeer', 'allosaurus'). Centred: the h1 with 'Whiteboard' in a hand-drawn face on a mint highlight, a one-line subhead, a yellow '134.2k on GitHub' star badge and a sketched pen. A framed screenshot of the editor (toolbar, style panel, comments) starts at the bottom of the first screen. The hero body has no primary button; the nav holds 'Free whiteboard'.
observations.typography: Measured h1 56px, weight 600, line-height 1.2, tracking 0, family Assistant; body 14px Assistant at 1.4, about 46ch. Measured families also include Excalifont, the hand-drawn face used for highlighted words ('Whiteboard', 'Excalidraw'), section tags and margin notes ('14 days of free trial'). Text is navy throughout. The phone h1 stays at 56px, the same as desktop.
observations.visual_system: White and pale mint ground, navy text, an indigo-violet primary button, mint highlighter blocks behind handwritten words, pastel confetti doodles and cursor name tags borrowed from the editor. Features hang off a thin vertical timeline with round sketched icons; each has a browser-frame media slot and small white cards. Tweet cards carry doodle corners. Plus gets a pale blue band with a sketched illustration; the footer is near-black with a faint doodle pattern.
observations.page_sequence: Hero + editor screenshot → 'Trusted by the largest companies in the world' logo row → 'Say hi to Excalidraw' ('Free & Open source', Start drawing / Try Plus) → timeline: Create → Collaborate → Common usecases → Generative AI → 'The easiest way to get your thoughts on screen' (two tweets) → 'Online whiteboard' Draw now / Try Plus for free → 'Loved by individuals' tweet carousel → 'Free' editor CTA (Draw now / Checkout Github) → 'Plus' upsell → dark footer.
observations.copy: H1: 'Online Whiteboard made simple'. Subhead: 'Ideate, Collaborate, Share. Simply with Excalidraw.' Primary button: 'Free whiteboard' in the nav; the first in-page buttons are 'Start drawing' and 'Try Plus', later 'Draw now'. The h1 itself names the category; the audience is individuals first ('Loved by individuals', 'No account is needed. Just start drawing.'), with Plus offered to those wanting more.
observations.interaction: Clicked the 'Next' arrow on 'Loved by individuals': the row shifted one card (François Fleuret / Theo / Gergely Orosz → Theo / Gergely Orosz / Andrej Karpathy). Nothing moved on the first screen in normal or reduced-motion captures. The five feature videos did not play in this Chromium (each reported a media-not-supported error), so their browser frames stayed blank; with reduced motion they were also reported paused.
observations.accessibility: Navy on white or mint reads strongly. Handwritten margin notes are small, light violet script. The Plus carousel's dot buttons are 8×8px (one 16×8px) and labelled only '0'–'4'. Phone: 'Menu' 81×38px, GitHub badge 30px tall; no unlabelled controls counted; no horizontal overflow. On phone the editor screenshot shrinks to an unreadable thumbnail.
observations.mobile: The h1 keeps its 56px size and breaks into three lines, 'Whiteboard' alone on the middle line. The nav collapses to a 'Menu' pill, and after scrolling only that pill stays visible. The logo row is cropped to three logos, buttons go full width, timeline cards stack singly, and the tweet carousel shows one card with neighbours peeking. The dark footer stacks.

principles: Turn the product's own output style (hand-drawn type, doodles, cursor tags) into the page's brand system so the page previews what users will make.
Repeat the zero-friction start ('No account is needed') beside the primary buttons of a free tool.
Hang a long feature list on one vertical timeline with icon nodes so it reads as a sequence rather than a grid.
interpretation.fit: Suits free or open-source creative tools whose output has a recognisable look. Wrong for enterprise or regulated products, where a playful handwritten idiom would undercut credibility with buyers.
interpretation.risks: The hero has no in-body action and shows the editor as a static screenshot rather than a usable canvas; feature sections depend on MP4 videos and showed empty frames, with no visible fallback, when they failed to play here; small handwritten notes and 8px carousel dots are hard to read and hit; the 56px phone h1 takes three lines.

limitations: The five feature videos failed to decode in Playwright's Chromium (MEDIA_ERR_SRC_NOT_SUPPORTED), so their content is unknown.
The linked editor ('Start drawing', 'Draw now') was not opened.
No control was operated at 390 wide.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Tailscale
summary: A centred category claim is followed, inside the first screen, by five product cards that swap a full product panel, sorting the platform by job before proof.

observations.hero: Dark utility bar with a monospaced uppercase announcement, then a light nav ending in a black 'Get started - it's free!' button. Centred two-line h1, three-line centred subhead, black primary button beside an underlined 'Contact sales' link. Still in the first screen: a row of five product cards (icon, name, one-line job), the first filled red, with the top of a white product panel below. A Ketch privacy banner covered the lower fifth in the measurement capture.
observations.typography: Measured h1 64px, weight 500, line-height 1.1, tracking -0.01em, family inter; 37.5px at 390. Measured body 14px Arial at desktop and 16.9px inter at 390. A second measured family is mdio; the utility bar and footer column labels are set in monospaced uppercase. Section headings use two tones: first line mid-grey, second near-black ('50,000 businesses / choose Tailscale').
observations.visual_system: Warm off-white ground, white rounded panels, black buttons. Each product has its own accent (red for Business VPN, purple for Privileged Access) on the active card and the panel eyebrow. Proof is product UI: a laptop with an app and a 'Tailscale Status' card; later a terminal install, a login screen and an admin 'Machines' table. One blue gradient panel and one near-black CTA band break the light rhythm. Customer logos sit in grey tiles.
observations.page_sequence: Utility bar → nav → centred hero + five product cards → product panel (bullets, button, laptop UI) → '50,000 businesses choose Tailscale' with three metric case cards → 17-logo wall → blue panel 'Easy, secure, identity-based access to anything' with role pills and UI composite → three benefit columns → developer tweets row → integrations icon grid with 'Over 100 integrations' card → dark CTA band → footer.
observations.copy: H1: 'The best secure connectivity platform for the AI era'. Subhead: a Zero Trust identity-based platform that replaces legacy VPN, SASE and PAM and connects remote teams, multi-cloud, CI/CD, Edge & IoT and AI workloads. Primary button 'Start connecting devices'; nav CTA 'Get started - it's free!'. Audience is named by product job (five cards) and by role (IT, Security, DevOps, Engineering pills); proof copy addresses developers ('Developer approved').
observations.interaction: Clicked the 'Privileged Access' card: it filled purple, Business VPN reverted to plain, and the panel below changed its heading to 'Privileged Access' with a purple eyebrow, keeping a laptop mock. On load the first screen did not change over 1.5 s. Measurement counted 2 running animations on load (1 at 390); reduced-motion rule 'unverified'. With reduced motion, frames 1.5 s apart were identical at the top and at 35% depth.
observations.accessibility: Grey first lines of two-tone headings and grey logos on grey tiles sit at lower contrast on the off-white ground. At 390 a DOM check found utility links 30px tall and 'Read case study' and 'Contact sales' text links 23px tall. The measured desktop body family is Arial while display text is inter. No horizontal overflow at either width.
observations.mobile: The utility bar wraps to two centred lines; the nav collapses to logo and a black menu button. H1 drops to 37.5px over four lines. Product cards become wrapped icon-and-label chips without descriptions, the active one a red pill. The product panel stacks eyebrow, heading, laptop image, bullets and button. Metric cards stack, logos go to three columns, integrations to four columns around the text card, and the CTA band stacks.

principles: Put the product menu directly under the hero as selectable cards that swap a full panel, so each buyer reaches their job within the first scroll.
Give each product its own accent colour and reuse it on the active control and the panel it opens.
Back a logo wall with a few quantified customer results that link to case studies.
Offer a second entry by role (IT, Security, DevOps, Engineering) for buyers who think in teams rather than products.
interpretation.fit: Suits infrastructure or security platforms with several products and both self-serve and sales paths. Wrong for a single-feature tool, where a five-way product switch would invent breadth.
interpretation.risks: The centred hero and superlative claim ('the best … for the AI era') are generic and unproven in the first screen; the specific mechanism appears only in the panel and the blue section. Five products, four roles and two CTAs add choices before any explanation of how it works.

limitations: Two reduced-motion loads failed with an upstream proxy 502 ('upstream request failed'); a third, sequential load succeeded.
The first desktop and mobile loads timed out before the load event; the product-card click was verified on a later sequential load.
Did not open nav dropdowns, the role pills or the tweets row; whether the tweets row moves was not checked.
Tap-target sizes come from a DOM bounding-box check, not a device test.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Runway
summary: A mission statement over a cinematic still, then the company splits into three buyer platforms (Creative, Dev, Robotics) that share one model claim.

observations.hero: A gradient promo bar ('Enterprises get 2 months of usage free. Sign by 10/31.') above a white nav with 'Enterprise Sales', 'Login' and 'Try Runway' buttons. The first screen is one rounded black card across the width: a dark close-up still with an orange light streak, the h1 and a four-line paragraph bottom-left in white, and a white 'Try Runway for free' button.
