A partner-logo strip sits below the card. A Cookiebot dialog covered the lower third in the measurement capture.
observations.typography: Measured h1 40px, weight 400, line-height 1.2, tracking -0.012em, family abcNormal; the measured display size is 56px, and the 'Three platforms…' heading is visibly larger than the h1. Body 15px/1.6, measured family generic sans-serif. Nav buttons ('Enterprise Sales', 'Login', 'Try Runway') and the product-switcher labels render in a serif face in the measurement capture and the live visit. At 390: h1 28px, display 36px.
observations.visual_system: White ground with large rounded media cards, near-black primary buttons and light-grey secondary buttons. Imagery is photographic: an abstract cinematic still, one documentary photo per platform (students, a developer in a workshop, robot grippers over a cup), a pencil sketch of a sofa and cat in the switcher, a blurred green-brown field behind the research block. The footer is a black link directory in eight groups.
observations.page_sequence: Promo bar → nav → hero card → partner-logo strip → 'Three platforms built on-top of the same Real-World Intelligence models' with Creative / Dev / Robotics columns → product switcher (three labels with progress rules, list of uses beside media) → Runway Research block (GWM-1, Gen-4.5, General World Models) → 'See the latest from Runway' four news cards → black footer.
observations.copy: H1: 'Building Real-World Intelligence'. The paragraph says Runway builds foundational Real-World Intelligence that can understand, simulate and act, with products for individuals and organisations. Primary button 'Try Runway for free'. Audiences are three platforms: Creative ('Used by 60m+ creatives'), Dev ('for developers') and Robotics ('policy inference'), each with its own buttons (Try now, Get API Key, View documentation, Learn more, For Enterprise, Contact Sales). The nav repeats the split: Creative, Dev, Robotics.
observations.interaction: Clicked 'Runway Robotics' in the product switcher: within about 1 s nothing switched and the rule under 'Runway Creative' kept filling. During the scroll pass the switcher had advanced by itself to Runway Dev (dark panel: Workflows, Recipes, Characters). The hero did not change over 1.5 s; the partner-logo strip changed between frames, also with reduced motion. Measurement counted 0 running animations; reduced-motion rule 'observed'.
observations.accessibility: Inactive switcher items are very light grey on white; research-block descriptions are small light text over a blurred photo; footer column labels are dim grey on black. At 390 the Cookiebot dialog filled almost the whole first screen in the measurement capture. A DOM check at 390 found switcher labels 25px tall, list items 26px and 'See terms' 18px. No horizontal overflow.
observations.mobile: The promo bar wraps to three lines; the nav keeps wordmark, 'Try Runway' and a menu icon. The hero card becomes tall with the image cropped and text over it. The three platform columns stack into label, photo, headline, paragraph and buttons. Switcher labels wrap onto two lines above a stacked list and a small media panel. The research block, news cards and footer go to one column; page height grows from 5144 to 9396px.

principles: When one technology serves distinct buyers, state the shared foundation once, then give each buyer a parallel column with its own primary action.
Mirror the buyer split in the top nav so routing is consistent from the first screen to the footer.
Give research credibility its own block with direct links to named models rather than mixing it into product copy.
interpretation.fit: Suits companies with one core capability sold to several distinct audiences (creative, developer, robotics or enterprise). Wrong for a single-audience startup, where three platform columns would read as unfocused.
interpretation.risks: The first screen shows an abstract image rather than the product, so what Runway makes becomes clear only after scrolling. The h1 is smaller than a later heading, which flattens hierarchy. The auto-advancing switcher did not respond to a click within a second, and serif rendering on buttons and switcher labels breaks the typographic system.

limitations: The first live desktop visit (run in parallel with other sites) loaded without web fonts or images; a second sequential visit was used for scroll observations.
One mobile load returned an upstream proxy 502; a later sequential load succeeded.
The switcher click was checked about 1 s after clicking; a slower response was not tested.
Cookie dialogs covered part of the measurement captures; the live visit hid them with CSS rather than answering them.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: tldraw
summary: The hero ships the product itself: an npm command, a ten-line App.tsx and a live, drawable tldraw canvas side by side.

observations.hero: Left-aligned on white: two-line h1, one-line subhead with 'high-performance web canvas' in bold, a black monospaced 'npm create tldraw' button with copy icon and an 'or Build with a starter kit →' blue link. Below, two framed panels: a dark 'App.tsx' code panel with a ten-line React example, and a blue-bordered live canvas with toolbar (draw tool preselected) and style panel. A customer-logo strip starts at the fold.
observations.typography: Measured h1 48px, weight 600, line-height 0.9, tracking -0.02em, family Archivo; 32px with -0.03em at 390. Body 14px/1.5 Archivo. Measured families also include Inter and Geist Mono; the command button and code panel are monospaced. Section headings are short, bold and left-aligned ('Why tldraw?', 'What's inside'); a customer quote is set large in grey italic.
observations.visual_system: White ground, full-width hairline dividers between sections and a narrow (1024px measured) content column. One accent blue for links, the Quick Start button and the canvas frame; black for the command button, code panel and footer. Case cards use tilted isometric screenshots of customer products. The tldraw toolbar and style panel recur as the motif: in the hero, in 'Save months of work' and in the starter-kit illustration.
observations.page_sequence: Hero (command, code, live canvas) → customer-logo strip → 'Why tldraw?' four points in 2×2 → 'Powering software across industries' four case cards (ClickUp, Padlet, Mobbin, Jam) → 'What's inside' six features → 'Join the community' stats (51K stars, 74K followers, 8.72K Discord, 265.5K weekly npm downloads with chart) → 'Save months of work' wide canvas with three overlay cards → 'Starter kits' accordion → ClickUp quote and case-study links → black footer.
observations.copy: H1: 'Build infinite canvas apps in React with the tldraw SDK'. Subhead: make whiteboards, diagrams and canvas tools with tldraw's high-performance web canvas. Primary action is the copyable command 'npm create tldraw'; nav button 'Quick Start'. The category ('infinite canvas apps', 'SDK') and audience (React developers) are both in the h1; case cards add industries (productivity, education, design, issue tracking).
observations.interaction: Dragged across the hero canvas with the preselected draw tool: a black freehand stroke appeared and the undo button became active. On load the hero did not change over 1.5 s; the logo strip at the fold changed between frames in both normal and reduced-motion loads. Measurement counted 2 running animations on load and after scroll at both widths; reduced-motion rule 'observed'.
observations.accessibility: Body text is 14px grey on white and the italic quote is mid-grey. At 390 a DOM check found the menu button 28×28px and text links ('Learn more', 'Read case study', 'Build with a starter kit') 20px tall. The hero canvas was operated by pointer only; keyboard access was not tested. No horizontal overflow.
observations.mobile: The canvas moves above the code panel and fills the width; its toolbar shrinks to five tools plus an expand control and the style panel is hidden. Command button and starter-kit link stack; the nav becomes logo and menu icon. Features and case cards go to one column, images above text. Community stats regroup (stars full width, two small cards, then the npm chart). In 'Save months of work' the wide canvas is absent and its three cards stack. Footer becomes two columns.

principles: For an SDK, put the install command, the minimal code and the running result in one view so the claim can be checked in seconds.
Make the hero demo the real component with a sensible tool preselected, so the first pointer action already produces output.
Use the product's own interface chrome as the page's recurring motif instead of decorative illustration.
For open-source developer products, show adoption as concrete numbers (stars, weekly downloads) next to named customer cases.
interpretation.fit: Suits embeddable UI SDKs, component libraries and editors whose output is visual and safe to run in the page. Wrong for backend or data APIs, where a live widget in the hero would show nothing meaningful.
interpretation.risks: The hero canvas starts empty, so a visitor who does not draw sees a framed blank box; the narrow column leaves wide unused margins at 1440. The main proof depends on a script-rendered component; in one live load at 390 the canvas toolbar had not rendered when captured.

limitations: The first desktop visit ran in parallel with other sites and loaded without toolbar icons; the canvas interaction was repeated in a clean sequential load.
Did not test keyboard operation of the canvas or the starter-kit accordion.
Whether the 'Save months of work' canvas is interactive was not tested.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.
Selected as a maintainer pick; no public design recognition was found and recorded.

name: Warp
summary: An all-monospace page built like a technical paper: numbered figures, section tags, a live task grid in the hero and factory config shown as real files.

observations.hero: Left-aligned on a pale lavender ground with a faint dot grid and vertical rules: two-line monospaced h1, one-line grey subhead, a dark 'REQUEST EARLY ACCESS' button and an outlined 'DOWNLOAD WARP TERMINAL' button. Below, a framed '[ fig. 1 — the factory ]' panel: an 8×28 grid of task squares in grey and electric blue, a queued/working/waiting/shipped legend and counters. Tiny vertical 'WARP · HOME · 2026' labels run on both edges; a speaker-icon button sits bottom-left.
observations.typography: Measured h1 54px, weight 400, line-height 1.1, tracking -0.037em, family azeretSemiMono; 32px with -0.062em at 390. Body 16px/1.7, also azeretSemiMono, so headings, body, nav and buttons share one monospaced voice. Measured families add theFuture; a proportional sans appears in the SDLC item titles and the case-study headline. Nav, buttons and section tags are spaced uppercase ('# CONFIGURATION [ONLINE]').
observations.visual_system: Near-white lavender ground, navy text, one electric blue (rgb(42, 30, 255) computed on the active tab) for states and a full-width case-study band, and a yellow 'BOOK A DEMO' button. Every artifact sits in a bordered 'fig.' frame with corner icons: task grid, file tree and code viewer, line charts, scatter plot, stacked layer diagram, control-plane dashboard. Photography appears only in two customer-story cards.
observations.page_sequence: Hero with fig. 1 → 'trusted by 800k+ devs at' logos → Configuration: 'Your software factory, defined in code.' with eight tabs and file viewer → SDLC coverage: six numbered points beside product UI → Quality loop: three charts → blue case-study band ('Cutting our cost per PR from $80 to $30') → Enterprise ready: two customer stories → 'Open at every layer' four-layer figure → Governance: control-plane figure → 'Use Warp everywhere': Factories, Terminal, Agent CLI → FAQ.
observations.copy: H1: 'Open infrastructure for cloud software factories'. Subhead: build on Warp with factories as code, any model or harness, and evals, benchmarks and self-improvement built in. Primary button 'REQUEST EARLY ACCESS'; secondary 'DOWNLOAD WARP TERMINAL'; nav adds 'BOOK A DEMO' and 'GET STARTED'. The h1 coins the category ('cloud software factories'); audience is developers ('800k+ devs') and enterprise teams. FAQ items are lowercase terminal prompts ('> what is a cloud software factory?').
observations.interaction: Clicked the 'AGENTS' tab: it turned electric blue, the description switched to agents and 'the Foreman', and the file tree opened agents/implementation/agent.md in the viewer instead of factory.yaml. On load, fig. 1 squares changed state between frames 1.5 s apart. After scrolling, the nav became a blue section index ([C] Configuration … [F] FAQ). Reduced motion: frames identical at top and at 35% depth. Measurement: 5 animations on load, 23 after scroll; rule 'observed'.
observations.accessibility: Small light-grey uppercase labels (edge labels, figure legends, chart axes) and pale pill labels in the layers figure are low contrast. At 390 the fig. 1 squares are interactive elements about 8×13px; a DOM check found 265 of 302 visible interactive elements under 32px, most of them those squares. The menu button is 30×30px and 'BOOK A DEMO' 32px tall. The speaker-icon button is present at both widths. No horizontal overflow.
observations.mobile: The nav keeps logo, yellow 'BOOK A DEMO' and a menu icon. The h1 wraps to three lines; buttons sit side by side with two-line labels. Fig. 1 recomposes into a denser grid with a wrapped legend. Configuration tabs become a vertical list above the description and viewer; quality-loop charts stack inside one figure; stories, layers and product cards stack. Page height grows from 9363 to 14029px.

principles: On a long technical page, number the figures and tag the sections so the page reads like a spec and can be navigated by section.
Prove an 'as code' claim with a browsable file tree whose files change with each tab.
Put one live-state figure in the hero (items moving through named states) to make an abstract system feel operational.
Replace the global nav with a section index once the reader is inside a long page.
interpretation.fit: Suits developer infrastructure and agent platforms whose buyers read configuration and metrics. Wrong for non-technical or consumer audiences, for whom an all-monospace page with 'fig.' framing reads as opaque.
interpretation.risks: Monospaced body text at 16px/1.7 with wide tracking is slow to read across long paragraphs, and many labels are pale. The hero figure is abstract squares, so it signals activity without showing what a task is. In the full-page measurement capture several sections below the case study rendered blank, so content depends on scroll-triggered rendering.

limitations: The desktop measurement capture was capped at 9000px and left several scroll-revealed sections blank; those sections were reviewed from the live scroll and the 390 capture.
The first live desktop visit (run in parallel) lost its stylesheet; a sequential visit was used. A locator click on the AGENTS tab did not register; a pointer click at the tab's coordinates did.
The footer below the FAQ was not captured.
The speaker-icon button was not operated.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Krea
summary: A dark photographed desk scene frames the app UI under a superlative claim, then a long catalogue of models, features and full pricing follows.

observations.hero: Dark full-bleed scene of a desk at night (a video element is present): a large monitor shows the Krea app ('Let's create something' prompt and thumbnails), with keyboard and mouse in warm light. Centred above it: a 'NEW · Try the new Seedance 2.5 model' pill, two-line h1, one-line subhead, a white 'Open Krea' pill and a translucent 'Krea Agent' pill that overlaps the top of the monitor. Nav: logo mark, ten links (Pricing with a '40% OFF' badge), 'Sign up for free' and 'Log in' pills.
observations.typography: Measured h1 60px, weight 400, line-height 1.1, tracking 0, family Suisse Intl; 36px with line-height 1.0 at 390. Body 14px/1.4 Suisse Intl. 'Krea.ai' in the h1 is filled with a grey gradient while the rest is white. Later section headings are heavier ('The industry's best Generative models.'), and bento tiles use oversized numerals ('22K', '4K', '64+').
observations.visual_system: Dark scene hero, then white and light-grey sections with rounded cards. A bento grid mixes photographic tiles (an eye, a portrait for 'Krea 3', light streaks) with plain grey tiles and big numerals. Black pill buttons on light sections; one blue for the '40% OFF' and 'New' badges. App UI appears inside cards; customer and investor logos are monochrome grey.
observations.page_sequence: Hero → model carousel (prompt cards with arrows) → 'The industry's best Generative models. In one subscription.' with model-provider logos → feature bento → 'Krea powers millions of creatives, enterprises, and everyday people.' logos → use-case list beside app video → 'Trusted by over 30,000,000 users… We've got a plan for everybody' pricing with Monthly/Yearly toggle → teams and enterprise plans → 'Dead simple UI' prompt-box demo → 'Krea 3' image carousel → investors and hiring → 'Edit images with Krea 3' card → footer.
observations.copy: H1: 'Krea.ai is the world's most powerful creative AI suite.' Subhead: generate, enhance and edit images, videos or 3D meshes for free with AI. Primary button 'Open Krea'; secondary 'Krea Agent'; nav 'Sign up for free'. The category is 'creative AI suite'; audience is named as 'creatives, enterprises, and everyday people' and 'pros and beginners alike', with the scale claim 'Trusted by over 30,000,000 users From 191 countries'.
observations.interaction: Clicked the right arrow of the model carousel below the hero: no visible change after 3 s and no horizontal scroll offset changed. The page scrolls inside a <main> element (document height equals the viewport), so scrolling worked via the wheel over content. The hero did not change over 1.5 s; a video element was present but not playing. Reduced motion: same static hero. Measurement: 10 animations on load and after scroll (12 at 390); rule 'observed'.
observations.accessibility: The carousel arrow buttons have no text or aria-label, and at 390 a header button has none either (the only icon button visible there is the menu icon). The h1 carries an aria-label ('Krea.ai is a powerful AI suite for Creatives.') that differs from its visible text. Inactive use-case items are light grey on white. Scrolling happens in an inner container, not the document. At 390 the home logo link is 22×22px. No horizontal overflow.
observations.mobile: The nav keeps logo, 'Sign up for free', 'Log in' and a menu icon. The hero photo is cropped to keyboard and chair, so the monitor with the app UI is not visible; the h1 wraps to three centred lines and the two CTAs stack as wide pills. The carousel shows one card with the next peeking. Bento tiles recompose into a two-column mosaic; pricing and enterprise plans stack; the prompt-box demo and Krea 3 carousel go full width.

principles: Stage the real app UI inside a physical scene (a desk, a monitor) so a software tool reads as a place where work happens.
When the product is self-serve with a free tier, put full pricing on the homepage rather than behind a link.
Use a bento grid with oversized numerals to compress a broad capability list into scannable claims.
Announce the newest model in a pill above the h1 so a fast-moving product shows freshness without rewriting the hero.
interpretation.fit: Suits broad, self-serve creative tools with many models and a free tier. Wrong for a focused single-job tool, where a large bento and multi-plan pricing would bury the one action.
interpretation.risks: The superlative h1 has no proof beside it, and the monitor in the hero scene is small and drops out entirely on mobile. The page is a long catalogue with repeated sign-up blocks. Inner-container scrolling defeats full-page capture; unlabeled carousel controls and the aria-label mismatch weaken accessibility.

limitations: The page scrolls inside <main>, so the measurement full-page captures equal one viewport; sections were reviewed from live scroll snapshots at both widths.
The carousel arrow produced no visible change; carousel media had not loaded in the control screenshots, so whether the carousel works after full load is unverified.
The first 390 scroll pass ended with the page closing; a second pass completed.
Did not operate the Monthly/Yearly pricing toggle, the plan sliders or the prompt-box demo.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.
Selected as a maintainer pick; no public design recognition was found and recorded.

name: Notion
summary: A centred 96px headline with one rotating verb chip sits above a framed product-UI video, so one general promise and the workspace itself share the first screen.

observations.hero: Centred stack on white: two-line h1 whose middle word sits in a coloured pill that swaps verbs, a one-line subhead, then blue 'Get Notion free' beside pale-blue 'Request a demo'. Below sits a framed Notion workspace (Ramp HQ board, agents sidebar) delivered as a video with a Pause button, with line-drawn characters peeking around it. A row of customer logos is pinned to the bottom edge of the viewport and overlaps the mockup.
observations.typography: One measured family, NotionInter, for display and body. Measured Lyon Text sets the testimonial quotes, and the footer quotation is also serif. h1 96px, weight 600, line-height 1, tracking -0.048em. Section h2 54px/700 at -1.875px, card titles 22px/700, subhead 20px, body 16px/1.5. At 390 the h1 is 42px at -0.036em. Weight and tight tracking create the hierarchy; there is no second display face.
observations.visual_system: White ground and black type. One saturated blue (computed rgb(0,117,222)) marks primary actions, with a pale-blue secondary. Other colour comes from the verb chip (teal, green, blue and purple seen), product-UI tags, and three duotone testimonial photos in red, blue and ochre. Light-grey rounded panels frame cropped product UI. Black line-drawn characters and emoji-style icons form the motif. The closing CTA sits on a warm grey band.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → hero (rotating-verb h1, CTAs, product video, pinned logo row) → logo wall 'The most ambitious companies run on Notion.' → 'AI where your team works.' with three job cards (capture knowledge, find answers, automate busywork), each with a UI crop → 'See what Notion can do', five use-case tiles → 'Trusted by teams that ship.', three photo quotes (Cursor, Faire, Ramp) → stats strip → 'Get started today.' → footer with a McLuhan quotation.
observations.copy: h1: 'Where teams and agents [verb] together.' The verb rotates; Scale, Ship, Think, Jam and Create were all seen. Subhead: capture context, find answers and automate tasks with AI built for your team. Primary button 'Get Notion free', secondary 'Request a demo'. The audience is named as 'teams and agents'. The page title, not the first screen, names the category ('The AI workspace that works for you'). Proof lines include 'Over 50% of YC companies'.
observations.interaction: Operated the Pause button at the bottom-left of the hero mockup: the video element paused and the button label changed to 'Play'. On load, the h1 chip changed word between captures taken 1.5 s apart, and a marquee animation was running. After scrolling, the pinned logo row became a two-row wall and a divider appeared under the nav. With reduced motion, the chip kept one word for 5 s, the marquee animation was no longer running, and the hero video did not start.
observations.accessibility: On the first desktop screen, the pinned logo row covers the lower edge of the hero mockup. The closing 'Request a demo' link computes to about 4.0:1 on white. Testimonial names and quotes are white text over duotone photos; their contrast was not measured. At 390, 42 of 54 visible targets are under 44px tall. The menu toggle is 44×44 and labelled 'Toggle main menu'. Neither width has horizontal overflow, and no unnamed buttons or links were found.
observations.mobile: The hero product video is dropped. A row of seven illustrated avatars sits above a three-line 42px h1, and the two CTAs become full-width stacked buttons. Logos run as a one-row marquee. Job cards stack, use-case tiles become full-width list rows, and testimonials become a horizontal swipe row with the next card peeking in. Footer columns pair up. The nav shrinks to the logo, 'Get Notion free' and a menu toggle.

principles: Keep the headline frame fixed and rotate one word inside a coloured chip; the claim can then cover several jobs and still read as one sentence.
Pair a short, type-only promise with a large, real product surface on the first screen, so the product is visible before any scrolling.
Organise capabilities by the job a buyer hires the product for (capture, find, automate), each with its own UI crop, instead of a feature list.
Under reduced motion, stop rotating copy and marquees and leave one static word in place.
interpretation.fit: Suits broad, well-known horizontal tools with many use cases, where the promise has to stay general and the UI proves the breadth. Wrong for a narrow, unknown product: a rotating verb and a generic promise to 'teams' would hide what it actually does.
interpretation.risks: The first screen never names a category noun. Because the verb rotates, a glance or a screenshot can catch a different claim each time. The pinned logo row hides part of the product mockup. With four measured sections, the page pushes pricing, security and integrations to other pages. When video cannot play, the hero shows only a poster frame.

limitations: The hero video did not decode in the test Chromium (no H.264 support), so only its poster frame and the Pause-to-Play label change were seen.
The rotating verb set was compiled across several loads; the full list and its order were not verified.
The first live load timed out through the proxy and was retried.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Cal.com
archetype_note: Closer to a conventional SaaS conversion page: product-UI hero, three steps, feature grid, social proof, FAQ.
summary: Sign-up buttons share a framed hero card with a recreated booking page and calendar, so visitors see the surface their invitees will use before reading feature copy.

observations.hero: A white rounded card on a light-grey ground holds two columns. Left: a release pill ('Cal.com launches v6.9.5'), a three-line h1, a grey subhead, a full-width dark 'Sign up with Google' button, a lighter 'Sign up with email' button and 'No credit card required'. Right: a recreated booking page (host avatar, meeting title, 15m/30m/45m/1h chips, video app, timezone) beside a May 2025 month grid cropped at the card edge, above Trustpilot, Product Hunt and G2 star rows. Customer logos sit below the card.
observations.typography: Display measured as Cal Sans: h1 64px, weight 600, line-height 1.1, tracking 0, a face that sets tight. Section h2 48px/600. Body and card titles use measured Cal Sans UI Variable Light at weight 300 (body 16px/1.5, h3 18px). Inter and Matter are also measured on the page. Body measure is 50ch at 1440 and 38ch at 390; the h1 is 40px at 390. The heavy display against light text weight is the main hierarchy device.
observations.visual_system: Light-grey ground (rgb 244) framed by thin vertical guide lines, with '+' crosshair marks at section seams. Every module is a white card with a hairline border and soft shadow. Buttons are near-black or white only; colour comes from third-party logos, rating stars and app icons. Imagery is recreated product UI: booking page, availability toggles, buffer selects, calendar overlay, notification toasts. The only photos are avatars. Small icon pills label each section.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → hero card → logo strip → 'How it works': three numbered steps (connect calendar, set availability, choose how to meet) → 'Benefits': 2×2 feature cards with UI → '…and so much more!': eight icon tiles → testimonial quote carousel → 'App store' integrations grid → 'Wall of love' masonry of social posts with 'Show more' → FAQ accordion → logo strip again → 'Smarter, simpler scheduling' CTA card with Product Hunt badges → footer with compliance badges and download links.
observations.copy: h1: 'The better way to schedule your meetings'. The subhead names three audiences: individuals, businesses taking calls, and developers building scheduling platforms. Primary button 'Sign up with Google'; the nav button is 'Get started'. The category is named plainly as a scheduling app or software ('Your all-purpose scheduling app'). Several section heads carry a dark-and-light button pair ('Get started' with 'Book a demo' or 'Explore apps'; 'Talk to sales' with 'Get started'). Testimonials and social posts compare it directly with Calendly.
observations.interaction: Clicking the hero '1h' chip and a date changed nothing; the cursor stayed default, so the booker acted as a static picture. I operated the FAQ instead: clicking the second question opened its answer and closed the first. It responded only after a long settle in this proxied session. After scrolling, the nav moved into a rounded white bar with a hairline border. No running animations or pixel changes appeared on the first screen, with or without reduced motion.
observations.accessibility: The subhead and most supporting text compute to rgb(137,137,137): about 3.5:1 on white and 3.2:1 on the grey ground. No <button> or aria-expanded elements were found, so FAQ rows are not exposed as buttons. The 390 menu trigger is a focusable div with no role or label. At 390, 85 of 124 targets are under 44px tall ('Sign in' is 45×16). In one capture the nav had no background and its links overlapped the FAQ heading. No horizontal overflow.
observations.mobile: The hero card stacks: copy and both sign-up buttons first, then the booker and the month grid, which stays cropped at its right edge. Section heads move from centred to left-aligned. Step and feature cards go single-column, and the eight icon tiles become two columns. In the capture the logo strip showed only its caption. The nav keeps the wordmark, 'Sign in', 'Get started' and a menu icon. The page grows from 8,569px to 11,874px.

principles: Put the artifact your users' customers will see (here, a booking page) in the hero, so visitors judge the output instead of reading claims.
Make one-click OAuth sign-up the primary hero action, and state the friction removed ('No credit card required') directly beneath it.
Use one module shape (a white bordered card on a quiet ground) for every section, so a long page stays scannable.
If a hero artifact looks interactive (chips, dates), make it respond locally or mark it as an illustration.
interpretation.fit: Suits self-serve SaaS whose output is a recognisable surface (booking pages, forms, invoices) and whose buyers compare it with a known incumbent. Wrong for products whose value does not show in one screen, such as back-end infrastructure, where a recreated UI would show little.
interpretation.risks: The hero booker invites clicks it ignores. Light-weight grey body text falls below 4.5:1. Repeated CTA pairs and a long run of proof sections (carousel, wall of love, FAQ, repeated logos) make the page long, close to 12,000px at 390. Interactive elements are not exposed as buttons, which hurts keyboard and screen-reader use.

limitations: The FAQ responded only after about 30 s in this proxied session; earlier clicks did nothing, so its behaviour on a normal connection is unverified.

The two measurement captures showed different sample bookers (Partnerships Meeting with 15m selected vs Academic Counseling with 45m). Whether the booker rotates was not confirmed: it stayed static for 20 s in my session.
The measurement record counted 2 (desktop) and 8 (390) running animations on load; I saw no movement and could not identify them.
Whether the testimonial carousel auto-advances was not verified.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Rive
summary: An all-caps Orbitron headline and a CLI install panel with OS tabs lead the first screen, while a column of use-case video tiles scrolls beside them.

observations.hero: Black ground, split layout in a 1000px column. Left: a column of bordered tiles labelled by use case (Product UI, Game UI, Mobile Apps, Film + TV, Websites, Games, Fantasy Interfaces) drifts upward. Right: a spaced 'RIVE' wordmark, a two-line uppercase h1 and a grey subhead. Below them, a dark panel holds 'RIVE CLI' (macOS/Linux and Windows tabs, a curl command, a copy button) and 'RIVE EDITOR' ('Sign up', 'Download desktop app'). A one-line trust claim closes the column.
observations.typography: Display measured as Orbitron: h1 40px, weight 900, tracking 0.01em, uppercase. Section h2 24px/700, uppercase. Eyebrows and labels use measured Tomorrow at 14px/500, uppercase with 1.4px tracking, some in orange. Body is measured Inter at 16px/1.6 with a 64ch measure; Inter Display is also present. The install command is set in monospace. At 390 the h1 shrinks to 21px and body to 14px, so the display loses most of its scale.
observations.visual_system: Black and near-black bands alternate. Text is white and mid-grey, with one orange accent for eyebrows and their icons. The command uses green and cyan syntax colour, which turns red and orange for the Windows command. Dark panels have small radii; buttons are uppercase with small icons. Imagery is product output: video tiles, a large video slot in the Editor section, a grid of 14 platform logos (Web, iOS, Android, Flutter, React, Unity, Unreal and others) and a two-row customer logo wall.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → hero (scrolling tile column beside the headline and CLI/Editor panel) → 'Rive Editor: Design, code, and animate' (copy left, large video slot right) → 'Rive Runtimes: Build once, ship anywhere' (platform icons left, copy right) → 'Products built with Rive reach over 2 billion users worldwide': logo wall, a positioning paragraph with comparison stats, and 18 testimonial cards in three columns → newsletter signup → six-column footer with underlined links → wordmark and social icons.
observations.copy: h1: 'The Interactive experience engine', rendered uppercase. Subhead: build interactive UI, motion and game experiences in the Editor, or have an agent generate them with the CLI; the output runs natively on mobile, desktop, web, consoles, TVs and vehicles. Primary actions are the copyable CLI command, 'Sign up' and 'Download desktop app'; the nav says 'Get started'. Audience: designers, animators and developers. Proof names Spotify Wrapped and Duolingo, and a paragraph compares Rive with After Effects, Figma, Lottie and CSS animations.
observations.interaction: Operated the CLI tab: clicking 'Windows' replaced 'curl -fsSL …/install.sh | sh' with 'irm …/install.ps1 | iex' and moved the underline. The hero tile column moved upward between captures taken 3 s apart, although getAnimations() listed no animations. With reduced motion the column still moved about the same distance. During the scroll getAnimations() stayed empty and no video played. The measurement record found no reduced-motion rule.
observations.accessibility: An automated contrast check found no body text under 4.5:1 on the dark ground. The 390 menu trigger is a div with no role or label, removed from the tab order (tabindex -1). The newsletter email field has a placeholder but no label. The CLI tabs are 23px tall and the copy button is 35×20. At 390, 47 of 105 targets are under 24px in one dimension, mostly 20px-tall underlined footer links. No horizontal overflow.
observations.mobile: The tile column becomes a horizontal row of tiles across the top, above the wordmark and h1. The h1 drops to 21px. The CLI command wraps onto three lines, and 'Download desktop app' shortens to 'Downloads'. The runtimes icon grid moves below its copy. The logo wall reflows into four rows, testimonials go single-column, and the footer becomes two columns. The nav keeps the logo, a menu icon and 'Get started'.

principles: For a product developers install, put the exact install command in the hero, with an OS selector and a copy button, next to the GUI sign-up path.
Let a moving column of real output tiles carry the use cases, so the headline can stay short.
Keep a distinctive display face for the headline and section titles only, and set body text in a neutral sans.
On phones, shrink the display size less than the body, or the headline stops reading as a headline.
interpretation.fit: Suits tools with two entry points, a GUI for designers and a CLI or SDK for developers, whose visual output proves itself in motion. Wrong for buyers who never install software or use a terminal, such as finance or HR teams, for whom a curl command in the hero means nothing.
interpretation.risks: The hero depends on video. In this browser every tile and the Editor video stayed blank, leaving grey boxes and an empty half-section. The drifting tile column ignores reduced motion. The futuristic display face sets a gaming tone that may undersell product-UI use. The 21px mobile h1 and the three-line command weaken the first phone screen. The menu trigger cannot be reached by keyboard.

limitations: The hero tiles and the Editor-section video are MP4s that failed to load in the test Chromium (no H.264), so their content was not seen.
In this proxied session the tile column appeared only after a long delay; its normal start-up timing is unverified.
Platform icons and some button icons were missing in some live loads but present in the measurement capture.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Retool
summary: A prompt box, not a screenshot, is the hero's centrepiece: the page asks visitors to describe an app, then spends most of its length on governance and enterprise proof.

observations.hero: A gradient announcement bar and a dark nav sit above a rounded blue-to-rust gradient panel, with tilted, dimmed dashboard screenshots behind the content. Centred in the panel: a light-weight h1, a 'NEW: Explore the new Retool app builder for free' pill, and a large cream prompt box (placeholder 'Write a prompt, use @ to include data', 'Starter prompts', submit arrow). Under the box are two dropdowns, 'Import code' and 'Build with AI agents', with tool logos, and a 'Watch the film' pill.
observations.typography: Display and body measured as saansFont: h1 72px, weight 300, line-height 1, tracking -0.022em. Section heads 48px/300; 'Start today' 60px/300. Labels, nav items and buttons use measured pxGroteskFont at 14px, with 12px uppercase in places; ui-monospace appears in code. Body 16px/1.5 with a 36ch measure. At 390 the h1 is 40px/300. The light weight at large size keeps headlines quiet against the dark ground.
observations.visual_system: Near-black ground (rgb 21,21,21) with off-white text (rgb 233,235,223) and cream surfaces for interactive objects (the prompt box, the primary pill button). Blue, violet and rust gradients appear only in the announcement bar, hero panel and closing scene. Product imagery: dashboard screenshots, an app gallery, and tall rounded media cards (MCP terminal, import drop zone, integrations constellation, compliance rings with SOC 2, ISO 27001 and SAML SSO). The closing scene shows glassy 3D shapes and a reaching hand.
observations.page_sequence: Announcement bar → nav → hero prompt panel → 'Apps that mean business' screenshot gallery → split scroll: pinned left heads ('Build powerful apps from anywhere', 'Securely connect to your production data', 'Ship safely, with governance built in') beside tall media cards → 'Why enterprises choose Retool', three columns → logo row and outcome grid ('Ramp saved $8M and 20,000+ hours') with industry cards → 'Start today', prompt box repeated → 'Get the latest from Retool' posts → footer with oversized wordmark.
observations.copy: h1: 'Secure your vibe-coded apps'. There is no subhead sentence; the 'NEW' pill line ('Explore the new Retool app builder for free') stands in for one. The announcement bar promotes 'A unified harness to run and govern AI agents'. Nav primary: 'Start for free'. Nav secondary: 'Contact sales' ('Book a demo' on one load). The audience is framed as enterprises ('Why enterprises choose Retool'). The page title says 'Build internal software better, with AI.'
observations.interaction: 'Starter prompts' did not open after two clicks, so I operated 'Import code': it opened an 'Import external React apps' panel with React App, Lovable and Replit tabs and an explanatory accordion. The prompt box then held 'Build a customer support queue'; other captures show other example prompts. On load the placeholder changed brightness between captures, and getAnimations() listed a text shimmer and a border pulse. On scroll the left heads stay pinned as media cards pass. With reduced motion only the shimmer was still listed.
observations.accessibility: Over mid-page content the fixed nav has no opaque backdrop: in one desktop capture, body copy showed through behind the nav links. The 'Import code' and 'Build with AI agents' labels are 60% black on light grey, about 4.3:1 from computed colours. There is a skip link. The 390 menu button is labelled 'Open navigation' (40×40), and no unnamed buttons or links were found. At 390, 82 of 95 targets are under 44px tall, and the tool-logo buttons are 20×20. No horizontal overflow.
observations.mobile: The hero keeps its order in a narrower rounded panel: a two-line 40px h1, the pill, a prompt box showing a typed example, and dropdowns shortened to 'Import' and 'Build'. A two-row logo grid follows (Amazon, Taco Bell, Conagra, EA, Lyft, Quest, Boeing, Adobe). The app gallery becomes a horizontal strip. The pinned split becomes stacked items, each with its media card above the copy. The nav shrinks to the wordmark, 'Contact sales' and a menu button.

principles: When the product starts from a sentence, make the input itself the hero object, with secondary entrances (import, agent integrations) beside it.
Name the visitor's current problem in the headline ('vibe-coded apps') and let the section order answer it with data-access, governance and security proof.
Walk through several capabilities with a pinned heading column and scrolling media cards, rather than a new section for each.
Repeat the hero input at the close, so the last screen offers an action rather than a summary.
interpretation.fit: Suits AI builders and agent platforms where a prompt is the real first step, and enterprise-leaning products that must pair speed with control. Wrong where the input cannot be described in a sentence, or where a prompt box that only leads to sign-up would read as a fake demo.
interpretation.risks: The hero prompt produces nothing until sign-up, so it promises an interaction and then defers it. The h1 is four words, there is no subhead, and a promo pill sits beside it; 'internal software' appears in the page title but not on the first screen. Captures show large dark gaps where content had not rendered. The transparent fixed nav collides with body text, and copy and nav labels varied between loads.

limitations: The hero film and video did not load in the test Chromium (no H.264), and 'Watch the film' was not opened.
'Starter prompts' gave no visible response; it may need a state I did not reach.
The nav CTA label ('Contact sales' vs 'Book a demo') and the example prompts varied between loads; this may be an experiment.
Several scroll-revealed cards and images stayed blank during fast scrolling and in the measurement full-page capture; one live load arrived unstyled and was reloaded.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Supabase
summary: Pairs a two-line outcome promise with a plain list of bundled services, then shows breadth through a seven-module bento and real dashboard and code views.

observations.hero: Nav: logo, Product/Developers/Solutions menus, Pricing, Docs, Blog, a GitHub star count (111.7K), Sign in and a green "Start your project" button. Below it, an offset two-column block: the two-line h1 and two buttons on the left, a three-line subhead top-aligned on the right. From about y=450 the first row of a seven-card product bento (wide Postgres Database card with an elephant line drawing, Authentication, Edge Functions) fills the rest of the first screen.
observations.typography: h1 measured 46px, weight 500, line-height 1, tracking 0, measured family Manrope; its second line is set in brand green. Section h2s are 34px in the same face, each split into a dark line and a grey line ("Stay productive and manage your app" / "without leaving the dashboard"). Body 16px/1.5, measured family Inter, hero subhead measure 46ch. Source Code Pro is in the measured families; a monospace sets the code sample and the auth card's email grid. Card titles are 16px h2s. Phone h1 34px, line-height 1.1.
observations.visual_system: Near-white ground (computed body oklch 0.995) with hairline section borders; white cards with 1px borders and rounded corners. One green accent on primary buttons, the h1's second line and some code tokens. Card art is grey line drawing (elephant, wire globe with route lines, isometric cube, table-to-endpoint rows). Customer logos are grey monochrome. Product proof is light-theme dashboard frames and a syntax-highlighted code block. The only saturated surface is a pink-to-orange Lovable story card. The measurement record flags dark_background true, but every render I saw was light (data-theme="light").
observations.page_sequence: Hero → seven-module bento closed by "Use one or all. Best of breed products. Integrated as a platform." → 12-logo grid → tabbed dashboard demo (Table Editor / SQL Editor / RLS Policies) → "Use Supabase with React" with six framework tabs and code → templates (2 large, 4 small) → customer stories (Lovable card plus four collapsed logo tiles) → wall of X posts → "Open source from day one" → closing CTA repeating the h1 → SOC2 / HIPAA / ISO 27001 strip → footer with newsletter and theme toggle.
observations.copy: h1: "Build in a weekend" / "Scale to millions". Subhead lists the bundle: start with a Postgres database, add Authentication, Data APIs, Edge Functions, Realtime Data, Storage and Vector embeddings. Primary button "Start your project"; secondary "Request a demo". The page names its category by components, Postgres first, rather than a label; the document title reads "The Postgres Development Platform". Audience cues are developer-specific: framework code, starter templates, testimonials about solo founders and vibe coding, footer Solutions listing "AI Builders", "Vibe Coders" and "Enterprise".
observations.interaction: Operated the dashboard tab "SQL Editor": its pill took the dark outline, Table Editor's cleared (aria-selected moved), and the framed panel switched from a countries table grid to an SQL editor with a query, a results grid and an Assistant side panel. It took effect on a second load, after the panel had mounted. Frames 1.5–3 s apart on the hero and testimonial wall showed no pixel change. The nav stayed pinned while scrolling (measurement record lists sticky_nav false). Under reduced motion nothing moved either; only late images appeared.
observations.accessibility: Skip-to-content link present. Probe found the header and footer logo links to "/" with no accessible name. The testimonial wall fades its edge columns to very light grey text. Grey body text on the near-white ground reads clearly by eye. At 390 the menu is a 40×40 button labelled "Open main menu" with aria-expanded; hero buttons are 38px tall; footer links are 20px tall and social icons 22×22 (69 of 124 visible targets under 24px in one dimension). No horizontal overflow at 1440 or 390.
observations.mobile: Header collapses to logo plus hamburger; the GitHub count, Sign in and header button go. Hero stacks h1 (34px), subhead, then both buttons side by side. The bento becomes a single column of text-only cards: the line drawings, email grid and globe are dropped. Logos move to a 3-column grid; the dashboard demo keeps its tabs over a cropped frame; templates and story logo tiles stack full width; footer goes to two columns. Page grows from 7,691px to 9,820px; 10 sections at both widths.

principles: Let the h1 carry the outcome and the subhead name the components buyers already search for, so the promise and the inventory arrive together.
Split each section heading into a dark claim line and a grey qualifier line so the headings alone read as the page's argument.
Place a tabbed real-UI view and a framework-switching code sample mid-page so evaluators see both the dashboard and the integration before templates and customer stories.
On phones, drop decorative card art and keep each module's name and one-sentence claim.
interpretation.fit: Suits developer platforms that bundle several recognisable primitives (database, auth, storage, functions) and sell to builders who judge by docs and code. Wrong for a single-feature product, where a seven-card bento would be padding, or for non-technical buyers who cannot read the code sample.
interpretation.risks: The first screen shows no product UI, only grey line drawings; the real dashboard sits about 1,700px down and its frame loaded late (blank until mounted). Every section uses the same white card and hairline treatment, so after the hero little signals which part matters most. The testimonial wall and the long footer add length without new product information.

limitations: The dashboard panel and code sample loaded late in headless Chromium; the first control attempt saw a blank panel and the tab click only took effect on a second load.

The measurement record reports 45 running animations on load, 15 after scroll and an observed reduced-motion rule; I saw no visible motion in frames 1.5–3 s apart and document.getAnimations returned 0, so what those animations drive is unverified.
Contrast was judged by eye; the automated contrast probe could not parse the page's oklch colours.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Framer
archetype_note: Closer to a dark product-film platform page: agent sessions staged beside outputs, then a feature bento and showcase.
summary: A 12-word category claim ("design agent") on black, then staged agent sessions and a platform bento argue the agent sits on a full site builder.

viewports.desktop: 1440 × 900: rendered, scrolled, three controls attempted; none changed state

observations.hero: Nav: logo, Platform/Solutions/Resources menus, Enterprise, Pricing; Log in and a white Sign up button on the right. The h1 sits left on two lines with "Get started for free" (white) and "Download app" (dark grey) beneath; a "New: Skills →" link aligns right on the same row. A full-width rounded tile below holds a video of a glowing blue prompt box ("New Chat", "Ask Framer…", model picker) with a 0:36 duration badge, filling the rest of the first screen.
observations.typography: h1 measured 54px, weight 500, line-height 1, tracking −0.04em, measured family GT Walsheim Medium (a geometric sans). Section h2s are 44px in the same face, left-aligned, mostly on two lines; the closing h2 returns to 54px and is centred. Body 18px/1.4, measured family Inter Variable, 58ch measure. Input Mono Regular is in the measured families; a monospace sets the terminal panel. Phone h1 36px over three lines.
observations.visual_system: Pure black ground (computed body rgb(0,0,0)) throughout, white type, white primary buttons and dark grey secondary ones. Surfaces are near-black rounded cards with faint borders. Most imagery is dark-mode Framer UI: chat panel, CMS table, Core Web Vitals meters, branch list, analytics chart, A/B table, a community feed window. Accent is electric blue (hero glow, metric values, progress bars) with some purple in charts. Customer logos are white monochrome. Photography appears inside mockups (Haus layouts, image-wheel cards) and in showcase thumbnails seen in the phone capture.
observations.page_sequence: Hero + video tile → 8-logo grid → "Agents that work alongside you, not instead of you": four feature cards (Design / Run your CMS / Code with an agent / Connect to any AI) beside a pinned agent chat panel, then a framer-agent terminal panel with claude/cursor/codex tabs → "Not just vibes, a full platform" bento (Performance, CMS, SEO, Hosting, Analytics, A/B Testing and more) → "Shipped with Framer" showcase → customer story cards → community feed window → "Your next idea starts here" prompt box with starter chips → large footer.
observations.copy: h1: "Framer is the design agent for every step from idea to launch". No subhead; the buttons follow directly. Primary "Get started for free", secondary "Download app". The h1 names the category ("design agent"), matching the document title "Framer: AI design agent". Section heads position against replacement and against vibe-coding ("not instead of you", "Not just vibes, a full platform"). Audience is professional teams ("teams shipping big sites"); the footer's Compare column names Webflow, Figma, Wix, Lovable, Claude Code and others.
observations.interaction: Tried the terminal tab "cursor" twice (second time after 7 s in view): "claude" stayed active and the session body stayed empty below its header. Clicking the hero tile only drew a white outline; the video stayed paused at frame 0. Hovering and clicking "Platform" opened no menu. The page never left readyState "interactive" and its mp4s never loaded. While scrolling, the nav and the agent chat panel stayed pinned. 16 running "ghostFlow" animations were reported in normal and reduced-motion loads; hero frames 1.5 s apart showed no pixel change in either.
observations.accessibility: At 390 the menu icon is a focusable div (tabindex 0) with no role, label or aria-expanded. Desktop probe: 2 buttons, 5 community-feed links and the footer logo link without accessible names, and one textarea with no label or placeholder. Feed metadata is #666 on #111 at 13px (about 3.3:1). Phone targets are small: "Log in" 40×17, hero buttons 29px tall, "Start with Agents" links 20px tall. No horizontal overflow. In the measurement capture a cookie banner covers the lower first screen on phone.
observations.mobile: Desktop menus collapse to a hamburger. The h1 wraps to three lines; buttons stay side by side and "New: Skills" drops below them. The video tile shrinks to a 219px strip. Logos become one row cropped at both edges. Agent cards stack with no pinned chat panel or terminal; the fourth reads "Connect to any agent". Story cards sit in a row cropped at the right. The closing prompt box becomes a "Get started for free" button over a canvas UI image.

principles: When the product is entering a new category, put the category noun in the h1 and skip the subhead so the claim and the two actions read as one unit.
Show an agent's work as a pinned session panel beside the outputs it produced, so stacked feature cards read as steps of one session.
Follow AI claims with a dense bento of operational proof (performance numbers, uptime, localization, A/B results) to answer the 'is it a toy' objection.
Replace a desktop-only interactive closer, such as a prompt box with starter chips, with a single button on phones rather than shrinking it.
interpretation.fit: Suits AI-forward creative or site-building tools that must also prove production depth to buyers who already know the base product. Wrong for regulated or infrastructure products whose buyers need parameters, pricing or code first; a near-text-free first screen of glowing UI would read as mood rather than evidence.
interpretation.risks: Almost all proof is media: in this headless session the hero video, showcase and story cards stayed unloaded and the controls did not respond, leaving large black voids in the desktop capture. Without a subhead, the first screen never says in words that the output is a website. The all-black ground, grey-on-black card copy and small phone tap targets trade legibility for atmosphere.

limitations: In headless Chromium the page stayed at readyState 'interactive', mp4 media never loaded, and the three controls tried (terminal tab, hero video, Platform menu) produced no state change; interactive behaviour is unverified.
Desktop captures of 'Shipped with Framer', 'Trusted by teams' and parts of the community feed were empty; their content is described from the 390 measurement capture.
The dimmed agent feature cards in desktop captures (full brightness on phone) may be an unfinished reveal effect rather than the intended state.
The 1440 full-page measurement capture stops at 9,000px of a 10,742px page; the closing CTA and footer were seen in the live scroll.
At 390 the measurement capture showed Log in and Sign up beside the hamburger and a cookie banner; my live capture showed only logo and hamburger and no banner.
The measurement record lists the reduced-motion rule as 'unverified' (desktop) and 'not_observed' (mobile).
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Paper
summary: A scripted agent terminal builds one playlist page inside a realistic editor window, and the page itself is drawn as an artboard with rulers and paper grain.

observations.hero: Left-aligned stack on a warm, grainy paper ground: a two-tone headline (dark 'design incredible', then a grey continuation), a one-sentence subhead, a black 'download Paper' button and a text link 'open Paper in the browser →'. From about y=430 a full-width editor window (pages panel, empty canvas, layout inspector) fills the rest of the screen, overlapped by a terminal pane running the prompt 'build my playlist screen with real data'. A tick-mark ruler and a folded-paper diagonal sit at the right edge.
observations.typography: h1 'design incredible' measured 48px, weight 360, line-height 1, tracking -0.02em, measured family Matter; the grey continuation is an h2 at the same size and weight, so the headline reads as one three-line block. Section h2s repeat 48px/360; card h3s are 18px weight 550. Body 18px/1.6, measure 67ch, Matter. Terminal text is monospace (Paper Mono is in the measured family list). Phone h1 40px, tracking -0.015em.
observations.visual_system: Off-white paper ground with visible grain (computed lab L 94). The content column is framed by hairlines with small square handles at the corners, like a selected artboard, plus a ruler and folded-corner diagonals at the right edge. Product windows use light-grey desktop chrome. Accent is sparse: one soft blue download button and coloured multiplayer cursor tags. Imagery is dithered or halftone (vinyl photo, Series A collage) and a Mondrian-like grid. Statement sections sit inside large white semicircles.
observations.page_sequence: Hero with editor and agent terminal → 'used in production by designers at' (11 logos) → 'Introducing Paper Desktop' with a cycling app-icon dock and download → semicircle 'finally a continuous loop, from Paper to code and back' → editor demo ('Vinyl Sundays' playlist page) → two feature cards → 'connected to real content, real data' + demo → two cards → 'hand off boilerplate work' + demo → two cards → semicircle 'the full-circle, anti-slop workflow' → roadmap → 'what's new' and Series A cards → footer.
observations.copy: h1: 'design incredible', continued by 'the connected canvas for teams shipping with agents'. Subhead: Paper connects teams, agents, code and data on one design space built on web standards, 'so nothing gets lost in translation'. Primary button 'download Paper' (later buttons read 'download for Linux' in this browser); secondary 'open Paper in the browser →'. Category named as a 'connected canvas'; audience as teams working with agents and designers at named companies. Copy is mostly lower-case, nav and buttons included, with lines like 'good bye lorem ipsum'.
observations.interaction: Clicked the 'Paper' app icon in the Desktop dock: the centre icon changed from a solid blue mark to a teal noise-filled version; the side icons cycled through other app icons before and after. On load the hero terminal typed its prompt and listed tool calls while the canvas stayed empty; later editor demos replayed typed prompts ('build my…', 'generate 6 mobi…') beside the playlist page. The nav stayed pinned. With reduced motion the hero loaded finished (full log, built page) and frames 1.5 s apart did not change.
observations.accessibility: The header logo link to '/' has no accessible name. The grey headline continuation computes to about 2.8:1 against the ground (lab L 60 on L 94), below 3:1 for large text. White text on the soft blue download button reads faint by eye. At 390 the menu is a 44×44 'Open menu' button and the main button is 40px tall; 34 of 38 visible targets are under 44px tall, two footer labels under 24px. No horizontal overflow at 1440 or 390.
observations.mobile: The header shows only the logo and a hamburger. The headline wraps to five lines (h1 40px), the subhead follows, and only 'download Paper' remains in the first screen. The editor window shows mainly its terminal pane. Feature card pairs stack. In the 390 full-page capture the demo windows under 'finally a continuous loop' and 'connected to real content' rendered as empty panels. The measurement counts 10 sections at 1440 and 4 at 390; page height 9,585px against 9,312px.

principles: Script an agent session inside a realistic editor window and reuse the same finished artifact in every demo, so each feature reads as a step on one piece of work.
Dress the page in the product's own medium (artboard handles, rulers, paper grain) so the brand and the tool share one visual language.
When reduced motion is requested, load a scripted demo in its finished state rather than an empty canvas.
Split the headline into a short dark claim and a lighter category line to get a memorable phrase and a clear category in one block.
interpretation.fit: Suits design and creative tools whose output can be shown being built, especially ones selling an agent or code workflow to designers. Wrong for a product with no visual artifact, such as an API or a back-office service, where a staged editor would be decoration.
interpretation.risks: Light 360-weight type and the grey second headline line trade contrast for tone. The same editor-window demo appears four times, so the middle of the page repeats itself, and the feature cards between demos are text-only. The download button names the visitor's OS ('download for Linux'). In the phone capture several demo panels rendered empty, leaving large blank areas.

limitations: The dock icon change after the click may be a timed swap rather than a response to the click; the side icons cycle on their own.
Buttons read 'download for Linux' because the headless browser reports Linux; other platforms will see a different label.
The empty demo panels in the 390 full-page capture may fill in on a real phone after lazy loading; not verified.
The measurement record's hero height (8,584px) and the drop from 10 to 4 sections at 390 were not explained by what I saw.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: mmm.page
summary: The homepage is itself an editable mmm page: visitors tap EDIT and get the real tool palette over a maximalist collage, with no sign-up first.

observations.hero: A persistent left sidebar (an info/LOGIN/SIGN UP pill, Home, Explore, a numbered 'An Internet for People' note, a botanical illustration) frames a white canvas. Centred on it: an oversized 'mmm' wordmark on a yellow-and-pink paint stroke with a pixel cursor, a two-line headline, grey instructions with an inline 'EDIT' chip, and two full-width buttons, purple 'EXPLORE →' and green 'SIGN UP →'. White 3D clay shapes float at the edges; a teal 'EDIT' button is fixed bottom right.
observations.typography: There is no h1; the measurement record has no h1 values. The wordmark is the largest text, measured 195.4px, family Playfair Display. The headline sets 48px in Lato regular; the measured body sample is 32px/1.3 Lato, measure 41ch. Section labels are 57.6px Playfair Display on ochre paint strokes. Sidebar text uses NationalPark-Variable (in the measured family list) at 14px. Near the end a heavy rounded slab face sets 'Digital Paper' at about 106px. Sizes stay large throughout; contrast comes from pairing a high-contrast serif with a plain sans.
observations.visual_system: White ground with a light grey sidebar. Collage is the system: tilted screenshots of user pages with thick black offset shadows, cut-out stickers (frog, balloon photo, orchid illustration, a psychedelic head), white clay 3D shapes, retro pixel cursors with click sparkles, ochre paint-stroke highlights, a purple scribble underline, and dotted vertical lines linking sections. Buttons are saturated purple and mint. The closing scene is a grass field with a painted seated figure and tilted email, Discord and Twitter tiles.
observations.page_sequence: Hero → dotted line → 'Join 100,000+ people in making fun websites' ringed by tilted user-page cards → 'Add Anything' collage → 'Works Everywhere' (one user page in a wide and a narrow window) → 'Messy Encouraged' → 'Free Forever' → 'Long term vision' arrow to 'Digital Paper' (with a 'click me' burst) → contact tiles on grass with 'Sorry, minimalism'. The page scrolls inside a container to the right of the sidebar, not the document.
observations.copy: No h1. Headline 'Dead simple, drag & drop websites for anything'. Subhead: websites 'don't have to be so cookie cutter', then an instruction to tap EDIT and 'tap anything on this page'. Two equal buttons, 'EXPLORE →' and 'SIGN UP →'. Use cases are named plainly: 'Link-in-bio, portfolios, landing pages, moodboards. Anything you want.' Section labels state positions against the category: 'Messy Encouraged' ('We prefer campy, kitschy, messy, imperfect'), 'Free Forever' ('Otherwise $0/mo'). Title: 'Your Corner of the Internet'.
observations.interaction: Clicked the fixed 'EDIT' button: the page entered edit mode with no login prompt. A vertical tool palette appeared beside the canvas (text, brush, GIF, shapes, image, more, colour palette, collapse arrow), and the EDIT button was replaced by 'ADVANCED', a 'Preview ⌘.' label and an eye button. A follow-up click on the headline did not register in automation. On load the pixel cursors and sparkle changed between frames 1.5 s apart; under reduced motion they still changed, while the one spinner animation the probe counted stopped.
observations.accessibility: The document has no h1 or h2; section titles are styled spans. Eleven visible links (the tilted user-page thumbnails) and the account icon button have no accessible name. White 44px text on the contact tiles measures 2.8:1 (Twitter blue), 3.3:1 (Discord) and 3.9:1 (email red). At 390, 14 of 29 targets are under 44px tall, and 'Sorry, minimalism' is a 13px-tall link. No horizontal overflow.
observations.mobile: The desktop sidebar stays at about 200px wide on a 390 screen, leaving about 190px for the canvas. The canvas is not reflowed: the measurement reports the same 195.4px wordmark and 32px body as desktop, and the screen shows the desktop composition scaled down, with instructions and buttons at very small sizes. The fixed EDIT button covers part of the collage. Because the page scrolls in an inner container, the measured document height is only 844px.

principles: Make the homepage a live instance of the product and invite visitors to edit it in place, so trying the product costs one click and no account.
State a stance against the category default in short section labels ('Messy Encouraged', 'Free Forever') and back each with one plain sentence.
For a self-expression product, use many real customer pages, tilted and overlapping, as social proof instead of a logo row.
interpretation.fit: Suits consumer creative tools where personality is the product and the output is a page or canvas visitors can touch. Wrong for B2B buyers who need security, pricing and integration detail, or for any audience that would read the collage as unserious.
interpretation.risks: No heading structure and many unnamed image links leave screen-reader users little to navigate. Scrolling inside an inner container breaks standard scroll measurement and can confuse keyboard and assistive scrolling. The phone layout keeps the desktop sidebar and shrinks the canvas into a narrow column, so copy becomes hard to read. Two equal-weight buttons leave the primary action unclear.

limitations: The measurement record's page height (900px) and section count (0) reflect only the viewport, because content scrolls in an inner container; the live container was 5,435px tall.
Only the EDIT click was verified; selecting and editing an element on the page did not register in automation, and I did not check whether edits persist.
Whether the moving cursor graphics are animated images or scripted could not be determined.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Whimsical
archetype_note: Closer to a screenshot-led product tour of one tool's modes, framed in painted scenes, than a multi-buyer platform.
summary: A dense, real board screenshot is framed inside a soft painted landscape under a plain category headline, then each product mode gets its own section.

observations.hero: A floating white pill nav (logo; Product, Resources, Pricing, Download; Contact sales, Log in, a dark 'Sign up') sits above a large rounded card filled with a grainy painted landscape: lilac sky, coral sun, deep blue hills. Centred in it are a two-line white headline, a two-line subhead and a dark 'Get started free' button with an arrow tile. A real board screenshot ('Implementation planning' with a flowchart, mind map and sticky notes) rises from about y=595 and is cut by the fold.
observations.typography: Display measured family Agrandir, a wide heavy grotesque: the visible headline is 64px (display_px), weight 700, tracking -0.64px, line-height 1.1 in a live probe. The measurement record's desktop h1 entry is empty (32px Manrope 700), so it did not capture the visible headline. Section h2s are 48px with gradient fills; the closing h2 is 96px. Body 16px/1.4, measured family Manrope, hero measure 55ch. At 390 the h1 measures 48px Agrandir, line-height 1.1, tracking -0.005em.
observations.visual_system: Light grey ground (computed p3 0.97) with large rounded-corner panels. The signature image is a soft, grainy painted landscape, reused in the hero, behind product shots and in the closing card. Text and buttons are dark aubergine; display words take purple-to-magenta or blue-to-coral gradients. Feature tiles float UI fragments (keyboard keys, comment threads, a version slider, cursor tags 'Marketing', 'Design', 'Engineering') over blurred colour blobs. Product cards are white with simple line previews.
observations.page_sequence: Hero card with board screenshot and a scrolling customer-logo row → scroll-filled statement 'Capture and share your ideas at the speed of thought' → 'Diagrams' (image left, text right) → 'Wireframes' (text left, image right) → 'Features / The essentials, done right', six tiles and 'Get started free' → 'An infinite canvas to capture all your ideas', five product cards (Diagrams, Flowcharts, Mind maps, Whimsical AI, Wireframes) → closing landscape card 'It's time to work differently.' with the footer set inside it.
observations.copy: h1: 'The whiteboard for product builders'. The subhead names three jobs: design and document implementation with diagrams, shape UI with wireframes, collaborate with your team and AI. Primary button 'Get started free'; nav button 'Sign up'. The h1 names the category ('whiteboard') and audience ('product builders'); feature art tags marketing, design and engineering. Section copy is short and benefit-led ('Built for speed', 'Multiplayer editing'), and the page closes on 'It's time to work differently.'
observations.interaction: Clicked the 'Product' nav button: a mega panel opened listing Tools (Boards, Mind maps, Diagrams, Wireframes, Flowcharts, Integrations) and Artificial Intelligence (AI Flowcharts, AI Wireframes, AI Mind Maps) with a release-note line; it stayed open after Escape and while scrolling. The logo row at the bottom of the hero card scrolls sideways continuously, and the statement fills word by word from pale to purple as it passes through the viewport. Under reduced motion both still happened.
observations.accessibility: The Product button exposes no aria-expanded state before or after opening. The footer logo link has no accessible name. White subhead text over the pale lilac part of the hero reads low-contrast by eye; the probe could not compute contrast over the image. Unfilled statement words are very pale on grey. At 390 the nav buttons are 48px tall and 'Open navigation' is 48×48; 39 of 51 targets are under 44px tall, footer legal links 20px. No horizontal overflow.
observations.mobile: The pill nav keeps logo, Log in, Sign up and a hamburger. The headline sets 48px over four centred lines, with the subhead and a larger 'Get started free' (56px tall) below; the board screenshot is cropped at the right edge. Diagrams and Wireframes stack text above a rounded image that bleeds off the right. Feature tiles become one column. Page height grows from 7,667px to 11,895px; five sections at both widths.

principles: Set a dense, real product screenshot inside a soft painted scene so a busy canvas reads calm without being simplified.
Name the category and the audience in the headline and use the subhead for the three main jobs the product does.
Give each product mode its own alternating section with a large cropped screenshot before summarising features in a grid.
interpretation.fit: Suits visual collaboration tools with several modes whose screens already look good. Wrong for products whose UI is plain tables or text, where a painted backdrop sets expectations the product cannot meet.
interpretation.risks: Static screenshots do all the explaining; nothing on the page lets a visitor try the canvas. The scroll-filled statement and gradient headings lose legibility while unfilled. Motion ignores the reduced-motion preference. The Product menu has no expanded state, and the hero's white subhead depends on the image behind it for contrast.

limitations: The measurement record's desktop h1 (empty, 32px Manrope) and hero height (0px) disagree with the visible 64px headline; typography values for the headline come from a live probe.
The mega panel did not close on Escape in automation; whether it closes on pointer-out for a real mouse was not checked.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Deel
summary: A task-picker hero ('What would you like to do with Deel?') sits beside a photo with payroll UI, then six product cards map the platform.

observations.hero: A black offer bar ('Get 3 months free of PEO*', 'Claim offer') and a white nav sit above two rounded panels. Left: an indigo-to-violet gradient card with a three-line white headline, the question 'What would you like to do with Deel?' and five checkbox tiles (Hire anywhere, Run payroll, Secure visas, Manage HR & people, Ship equipment), then 'Book a demo', review scores and a customer quote. Right: a photo of a person at a laptop overlaid with product cards (a payroll total, currency, visa and worker-type chips).
observations.typography: h1 measured 60px, weight 500, line-height 1.1, tracking -0.003em, measured family BagossCondensedFont; section h2s are 44px/500 and card h3s 24px in the same condensed face. Stats ('150+', '$20B+') are 64px weight 600 in BagossExtendedFont, a wide cut of the family. Body and UI text 18px/1.5, measured family Inter, hero measure 30ch. Small uppercase eyebrows label sections ('WHAT DEEL DOES', 'DEEL SPEED'). Phone h1 38px.
observations.visual_system: White ground. The hero pairs a saturated indigo-violet gradient panel with a warm photo; elsewhere colour is restrained: warm off-white product cards, near-black bands for the 'modern experience' and review sections, black pill buttons, and lavender for selected states and the expert-call pill. Product cards carry miniature, job-specific UI (flags and avatars for payroll, a shipping timeline for IT, benefit chips, a visa status card). Customer logos are grey.
observations.page_sequence: Offer bar + nav → split hero (intent tiles | photo with UI) → 'Speak with a trusted expert' pill and 'Trusted by 40,000+ companies' two-row logo marquee → 'The global people platform', six product cards → 'Accomplish more in less time' with a product toggle (Payroll, HR, IT, Hire) and a Today / Hours later / Tomorrow timeline → dark 'One modern experience for today's workforce' → 'Our customer reviews' video carousel → stats band → dark G2 reviews carousel ('Excellent global payroll', 4.7/5) → footer.
observations.copy: h1: 'Hire, manage, pay, & equip anyone, anywhere.' There is no subhead; the question 'What would you like to do with Deel?' takes its place above five task tiles. Primary button 'Book a demo' (hero and header); 'Claim offer' in the bar. The category is named in the first h2, 'The global people platform', and in the title ('Global Payroll, Compliance, HR Solutions | HRIS'). Proof is numeric and repeated: '40,000+ companies', '150+ countries', '$20B+ compliantly processed global payroll', review counts.
observations.interaction: Ticked the 'Run payroll' tile: its aria-checked changed from false to true, and the tile filled lavender with a check mark; the other tiles, the 'Book a demo' button and the URL did not change. In the same interval the hero quote switched from a Robinhood quote to a Hugging Face quote. The two-row logo marquee scrolls continuously and kept moving under reduced motion. The offer bar and nav stayed pinned while scrolling. No other motion seen.
observations.accessibility: Hero tiles are buttons with role checkbox, an aria-label and aria-checked. A Cookiebot banner covered the bottom 176px of the 1440 first screen and roughly the lower 240px at 390. Grey quote attribution measures 3.6:1. At 390 the hero tiles are 73–106px tall, the menu button 40×40 and the offer-bar close 24×24; 85 of 124 targets are under 44px tall, footer legal links 20px. No horizontal overflow.
observations.mobile: The offer bar wraps, with 'Claim offer' on its own line. The header keeps logo, 'Book a demo' and a hamburger. The gradient card holds a centred 38px headline, the question and the same two-then-three tile grid; the cookie banner covered the rest of the first screen. Product cards, the timeline and the dark sections stack to one column, and the footer lists every link group in full. Page height grows from 7,787px to 10,540px.

principles: Replace the subhead with a multi-select 'what do you need?' question so the first click segments visitors before the demo request.
Give every product card a miniature UI fragment specific to its job (pay statuses, shipping steps, visa state) instead of a generic icon.
Turn speed claims into a three-step Today / Hours later / Tomorrow timeline for each product.
interpretation.fit: Suits broad B2B suites sold to operations or HR buyers who arrive with one job in mind and convert through a sales demo. Wrong for a single-purpose self-serve tool, where task tiles that all lead to the same demo button add a step with no payoff.
