interpretation.risks: Ticking a tile changed nothing else on the page, so the visitor sees no result from the selection. The offer bar, cookie banner, rotating quote and marquee all compete with the hero. The marquee ignores reduced motion. Repeated numeric claims and two separate review sections lengthen the page without adding product detail.

limitations: The right hero panel showed a different photo and overlay on another load (a 'Pay run · May 2026' list instead of a payroll total); whether it rotates or varies per visit was not determined.
Whether the quote change was triggered by the tile click or by an automatic rotation could not be separated.
The cookie banner was left in place to avoid setting consent; parts of both first screens were inspected only through the DOM.
Whether the tile selection is passed to the demo form was not checked, since that would mean submitting it.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Vanta
summary: A light serif 'Get your compliance together' over lilac, an email-to-demo field and a llama mascot, with an agent demo that walks through the compliance steps.

observations.hero: Under a white nav and a dark purple event banner ('Don't tackle AI risk alone. Join us at VantaCon'), a lilac field holds a centred three-line serif headline, a two-line serif subhead and an inline email field with a purple 'Get a demo' button. A line-drawn llama wearing framework medals (HIPAA, GDPR, SOC 2, ISO) stands at the right. A product frame begins at the fold, and a customer logo strip runs along the bottom edge of the viewport.
observations.typography: h1 measured 88px, weight 300, line-height 1 (computed 83.6px), tracking 0, measured family SC Ripley, a light serif; the subhead is the same serif (the record's 30px/1.3 body sample, 41ch). Section h2s are 56px weight 400 and the closing 'The new standard for trust' 96px weight 300 in that serif. Product card titles (24px weight 500) and paragraph copy are sans; the probe gave the card titles the other measured family, Soehne. Eyebrows are small uppercase sans ('GET COMPLIANT'). Phone h1 48px.
observations.visual_system: White and warm off-white grounds alternate with lilac fields and a dark navy band ('Built for you', proof portraits); the footer is deep aubergine. One violet accent for pill buttons with a circled arrow. A line-drawn llama mascot in aubergine and white recurs in the hero, the three audience cards (couch, doorway, window ledge) and the closing tightrope scene. Product proof is light UI: agent chat, framework progress cards, a risk heat map, a vendor table, a trust-center page. Customer portraits are photographic.
observations.page_sequence: Nav + event banner → lilac hero with email capture, llama and agent product frame → '16,000+ customers' logos → 'It's all here', six product cards (Compliance, Risk, Third Party Risk, Audit, Trust Center, Questionnaire Automation) → 'The Vanta Agent: your 24/7 GRC engineering team' → GitHub quote in large serif → frameworks carousel (8) → navy 'Built for you' (Startups, Mid-market, Enterprise) → 'Proof? We've got proof.' portraits → Forrester Wave → resources → 'The new standard for trust' CTA → footer with badges.
observations.copy: h1: 'Get your compliance together'. Subhead: 'SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, and 35+ frameworks—automated and continuously monitored.' Primary 'Get a demo', paired with an email field whose placeholder is 'nodrama@llama.com'. The page names its category as the '#1 Agentic Trust Platform' and 'GRC', and its audiences by company stage (Startups, Mid-market, Enterprise) and role ('CISOs and security leaders'). The tone is wry: 'Proof? We've got proof.', a founder 'in need of a SOC 2 yesterday'.
observations.interaction: Clicked the next arrow on 'All the frameworks you need': the eight cards shifted one position left (SOC 2 left, 'NIST AI RMF / Manage AI risk' entered) and a live region read 'Slide 2 of 8.'; the previous arrow stayed enabled. On load the hero frame cycles an agent run: 'Thinking… Connecting AWS…', then 'Connected', a remediation card ('RDS snapshots are not encrypted', 'Generate fix'), as the ISO 42001 progress bar and checklist advance. It kept cycling under reduced motion. Resource cards faded in on scroll. The nav stayed pinned.
observations.accessibility: The hero email field has only a placeholder, no label. An Osano consent dialog covered the lower-left of the 1440 first screen, including part of the product frame. Nav dropdowns and the phone menu are div elements with role button and aria-expanded. The probe found no text under 4.5:1. At 390 the menu target is 40×48; 86 of 101 targets are under 44px tall, one under 24px. No horizontal overflow.
observations.mobile: The header reduces to logo and hamburger; Log in and Get a demo leave the header. The event banner wraps. The hero centres a 48px three-line headline, the serif subhead and the email-plus-button pill, then the product frame shrunk to full width with unreadably small text, then the llama. Logos become a two-column grid; product cards stack with their UI. Page height grows from 10,276px to 14,637px; eight sections at both widths.

principles: Put the standards buyers must satisfy (SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA) in the subhead, since that is how they search and qualify vendors.
Animate the actual workflow in the hero (connect tools, find a failing test, fix it, progress toward audit) so the outcome promise has visible steps.
Soften a fear-driven category with a light serif headline and one recurring mascot, while keeping product UI as the proof in every section.
Segment by company stage in one row of cards rather than separate hero variants.
interpretation.fit: Suits compliance, security and risk products sold to both founders and security leaders, where reassurance and evidence must coexist. Wrong for a developer-first infrastructure tool, where a mascot and wry copy can read as unserious next to code.
interpretation.risks: The hero's agent demo is small, partly behind the consent dialog and the fold, and illegible on phones. It keeps cycling under reduced motion. The page is long (eight measured sections plus analyst report, resources and closing CTA) and repeats logo rows and proof blocks. The email field lacks a label.

limitations: The measurement record lists sticky_nav false and a 1,519px nav height, but the nav stayed pinned in every scroll capture; the nav metrics look unreliable for this page.
The measurement record reports a reduced-motion rule as observed, yet the hero demo still cycled with reduced motion set; which animations the rule covers was not determined.
The consent dialog was left in place to avoid setting consent.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Webflow
summary: A generic headline is offset by an inline role selector that swaps the proof cards, so marketing, design, engineering and agency buyers each see their own reasons.

observations.hero: A blue announcement bar ('The biggest announcements from Webflow Conf '26') sits above a white nav with a blue 'Start for free'. The hero is left-aligned: a one-line 80px headline, a two-line subhead and two buttons, blue 'Get started' and grey 'Talk to Sales'. At the right, a sentence with an inline dropdown reads 'What [marketing teams] love about Webflow'. Below, a row of image cards (product UI scenes and customer stat cards) drifts sideways, cropped at both edges.
observations.typography: h1 measured 80px, weight 600, line-height 1 (computed 83.2px), tracking -0.01em, measured family WF Visual Sans Variable, the only family on the page. Section h2s are 56px/600; card and footer headings 20px/500; '#MadeinWebflow' is a second 80px h1. Body 16px/1.6, measure 49ch. With one grotesque family and tight tracking, hierarchy is carried by size alone. Phone h1 46.3px.
observations.visual_system: White ground with thin grey rules; a saturated blue for primary buttons, links and the announcement bar; light grey secondary buttons. Imagery is mostly real: dark product UI (agent sessions beside a site preview), customer portrait videos with white stats, a builder screenshot of a Dyson product page, and a skewed collage of customer websites. A fixed 'Made in Webflow' badge sits bottom right.
observations.page_sequence: Announcement bar → hero with audience selector → drifting card row → 16-logo grid → 'Introducing Source by Webflow' with a large agent-and-preview product frame and 'Watch launch video' → 'Where modern teams and agents run the web' with four capability lines → '300,000+ brands move the needle with Webflow' customer video carousel → 'Turn your website into a growth engine' contact-sales form beside a builder screenshot → 'Recent updates' (three cards) → '#MadeinWebflow' skewed site collage → footer.
observations.copy: h1: 'Build for what's next'. Subhead: Webflow gives every team the tools to build, manage and grow a website that drives real revenue. Primary 'Get started'; header 'Start for free'; secondary 'Talk to Sales' and 'Contact Sales'. The title names the category, 'The agentic web platform for modern businesses'. The visitor chooses the audience: marketing, design or engineering teams, or agencies. Proof is outcome numbers ('$200M in new pipeline', '20% increase in site-wide conversion') and '300,000+ brands'.
observations.interaction: Opened the 'What ___ love about Webflow' dropdown (Marketing teams, Design teams, Engineering teams, Agencies) and chose Design teams: the inline label changed to 'design teams', its aria-label to 'Designer, selected item 2 of 4', and the card row swapped to design cards (GSAP interactions, AI handling repetitive work, Shared Libraries) plus an Amazon '49.5% reduction in development time' card. The card row drifts left continuously, also under reduced motion. Six story videos stayed paused. The nav stayed pinned after the bar scrolled away.
observations.accessibility: A 'SKIP TO MAIN CONTENT' link is present. The page has two h1 elements. A cookie dialog covered the lower-left of the 1440 first screen, over the card row. White stat and quote text sits on photos and video stills; contrast could not be computed there. At 390 the menu is a 36×38 div with role button; 99 of 150 targets are under 44px tall and nine under 24px (customer name links 22px, 'Talk to sales →' 19px). No horizontal overflow.
observations.mobile: The announcement bar wraps to two lines; the header keeps logo, 'Contact Sales' and a hamburger. The hero centres a two-line 46px headline, the subhead and both buttons side by side, then the audience sentence, then the drifting card row cropped at both edges. Customer stories become a one-card carousel with arrows, and the contact form stacks its six fields in one column. Page height grows from 7,577px to 9,403px.

principles: Let visitors pick their role in a sentence-shaped selector ('What [design teams] love about…') and swap the proof cards beneath it, so one hero serves several buyers.
Back each customer story with one outcome number set larger than the quote.
When the product's output is visual, close with a collage of real customer work instead of another logo row.
interpretation.fit: Suits mature platforms with several buyer roles and both self-serve and sales paths. Wrong for an early product with one buyer and few customers, where a role selector, logo grid and contact form would expose thin proof.
interpretation.risks: The h1 'Build for what's next' says nothing about websites; the category lives in the subhead and the page title. Continuous drift in the card row ignores reduced motion and makes the cards hard to read. Several conversion paths (Get started, Start for free, Talk to Sales, Contact Sales, the form) compete. The page carries two h1s.

limitations: The cookie dialog was left in place to avoid setting consent.
Customer story videos did not load or play in headless Chromium.
The measurement record lists sticky_nav false and a 0px mobile nav height, but the nav stayed pinned while scrolling at 1440 and a header was visible at 390.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Daylight
summary: One device lying on grass carries the page: a pinned hero turns from day to amber night on scroll, and a 'de-invented' manifesto sells focus over specs.

observations.hero: A rounded full-bleed card holds a photo-real overhead scene: a pale tablet showing a botanical engraving lies on grass among leaves. Top left: white serif h1 and a two-line subhead; bottom left: an amber-framed video thumbnail with a play triangle. Top right: a grey nav cluster (Home, Product, FAQ, orange ORDER NOW) with a 'Meet Daylight Kids' card and round 'Limited daylight KIDS bundle' badge; bottom right: a Newsletter card, 'IN STOCK · SHIPS IN 3-5 BUSINESS DAYS' and a wide orange ORDER NOW.
observations.typography: Measured h1 60px, weight 300, tracking -0.07em, line-height 1.0, family __abcArizonaFlareFont (a light serif); 40px at 390. Section headings repeat the light serif at 55-65px, weight 300, with single words in italic ('Daylight', 'paper-like', 'computer', 'outside'). Body 18px/1.1 in measured family __abcRoomFont (a sans), measure 45ch; small uppercase labels ('GET UPDATES · NO SPAM') carry metadata. A third measured family, __abcRoomExtendedFont, is in the families list.
observations.visual_system: Warm off-white ground (rgb 250,245,242) with a diagonal window-blind shadow over the light sections. Saturated orange is reserved for ORDER NOW and accents. Imagery is warm lifestyle photography (hands, grass, sky, backpack) and device close-ups. Chapter grounds shift: off-white, sky blue for outdoor use, amber/peach then black for night use, ending on an orange-gradient footer with a giant orange 'daylight' wordmark. Rounded cards, line icons and a dotted sunburst motif.
observations.page_sequence: Pinned hero → manifesto line 'We refuse to accept a future…' → 'Introducing Daylight' → full-bleed 'The world's first full-speed paper-like display' + three benefits → sideways stretch: Reading / Note-taking / Writing photos, 'With all the apps you need' icon grid, lifestyle photo, sunburst vision statement → 'it's a computer you can use outside' → amber 'When the lights go off…' → black 'Goodbye, blue light' → 'Dive deeper' tiles → testimonials → press logos → founder letter → 'DC-1 at a glance' → wordmark, ORDER NOW, footer.
observations.copy: H1: 'The computer, de-invented'. Subhead: 'Meet DC-1. A new kind of computer, designed for deep focus and wellbeing.' Primary button 'ORDER NOW' (nav, hero, footer). The category is named by negation ('de-invented'; 'We refuse to accept a future where our devices are exhausting, addictive, and distracting') and by benefits (paper-like display, amber glow, no blue light). The audience is implied as people seeking focus and health; families are addressed through 'Daylight Kids'.
observations.interaction: Clicked the hero 'Play video' thumbnail: a dark full-card player with native controls and a close × replaced the hero; it stayed at 0:00 because the video did not load in this browser. On load the Kids card slid down from under the nav. Scrolling the pinned hero turned the scene to night with an amber device screen; manifesto words revealed progressively; a mid-page stretch moved panels sideways. Reduced motion: no running animations, manifesto text shown whole, window shadow absent; the Kids card still slid down.
observations.accessibility: No horizontal overflow at either width. Two h1 elements (hero and the paper-like display chapter). Three email inputs are labelled only by the placeholder 'E-MAIL'. White hero text sits on the photo scene without a scrim. The Newsletter card stays pinned bottom right on every desktop screen. At 390, 17 of 23 visible targets were under 44px tall: menu toggle 28×28 (labelled 'Toggle menu'), nav ORDER NOW 34px, footer links 16px, social icons 22px.
observations.mobile: The hero stays one full-height card (measured 844px versus 1,800px pinned on desktop): h1 breaks to two lines at 40px, nav collapses to ORDER NOW plus a menu icon, the video thumbnail shrinks to the bottom left and the Newsletter card overlaps it; the Kids card drops below the hero. Reading / Note-taking / Writing photos stack vertically, the app grid becomes a centred 3×3, and benefits become icon rows. Page height 19,840px.

principles: Let one physical object carry the hero and change its state on scroll (day to night, white to amber) so the product's signature mode is demonstrated rather than listed.
When the product's value is what it leaves out, name the category by negating the incumbent ('de-invented', a 'we refuse' manifesto) before naming features.
Repeat one purchase action in fixed positions (nav, hero, footer) so a long narrative page never strands a ready buyer.
Tie each chapter's ground colour to the benefit it describes, such as sky blue for outdoor reading and amber then black for night use.
interpretation.fit: Suits consumer hardware and wellbeing products bought on feeling and daily ritual; wrong for B2B tools whose buyers need specs, integrations and pricing within the first screens.
interpretation.risks: 18,848px of pinned and sideways scroll, canvas scenes and word-by-word reveals make content depend on scroll position (the desktop full-page capture is blank below the hero). The first screen stacks four overlays (nav, Kids card, newsletter, order bar) around the product. Specs are deferred to other pages, and two h1s blur the outline.

limitations: The hero player and the display-chapter video stayed at readyState 0 in headless Chromium, so their content was not seen.
The desktop full-page capture was blank below the hero; the desktop sequence comes from slow-scroll live captures.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Opal Electronics
summary: The homepage is one dated letter set in a narrow column over an overhead photograph of the company's prototype table, with no menu, buttons or product listing.

observations.hero: No conventional hero. The first screen is an overhead photograph of a concrete table crowded with cameras, circuit boards, chrome parts and coloured prototypes, with a narrow centred white text column on top: bold 'the table', the date 'June 1, 2026', then the opening paragraphs of a letter. Only a small two-line 'opal electronics' wordmark sits top left; there is no navigation menu and no button.
observations.typography: No h1. The title 'the table' is an h2 measured at 48.9px, weight 700, in the single measured family Die Grotesk C (a grotesque sans). Measured display sample 21px; body 16px/1.5 at 1440 and 14.6px/1.1 at 390, same family. Paragraphs are ragged right in a column about 360px wide in the desktop capture, white on the photograph; the sign-off 'See you soon.' is yellow.
observations.visual_system: Black ground under one long overhead photograph that runs the length of the letter and fades to black at its end. Colour comes only from the photographed objects (yellow, red, teal, chrome). Below the letter, a giant 'opal' wordmark drawn in grey dots on a canvas fills the width, then a minimal black footer. A faint full-page grain overlay (opacity 0.04) sits over everything.
observations.page_sequence: Wordmark + title and date → letter over the table photograph (company history, the target customer, an investment announcement, three wishes) → 'See you soon.' → dotted 'opal' wordmark canvas → footer (Support, Terms, Privacy, Jobs, Contact, 'All rights reserved').
observations.copy: No h1; title 'the table', dated 'June 1, 2026'. The letter opens 'In our office, there is a table.' and describes the company's webcams, its customer ('the golden decile: the ten percent of people who want something of extreme difference'), an investment announcement and three wishes. No primary button; the only links are the footer and the wordmark. The category is named in the text as 'top electronics for demanding customers'.
observations.interaction: The page has no tabs, buttons or toggles; the one operable surface is the dotted wordmark canvas, which sets a crosshair cursor. Brighter patches of dots drifted across the letters while idle; after sweeping the pointer across it, lit patches covered more of 'pal', but the idle drift prevents attributing that to the pointer. Nothing else moved on load or scroll apart from the grain overlay. With reduced motion the grain overlay's animation still ran (frame-to-frame pixel changes up to 10/255).
observations.accessibility: No h1 and no main landmark; the logo link has no text or label. White body text sits on a busy photograph without a scrim; at 390 several paragraphs overlap objects (for example the investors paragraph over dark glass shapes). At 390 the five footer links are 21px tall. No horizontal overflow at either width.
observations.mobile: The photograph is recomposed, not just cropped: at 390 'the table' sits large on two lines beside a stack of cameras, and the letter breaks into blocks that alternate left and right around individual objects. The dotted-wordmark area rendered as black space in the 390 full-page capture, and footer links stack vertically. Page height 3,176px versus 3,656px on desktop.

principles: When there is little product to show yet, publish one dated letter as the homepage and let the voice and the taste of its imagery do the selling.
Use a single photograph of real artefacts as the page ground so the body of work is visible without product cards.
Drop navigation and calls to action entirely when the page's job is announcement and recall rather than conversion.
Art-direct the mobile version separately, moving text blocks around objects instead of shrinking the desktop composition.
interpretation.fit: Suits design-led hardware companies at an announcement or stealth stage with a strong founder voice; wrong for any product that needs sign-ups, pricing comparison or self-serve onboarding.
interpretation.risks: No path to buy, sign up or learn product details; no h1, main landmark or named logo link; long white text over a busy photo strains legibility, worse at 390 where text overlaps objects; a dated letter goes stale; the grain overlay ignores reduced motion.

limitations: Whether the dotted canvas responds to the pointer could not be separated from its idle motion.
Reduced motion was checked at the top and mid-letter; the canvas was not re-checked under reduced motion.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Phantom
category: Fintech (self-custodial crypto wallet and trading app)
summary: A consumer-app page built from three chapters (trade, move money, stay secure), each a headline with the ghost mascot set inline and a one-sentence card carousel.

observations.hero: A lavender page with a floating white nav pill (Features, Learn, Explore, Company, Developers, Support), a round search button and a lavender 'Download' pill. Below, a large rounded panel holds centred white text: eyebrow 'Where the world trades', a three-line h1 and a pale 'Download Phantom' pill with a phone icon. The panel is a video element that never loaded here and rendered flat grey. A cookie banner covers the lower right.
observations.typography: Single measured family 'Phantom' (a rounded geometric sans) for everything. Measured h1 80px, weight 400, tracking -0.025em, line-height 1.1; 29.3px at 390. Section h2s are larger than the h1, 96px (measured display_px), also weight 400. Body 20px/1.4, 16px at 390; card statements about 30px. Hierarchy comes from size alone; no bold weights seen. Legal disclosures near the footer are small italic.
observations.visual_system: Lavender ground (rgb 245,242,255) with rounded cards in lavender, near-black, grey, blue, aubergine, cream, yellow and pink. The purple ghost mascot is set inline inside headlines as a glyph ('for [ghost] everyone', 'secured [ghost] by us', 'Download [ghost] Phantom.'). In live scrolling the ground changed per chapter: lavender, then dark aubergine for Move Money and Security, then lilac for the closing CTA and footer. Security cards carry flat illustrations (chat bubbles, a transaction warning).
observations.page_sequence: Hero panel → 'Trading tools for everyone' + See more → Trading carousel (buy/sell, trending tokens, prediction markets, perps, Terminal) → 'Spend, Send, & Save' → Move Money cards → 'Controlled by you, secured by us' → Your security cards (self-custody, 24/7 support, scam detection) → 'Trusted by a community of 20+ million users' → 'Get started. Download Phantom.' → card legal disclosures → footer with large email field and link columns.
observations.copy: H1: 'Your home for trading crypto, predictions, perps, and more'. Eyebrow 'Where the world trades'; no subhead paragraph. Primary button 'Download Phantom'. The category is named directly as trading crypto, predictions and perps; the audience is 'everyone'. Proof is one number: 'Trusted by a community of 20+ million users. It's more than a wallet.' Cards hold one sentence each, e.g. 'Self-custodial means you control your funds. We never have access.'
observations.interaction: Clicked 'Next slide' on the Trading carousel: the row shifted one card, so 'Buy and sell all types of crypto in an instant.' left the view and 'Go long, go short, go anywhere with Perps.' entered at the right. Scrolling changed the page ground colour per chapter. No CSS animations ran on load or scroll and every video stayed unloaded, so media motion was not seen. Reduced motion: no running animations and identical frames, the same as the default load here.
observations.accessibility: No horizontal overflow. The h1 is near-white (rgb 255,253,248); with the hero video unloaded it sat on mid-grey at low contrast. Footer column labels measured 3.6:1 at 16px; white 30px card text on blue 3.42:1. The newsletter email field has no label beyond its placeholder. At 390, 34 of 56 visible targets were under 44px tall, with footer links 16px tall. The cookie banner covers part of the first screen at both widths.
observations.mobile: The nav reduces to the ghost logo, a 'Download' pill and a 47px round menu button. The hero keeps its rounded panel with the h1 on three lines at 29.3px. Each carousel shows one full-width card with the next one peeking at the right edge, arrows above the row. Footer link columns become a two-column grid. Page height 7,228px versus 8,075px on desktop.

principles: Set the mascot inside the headline as a glyph so brand character recurs in every chapter without separate illustration.
Organise a broad app into three verb-led chapters (trade, move money, stay secure), each a headline plus a swipeable row of one-sentence cards.
Change the page ground colour per chapter to mark topic shifts without dividers.
Give trust a single plain number ('20+ million users') right before the final download call.
interpretation.fit: Suits consumer finance and multi-feature mobile apps with a strong brand character; wrong for institutional or compliance-heavy products, where a cartoon mascot and one-line claims undercut seriousness.
interpretation.risks: Nearly every proof surface is video, so when media fails the hero becomes a grey block with low-contrast white text and the cards become empty colour slabs. Section h2s outsize the h1, flattening the outline. One-sentence cards trade depth for brevity, and fees and risk appear only in small italic legal text near the footer.

limitations: All videos stayed at readyState 0 in headless Chromium; hero and card media were not seen.
Reduced-motion behaviour could not be told apart because nothing moved in the default load in this browser either.
In the 390 full-page capture the chapter h2s were missing (scroll-dependent rendering); mobile chapter headings were not verified.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Clay
summary: A handmade claymation toy world brands the page, and each product chapter gets its own colour, 3D object and named customer result, with use-case tabs swapping product mocks.

observations.hero: The upper two-thirds is a full-bleed claymation-style scene of green hills, trees and toy machinery (funnel, magnifier, seesaw, coiled tube, block bar chart, mailbox) with coloured balls. A lower dark-green band holds a large white two-line h1 at left; at right a three-line subhead, a white 'Start free trial' button, a lime 'Get a demo' button and 'or install directly with' three AI-app icons. A floating white nav has ⌘K search, Log in, Get a demo and a black Start free trial.
observations.typography: Single measured family Roobertvf (a variable grotesque sans). Measured h1 88px, weight 575, tracking -0.04em, line-height 1.0; 41.6px at 390. The section h2 is 72px and chapter headings 48px, weight 500, with each heading's second line in that chapter's accent colour (blue, rust, olive, magenta, teal). Measured body sample 12px/1.3, measure 30ch; uppercase letter-spaced pill labels (DATA, AGENTS, ORCHESTRATION, ACTIVATION) open each chapter.
observations.visual_system: After the dark-green hero the ground is white and warm grey. Each product chapter is a rounded panel tinted light blue, peach, pale lime or pink, with a matching saturated accent on the label pill, heading line and button, beside a 3D clay object on a sand-coloured stage; the infrastructure panel assembles all the objects together. Product evidence is light spreadsheet-style tables with side panels. The footer sits on a ball-pit illustration.
observations.page_sequence: Hero → customer grid (logos, quotes, stats such as '80%+ enrichment coverage') → 'GTM engineers build on Clay' use-case tabs + product mock → 'What do you want to build?' prompt box with three chips → Data, Agents, Orchestration, Activation chapters → 'Build systems that make reps more productive' → video testimonial carousel → 'Learn more about GTM engineering' content grid → 'Turn your growth ideas into reality today' CTA → link-dense footer.
observations.copy: H1: 'Build systems to grow revenue'. Subhead: 'Infrastructure to get any data, run agentic workflows, and launch GTM plays.' Primary button 'Start free trial'; secondary 'Get a demo'. The audience is named as 'GTM engineers' and the field as 'GTM engineering'. Each chapter carries one named customer result; the named customers differed between loads (e.g. Rippling, Mistral AI, Intercom). The closing CTA adds 'Start for free today. No credit card required.'
observations.interaction: Clicked the 'Lead Scoring' tab: it turned purple and centred in the row, the subhead changed to 'Prioritize the highest-converting leads using real-time intent and engagement signals.', and the mock swapped from a demo-form table with an email preview on lime to a lead-scoring table, 'Lead Score Formula' panel and 'Sample Outputs' on purple. The customer grid drifted left on its own, and the prompt placeholder showed different text across captures. No CSS animations ran; the hero video did not load. With reduced motion the customer grid stayed still.
observations.accessibility: No horizontal overflow. 69 visible images had no alt attribute, and the prompt textarea has no label. Accent heading lines measured 4.08:1 ('visual canvas', olive on pale lime) and 3.57:1 ('reps more productive', teal on grey) at 48px. At 390, 118 of 157 visible targets were under 44px tall (footer links 16px), and several customer-grid links reported only the text 'text'. The cookie banner covers the h1 at 1440.
observations.mobile: The hero scene crops to a band behind the nav and the 41.6px two-line h1 overlaps its lower edge; subhead and the two buttons stack below. The nav reduces to logo, 'Get a demo' and a menu icon. The tab row scrolls sideways above the mock, and the prompt chips stack vertically. Each chapter becomes label, heading, copy, proof and buttons with its 3D image below. The footer becomes two columns over the ball-pit art. Page height 11,352px.

principles: Give each product module its own colour, label pill and physical object, and reuse that colour in its heading, button and proof, so a long platform page reads as distinct chapters.
Make the use-case selector a tab row that swaps both the one-line promise and the product mock, so each buyer sees their own workflow in one click.
Attach one named customer and one number to every chapter instead of relying on a single logo wall.
Carry one illustration language from hero to footer so the brand world doubles as an icon system for modules.
interpretation.fit: Suits multi-module B2B platforms selling to operators who want to see real tables and outcomes; wrong for a single-feature tool, where the chapter apparatus and illustration budget would outweigh the product.
interpretation.risks: The hero spends two-thirds of the first screen on illustration, so the h1 and buttons sit low and the cookie banner covers them. Ten thousand pixels of dense proof grids and chapters ask for a lot of scrolling; images widely lack alt attributes; proof rotating between loads makes the page's claims inconsistent from visit to visit.

limitations: The hero and chapter videos stayed at readyState 0 in headless Chromium; the hero was seen only as a still.
The desktop full-page capture stops at 9,000px of a 10,255px page; the end was seen in live captures.
Customer proof lines differed between loads; the examples recorded are samples.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: FLORA
summary: Generated imagery scattered on a dotted canvas grid is the hero, and the page proves the product with a draggable node graph and one workflow graph per creative discipline.

observations.hero: Black ground with a faint dot grid. A scattered collage of generated fashion and product images (a bag, lips with a 'made in FLORA' mark, red shoes, portraits) floats at the edges around a centred block: h1, one-line subhead, green 'Get started for free' and outlined 'Copy setup prompt' buttons, and 'Works with' four AI-app icons. A greyscale customer logo strip runs along the bottom; a cookie panel overlays the lower middle.
observations.typography: Measured h1 52px, weight 400, tracking -0.04em, line-height 1.2, family Marketing Redaction 10 (a serif), with 'creative' in italic; at 390 that word renders with a visibly pixelated texture. Headings and body use measured family Geist (a sans): h2s about 30px, weight 500; step titles such as '01 Ideate' 60px with grey numerals. Body 20px/1.4, 16px/1.3 at 390. A third family, Marketing Redaction 35, is in the families list.
observations.visual_system: Near-black throughout, with the dotted canvas grid as a recurring motif. Colour comes from generated imagery: fashion photos, product renders, cinematic stills. Product evidence is shown as node graphs: image nodes labelled with model names (Nano, Nano Pro, Veo 3.1, Aleph) joined by thin curves. The use-case chapter puts a muted full-bleed photo behind its graph; model providers appear as photographic tiles with logos. The only accent is green on primary buttons and links.
observations.page_sequence: Hero collage → logo marquee → 'Never let a good idea go unexplored.' 01 Ideate / 02 Iterate / 03 Scale cards → 'Every model. One canvas.' draggable node demo → 'Generative workflows that scale.' scroll-switched discipline list with graph → Techniques → Featured Techniques (six creator cards) → 'One subscription to rule them all.' model-provider grid → case studies → 'Read about us.' press → 'A new medium needs a new canvas.' + footer.
observations.copy: H1: 'Your creative workspace'. Subhead: 'Purpose-built AI tools for every step of your process.' Primary button 'Get started for free'; secondary 'Copy setup prompt'. The audience is creative teams ('Teams from Pentagram to Lionsgate'; 'professionals across film, fashion, branding, and design'), and the category is framed as a canvas over many models: 'One plan. 50+ models.' Use cases are named by discipline: Visual Effects, Fashion, Advertising, Photography, Concepting, Branding, Motion, Architecture.
observations.interaction: Dragged the 'Star Shoe' node in the canvas demo (labelled 'Move Star Shoe node'): it moved 210px right and 180px up, stayed slightly enlarged, and its connector curve re-routed to the Sneaker Showcase node. On load the logo strip scrolled continuously. Scrolling the use-case list highlighted one discipline at a time and swapped the backdrop photo and graph. With reduced motion no animations ran and top and mid-page frames were identical.
observations.accessibility: No horizontal overflow; a 'Skip to content' link is present, and the desktop probe found no unnamed buttons or links and no sampled text under 4.5:1. Inactive discipline names are dimmed grey over the photo. At 390, 70 of 94 visible targets were under 44px tall (technique title links 18px, the footer 'Cookie settings' button 16px); the menu button is 40×40 and labelled 'Menu'. The cookie panel covers the h1 at 390.
observations.mobile: The h1 stays 52px and breaks to three lines, with collage images crowding the edges; the nav reduces to logo and menu. Sections are reordered and retitled: the node demo follows the hero under 'Take your work further.' with nodes stacked vertically; the discipline list becomes stacked cards, each with title, graph and caption; the model grid becomes a sideways card row; the 01/02/03 cards move lower under 'Create at the speed of thought.' Page height 16,306px.

principles: Make the hero a sample of output, a collage of generated work on the product's own grid, so quality is shown before any claim.
Embed a small, real piece of the product's interaction (draggable nodes with live connectors) in the marketing page.
Map use cases to the buyer's disciplines and give each one concrete workflow graph, switched by scroll on desktop and stacked on mobile.
Recompose sections for mobile, including reordering and retitling them, rather than only shrinking the desktop layout.
interpretation.fit: Suits creative and generative tools whose output is visual and whose buyers judge by taste; wrong for data or back-office products where output is not visually persuasive.
interpretation.risks: A long dark page (10,854px) of image-heavy grids; node labels inside the graphs are too small to read at either width; dimmed list items over photos lower legibility; the pixel-textured italic in the 390 h1 trades crispness for style; a wall of third-party model logos dates quickly as providers change.

limitations: Whether media inside the node demo (the Sneaker Showcase output changed between captures) responds to the drag or plays on its own was not determined.
The desktop full-page capture stops at 9,000px of a 10,854px page; the end was seen in live captures.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Sponge
summary: A one-column, light, text-led page that explains agent payments through small inline product demos (a card and chat transcripts) instead of screenshots or motion.

observations.hero: Left-aligned two-line headline on a near-white ground with a pale blue wash at the top; the phrase 'agent economy' is set in bright blue. One short subhead sits below, with no hero button. The first 'Give your agent an account' block starts within the first screen: a dark card mock showing a balance and 'ERIC'S AGENT', beside a chat-bubble demo. Nav has a 'BACKED BY Y' badge, six text links, social icons and a black 'Contact' pill.
observations.typography: Measured h1 72px, weight 500, line-height 1, tracking -0.02em, family Inter; body 18px at 1.6 line-height, measure 64ch, also Inter. A ui-monospace family appears on card details and inline code tags such as 'sponge.transfer'. Mobile h1 drops to 48px, body to 16px. Section headings use the same medium-weight sans at smaller sizes.
observations.visual_system: Off-white ground with a faint blue gradient at the top, black text, one blue accent and a single orange YC badge. Surfaces are white or light-grey rounded cards with thin borders; the product card is the only dark object. No photography, no illustration; imagery is small partner and chain logos. Chat bubbles in grey act as the recurring motif.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → headline + subhead → 'Give your agent an account' (card + chat demo, Launch Wallet) → 'Sell directly to agents' (URL-input demo, Launch Gateway) → three-column integrations row (SDKs, agent tools, chains) → 'Use cases' three cards with code tags and chat demos → FAQ accordion (7 items) → footer.
observations.interaction: Operated the 'What is x402?' FAQ item: the plus became an x, aria-expanded flipped to true and a two-paragraph answer expanded in place; URL unchanged. On load one animation ran in the hero card area; the card balance read $49.00 in the capture and $50.00 on the live visit. After scrolling, three more animations ran on card blocks. With reduced motion the page still showed moving SVG circle transitions and the top screenshot changed over 1.2s.
observations.accessibility: Grey body and caption text on off-white is low-contrast in places (card fine print, footer links, the placeholder URL in the gateway demo). FAQ buttons carry aria-expanded. No horizontal overflow measured at either width. The 'Submit URL' demo button is 32×32 on desktop.
observations.mobile: Nav collapses to logo plus hamburger. Headline wraps to four lines at 48px. Each demo block stacks: copy, button, then the card or chat demo below it. The integrations row becomes three stacked groups; the three use-case cards and FAQ stack full-width. Page height grows from 2592 to 3897px with one measured section.

principles: Show the product as a miniature of itself (a card, a chat exchange, an input) rather than a screenshot, so the demo reads at any width.
Pair every claim with a button that names the artefact it opens (Launch Wallet, Launch Gateway) instead of a generic sign-up.
A single accent colour used once in the headline and nowhere else keeps a text-heavy page from feeling flat without adding imagery.
Put the FAQ on the homepage when the category needs vocabulary explained (x402, MPP) and let it carry the depth the hero omits.
interpretation.fit: Suits developer-facing infrastructure and API products whose value is a protocol or integration surface; wrong for consumer fintech that needs trust cues like faces, security badges or app imagery.
interpretation.risks: No hero CTA and no social proof beyond logos; the reduced-motion rule leaves some elements moving; low-contrast grey captions; the page relies on the reader already knowing what agents and x402 are.

limitations: Could not verify whether the ticking card balance is a looped demo or live data.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: InLoop Robotics
archetype_note: Launch-countdown teaser hero placed above a conventional capabilities, ROI-comparison and demo-video product page.
summary: The first screen withholds the product behind a 14-day countdown drawn inside a loop-shaped stroke, then switches to a light, conventional capabilities-and-ROI page.

observations.hero: Black full-height screen. A large pill-shaped outline (echoing the two linked O's of the INLOOP wordmark) encloses four big numerals labelled days, hours, minutes, seconds; a thick white stroke travels around the pill. Below it the single word 'Loading..'. No headline, no subhead, no hero button. The nav is a floating dark rounded bar with the wordmark, Home, Team and an orange 'Contact' pill.
observations.typography: No h1 was measured at either width. Measured display 72px desktop and 36px mobile, body 14px at 1.6 line-height, measure 54ch desktop and 36ch mobile; the only measured family is Instrument Sans. Countdown numerals are bold and large; section headlines are bold, tight sans; body copy is small grey sans. An orange all-caps eyebrow ('CAPABILITIES') labels sections.
observations.visual_system: Two grounds: black for the hero and the closing CTA/footer, white for everything between. One orange accent for buttons, eyebrows and the active-tab progress bar. Surfaces are light-grey rounded panels and white cards with soft shadows. Imagery is video: a hero video and seven task videos presented as tilted black cards with play buttons scattered across a grey panel.
observations.page_sequence: Floating nav → countdown hero ('Loading..') → 'Run the Full Labor Workflow' accordion of five capabilities beside a video pane → 'Maximum impact. Minimal investment.' two-card comparison (Traditional Automation vs InLoop RaaS, Calculate Your ROI) → 'Take a look around' scattered video cards, Book a Demo → FAQ accordion (4 items) → black 'Ready to automate?' Schedule a Demo → footer.
observations.interaction: Operated the capabilities accordion: it auto-advances (an orange progress bar runs under the active item); clicking 'Prepare Content' collapsed 'Kitting', expanded the new description and reset the bar. The video pane beside it stayed blank grey in the headless browser. On load the countdown ticked and the stroke moved around the pill; FAQ items were blank in the full-page capture but present live after scrolling. With reduced motion the progress bar still animated and the countdown still ticked.
observations.accessibility: The sticky dark nav bar is semi-transparent, so light-page headlines show through behind it when scrolled. Grey body text at 14px on white and grey labels on black (days/hours) are low-contrast. The floating play buttons on video cards are 33×33px. Accordion buttons carry no aria-expanded. No horizontal overflow measured.
observations.mobile: The pill splits into a vertical capsule with days/hours above minutes/seconds; nav collapses to wordmark plus hamburger. The accordion stacks above the video pane; the comparison cards stack; the scattered video cards become a two-up grid of cropped tiles. Page height is 5167px, close to desktop's 5164px.

principles: Make the brand mark do structural work: the loop shape frames the hero so the identity is read before a word is.
An auto-advancing accordion with a visible progress bar tells visitors the list is a tour, not a menu.
A two-card 'old way vs our way' comparison carries the business case without a pricing page.
If the hero is a teaser, put the first real headline within one scroll so the page still explains the product.
interpretation.fit: Suits a pre-launch hardware company courting a demo pipeline through a Contact button; wrong for any product that needs the first screen to state what it is, and for self-serve software.
interpretation.risks: The first screen says nothing about robots or warehouses; a countdown has an expiry after which the hero is stale; videos are the only product evidence and they did not render headlessly; reduced motion is not honoured; the semi-transparent nav collides with content.

limitations: Task and hero videos did not render in headless Chromium, so their content could not be seen.
Could not verify what the countdown resolves to.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Voxel Energy
summary: A full-bleed solar-farm video hero with a bottom-anchored headline, followed by magazine-style sections (claims, a US wait-time map, process, team, newsroom) on alternating grounds.

observations.hero: Edge-to-edge aerial footage of a desert solar array fills the first screen, darkened by an overlay. Content hugs the bottom edge: an orange-outlined 'Backed by Y Combinator' pill, a two-line white headline at bottom-left, and at bottom-right a one-line claim ('builds data centers in months, not years') with a small translucent 'Talk to our team' button. The nav is only the wordmark; no links.
observations.typography: Desktop measured no h1 (the headline is an h2); display 22px and body 16px at 1.3 line-height, measure 29ch, family Geist. Mobile measured h1 51.2px, weight 400, line-height 1, tracking -0.07em, Geist. Families present: Geist, Inter, Fragment Mono, sans-serif; a monospace is used for small all-caps eyebrows ('+ WHAT WE DO', '[01]') and card dates. Headlines are regular-weight, tightly tracked sans.
observations.visual_system: Alternating grounds: dark photo/video, warm off-white, dark photo again, off-white, then a lime-green newsroom band and a sky-blue photo band before a black footer. Imagery is photographic (solar fields, team portraits, article covers). A choropleth US map in a yellow-to-dark-red scale is the one data graphic. Small line icons sit in three claim cards.
observations.page_sequence: Wordmark → video hero → 'What we do' statement + three claim cards → 'Interconnection Wait Times' US map with Grid/Vessel toggle and 'Can you afford to wait for the grid?' → dark 'How we work' three numbered steps over solar imagery → 'Who we are' three founder portraits and bios → lime 'Newsroom' carousel with arrows → sky photo 'Let's get to work' Contact → footer.
observations.interaction: Operated the Newsroom 'Next' arrow: the row slid one card left, the first article moved out and later cards came into view; URL unchanged. On load about 40 span-level animations ran; the mobile capture shows the headline only partly rendered. Nothing was still running after scroll. The hero video element was paused in the headless browser. With reduced motion the same span animations still ran on load; the top screen was static 1.2s later.
observations.accessibility: White headline over bright sunlit panels on mobile has uneven contrast where text crosses light cells. The hero 'Talk to our team' button is translucent grey on dark footage. Carousel arrows are 42×42 and labelled; pagination dots are 10px wide. Eyebrow mono text is very small. No horizontal overflow measured. The nav has no links, so in-page navigation relies on scrolling.
observations.mobile: Headline wraps to four lines and the CTA drops below the fold. Sections reorder: 'How we work' appears before the map on mobile, after it on desktop. Claim cards, process steps, founder cards and news cards all stack to one column; the map keeps its toggle and legend. Page height grows from 6271 to 7070px.

principles: Anchor hero text to the bottom edge so the full-bleed footage reads first and the claim second, without a centred overlay.
Use one data graphic (a map of the problem) to argue urgency instead of a feature list.
Change ground colour at each section boundary so a long editorial page still has rhythm without motion.
Put founder bios on the homepage when the buyer is betting on execution of physical infrastructure.
interpretation.fit: Suits capital-intensive, physical-world companies selling to a few enterprise buyers through conversations; wrong for self-serve software that needs a product screenshot and sign-up above the fold.
interpretation.risks: No nav links and a single quiet CTA; reduced motion is ignored for the load animations; headline contrast depends on the frame of video behind it; the desktop headline is an h2 while mobile has an h1, so the document outline differs by viewport.

limitations: The hero video did not play in headless Chromium, so its motion could not be observed.
The Grid/Vessel map toggle could not be located as an element to operate.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Stilta
summary: A full-screen microscope-footage hero with a centred two-line claim, then a long, quiet enterprise narrative that alternates product panels, proof and a chat-styled FAQ across light and dark grounds.

observations.hero: The whole first screen is blurred microscope footage (a green rod-shaped organism among dark particles) with a white two-line headline centred mid-screen, a one-line proof subhead ('Used on high-stakes patent matters by Fortune 500s and AmLaw 100s'), and a white 'Book a demo' pill beside a translucent 'Log in'. A 'Trusted by 100+ IP teams' logo marquee runs along the bottom edge. A cookie banner covers the lower right. Nav: wordmark, three left links, three right links and a white CTA pill.
observations.typography: Measured h1 60px, weight 500, line-height 1, tracking 0, family Haas Recast Open; display 60px; body 16px at 1.4 line-height. Families present: Haas Recast Open and Haas Recast Dense. Mobile h1 44px, measure 44ch. Section headlines are two-line, medium-weight sans; eyebrows are small plain text ('Product', 'Technology'); on-screen UI mock text and chart labels are much smaller.
observations.visual_system: Warm off-white ground for product sections, a dark blue-to-black gradient panel for the product screen, near-black for 'Built beyond the prompt' and the FAQ, and a blue-grey gradient for the closing CTA and footer. Imagery: hero video, soft grey product-screen mocks under pill tags, a dotted-line pyramid diagram on a faint grid, a telecom-tower photograph, blurred-portrait testimonial cards with client logos (KUKA, Spotify). Rounded pills everywhere: tags, buttons, FAQ bubbles.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → video hero + logo marquee → 'Litigation-grade' three mode cards (Offense/Defense/Strategy) → 'Two modes. One standard of evidence' dark panel with Project/Portfolio tabs and a laptop screen → 'Built to answer the hardest patent questions' pyramid diagram with three callout cards → 'Built for every field of innovation' practice-area list + photo → testimonial slider → dark 'Built beyond the prompt' → chat-styled FAQ with input → 'Bring a patent matter' CTA → footer.
observations.interaction: Operated the '02 Portfolio' tab: aria-selected moved to it, the caption changed from 'Deep analysis for a high-stakes matter' to 'At-scale analysis across portfolios' and the laptop screen content changed to a prompt reading 'type @ to tag a portfolio'. On load the logo marquee scrolled and a progress-fill animation inside a 'patent-landscape' element ran; nothing ran after scroll. The nav switched from white-on-video to black-on-cream over light sections. With reduced motion no animations ran at all and the top screen was static.
observations.accessibility: The hero video element exists but only its poster rendered in headless Chromium. Testimonial slider indicators are 6×6px dots (one 32×6), labelled by aria-label. Grey eyebrow and body text on cream, and grey text on near-black, are low-contrast. The cookie banner overlaps hero content on both widths. The FAQ's 'Send question' button is 32×32. No horizontal overflow measured.
observations.mobile: Nav keeps the 'Book a demo' pill beside a hamburger. Headline 44px over the same footage; buttons stay in a row. The three mode cards, the pyramid callouts, the practice-area list and photo, and testimonials all stack to one column; the FAQ bubbles become full-width stacked pills. Page height grows from 9881 to 10992px with eight measured sections; the cookie banner occupies the bottom fifth of the first screen.

principles: Use footage of the subject matter (a microscope slide for patents) rather than the software to set tone, then show the product only in a framed panel further down.
Let a two-option tab switch both the caption and the screen so one panel demonstrates two product modes without doubling the page.
Phrase the FAQ as a chat transcript when the product itself is conversational, so the format demonstrates the interaction model.
Swap nav colour by section ground instead of pinning a fixed bar, so the first screen stays uninterrupted.
interpretation.fit: Suits enterprise AI sold to conservative professional buyers (law, finance, compliance) who want calm proof over flash; wrong for a consumer or developer tool where visitors expect to try the product within the first screen.
interpretation.risks: Very long page (almost 10,000px) with the product first shown around 2,500px down; low-contrast grey copy throughout; tiny slider dots; the cookie banner competes with the hero CTA on every first visit; hero footage is decorative and says nothing about patents until the headline is read.

limitations: Hero video did not play in headless Chromium; only the poster frame was seen.
Did not dismiss the cookie banner or submit the FAQ input.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Endra
summary: A black page led by an isometric stack of wireframe floor plates under a condensed serif headline, then product UI mocks in cards and one electric-blue CTA block.

observations.hero: Near-black screen with four stacked isometric plates drawn in thin white outline, centred and occupying the upper two-thirds. The headline 'MEP engineering at full speed' sits below the stack in a condensed serif, with a one-line grey subhead. No hero button; the only CTA is the blue 'Book demo' pill in the nav. A logo marquee of engineering firms runs along the bottom; a cookie dialog covers the lower right. Nav: pill-shaped wordmark, a centred pill with Product, Company, Security.
observations.typography: Measured h1 72px, weight 400, line-height 1, tracking -0.02em, family Serrif Compressed (a condensed high-contrast serif); body 16px at 1.4, family Endra Sans Text, measure 44ch. Families present: Endra Sans Text, Serrif Compressed, Lab Grotesque, Geist Mono (DM Mono on mobile). Monospace is used for tiny labels inside UI mocks ('REGION', 'ITEM'). Mobile h1 40px. Serif is reserved for section titles; everything else is a plain sans.
observations.visual_system: Single near-black ground with slightly lighter card panels and 1px borders. Accent is one saturated blue used for 'Book demo', the 'LIVE' badge and the closing CTA block. Imagery: white line-art of equipment (air handler, cable bundle, pipe fitting) in three discipline cards, a blurred studio photograph behind 'Endra Power Studio', dark product-UI mocks (playbook picker, room plan, agent chat, Revit sync table). Security badges are thin line icons.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → isometric stack hero + logo marquee → three discipline cards (Mechanical ETA 2027, Electrical LIVE, Plumbing to be announced) → 'Endra Power Studio' video panel with Play button → 2×2 feature grid (Playbooks, Typical Rooms, Agents, Revit Integration) each with a UI mock → stats 'We let engineers do more' (12x, 91%, 97%) → 'What you need to know' two-column FAQ → 'Secure by default' badges → blue 'See what your engineers could do. Live.' block → footer with large wordmark.
observations.interaction: Operated the first FAQ item ('What happens when the models change?'): the plus became a minus, aria-expanded flipped and a five-line answer expanded beneath; URL unchanged. On load about 50 animations ran: the h1, hero images and marquee slots; after scrolling 8 were still running (marquee and image animations). In the full-page capture the stats, FAQ and security sections rendered blank, consistent with scroll-triggered reveals. With reduced motion zero animations ran and the top screen was static.
observations.accessibility: Grey body copy on near-black is low-contrast in card descriptions and the subhead. The cookie dialog overlaps the logo marquee on desktop and covers the headline's second line on mobile. FAQ triggers are 40px tall and carry aria-expanded. A 'Skip to content' link exists. No horizontal overflow measured at either width.
observations.mobile: Nav keeps the blue 'Book demo' pill beside a hamburger; the centred link pill disappears. The isometric stack shrinks to fit and the headline wraps to two lines at 40px, partly hidden by the cookie dialog. Discipline cards, feature cards and FAQ become one column; stats stack vertically over a dark photo. Page height grows from 7498 to 9141px.

principles: A single abstract object (stacked floor plates) can stand for the product category without a screenshot, if the headline directly beneath names it.
Mark product maturity on the page itself (LIVE, ETA 2027, to be announced) so the roadmap is honest and the scope is clear.
Keep one accent colour for one action: when only 'Book demo' is blue, the eye finds the conversion path on every screen.
Show feature UI as dark mocks inside bordered cards so the product reads as part of the page's surface rather than a pasted screenshot.
interpretation.fit: Suits enterprise tools sold by demo to technical professionals who value restraint and evidence of real UI; wrong for consumer products or any page that must convert without a sales call.
interpretation.risks: No hero CTA and no hero product shot; grey-on-black copy is hard to read; the cookie dialog collides with the headline on mobile; scroll-reveal sections render empty in static captures and for readers who scroll fast; the serif is used only for titles, so the type system leans on two families plus mono.

limitations: Did not play the 'Endra Power Studio' video, so its content was not observed.
Did not dismiss the cookie dialog.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: CentralComs
summary: A trades-photo hero with a plain benefit headline, then two tabbed demo sections that play call and text transcripts as examples, each with its own free-trial button.

observations.hero: A dark-blue announcement bar ('raises Seed round at a $30M valuation, led by Y Combinator') sits above a white-on-dark nav with Solutions, Pricing, Integrations, Resources, Login and a blue 'Start a free trial'. The first screen is a full-bleed photograph of two roofers, darkened, with a centred two-line white headline, a two-line subhead and one blue 'Start a free trial' button. Nothing else competes in the first screen.
observations.typography: Measured h1 76px, weight 600, line-height 1.1, tracking -0.026em, family Figtree; body 20px at 1.6 line-height, measure 58ch, Figtree. A second family, foundryGridnik, is present and the wordmark is a serif-like logotype. Mobile h1 48px, body 18px. Section titles are medium-weight sans around half the h1 size; bullets and transcript text are small sans.
observations.visual_system: Mostly white and very pale blue-grey section bands; dark navy for the announcement bar, hero overlay, footer, transcript bubbles and phone mock; one mid-blue for every button. Imagery is photographic in the hero and closing band (tradespeople on a roof and at an HVAC unit), a teal video card with an illustrated air-conditioner, and chat/phone/email mocks with avatars. Integration logos float around a centred headline.
observations.page_sequence: Announcement bar → nav → photo hero → video card ('Home Service Owners', mute and play controls) → 'Capture lost revenue' three tabs with example panel and bullets → 'Generate more revenue' four tabs with example panel → 'From first hello to a booked visit' three icons → 'Works with the tools you already use' logo cloud → FAQ (7 items, native details) → photo CTA 'Ready to book more of your leads?' → navy footer.
observations.interaction: Operated the 'Reply to every text and email' tab: aria-selected moved to it, the phone-call mock was replaced by a text-message transcript ('Can you fix a clogged sink...') and the heading changed to 'Reply while they're ready to book'. On load and after scrolling zero animations were running; the nav became a translucent white bar with dark text once scrolled. With reduced motion nothing moved and the top screen was static.
observations.accessibility: Video controls are 44×44 and labelled (Unmute, Play) with a range input for progress. FAQ uses native summary elements, 83px tall. Tabs carry role=tab and aria-selected. Hero white text over the sky area of the photo has reduced contrast at the headline's top edge. Mobile offers a 'Pause logo animation' link under the logo cloud. No horizontal overflow measured; the measurement record reports nav height 0, suggesting the sticky nav was not detected as a nav element.
observations.mobile: Tabs disappear: every tab's example panel and copy are laid out in sequence as stacked blocks, each with its own free-trial button, so the page grows from 6978 to 12621px. The headline wraps to three lines at 48px; nav collapses to wordmark plus hamburger; the video card, icons row, logo cloud and FAQ stack one column; the closing photo band keeps its text left-aligned.

principles: Demonstrate a conversational product with short, labelled example transcripts (Customer / Assistant) instead of describing features.
Use tabs on desktop to keep seven scenarios compact, but on mobile unroll them in full rather than hiding them behind a swipe.
Repeat one identical primary button after every section so the next step never depends on scrolling back to the nav.
Choose photographs of the customer's trade, not the software, when the buyer is a small-business owner.
interpretation.fit: Suits SMB software sold to non-technical operators through a free trial, where trust and clarity beat novelty; wrong for a design-led or developer brand, where the stock-photo hero and template-like layout would read as generic.
interpretation.risks: Mobile page length doubles because tab content is unrolled; the hero depends on a stock-style photo for personality; no social proof beyond the funding bar and partner logos; the dark-on-dark nav over the photo and the near-identical repeated CTA blocks make the page feel templated.

limitations: Did not play the product video.
Could not confirm what the 'Pause logo animation' control pauses, since no animations were measured running.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Plena Health
summary: A rotating problem-statement headline hands off to a carousel of before/after workflow cases, each paired with a mock product screen and a hard number.

observations.hero: A thin lavender announcement bar (a customer result) sits above a white sticky nav with a pill 'Book a demo' button. The hero is a large rounded card with a pale lavender gradient, left-aligned: a 'Backed by Y Combinator' badge, a three-line headline whose last line is in violet and changes between captures ('patients stuck on hold', 'prior auths that stall for days', 'fax queues that never empty'), one paragraph of body, and a single violet pill CTA. No product image in the first screen.
observations.typography: Measured h1 86.4px, weight 800, line-height 1, tracking -0.04em, family 'Inter Display'; body 20px / 1.6 in 'Inter', measure 66ch. Section headings reuse the same heavy tight-set display style; a monospace family ('JetBrains Mono') appears for the mock-window title bars and the '+ Allscripts · Practice Fusion…' line. Small uppercase tracked labels ('THE PROBLEM', 'THE WORKFLOW') mark card sections.
observations.visual_system: White ground with large rounded lavender-gradient cards for hero, manifesto, CTA and security sections. Palette is near-black navy text, one violet accent, pale lavender fills, a pink 'problem' box and green 'done' / result boxes. Imagery is fabricated product windows (mac-style traffic-light dots, 'Plena AutoFlow · Referrals') on a dark navy panel. Customer and EMR logos appear in greyscale; two round HIPAA/SOC 2 seals.
observations.page_sequence: Announcement bar → nav → hero card → trusted-by logo marquee → 'Technology that adapts' workflow carousel (problem box, numbered workflow steps, result stat, mock screen) → 'Results from practices like yours' three case cards → 'Don't think in agents. Think in workflows' manifesto with three-column vendor-claims table → demo CTA card → EMR integrations card → 'Real numbers' four stat-plus-quote cards → second demo CTA card → security card → navy footer.
observations.interaction: Operated the carousel's right arrow: the indicator pill moved one step, the case swapped from a scheduling/waitlist case to 'Recover down coded claims' with a new problem box, new steps and a 'Revenue Cycle' mock window. The headline's violet last line also cycled on its own between page loads. Measurement counted 8–9 running animations; live, logo positions in the strip differed between captures and the workflow rows were blank in the 390 capture until scrolled into view. With reducedMotion set, the page still reported 1–6 running animations during scroll; which ones kept moving was not verified.
observations.accessibility: Headline and body contrast is high (navy on lavender). The announcement-bar text is small violet-on-lavender. The logo marquee moves continuously with no visible pause control. The carousel arrows are 38px circles. In the 390 full-page capture the workflow step rows under 'THE WORKFLOW' rendered as blank until scrolled into view, so scroll-reveal content is invisible to a non-scrolling snapshot. No horizontal overflow measured at either width.
observations.mobile: Nav collapses to logo plus hamburger. Hero card keeps the same layout at h1 35.1px; the headline's last line still rotates. Logo marquee becomes a two-logo-wide scrolling strip. Carousel card stacks text above the mock screen, which becomes a tall dark panel. The vendor-claims table keeps three narrow columns with wrapped text. Stat-plus-quote cards stack to one column; EMR logos become a 2×4 grid. Page grows from 7119px to 10442px.

principles: Rotate the pain point in the headline rather than the product claim, so one hero speaks to several buyer segments without lengthening the copy.
Pair every workflow story with a problem box, numbered steps, a single outcome number and a mock screen; the repeated structure lets a reader compare cases fast.
Position against the market's vocabulary explicitly (a 'what vendors say / what you need / what we do' table) when buyers are fatigued by generic AI claims.
Reuse one rounded gradient card as the container for every high-emphasis section so the page reads as a system without a second colour.
interpretation.fit: Suits vertical B2B services sold to operators who buy on outcomes and integration proof (clinics, back-office automation). Wrong for a self-serve developer tool or a consumer app, where a demo-only CTA and fabricated screens would read as evasive.
interpretation.risks: Two 'Book a demo' cards, a nav CTA and a hero CTA repeat the same ask; there is no product to try. The mock screens are illustrations, not captures, so the product remains unseen. Continuous marquee and rotating headline keep moving under reduced motion. Scroll-reveal hides workflow steps from anyone who does not scroll.

limitations: Could not verify whether the mock product windows reflect the real product UI.
Could not determine the full set of headline phrases; three variants were observed.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Remix
summary: The hero is a before/after phone pair driven by a 'simple to complex' slider, so the product's output is the first thing shown, not the product.

observations.hero: remix.re redirects to remix.is. Centred two-line headline, second line olive green, above a split stage: left, a fanned stack of portrait phone frames labelled 'The original'; centre, the logo, 'Remix any trend, reference, product or idea' and an arrow; right, one larger phone labelled 'Your remix'. Below: a row of trend names, left/right arrows and a gradient range slider from 'Simple' to 'Complex'. Nav holds four anchors, 'Book Demo' and a black 'Start Creating' button. Videos showed 'This video couldn't load' in the capture and the live session.
observations.typography: Measured h1 60px, weight 600, line-height 1, tracking -0.06em, family 'Bricolage Grotesque'; body 17px / 1.7 in the same single family, measure 59ch. Section headings repeat a two-line pattern with the second line in olive; eyebrow labels are uppercase tracked ('CONTENT FACTORY', 'HOW IT WORKS'). The 'POLISH IT. POST IT. ANYWHERE.' heading is set in caps.
observations.visual_system: Warm off-white ground alternating with pale sage-green bands and cards; near-black text, one olive accent, a blue-to-pink gradient only on the slider. Imagery is dense: phone frames, product-UI mock panels ('Content Factory', 'Your assets', 'Your next campaign'), 3×3 grids of social-post thumbnails with view counts, a 5×4×3=60 arithmetic strip, and tool icons (Claude, Codex, Cursor) connected by a tree line. Rounded cards with 1px borders throughout.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → hero showcase (originals → remix, slider) → 'Content Factory' batch math plus workspace mock → 'How it works' three numbered cards → 'Made for production' four video cards → 'Assets' media-library mock with tabs → 'Millions of views' two account cards with thumbnail grids → 'Polish it. Post it.' editor mock plus mobile phone → 'Advanced workflows & integrations' MCP tree → closing CTA band with two buttons → footer with a 'Pause effects' control.
observations.interaction: Operated the hero's right arrow: the active trend label moved from 'Podcast Chemistry' to 'UGC in Motion', the slider handle slid right, and both phone frames swapped to a different original/remix pair. Clicking a trend label alone changed nothing. Live, 3 animations ran at the top on load, 1 during scroll; the seven hero/feature videos never played (load errors). With reducedMotion set, 0 animations ran at every sample point.
observations.accessibility: The page exposes a 'Skip to content' link, a labelled range input ('Explore trends from simple to complex') and a footer 'Pause effects' control. Body copy in grey-olive on off-white is lower contrast than the headings. Phone-cover buttons in the fanned stack overlap each other and are partly off-canvas. A caption states 'Views shown in the captured Instagram posts, not live account totals'. No horizontal overflow measured.
observations.mobile: Nav keeps a 'Create' button plus hamburger. Headline h1 34.3px; the centre explainer text moves above the phones, which sit side by side at reduced size; trend labels clip at the right edge. Feature cards go to a 2×2 grid, asset tiles stack vertically, the two results cards stack, and the MCP tree stacks. Page grows from 6323px to 9807px.

principles: If the product's output is the proof, make the hero an input-to-output comparison and let a single slider tour the range of what it can do.
Use one accent colour and a two-line heading pattern (plain line, accent line) across every section so a long page still reads as one voice.
Make scale legible with arithmetic (5 × 4 × 3 = 60) rather than adjectives when the pitch is volume of variations.
Expose a visible 'pause effects' control and a labelled slider so a motion-heavy page stays controllable without hunting for OS settings.
interpretation.fit: Suits creative and media-generation tools whose value is visible in a sample. Wrong for infrastructure or compliance products, where example outputs cannot carry the argument and the many mock panels would read as decoration.
interpretation.risks: The whole first screen depends on streamed video; when it fails, the hero is two dark rectangles with error buttons. Nine sections of product mocks and thumbnails make the page long and image-heavy on mobile. The 'Millions of views' claims rest on two accounts with a caveat footnote.

limitations: Hero and feature videos did not load in the headless browser (load errors), so their motion and content were not observed.
Could not verify whether the mock product panels reflect the real product UI.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Fixture
summary: Almost the entire page is one scroll-pinned 'day in the life' narrative: a clock, a You/Fixture ledger and a swapping product panel on a gradient stage.

observations.hero: Black ground. Left column: a two-line white headline ('Talk to customers. Fixture does the rest.'), grey body paragraph, a blue 'Request access' button and an outlined 'Watch the day' play button; below, 'WORKS WITH YOUR FAVORITE AGENTS.' with a scrolling row of AI-tool icons. Right two-thirds: a rounded panel with a purple-to-orange gradient holding a pipeline-board product screenshot and an overlapping phone mock. A cookie banner with Decline/Allow sits along the bottom edge.
observations.typography: Measured h1 36px, weight 700, line-height 1.1, tracking 0, family 'PP Object Sans'; the largest display text is 84px in the measured family 'Inter' (the orange '8:00 AM' chapter clock). Body 18px / 1.3 in 'Inter', measure 40ch. Nav links, chapter index and footer use a monospace family ('JetBrains Mono') in small tracked caps. Story copy bolds 'You' and 'Fixture' in white against grey sentences.
observations.visual_system: Pure black page with white and grey text, one saturated blue for buttons, orange for the clock and index tick. Colour otherwise lives only inside the large rounded stage panel, whose gradient shifts between purple, blue and orange across chapters. Product imagery is rendered mock screens (phone, transcript window, pipeline board) tilted in perspective. A vertical tick ruler with hour markers runs down the left edge; a monospace chapter index with up/down arrow buttons sits bottom-left.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → hero (headline, CTAs, agent icons, stage panel) → scroll-pinned day story: 8:00 AM 'Your day, already sorted' → 'Walk in knowing everything' → 10:00 AM 'Just talk. Fixture listens.' → 'Know when a cold deal warms up' → 'Hear about risk before it costs you' → further chapters (Slack, pipeline, prospecting) → Saturday check-in → 'You talked to customers. Fixture did the other 36 things.' summary → split card with headline and 'Request early access' email form → footer. Measurement counts 3 sections, with the story measured as a 6599px hero.
observations.interaction: Operated 'Watch the day': the URL gained '#story' and the page scrolled to the 8:00 AM chapter, where the stage showed a phone mock and the ledger read 'You 1 / Fixture 3'. During scroll the stage stayed pinned while chapter text, the clock, the index highlight and the ledger changed (10:00 AM: 'You 3 / Fixture 7'). Measurement reported 409 animations and 5 canvases; live, 12–20 ran while scrolling. Agent icon order differed between captures. With reducedMotion set, 0 animations ran at every sample and the stage video had no source.
observations.accessibility: Grey story copy on black is mid-contrast; the chapter index items are small grey monospace. The cookie banner overlaps the bottom 70px of every screen until dismissed. The ruler's hour labels are tiny ('8A', '10A'). The full-page capture rendered the pinned stage blank, so the product visuals exist only in-viewport. No horizontal overflow measured. Email form present but not submitted.
observations.mobile: Nav shrinks to logo only (no menu, CTAs, or login visible). Hero stacks: headline 26px, body, two full-width buttons, icon row, then the gradient stage panel. The pinned story is unpinned: each chapter becomes a heading, You/Fixture copy and its own gradient image panel in sequence; the clock, ruler and chapter index are gone. Cookie banner covers the lower screen. Page height 7181px, shorter than desktop.

principles: If the product's value is 'things done while you weren't looking', narrate a day with a running tally of your actions versus the product's rather than listing features.
Keep the page monochrome and confine all colour to one stage panel so the product mocks are the only saturated thing on screen.
Give a long pinned narrative visible instruments (a clock, a ruler, a chapter index with arrows) so the reader knows where they are and can skip.
Offer a 'watch' CTA beside the conversion CTA so a visitor who is not ready to sign up still has a next step.
interpretation.fit: Suits agentic or automation products aimed at a single persona whose day can be scripted (founders who sell, ops leads). Wrong for multi-persona platforms or products buyers need to evaluate on specifics, where a linear story hides the feature surface.
interpretation.risks: One scroll-pinned story is the whole argument; nothing is skimmable, and the full-page snapshot shows how much depends on JavaScript.
