Hundreds of animations and five canvases load on a page with no fallback imagery. Mobile loses the clock, ruler and index that made the story navigable. The cookie banner competes with every CTA.

limitations: The pinned stage rendered blank in the full-page capture; chapter visuals were observed only in-viewport at two scroll positions.
Could not observe the stage video (no source loaded in the headless session) or verify whether the mock screens match the real product.
Did not count the full number of story chapters precisely; at least eight chapter labels appear in the index.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Anchr
archetype_note: Closer to an enterprise brochure long-scroll: typewriter hero, pinned system diagram, outcomes, industries, press, contact form.
summary: A typewriter headline cycles target industries, then a 14,000px enterprise brochure stacks a mock console, a pinned four-layer system diagram, outcomes, industries, roles, press and a form.

observations.hero: White-to-blush ground. Left: a light line 'The AI Supply Chain Employee for…' above a larger dark-red line with a blinking caret whose text differed across captures ('Ind', 'Healthcare & pharma', 'Food distribution'). Below, a round logo badge beside a tagline pill, then an outlined 'Schedule a demo' button. Right: a large chevron drawn in thin red outline, facets filled with food-market photos, framed by dotted diagonal guides. Nav: seven uppercase links, a theme toggle, a dark-red 'Get a demo' button. In the measurement capture the nav logo image was broken (alt text showed) and the right side was empty.
observations.typography: The page has no h1 (measurement h1 fields null); the largest display text is 67.7px in the measured family 'Outfit', set light with the industry line in dark red. Body 16px / 1.5, also 'Outfit', the only family measured. Section eyebrows ('THE PRODUCT', 'OUTCOMES') are small tracked dark-red caps; section headings are thin, large and centred or left-aligned by section. Outcome figures ('+15k', '~99%', '~30%') are set very large in the same light weight.
observations.visual_system: Near-white ground with a faint warm gradient and a dotted-grid texture in alternating bands. One dark-red brand colour for buttons, eyebrows, chevron and the typed line; black for headings. Imagery: a light-UI mock console ('Hey, John', notifications, upcoming sessions), isometric translucent plates that stack into a four-layer diagram ending with the chevron logo, a pink brain glyph with connector lines, greyscale logo strips (universities, IBM, Cisco, press mastheads), photo tiles per industry, role cards with mini chat mocks, and a SOC badge in the footer.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → typewriter hero with chevron graphic → 'Built & backed by the best' logo marquee → 'The agent builder' mock console → 'The product' pinned four-layer plate diagram with accordion tabs → 'Systems: Connect every system. Replace none.' brain diagram → 'Outcomes' heading with three large figures labelled 'illustrative value capture' → 'Industries' photo carousel → role cards (Sales, Purchasing, Finance, Executive) → 'What our customers say' testimonials → 'Press: Media mentions' three article cards → 'Contact us' with a name/email/message form → footer with SOC badge.
observations.interaction: Operated the 'Company brain + ontology' accordion tab in the product section: it expanded with 'Give every agent one shared understanding of your business', the previous tab collapsed, and the isometric plate relabelled from 'Data + integration fabric' to 'Company brain + ontology'. On scroll the plates stacked one by one while the section stayed pinned; headline text and logo-strip positions differed between captures; live counts of running animations ranged from 12 to 107 while scrolling. With reducedMotion set, 11 animations ran briefly on load then 0 at every later sample.
observations.accessibility: Light-weight display type at 67.7px is thin against the pale ground; the dotted grid sits behind body text in several bands. After the slow scroll-through and return to top, the console mock's text re-rendered unstyled and overflowed onto the product section in the live session (observed twice), overlapping headings. The typed headline has a permanently blinking caret. Logo marquee has no visible pause control. Outcome figures carry an 'illustrative value capture' disclaimer in small caps. No horizontal overflow measured. Contact form present, not submitted.
observations.mobile: Nav collapses to logo and a round hamburger. The chevron graphic moves above the headline; display drops to 23.4px while the typed industry line continues. Tagline pill and demo button stack full-width. Logo strip shows two logos at a time. The product section keeps accordion tabs but the pinned plate diagram yields a long near-empty gradient run (over 2000px) before the 'Systems' heading in the full-page capture. Page height 13394px, near desktop's 13909px.

principles: If you sell to several verticals, type the industry into the headline rather than listing them, so each visitor sees their own sector named within seconds.
Explain a layered platform with one pinned diagram whose layers accumulate as the reader scrolls, with a matching accordion so the reader can also jump.
Label projected outcome figures as illustrative on the page itself rather than letting large numbers imply measured results.
Keep one brand colour and one typeface across a very long page; the restraint is what holds fourteen sections together.
interpretation.fit: Suits enterprise B2B sellers to operations buyers who expect proof of credibility (logos, press, SOC) and a contact form rather than self-serve. Wrong for a developer tool or a consumer product, where fourteen sections and a demo-only ask would lose the visitor before the product appears.
interpretation.risks: The page is very long and front-loads credibility logos before showing what the product does. Pinned sections leave large blank runs in non-JS captures and on mobile. The console mock broke layout in the live session after scrolling. Thin light type on a pale textured ground reduces legibility. Outcomes are explicitly illustrative, which undercuts the 'Outcomes' heading.

limitations: The 1440 full-page capture stopped at 9000px and was blank below the product section; lower sections were observed only via viewport screenshots in the live browser.
Could not verify whether the console and chat mocks reflect the real product, or whether the unstyled-overflow glitch occurs in a non-headless browser.
Did not observe the full set of typed industries; three variants were seen.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Gutgutgoose
summary: A DTC product page built on a sky-and-moss photographic world, with a symptom explorer and a comparison table doing the persuasion instead of science copy.

observations.hero: A dark-green announcement bar ('Take the quiz') sits above a floating nav: a frosted logo pill at left, a frosted five-link pill in the centre, a solid green 'Get Started' pill at right. The hero is a full-bleed blue-sky photograph with a centred white two-line headline, three lines of body, one green pill CTA, and below it a rendered product jar standing on a mossy mound. A 'Backed by Y Combinator' tag and a row of white institution logos (Calico, Johns Hopkins, Oxford, Alphabet, Griffith) sit on the lower edge of the photo.
observations.typography: The page has no h1 (measurement h1 fields null) and no section landmarks counted. The largest text the measurement found is 18px in 'Manrope'; body is 20px / 1.3 in 'Figtree', measure 58ch; a third family 'Griffith Sans Text' is listed. Visually the hero and section headings are large, light-to-regular weight geometric sans in white or dark green; the footer carries a wordmark set at near-viewport width in low-contrast green.
observations.visual_system: Two grounds: off-white/warm grey for product and science sections, and deep forest green for the comparison table, booking card and footer. Sky and moss photography bookends the page (hero and the 'Go through your day without…' band). Rounded pill buttons and large-radius cards throughout. Imagery: rendered jars in green and plum, macro science photos (bacteria, DNA gel, capsule), a translucent anatomical figure whose highlighted band tracks the selected body region, and three advisor portraits on green backdrops.
observations.page_sequence: Announcement bar → floating nav → sky hero with jar and logo row → 'Two formulas' product cards with prices and 180-day guarantee → symptom explorer (Head/Abdomen/Intestines) → dark green comparison table vs generic probiotics → 'Fifty strains' three science cards → 'What personalized means' → 'Every cycle knows more' six-step dark panel with DNA gel → 'Six inputs' six cards → 'The experts who check our work' three portraits → 'Got questions?' booking card with phone number → sky band listing daily frustrations, one highlighted → footer with giant wordmark.
observations.interaction: Operated the 'Abdomen' tab in the symptom explorer: the four symptom rows swapped (Bloated, Stomach pain, Food reactions, Feeling sick), the italic quote and explanation changed, and the figure's dark highlight band moved from the head to the torso. Live, 0–1 animations ran at the top but 93–355 were running mid-scroll, matching the measurement's 0 on load / 93 after scroll. The sky band showed a phrase list with one line highlighted. With reducedMotion set, 2–4 animations still ran during scroll; the measurement records no reduced-motion rule.
observations.accessibility: White body copy over the sky photo and grey text on the dark comparison panel are mid-contrast. The symptom tabs are plain text elements, not buttons; my control scan found zero native buttons, tabs or inputs on the page. The 390 hero paragraph breaks mid-word ('m ade-to-order'). The footer wordmark is decorative low-contrast text. No h1 or section landmarks measured. No horizontal overflow at either width.
observations.mobile: Floating nav keeps the logo pill and a hamburger pill. Hero headline shrinks to fit two lines; the jar sits below the CTA and the logo row scrolls. Product cards stack; the symptom explorer stacks list above figure; the comparison table keeps three columns in a narrow dark panel; science and input cards go to one column; advisor cards stack. Body drops to 18px / 1.5. Page grows from 11315px to 12124px.

principles: Let the visitor pick their own symptom and watch the page re-explain itself around it; a self-selected path reads as personal in a way a generic benefits list does not.
Put the price and guarantee in the second screen so a consumer product page answers 'how much' before the science.
Frame against the generic alternative in a plain two-column check/cross table when the category is crowded with look-alikes.
Use one deep brand colour for both trust sections (comparison, booking, footer) so the dark panels read as authority rather than mood.
interpretation.fit: Suits DTC health and wellness products with a tangible object to photograph and a quiz or consult as the entry step. Wrong for B2B software or anything bought on specification, where the sky-and-moss world would feel like packaging over substance.
interpretation.risks: Headings are not real headings and controls are not real controls, so screen readers and keyboards get little structure. Hundreds of animations run mid-scroll with no reduced-motion rule. The page is long for a two-SKU store, and mid-word wrapping on mobile shows the copy was not checked at 390.

limitations: The 1440 full-page capture stopped at 9000px; the booking, phrase band and footer were observed only in the live browser.
Could not verify the identities or affiliations of the advisors shown, or that the product renders match shipped packaging.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Bloomy
summary: A split hero whose right panel is a tabbed, self-cycling product mock (diagnostic, gating, tutor), followed by a research-and-proof ladder aimed at school buyers.

observations.hero: Pale blue-to-mint ground with a faint dot grid. Left: a two-line headline with the second line in a blue-to-teal gradient, a four-line body paragraph, three feature labels separated by rules, a full-width gradient 'Request a school demo' button, and two small linked lines for parents and sign-in. Right: a white card with a gradient header bar and a product mock that differs between captures ('BloomyBot scaffolds student learning' chat; 'integrates with your 3rd-party data' diagram), with three pill tabs below it. Nav: logo, two links, gradient CTA, 'Sign in'.
observations.typography: Measured h1 55.2px, weight 700, line-height 1, tracking -0.025em, family 'Inter'; the largest display text is 80px (the stat numerals '90%', '~25', '3', '1'), also 'Inter'. Body 16.8px / 1.7, 'Inter', measure 63ch. The mock's reading passage uses a serif (measured family 'Georgia'); a monospace family is listed. Section eyebrows are small tracked caps inside outlined pills ('PEDAGOGY', 'TRUSTED BY EDUCATORS').
observations.visual_system: Alternating bands: off-white sections with white rounded cards, and full-bleed blue-to-teal gradient bands for the K-12 strip, testimonials and the demo form. One gradient (blue to green) carries the CTA, the headline accent, stat numerals and panel headers. Imagery is entirely product mocks: diagnostic node diagram, skill list with a 97% ring, Socratic chat, three stage cards (Base Camp complete, Climb active, Summit locked), accessibility widgets, curriculum map, teacher dashboard. School logos appear in white tiles. Footer is near-black.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → split hero with tabbed mock → gradient strip (K-12 / Standards-aligned / Self-paced) → 'Designed by educators. Backed by research' with named theories and four stat cards (90%, ~25 min, 3 stages, 1 tutor) → gradient testimonials from three school leaders → 'Intelligent learning that scaffolds to mastery' three stage cards → 'Designed for every student' accessibility cards → BloomyBot Socratic chat → curriculum map (1,200+ skills, ELA/Math totals) → real-time teacher dashboard → gradient 'Want to learn more?' demo form with Cloudflare human check → dark footer.
observations.interaction: Operated the hero's 'Mastery gating' tab: the panel header changed to 'Students advance only after proving mastery', the mock became a skill list with a locked next skill, a 97% mastery ring, '301 Bloomy Bucks' and a '4 day streak'; the tab pill filled with the gradient. The hero panel's content differed between captures without a click. Live, 42 animations ran at the top, 8–19 during scroll. With reducedMotion set, 4 ran at the top and 7–19 during scroll. The full-page capture had a 1700px blank run after the stage cards.
observations.accessibility: The page documents its own accessibility (read-aloud, text size, keyboard navigation) in a dedicated section. Hero body and feature labels are grey on pale blue, mid-contrast; white text on the gradient bands is high-contrast. Mock text inside cards is very small (approx. 9–11px in the stage cards). Tabs are native buttons. The demo form includes a Cloudflare 'verify you are human' box and was not submitted. No horizontal overflow measured.
observations.mobile: Nav collapses to logo and hamburger; CTA leaves the bar. The hero's mock panel and tabs are removed entirely; the three feature labels become a checklist with green ticks, and the gradient CTA goes full-width. h1 36px / 1.1. The gradient strip stacks its three claims vertically; stat cards, testimonials, stage cards and accessibility cards all go to one column. Page nearly doubles from 8225px to 15611px.

principles: Make the hero mock tabbed and let it cycle on its own, so a visitor sees three product moments without scrolling or clicking.
For a buyer who answers to a board, name the research (authors and theories) and put the operating numbers (90% threshold, 25 minutes) in oversized numerals before any testimonial.
Show the product's state model (complete / active / locked) as three side-by-side cards; a reader grasps gating faster from state than from prose.
Carry a single gradient through the CTA, headline accent and stat numerals so the page has one signature without a second brand colour.
interpretation.fit: Suits institutional edtech and other B2B products sold to administrators who want pedagogy, compliance and proof in one scroll. Wrong for a consumer or student-facing product, where the research ladder and demo form would read as a sales deck.
interpretation.risks: Ten sections of mock UI make a long page whose proof is self-illustrated rather than captured. Mobile drops the hero mock, so the product is unseen until far down a 15,600px page. Scroll-reveal leaves large blanks for non-scrolling readers, and reduced motion still leaves animations running. Stat numerals are framed as product rules, not outcomes.

limitations: Lower sections were observed in-viewport only, since the 1440 full-page capture rendered a 1700px blank after the stage cards.
Could not verify whether the product mocks match the real product or the school testimonials' provenance.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: InsForge (InstaCloud)
summary: A fixed HUMAN/AGENT toggle swaps the whole marketing page for a monospace markdown overview with a 'Copy page' button, making the agent a first-class reader.

observations.hero: Black ground with a faint grey grid; a slim nav (Products, Blogs, Docs, Integrations, Templates, Pricing, Careers, Roadmap, language, Discord, GitHub count, Login, green Sign Up). Centred stack: orange 'Backed by Y Combinator' chip, a two-line headline with the first line mint green and the second white, a grey subhead, a small pixel-art robot sprite, then a wide white 'Start Building Today' button beside an outlined 'Read Docs'. A 'Works perfectly with' logo strip and a floating HUMAN/AGENT pill close the first screen.
observations.typography: Measured h1 48px, weight 400, line-height 1.2, tracking 0, family Manrope; body 16px / 1.5 Manrope, measure 74ch. Families present: Manrope, Inter, Source Code Pro. The headline is regular weight rather than bold, with colour (mint vs white) doing the emphasis work. Service-card titles are small and regular; small monospace chips ('item', 'price', '<Hello World>') label the service cards. The AGENT view renders the entire page in a monospace family.
observations.visual_system: Near-black ground, thin grid lines in the hero and the 'Safe for Agents' section, one mint-green accent (headline line, active toggle, status dot, 'Real Apps'), orange only for the YC chip. Surfaces are dark cards with 1px borders; no photography. Imagery is a pixel-art robot sprite, a 3D-ish logo mark in a centre tile flanked by service icon tiles, small per-service glyphs, and avatar-plus-handle testimonial cards. Four large stat tiles at the bottom.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → hero (chip, headline, subhead, robot, two CTAs) → 'Works perfectly with' logo marquee → 'Ship Faster' / 'Let your agent run the whole stack' icon-tile diagram → 'Everything You Need for Production' 12-card service grid → 'Safe for Agents to Operate' branch-preview diagram → Changelog four cards → 'Join Our Community' testimonials (GitHub Discussion, Discord buttons) → FAQ accordion → 'Start Building Real Apps' CTA → four stat tiles → footer with status line.
observations.interaction: Operated the fixed HUMAN/AGENT tab pill: AGENT became aria-selected and the whole page was replaced by a monospace markdown document ('InsForge Machine-Readable Overview', front-matter listing index.md, agents.md, llms.txt) with a 'Copy page' button top right; the pill stayed fixed at the viewport bottom. On load the logo strip scrolled right-to-left and the robot sprite sat at different positions between captures. With reducedMotion set the marquee reported no running animation, yet the first screen still changed over one second, and scrolling to the bottom started line-draw animations in the 'Safe for Agents' diagram and digit-roll transitions in the stat tiles.
observations.accessibility: Grey subhead and card descriptions on black are mid-contrast; the service-card chips are very small. The floating pill overlaps page content (the 'Works perfectly with' strip, and the 'Ship Faster' heading on mobile), and its tabs are about 33px tall. The first FAQ item is expanded by default. No horizontal overflow at either width. Measured desktop nav height was 0px.
observations.mobile: Nav collapses to logo, globe icon and hamburger. Headline wraps to three lines at 32px; the two CTAs stack to full width. The logo strip persists, overlapped by the fixed HUMAN/AGENT pill. The 'Ship Faster' diagram recomposes as a centre tile with icon tiles in left and right columns; the 12-card service grid becomes a single column list; testimonials and stat tiles stack one per row. Page height grows from 6358px to 11193px.

principles: If your buyer is partly a machine, publish the page in the machine's format too and make the switch a one-tap toggle rather than a hidden /llms.txt.
Carry emphasis with one accent colour at regular weight rather than heavy type; it keeps a dense developer page quiet.
Put the whole product surface in one scannable grid of small cards so breadth reads at a glance before any single feature is argued.
A fixed floating control must have a reserved lane; otherwise it will collide with content, especially on narrow screens.
interpretation.fit: Suits infrastructure and developer platforms whose users arrive via coding agents, docs or CLIs and want to verify scope quickly. Wrong for a consumer or design-led product where the dark grid, monospace chips and feature-inventory layout would read as cold and undifferentiated.
interpretation.risks: Twelve equal-weight service cards and a 12-item nav dilute any single argument; nothing on the page shows the product actually being operated. The fixed pill overlaps content, the hero headline is regular weight at 48px and competes with the toggle for attention, and scroll-triggered line draws and counters keep running under reduced motion.

limitations: First live load returned HTTP 502 and succeeded on retry; the AGENT view was inspected only at 1440 wide.
Could not determine what moved on the first screen under reduced motion (likely the sprite), nor the behaviour of the Products dropdown or FAQ items beyond their default state.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Doomersion
archetype_note: Closer to a mobile app-store showcase: mascot wordmark, phone videos, pastel tiles, two store buttons.
summary: A giant mascot wordmark and three looping phone screens stand in for any argument; the page has no buttons, only two app-store links.

observations.hero: No nav. A black ground carries a pink-faced mascot with a blue tuft beside a very large white 'Doomersion' wordmark, a small globe glyph dotting the i. Below, two phone screens flank a centred pink three-line headline 'Learn Languages By Doomscrolling.' and a grey subhead: left a search/explore screen with Spanish cooking videos, right a 'For You' feed with an Arabic transcript panel and a tapped-word definition. A third phone (a Japanese video) begins at the bottom edge.
observations.typography: Measured h1 55.4px, weight 700, line-height 1, tracking -0.03em, family Arial; body 25.8px / 1.4 Arial, measure 29ch; Arial is the only family. The wordmark is a rounded heavy sans rendered as an image. Section headings are bold Arial in pink, yellow, mint and cyan; body copy is bold grey. On mobile h1 is 32px and body 14px.
observations.visual_system: Flat black ground, no gradients, no borders. Colour arrives through pastel pink, yellow, mint and cyan: as heading colour on desktop, and on mobile as floating language pills and full-bleed rounded tiles. Imagery is entirely phone-shaped product video (muted looping video elements with poster frames) showing the feed, transcript, lessons and flashcards screens, which share the same pastel palette. The mascot recurs inside the app screens.
observations.page_sequence: Mascot + wordmark → hero (explore phone, pink headline and subhead, feed phone) → three-column row: 'Every Subtitle Is A Lesson' (yellow) | Japanese feed phone | '11 Languages. Every Level.' (mint) with a language list → three-column row: lessons phone | 'Built-in Language Learning Center.' (cyan) | flashcards phone → 'Get Doomersion.' with App Store and Google Play buttons → footer links (Privacy, Terms, Support, Careers, Creators, Contact).
observations.interaction: At 1440 the DOM held no buttons, tabs or inputs, only store and footer links, so the one control operated was the 'see how it works' anchor, which is visible only at 390: it scrolled the page one screen (to y=844) to the yellow 'Learn from Subtitles' tile. Measurement reported 0 running animations at 1440 and 11 at 390; live at 390 the eleven language pills alternated between English and native-script labels ('Japanese'/'日本語'). With reducedMotion set only the English labels rendered and the first screen stayed still. Videos did not play in headless Chromium; posters showed.
observations.accessibility: Grey bold body on black is mid-contrast; the pink and yellow headings are readable. The phone videos have no visible captions or controls and carry status-bar chrome. Footer links are small (about 14px). At 390 the store buttons are large full-width targets; the pills are decorative and not interactive. No horizontal overflow at either width. No h-level structure was visible for the three-column rows beyond coloured headings.
observations.mobile: A different composition rather than a stacked desktop: a small mascot-plus-wordmark header, a cloud of eleven tilted pastel language pills, a white two-line headline, two full-width store buttons and a 'see how it works' chevron fill the first screen. Below, content becomes bento tiles: a yellow 'Learn from Subtitles' tile with a phone video, a cyan '11' tile beside a pink explore-phone tile, a green 'Language Learning Center' tile with two phones, then repeated store buttons and footer. Page height 2710px, measured section count 0.

principles: If the product is a feed, show the feed moving in a phone frame and let the screens carry the explanation instead of feature prose.
Design the phone layout as its own composition when the product is mobile-only; the first screen should already be the install decision.
Pick three or four pastel accents and reuse them identically in the app screens and the page so product and marketing read as one object.
A page with no secondary navigation forces one outcome; accept that only when install is the sole conversion.
interpretation.fit: Suits consumer mobile apps with a visually self-explanatory loop (short video, games, social) where install is the only ask. Wrong for anything that must justify a price, integrate with other tools or be evaluated on desktop, since the desktop page is a shrunken phone showcase with no proof, pricing or depth.
interpretation.risks: Desktop is served by the same five phone videos with no interaction, no social proof and no way to try anything; large grey bold body copy in a system font and a 29ch measure make the desktop layout feel unfinished next to the mobile one. Autoplaying video posters depend on codec support, and the only CTA is an outbound store link.

limitations: Headless Chromium could not decode the H.264 phone videos (media error 4), so looping video playback and what it shows was inferred from poster frames only.
First live load returned HTTP 502 on one attempt and succeeded on retry; no operable control existed at 1440, so the anchor link was operated at 390 instead.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Congruent
summary: A 100px all-caps claim and an exploded hardware render hand off to a scroll-pinned city scene whose caption steps through Record, Augment, Get synthetic data.

observations.hero: A fixed 65px header: wordmark at left, small tracked monospace links HOME, TECHNOLOGY, ABOUT US centred and CONTACT US at right. On a near-black ground with a blue radial glow, a three-line all-caps headline fills the left two-thirds: 'THE ONLY RADAR FOR' in white, 'END-TO-END AUTONOMY' in cyan. A three-line monospace paragraph, a cyan rectangular 'BOOK A DEMO' button and a 'Backed by Y Combinator' line sit beneath. An exploded render of the radar module (lid, antenna board, housing on pins) floats at the right, overlapping the headline's last word.
observations.typography: Measured h1 100px, weight 800, line-height 1.1, tracking -0.02em, family Outfit, all caps; body 16px / 1.8 in JetBrains Mono, measure 65ch; only those two families. Section headings reuse Outfit bold with one cyan word ('Record real data.', 'Augment the scene…'); the later claim rows mix a light-weight Outfit first half with a bold second half. Nav, button labels and the demo-form fields are small tracked monospace. On mobile h1 is 32px and body drops to 12px at 24ch.
observations.visual_system: Dark navy-black ground, a single cyan accent used for the headline, the CTA, the 'TEAM' label and one word per heading; orange only in the YC mark. No cards or borders. Imagery is rendered 3D: the exploded radar module, a bird's-eye street with blue, yellow and red radar fans, a night-time street video that gains a cyan wireframe overlay and red bounding boxes, and a frontal car render with a cyan point-cloud skin. A faint perspective floor grid closes the hero. Two circular team photos at the end.
observations.page_sequence: Fixed nav → hero (headline, mono paragraph, Book a Demo, YC line, exploded render) → 'the only radar with raw data, real or synthetic' beside a radar-fan street render → 'The Paradigm Shift: End-to-end Training' → pinned section: street video held left while the caption steps 'Record real data' → 'Augment the scene in your world model' (wireframe overlay, typed prompt '> Add a pedestrian on the sidewalk', a pedestrian appears) → 'Get synthetic raw data' → three claim rows with car renders → TEAM: two founders with bios → footer with Privacy Policy.
observations.interaction: Operated 'BOOK A DEMO': the button was replaced in place by an inline form (name, email, use-case textarea, a Formspree notice, Cancel and Submit), which pushed the hero text up under the fixed header; nothing was submitted. On load one muted looping video autoplayed in the pinned section and a cursor blinked in the typed-prompt span. On scroll the video stayed pinned while captions and overlays changed and the prompt typed out. With reducedMotion set the video still autoplayed and the cursor still blinked; the first screen itself did not change over one second.
observations.accessibility: The monospace paragraph is light grey on dark, fine at 16px but 12px on mobile where the radar render sits behind it. The exploded render overlaps 'AUTONOMY' at 1440. Demo-form fields have placeholders but no label elements. HOME, TECHNOLOGY and CONTACT US link to '#'. Opening the form pushes the headline under the fixed header, clipping it. The full-page capture rendered the sticky section as large blank areas.
observations.mobile: Nav shrinks to the centred wordmark alone; the three nav links and CONTACT US disappear with no menu control. The headline becomes four centred lines at 32px; the exploded render moves behind the body paragraph instead of beside it, and the YC line wraps. The pinned street video becomes a small full-width strip with the wordmark bar overlapping it in the capture; the claim rows and team cards stack to one column. Page height 13302px with large empty stretches between pinned steps.

principles: Pin one scene and change only the caption and overlay as the reader scrolls; the constant frame makes a three-step pipeline legible without a diagram.
Reserve the accent colour for one word per heading so the claim hierarchy survives an all-dark page.
Pair a geometric display face with a monospace body when the product is hardware plus data; the contrast separates the claim from the specification.
Expanding a demo form in place keeps the reader in context, but reserve the vertical room for it so the hero does not jump.
interpretation.fit: Suits deep-tech hardware or simulation products whose pitch is a before/after transformation of a scene (sensors, robotics, synthetic data). Wrong for a product with many features or self-serve signup, since the page offers a single demo request and nothing to try.
interpretation.risks: Everything hinges on the pinned video; headless capture, slow connections or reduced-motion users get a long page of blank space and a video that keeps playing. Three nav links go nowhere, the hero render collides with the headline at 1440 and with the body text at 390, 12px body on mobile is hard to read, and 'the only radar' is asserted five times without evidence beyond renders.

limitations: The pinned video's content was seen through viewport captures during scroll; frame-level changes between captures were not verified.
Nav links resolve to '#', so TECHNOLOGY and CONTACT US targets could not be checked; the reduced-motion rule is 'unverified' in the measurement record and only live behaviour was observed.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

observations.page_sequence: Sticky nav → hero (eyebrow, headline, subhead, Book a demo, backers, building animation) → grey proof band: one sentence of value and three institution logos → 'How it works' row: pipe-network animation left, 'Full visibility. Zero disruption.' and one paragraph right → 'Real-time monitoring' row: 'Learn. Detect. Prevent.' and paragraph left, building-plus-chart animation right → 'Book a demo' centred: 'See AquaShield in action', one line, a wide blue pill 'Schedule a Demo for Your Buildings' → footer: copyright, mail and LinkedIn icons.
observations.interaction: Operated the nav's 'Get in touch' link (an in-page anchor to #contact): the page scrolled from 0 to 2267px to the demo section; nothing else changed. The 'Schedule a Demo' button carries an inline handler that opens a Calendly popup; it was not operated. On load the hero building animation inside its iframe kept changing between captures 1.5s apart. On scroll each block (proof logos, copy, animation panels, contact card) ran a CSS transition as it entered view; measurement counted 19. With reducedMotion set no page-level animations ran but the hero iframe still changed over one second.
observations.accessibility: Headline and button contrast is high; grey body copy and the 'Backed by' line are mid-contrast on black. The two animation panels are iframes with aria-labels ('Water network solution preview', 'AquaShield dashboard preview'). The hero iframe has a title but is tabindex -1. The 'Get in touch' pill is removed from the nav on mobile, leaving the demo button as the only CTA until the bottom. The 390 capture shows no horizontal overflow; the measured mobile content width is 250px, giving a 46ch body measure.
observations.mobile: The nav keeps only the logo and wordmark; 'Get in touch' disappears. The hero recomposes centred: the building animation moves above the text, then the eyebrow (wrapping to two lines), a four-line 42px headline, subhead, the 'Book a demo' pill and backers. The proof band stacks its sentence over three logos. The two feature rows become single columns with the heading and paragraph above the animation. Page height 2890px versus 3167px on desktop.

principles: If the product makes something invisible visible, build the page around one recurring visual of that reveal and let every section reuse it at a different zoom.
Isolate heavy animations in their own embedded documents so the marketing page stays plain HTML with a single font.
Three sections and one Calendly button is enough when the only next step is a sales call; do not add pricing or feature grids you cannot support yet.
Use orange for exactly one thing, the problem, and keep the brand accent for everything else.
interpretation.fit: Suits early B2B hardware or property-tech companies selling to a small number of portfolio owners by demo. Wrong for a self-serve or developer product, where the lack of any product UI, pricing or documentation would stall evaluation.
interpretation.risks: No real product screenshot, customer or number appears; the proof strip offers institutions, not clients. The animations run inside iframes that ignore reduced motion and were the only visual interest, so a blocked or slow frame leaves an empty hero. The page's single CTA depends on a third-party popup, and the mobile nav loses its contact link.

limitations: The Calendly 'Schedule a Demo' button was not operated, so the popup was not verified; the animations inside the iframes were observed only as changing pixels, not frame by frame.
What the hero iframe animates under reduced motion was not inspected inside the frame.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Kuli
summary: A self-running chat demo under the headline scans 1,284 creators into a shortlist while every later section is another fabricated product panel with hard numbers.

observations.hero: A white sticky 65px nav: wordmark, six text links, an 'FR' globe pill, 'Log in' and a dark purple pill 'Book a Demo'. On a pale lavender dot-grid with a soft glow, a centred 'Backed by Y Combinator' chip sits over a one-line headline 'Run [rotating phrase] 10× faster.' whose middle phrase is a lilac italic serif ('social media' at 1440, 'creator marketing' at 390 in measurement). Two lines of grey body, a purple pill 'Book a Demo' and a text link 'See how it works'. A greyscale logo marquee and the top of a two-pane product demo close the first screen.
observations.typography: Measured h1 68px, weight 700, line-height 1, tracking -0.035em, family Manrope, with the rotating phrase in the measured display family Fraunces (italic); body 18px / 1.5 Manrope, measure 77ch. Families present: Manrope, Inter, ui-monospace, Fraunces. Section headings mix bold Manrope with an italic serif phrase ('manual work', 'millions of videos'); eyebrows are small lilac uppercase pills; stats and timestamps inside panels are monospace. The closing headline sets '10×' in a very large lilac italic serif. Mobile h1 36px.
observations.visual_system: Off-white and lavender ground with a faint dot grid and plus-sign corner marks in the hero. Palette: deep aubergine text and buttons, lilac accent, green for 'do's' and uplift percentages, red-pink for 'don'ts' and rival alerts. Surfaces are white rounded panels with 1px borders and soft shadows styled as product UI (chat pane, shortlist cards, 'Brand HQ' brain, video-watching strip, post-analysis checklist, rivals' top posts, comparison table). Creator video thumbnails and greyscale brand logos are the only photography.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → hero (chip, rotating headline, body, two CTAs) → 'Iconic brands and agencies trust Kuli' logo marquee → self-running demo: chat pane left ('Find me US clean-beauty micro-influencers…', progress steps) and shortlist pane right (1,284 scanned → 38 strong fits → 6 picks, ranked creator cards) → 'How Kuli works': alternating rows (Brand HQ do's/don'ts panel; video-watching strip with 'Kuli's read'; a third row) → 'Four jobs your spreadsheet can't do' cards → comparison table Kuli vs agencies vs influencer platforms → 'Make your team 10× more productive' CTA with Book a Demo and Talk to sales → five-column footer.
observations.interaction: Operated the 'FR' toggle (aria 'Passer en français'): the page navigated to /fr/, the nav, headline ('Pilotez votre stratégie d'influence 10× plus vite.'), body and CTAs switched to French, the demo's chat brief stayed in English, and the toggle read 'EN'. On load 46 transitions were running: the hero demo typed a brief, stepped through 'Pulled 1,284 candidates… Watched 6,400 posts… Scored brand fit' and filled the shortlist; 'live' dots pulsed; one of 26 creator videos played. With reducedMotion set the first screen was still over one second but 11–13 animations (ping/pulse dots, chip transitions) kept running and all videos stayed paused.
observations.accessibility: Headline contrast is high; grey body and the tiny monospace meta text inside panels (around 10–11px) are low-contrast and small. The demo's 'send' button is 24×24px, and 'Export' and 'Brief campaign on these' are 22–24px tall. The hero demo input has a placeholder but no visible label. The full-page capture left large blank regions where sections had not yet been revealed by scroll. No horizontal overflow at either width.
observations.mobile: Nav keeps the wordmark, a 'Book a Demo' pill and a hamburger; the FR toggle and Log in move out of view. The headline stacks to three centred lines with the rotating phrase on its own line; CTAs sit side by side. The logo marquee shows two logos at a time. The two-pane hero demo is not present in the 390 capture; the page goes from logos to 'How Kuli works', and each feature row stacks copy above a full-width product panel. Page height 10150px versus 7400px at 1440.

principles: Let the hero demo run itself from a real-looking brief to a ranked result so the visitor sees the whole job finish before reading a feature.
Switch one phrase of the headline into an italic serif to carry the brand voice; keep everything else in a single quiet sans.
Give every section a fabricated product panel with specific numbers rather than an illustration; specificity reads as proof even without customers.
Localise the whole page behind a one-tap toggle, but make sure demo content switches too or the seam shows.
interpretation.fit: Suits B2B AI agents sold to marketing or operations teams where the output (a shortlist, a report) is more convincing than the interface. Wrong for products that cannot script a believable end-to-end run, or for audiences who will test the numbers, since every figure on the page is illustrative.
interpretation.risks: Dozens of concurrent transitions and 26 video elements make the page heavy, and reduced motion only partly quiets it. The demo and panels present invented stats (1,284 scanned, €1.2M EMV) with no customer attribution; the comparison table prices competitors without sources. The hero demo disappears on mobile, removing the page's main argument for phone visitors.

limitations: Only one creator video played in headless Chromium; the content of the 26 video elements was not verified. Which sections stay blank until scroll-reveal on a real device was not confirmed.
The FR toggle was operated once; the rotating headline phrases beyond 'social media', 'creator marketing' and 'd'influence' were not enumerated.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Origin
summary: A typed-out serif question over a live embedded platform opens a scroll-pinned, 6-plus-7-step data-driven essay that argues from trial statistics to tumour samples.

observations.hero: Deep navy ground with a soft radial glow. A small ring logo and wordmark top-left; a centred frosted pill holds DATA ENGINE, RESEARCH and an outlined GET ACCESS button. One line of serif headline types itself out with a blinking caret ('What if we made as many cancer drugs next year as we have in the last decade?', last word italic). Beneath, a mac-style window frames a live embed of 'Origin Spatial': layers panel, a circular lung tissue section coloured by predicted cell type, and a right panel of tabs with tissue-composition percentages. A 'Click to interact' hint sits at the window's bottom edge.
observations.typography: Measured h1 43.2px, weight 400, line-height 1.2, tracking -0.012em, family Instrument Serif; measured body 10.2px in Inter, measure 45ch (the sampler caught the small caption text; essay paragraphs render larger). Families: Inter, Instrument Serif. Every section heading is regular-weight serif, often broken into four short lines ('Most patients / are unlikely / to respond / to a drug.'); labels, step counters ('2 / 6'), nav and tables use small tracked uppercase sans; the drug table sets names in serif and dosages in tiny tracked caps. Mobile h1 24.8px.
observations.visual_system: Two grounds: navy with radial glow for the hero, the 'How do we know who will respond?' interlude and the Data Engine intro; near-white for the two essay sequences. Colour is carried by data: a blue/green stacked area chart, blue sparklines, 3D clusters of pink, mauve, blue and tan spheres, H&E tissue thumbnails in pink-purple and greyscale, blue versus rose person glyphs. Progress bars run navy-to-pink. The embedded platform is a dark UI around a light slide viewport. Three research cards show grey placeholders; the footer logo rendered as alt text.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → typed question → embedded platform window → 'Data & logs' row → Advisors (three) and Investors (eighteen names) → pinned sequence 1/6–6/6: drugs-tested area chart → Phase 1–3 success sparklines → 'But why?' annotated tumour cluster → '20.6 million new cases' → 'Most patients are unlikely to respond' 20-cluster grid → 'Response could be predicted before enrollment' → navy interlude 'How do we know who will respond?' → DATA ENGINE intro → pinned sequence 1/7–7/7 from real tumour through regions, spatial transcriptomics, cohorts and model training to a responders person-grid → 'Optimized trials cost less' with Get in touch / See the platform and a seven-drug table → Research: three cards → footer.
observations.interaction: Operated the 'Genes' tab inside the embedded platform. A first click on the window removed the cover layer ('Click to interact'); clicking the tab then marked Genes active, blurred the app and raised a centred 'Request access' form (first name, last name, work email, company). Nothing was submitted. On load the headline typed out over several seconds with a blinking caret; three videos were present but paused. On scroll each pinned sequence held its figure while text and figure state changed and a counter advanced; 'SKIP AHEAD' is an anchor past each sequence. With reducedMotion set the caret still blinked and the first screen still changed over one second; nothing else was reported running.
observations.accessibility: Headline contrast on navy is good; the essay's grey body on off-white and the tiny tracked captions (measured 10.2px) are low-contrast and small. The nav's first link has no text (logo link). The embedded platform gates every control behind a request-access form. Pinned sequences produce full-page captures that are mostly blank, so the page depends on scroll position to be legible. The research cards' images did not load and the footer logo image was broken at inspection. No horizontal overflow at either width.
observations.mobile: The nav becomes one frosted pill with the ring logo, two links and GET ACCESS. The typed question wraps to two lines at 24.8px. The platform embed recomposes vertically: hamburger toolbar, a small square slide viewport with 'Tap to interact', a 'Data & logs' disclosure and the tissue-composition list below. Advisors and investors become two columns. Each pinned step stacks the figure above its heading and paragraph with the counter and SKIP AHEAD beneath; 20-cluster grids become 3×4; the drug table becomes stacked rows. Page height 20477px versus 22751px.

principles: Open with a single typed question and a live product window; the question sets the thesis and the window proves the product exists before any argument begins.
Build the page as a numbered, scroll-pinned essay where each step changes one figure; the counter and a skip link let readers control pace without losing the argument.
Use a regular-weight serif for every claim and reserve colour for data, so the charts and tissue images carry the emotion the type withholds.
Gate the embedded product's controls behind an access form, but let visitors see the real interface first.
interpretation.fit: Suits research-led deep-tech and biotech companies selling datasets or platforms to scientific buyers who will read a long argument and value primary figures. Wrong for a transactional or self-serve product, where a 20,000px pinned essay delays the call to action by many screens.
interpretation.risks: The argument lives in scroll-pinned sequences that render as blank pages in static capture, in feeds and under broken JavaScript. Body and caption type are small and grey on both grounds. The product embed invites interaction and then blocks it with a form, which can read as bait. Broken research-card images and a broken footer logo were visible at inspection, and the typed headline delays the thesis by several seconds.

limitations: Two full-viewport canvases exist in the main page and three inside the platform embed; what they render was not verified. Three videos (in research assets) were paused and not inspected.
Frame-by-frame changes inside each pinned sequence were seen only at 900px scroll intervals; intermediate states and the 'Data & logs' disclosure were not operated.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Mindy
archetype_note: Really a sunset/acquisition notice: one centered letter card, no product, no navigation, no call to action.
summary: The homepage has been replaced by a single acquisition letter in a bordered card; the only action is an outbound press-release link.

observations.hero: A white rounded logo tile sits centered at the top of a near-black page, followed by the centered heading "Mindy's Next Chapter" and a bordered, slightly lighter card holding a letter. The card (about 710 px wide at 1440) begins in the first screen and the letter runs below the fold. There is no navigation bar, no button and no image.
observations.typography: Single measured family Instrument Sans for everything. H1 measured 48 px, weight 600, line-height 1.1, tracking -0.02 em (36 px on mobile). Body 16 px at 1.7 line-height in mid-grey (rgb 161,161,170) on near-black; key phrases are bolded in white. The link is set in a muted violet without underline until hover.
observations.visual_system: Body background rgb(17,17,17) with a faint violet radial glow at the top centre; the letter sits in a card with a thin lighter border and rounded corners. Colour is limited to white text, grey body, one violet accent for the link and the small star in the logo. No imagery, no product screenshots, no motifs beyond the glow.
observations.page_sequence: Logo tile → h1 → letter card (origin story → acquisition announcement → gratitude → sign-off with press-release link) → one-line footer "© 2026 Mindy. With gratitude."
observations.interaction: No buttons, tabs, inputs or toggles exist on the page (control scan returned zero elements). The only operable element is the press-release text link; hovering it added an underline and nothing else changed. Nothing moved on load or scroll (0 running animations at both viewports). With reduced motion on, the page was identical; no prefers-reduced-motion rule was found in accessible stylesheets.
observations.accessibility: Body copy is mid-grey on near-black, which looks low-contrast in the screenshot though it was not measured. The link relies on colour alone at rest (underline only on hover). No horizontal overflow at either width. Only one link and no form controls, so tap-target concerns are minimal.
observations.mobile: Same single column: logo tile, 36 px heading, and the card shrinks to 348 px content width with the letter wrapping to roughly 41 characters per line, making the page 1808 px tall versus 1260 px on desktop. Nothing is hidden or recomposed; the footer stays at the bottom.
observations.copy: H1: "Mindy's Next Chapter". There is no primary action button; the only labelled action is the text link "Mindy's Team Joins WorkWhile to Accelerate AI Adoption in Enterprise Workforce Management". The first screen offers no proof: no logos, numbers or demo, only the opening of the letter.

principles: When the product is gone, replace the homepage with one honest letter rather than leaving a stale marketing site live.
A single column of about 700 px with 1.7 line-height makes long-form text readable without any layout machinery.
Keep the brand's existing palette (dark ground, one accent) so a transition notice still reads as the same company.
interpretation.fit: Suits acquisition, sunset or wind-down notices and investor-facing updates; wrong for any company that still needs to convert visitors, since there is no navigation, product or call to action.
interpretation.risks: Grey-on-black body text and a colour-only link are weak for readability; the page gives no route to the acquirer's product or a contact beyond an external press release, and nothing signals what visitors should do next.

limitations: Contrast ratios were not measured, only judged visually.
No operable control other than a text link existed, so the control test was a hover rather than a click.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Astro Mechanica
summary: A full-bleed test-stand video with one line of copy, followed by a pinned scroll-reveal statement and a single product claim; news and a newsletter stand in for a CTA.

observations.hero: The first screen is a looping video of a jet engine on a test stand with a glowing exhaust window, filling the viewport edge to edge. A small logo lockup sits top-left and four spaced-caps nav links (HOME underlined) top-right over the video. The only text is a two-line statement bottom-left, "We're building the next generation of flight." There is no button, no subhead and no proof element in the first screen.
observations.typography: One measured family, TWK lausanne, for everything. The hero statement is the measured display at 60 px; the semantic h1 is lower on the page, measured 42 px, weight 300, line-height 1.2, zero tracking (33.6 px on mobile). Body 16 px at 1.4. Eyebrow labels, nav and footer legal are small letter-spaced caps; the footer closes with the company name set as a very large wordmark across the full content width.
observations.visual_system: Black ground throughout; the hero and a later section use full-bleed video, and a pinned section shows faint concentric arc lines on near-black while a statement fills in word by word from grey to white. The product section pairs the h1 with a cut-away engine render on a dark grid. A single cyan accent is used for the eyebrow, the MORE NEWS outline button and the Subscribe button. News cards use dark photos with publication logos overlaid.
observations.page_sequence: Full-bleed hero video with statement → second full-bleed video band → pinned section where a one-sentence mission statement reveals word by word on scroll → product claim (eyebrow + h1 + engine cut-away render) → Recent News (three cards, MORE NEWS button) → newsletter form + link columns → giant wordmark and legal line.
observations.interaction: Operated the newsletter email input by typing "audit" without submitting: the field rendered the text in uppercase and nothing else on the page changed. On load two videos were already playing (hero and second band) and a third started when scrolled into view; the control scan found no tabs, toggles or carousels, only the email input and submit button. Running animations rose from 0 to 7 while the pinned text revealed, then back to 0. With reduced motion on, all three videos still played and the reveal still ran; no prefers-reduced-motion rule was found in accessible stylesheets.
observations.accessibility: White text sits directly over moving video without a scrim in the hero, and the nav links are small letter-spaced caps over the video. The reveal section renders unread words in dark grey on near-black, which looks very low contrast until scrolled. The email input uppercases typed text, which may hide case errors. No horizontal overflow at either width. The full-page capture shows a blank band where the pinned section is, so content there depends on scroll position.
observations.mobile: The nav collapses to a logo and hamburger icon. The hero keeps the video with the statement near the bottom. The product section stacks: eyebrow, 33.6 px h1, then the engine render below. The three news cards stack vertically with the MORE NEWS button moved above them; the newsletter input and Subscribe button stack full width; footer link columns sit side by side and the wordmark shrinks to a single line. Page grows to 5766 px.
observations.copy: H1 (semantic): "The world’s first jet engine that’s engineered for efficiency across subsonic and supersonic speeds."; the hero display line reads "We're building the next generation of flight." There is no primary action in the first screen; the first labelled action on the page is the outline button "MORE NEWS" and the form button "SUBSCRIBE". First-screen proof is the test-stand footage itself; no logos or numbers.

principles: When you have real hardware footage, let it be the entire first screen and keep copy to one sentence.
Put the semantic h1 on the single concrete product claim, not on the mission slogan, so the page's strongest statement is also its most specific.
Use one accent colour for every clickable element so sparse pages still signal where the actions are.
A pinned word-by-word reveal buys attention for a mission sentence but should degrade to static text under reduced motion.
interpretation.fit: Suits deep-tech and hardware companies whose audience is press, recruits and investors rather than self-serve buyers; wrong for a SaaS product that needs to explain features, show pricing or convert in the first screen.
interpretation.risks: Autoplaying video ignores reduced motion and raises page weight; the pinned reveal leaves a large empty band in non-scrolled renders and crawlers; there is no primary CTA, so the only conversions are a newsletter and news links.

limitations: Video playback under reduced motion was checked by media state, not by frame comparison.
The news cards' link targets and the MORE NEWS button were not followed.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Scarlet
summary: A clinical-footage video hero carrying one promise, then a long white page that stacks every trust device a regulator-adjacent buyer expects: logos, quotes, films, accreditations, FAQ.

observations.hero: A white 68 px nav (logo, eight text links, outlined "Get in touch") sits above a full-width looping video of patients and clinicians using health apps; the frame changes between captures (phone glucose app, nurse with tablet, smartwatch). A single centred white line, "Certify your AI medical device without unnecessary delays", sits over the footage with no button beneath it. A cookie consent panel with Reject/Accept covers the bottom-right corner.
observations.typography: Measured families Aeonik Pro Medium for headings, Aeonik Pro Regular for body, with Inter also loaded. The semantic h1 is below the video: 48 px, weight 500, line-height 1.1, tracking -0.01 em, dark grey on white (32 px on mobile). Body 16 px at 1.4; section eyebrows are small letter-spaced caps. The hero line over video is a lighter-weight white sans of similar size; the footer ends with a large wordmark in a purple-to-blue gradient.
observations.visual_system: White and pale grey alternating bands; the only strong colour is a small pink-red "Get in touch" button and red accents inside the device photography. Imagery is documentary: people holding devices, a clinician laughing, a customer-story film with a play button. Proof blocks are set as cards with thin borders: six customer logos, a 2×3 grid of testimonial cards, and a row of six regulator badges (EU flag, UK, US flag, MHRA, others).
observations.page_sequence: Nav → video hero with one line → h1 + "Get in touch" → customer logo row → single large pull-quote → "Why Scarlet" three photo cards with linked stories → "Our customers" film with play button → six testimonial cards → full-bleed photo band "Transfer to Scarlet in 4 weeks" with button → accreditation badges → news list (four posts) → FAQ accordion → dark CTA band "Need to certify an AI medical device?" → footer links and gradient wordmark.
observations.interaction: Operated the first FAQ item "Which jurisdictions does Scarlet cover?": the question expanded to a list of seven jurisdictions and a CE-marking note, the plus icon became a cross, page height grew from 8505 to 8803 px, and nothing else changed. On load the hero video was playing; five other videos were present but paused. Measurement recorded one running animation on load and after scroll on desktop, none on mobile. With reduced motion on, the hero video still played on load and was paused after scrolling away; no prefers-reduced-motion rule was found in accessible stylesheets.
observations.accessibility: White hero text sits over bright moving footage with no visible scrim, so legibility depends on the frame. The cookie panel stays fixed over content while scrolling and overlaps the FAQ on desktop. The nav bar stayed visible at the top when scrolled to the FAQ in the live visit. Accordion triggers were not exposed as buttons to the control scan. No horizontal overflow at either width.
observations.mobile: Nav collapses to logo plus hamburger; the hero keeps video with the line wrapping to three lines; the cookie panel covers the lower third of the first screen. Grids collapse: logos and regulator badges into two columns, the three story cards and six testimonials into one column. Blog entries and FAQ run full width; the footer stacks link columns above the wordmark. Page grows to 9296 px.
observations.copy: H1: "Get your life-changing technology to the people who need it with the global AI certification body"; the hero overlay reads "Certify your AI medical device without unnecessary delays". Primary action: "Get in touch" (nav and below h1). The first screen offers footage only; logos and a founder quote arrive after the fold.

principles: For a regulated-market buyer, sequence trust devices in rising formality: logos, then quotes, then film, then official accreditations.
Keep the hero to one promise and move the long descriptive h1 to the first white band, where it can be read without competing with imagery.
Use one small saturated button colour on an otherwise monochrome page so the single action is always findable.
An FAQ accordion is a cheap way to answer jurisdiction and pricing questions without lengthening the page for everyone.
interpretation.fit: Suits B2B services sold on credibility (compliance, certification, legal, clinical) with long consideration cycles; wrong for a self-serve product that needs a demo or sign-up in the first screen.
interpretation.risks: Text over unscrimmed video and a persistent cookie panel hurt the first screen; six embedded videos add weight; the page relies on scrolling through many proof blocks before the first explanation of what the product actually does.

limitations: Hero video legibility varies by frame; only a few frames were seen.
Testimonial, logo and accreditation claims were not verified beyond their presence on the page.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Sway
summary: The hero is the product's first step: an address field inside a purple panel, with a live countdown and a four-step tracker underneath, before any explanation.

observations.hero: A white 69 px sticky nav (logo, three links, purple "Log in" pill) sits over a pale promo strip ("Throw a ballot party. Get $500 from Sway." with floating badge illustrations and a "See how it works" button). Below it a rounded deep-purple panel holds a yellow countdown pill ("15 days to Nov 3"), the h1, a subline, a white address input with a "Preview my ballot" button, and a registration link; tilted ballot cards decorate both edges. A "Your 4 steps" tracker (Address, Ballot, Plan, Save) and the first row of group cards complete the first screen.
observations.typography: Measured families: Manrope for headings, Inter for body. H1 40 px, weight 600, line-height 1.2, tracking -0.012 em, white on purple (32 px, weight 500 on mobile). Body 16 px at 1.4 with about 43 characters per line. Section headings are mid-size and centred; small green eyebrow labels ("Proven impact", "How it works") sit above them. The ballot-card decorations use a slightly rotated, hand-placed look.
observations.visual_system: White ground with one saturated purple for the hero panel, buttons and links, plus yellow for the countdown pill and green for eyebrows and bar charts. Surfaces are rounded cards with thin grey borders. Imagery mixes photographic group cards (campaign-style photos and posters), halftone black-and-white illustrations (Capitol dome, scales of justice, raised fists with megaphones) and framed product screenshots of a map, office list, messaging form and leaderboard.
observations.page_sequence: Sticky nav → promo strip → purple hero with address input → 4-step tracker → "Voting groups across the country" carousel → "Popular voting groups" carousel → grey band "Regular people drive political change" with two buttons → "Proven impact" stat card (2.2× bar chart) → three-step how-it-works → "Free. Private. Neutral." band → "Everything you need to lead" feature cards (map, offices, messaging, results, referrals) → app-store CTA over halftone crowd image → footer with link columns and Español link.
observations.interaction: Operated the right arrow on the "Voting groups across the country" carousel: the row advanced by four cards (first card became "The Forward Party Voting Group") and the previously disabled, 40 %-opacity left arrow became enabled. The arrows carry aria-labels. Nothing was seen visibly moving on load in screenshots; the measurement record counted 0 running animations on load and 18 after scroll on desktop, and the live visit sampled 56 on first load dropping to 0–4 while scrolling. With reduced motion on the same first-load count appeared and then 0 after scrolling; a prefers-reduced-motion rule is present.
observations.accessibility: Carousel cards carry 20 × 20 px share icon buttons, which are small targets. Card titles are white text over photographs with a dark gradient band. The countdown pill is live data and changed between captures (15 days, then 14 days). No horizontal overflow at either width. Nav links and buttons are text-labelled.
observations.mobile: Nav keeps logo, "Explore" and "Log in". The promo strip shrinks to text plus a circular arrow button. The hero panel stacks and the address input loses its text button in favour of an arrow icon. The four step tiles become square icon tiles in one row; the carousels become horizontally scrollable rows with no arrows (arrows are hidden below the small breakpoint). All later sections stack to one column with the halftone illustrations placed below their text; feature screenshots stack vertically. Page height 9008 px.
observations.copy: H1: "Voting made easy" with subline "Make your plan and picks all in one spot." Primary action: "Preview my ballot" on the address field (secondary: "Register or check your registration", "See how it works", "Log in"). First-screen proof is live: a countdown to election day and a row of real voting groups with member and voter counts (for example "65 recs · 68 voters"); no logos.

principles: If the product starts with one input, make that input the hero and show the remaining steps as a tracker so the commitment looks small.
Use live data in the first screen (countdown, group counts) as proof that the product is in use, instead of static logos.
Reserve one saturated colour for the single most important panel and its buttons; keep every other section white or grey.
Hide carousel arrows on small screens and let the row scroll natively rather than shrinking the controls.
interpretation.fit: Suits consumer or civic products with a single clear first step tied to a deadline (voting, tax filing, enrolment, booking); wrong for products that need explanation or trust before any input is reasonable, such as high-ticket B2B or financial onboarding.
interpretation.risks: The page is dense: a promo strip, countdown, input, tracker and two carousels compete in the first 900 px, and tiny share icons and photo-overlaid titles reduce legibility. Date-bound copy ages daily and the group cards show partisan content that may alienate some visitors before they reach the "Neutral" claim.

limitations: The address input and "Preview my ballot" were not submitted, so the flow after the hero was not seen.
Running-animation counts differed between the measurement record and the live visit; no visible motion was identified in screenshots.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Casa
summary: A black serif hero with one address prompt gives way to a long cream page that treats each membership benefit as its own illustrated chapter before naming the price.

observations.hero: The first screen is black edge to edge: wordmark top-left, outlined "Benefits" and white "Get started" pills top-right, and a centred dark pill reading "AS FEATURED IN The New York Times" and "A letter from our CEO". The serif h1 and a four-line subline sit in the exact centre; near the bottom a rounded input-style bar reads "Find your home to get started" with a map thumbnail, above a line listing three served metros. A full-viewport autoplay video element exists but had not loaded in headless captures, so the ground appears solid black.
observations.typography: Measured display family casaLitteratur (a high-contrast serif) for the h1 at 68 px, weight 400, line-height 1.1, tracking -0.02 em (36 px on mobile); measured body family casaDiatype (a grotesque sans) at 24 px, line-height 1.3, about 32 characters per line (18 px on mobile). Section titles repeat the serif at a smaller size; eyebrows are tiny caps in coloured pills; the price line "All for $199/month." is set in the serif at display size.
observations.visual_system: Black hero, then a white/cream ground with pale-green rounded cards for explanatory blocks. Imagery is warm interior photography (a kitchen with a handwritten-style overlay of chores, a living room), isometric 3D illustrations (a house on a green lawn, small objects like a bell, boxes, a plant), and stacked notification-style cards showing tasks. Colour appears only in small eyebrow pills (peach, green, yellow) and a yellow credit badge.
observations.page_sequence: Black hero → "How Casa membership works" three-column card → "Your to-do list, done." → kitchen photo with chore-list overlay → Handyman (text, task cards, credit badge) → Concierge (chat card) → Autopilot → five-slide maintenance carousel → "And for the everyday chores" four cards → "Enabled by a deep understanding of your home" with isometric house and seven-tab inventory → "All for $199/month" with eight benefit rows → two trust cards → four-item FAQ → closing statement + newsletter → footer, "With love, from San Francisco".
observations.interaction: Operated the "Appliances" tab in the home-inventory section: the active label moved from "3D Model" to "Appliances" (grey to dark, underline moved) and the caption changed to a sentence about makes, models, serial numbers and warranties; the URL did not change. On load 0 animations ran and the hero video stayed unloaded; while scrolling, 1–6 animations ran as sections entered view (measurement: 9 after scroll desktop, 3 mobile). A subscribe toast with an email field appeared lower right after load. Under reduced motion counts were 0 and the video stayed paused; no prefers-reduced-motion rule found.
observations.accessibility: The inventory tabs are plain buttons without aria-selected; the carousel dots are 10 × 10 px targets with "Go to slide" labels. The chore-list text over the kitchen photograph is thin white on a mid-tone image. A newsletter toast overlays content on load and has a 32 px dismiss button. No horizontal overflow at either width. The full-page desktop capture was cut at 9000 px of a 10746 px page.
observations.mobile: Nav keeps the logo mark (wordmark dropped) with both pills. The hero stacks: press pill, 36 px serif h1, subline, and the address bar pinned near the bottom. All two-column benefit sections stack with imagery below text; the maintenance carousel becomes one card wide; the inventory tabs become a horizontally scrolling strip; the price benefit list becomes one column; FAQ and footer stack. Body drops to 18 px. Page height 10943 px.
observations.copy: H1: "Home, taken care of." Primary action: "Get started" (nav) and the hero bar "Find your home to get started". First-screen proof is a press mention (The New York Times) and a CEO letter link; no numbers, logos beyond the one outlet, or demo.

principles: Lead with a short serif promise on an empty ground and defer every feature to its own chapter below, so the hero reads as a brand rather than a feature list.
Name the price late but plainly, in display type, after the benefits have each been shown.
Let the first-screen input describe the first step in words ("Find your home") rather than presenting an empty form field.
Use one press mention in the hero rather than a logo wall when you have a single strong outlet.
interpretation.fit: Suits premium consumer memberships and services where tone matters more than feature comparison (home, health, hospitality); wrong for utility software where buyers want screenshots and pricing in the first screen.
interpretation.risks: A heavy 12 Mbps hero video that may not load leaves a flat black first screen; the page is very long (over 10,000 px) before price and FAQ; a newsletter toast competes with the hero on load; tab controls lack selected-state semantics.

limitations: The hero video never loaded in headless Chromium, so its content and motion are unknown.
The desktop full-page screenshot was truncated at 9000 px; the lower sections were read from the live visit and the mobile capture.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Squint
summary: An enterprise industrial-AI page: a cobalt video band under a floating white nav, then a two-column h1 and a long sequence of use-case panels, tablet-in-the-field footage and stat tiles.

observations.hero: A white rounded nav bar floats 16 px inside a full-width cobalt-blue video band (dim footage of a checklist and a worker in a hard hat), with a separate blue "Book a demo" pill to its right and a Fast Company "Most Innovative Companies 2026" badge bottom-right of the band. Below the band on white, the first screen ends with the h1 in a left column and a large grey subline in the right column; there is no button in the hero copy itself.
observations.typography: Measured family Abccameraplain for the h1 and the subline, both 48 px, line-height 1.0, tracking -0.02 em, h1 weight 500 in near-black and the subline in mid-grey (26 px on mobile). Inter, Geist Mono and ui-monospace are also loaded; small monospace-style caps eyebrows ("— OPERATIONAL KNOWLEDGE") label each section. Section titles are mid-size sans; stat tiles show very large figures (10x, 17%, $5M, 19%).
observations.visual_system: Cobalt blue is the single brand colour: hero band, demo button, link accents, icon tints and the footer. Sections alternate white, pale-blue-grey cards and one black band ("Purpose-built Industrial Agents" with wireframe diagrams). Imagery is workers in blue overalls holding rugged tablets, device mock-ups with checklists, isometric 3D renders (bottles, a car, a wind turbine, a garbage truck in the menu) and a node diagram linking sources (video, manuals, audits) to a central logo. Two customer logo marquees scroll continuously.
observations.page_sequence: Floating nav + video band → h1 and subline → logo marquee → "Your operational knowledge is everywhere" node diagram → black "Purpose-built Industrial Agents" band → "Transform every part of your operations" four use-case cards → "Turn frontline execution into competitive advantage" four photo steps → "Squint drives real impact" four stat tiles → second logo marquee → "Built for your team" → "Fast to deploy. Easy to integrate. Built to scale." → documentation-gap teaser → "Ready to put Industrial AI to work?" with Book a demo → blue footer with newsletter and link columns.
observations.interaction: Operated the "Solutions" nav item: hovering opened a full-width white mega-menu with a 3D garbage-truck render, four use-case cards and seven industry links; clicking changed nothing further and the URL stayed the same. On load the measurement recorded 138 running animations (143 on mobile), which the live visit attributed to the two logo marquees and the SVG node diagram (lines, circles, rects animating); the hero video was playing. With reduced motion on, running animations dropped to 4 and all seven videos were paused; a prefers-reduced-motion rule is present.
observations.accessibility: The logo marquee moves continuously and its images sit far off-canvas, so it cannot be paused by the user. The nav's expanding items are divs rather than buttons in the control scan. The subline is mid-grey at 48 px on white, acceptable at that size. The Fast Company badge is small grey text over dark video. No horizontal overflow at either width.
observations.mobile: The nav becomes a blue bar with logo, "Book a demo" pill and a hamburger; the hero video shows a silhouetted worker with the badge bottom-left. H1 and subline stack in one column at 26 px. Logo marquee rows stay as two scrolling bands. All four-card grids become single-column stacks (use cases, photo steps, stat tiles) and the stat tiles keep their 3D renders; the footer link columns stack. Page height 11728 px.
observations.copy: H1: "Industrial AI that reduces downtime and improves quality." Primary action: "Book a demo" (nav and closing band); secondary "Login". First-screen proof is the Fast Company 2026 badge inside the video band; the customer logo marquee (BHE GT&S, Komatsu, Nailor, Konecranes, NextEra, Tenneco, AFL, Path Robotics, Fortera, PepsiCo and others) appears just below the fold.

principles: Separate the brand band (video, badge) from the message (h1 on white) so the headline is never fighting footage for contrast.
Put the outcome in the h1 and the mechanism in a large grey subline beside it, so a buyer reads the result first and the how second.
Make the nav mega-menu carry the use-case and industry taxonomy so the homepage can stay a narrative rather than a catalogue.
Anchor each proof tile to a named customer segment and a single figure, with one illustration, rather than a wall of quotes.
interpretation.fit: Suits enterprise B2B software sold through demos to operations and plant leadership; wrong for a self-serve or consumer product, and too heavy for a pre-traction startup without logos and stats to fill it.
interpretation.risks: Over a hundred continuously running animations and seven autoplay videos raise CPU and page weight; the logo marquee cannot be paused; the page runs past 10,000 px with many H1-level headings competing for hierarchy; the hero band spends the most valuable screen area on dim footage with no copy.

limitations: Animation attribution was by DOM target type, not by visual inspection of each element.
Customer logos, stats and the Fast Company badge were not verified beyond their presence on the page.
The desktop full-page screenshot was truncated at 9000 px; lower sections were read from the live page and the mobile capture.
