Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Omnea
summary: A very long, light-ground enterprise page that stacks proof (logos, customer numbers, quotes, compliance badges) under one serif headline per section, with one scroll-pinned dark interlude.

observations.hero: Centred stack on an off-white ground: a small avatar-plus-mono 'DISCOVER THE AOS' link, a two-line serif h1, one sentence of body copy and a single black 'Book a demo' button. Behind the text sits a circular field of fine dots drawn on a canvas, with small mono labels ('INTAKE AGENT', 'REVIEW AGENT', 'PROCUREMENT OFFICER') scattered around its edge. A 'TRUSTED BY INDUSTRY LEADERS' logo row (Spotify, Albertsons, Proofpoint, Adyen, DeepL, Adecco) sits at the fold.
observations.typography: Display is a high-contrast serif, measured family 'Season Mix VF Variable Light': h1 68px, weight 300, line-height 1, tracking -0.026em (44px, line-height 1.1 on mobile). Body is measured 'Inter Variable' at 18px/1.4, measure ~55ch (16px/1.5 on mobile). Section eyebrows and hero labels use an all-caps monospace (measured 'Paper Mono Variable Regular' is in the family list). Many section headlines use a two-tone device: black first sentence, grey second sentence.
observations.visual_system: Warm off-white ground with thin 1px hairline card borders and very low-saturation surfaces; black is used only for buttons and two dark bands (the pinned 'Every agent's dream workplace' section and the footer). A small green dot precedes every eyebrow label. Imagery alternates between real photographs (PayPal card, customer portraits, a video still) and flat product-UI mockups on grey panels; the dark band uses an isometric line-drawn stack of layers. Dotted/particle textures recur as canvas backgrounds.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → canvas-particle hero → logo marquee → 'Platform' headline with arc of agent names → four pillar cards with link lists → '99% customer retention' proof block (photo, quote, three stats) → 'Why Omnea' two UI panels + three feature cards → testimonial carousel → three average-outcome stats → dark pinned layer explorer → dark 'Real humans' team-card cloud → customer story with video still → 'Enterprise ready' three security cards → trust badges → masonry wall of ~15 quotes → featured posts → newsletter form → dark CTA + footer.
observations.interaction: Operated: clicked the 'CONTEXT ENGINE' label in the dark pinned section; its description expanded beneath the label and one layer of the isometric stack turned pale green while the others stayed outline-only. On load the hero dot field redraws continuously (two screenshots 1.2s apart differed) and the logo row scrolls sideways. The dark section is pinned for roughly 900px of scroll and the nav switches to light-on-dark over it. With reducedMotion: 'reduce', zero CSS/WAAPI animations were running, but the canvas dot field and logo marquee still changed between frames.
observations.accessibility: Several headline second-sentences and stat captions are mid-grey on off-white (e.g. 'Built on trust. Measured on impact.'), and the pinned dark section's inactive labels are dark grey on near-black. Hero agent labels and eyebrows are very small mono caps. On mobile, product-pillar link rows measured 28px tall (51 links or buttons under 32px). No horizontal overflow at 390. The newsletter input has placeholder text only as its visible label.
observations.mobile: Everything stacks to one column: the four pillar cards, the PayPal proof block (photo above quote above three stats), security cards and stats. The agent arc shrinks to a compressed half-ring. The logo row becomes a narrow marquee showing two logos at a time. The testimonial carousel is cropped at the right edge, and the nav collapses to logo plus hamburger. Page height grows to 16,950px.
observations.copy: h1: "The Agentic Operating System for Procurement."; primary action: "Book a demo". First-screen proof is the customer logo row directly under the hero; the first numeric proof ('99% customer retention', '$5bn', '50%', '38%') arrives two screens later.

principles: If you sell to enterprise, let the page be long and front-load named customers; one proof block with a photo, quote and three numbers does more than a feature grid.
A single serif display face at light weight can carry a 16,000px page if every section repeats the same eyebrow-headline-body rhythm.
Use a dark band sparingly as a chapter break for the 'how it works' part, and let the nav recolour over it instead of staying opaque.
Pair a two-tone headline (black claim, grey consequence) with hairline cards to keep a dense page quiet.
interpretation.fit: Suits enterprise SaaS with a real customer roster and a demo-led sales motion; wrong for a self-serve or developer product where the visitor needs to try something within the first screen.
interpretation.risks: Length: the page is ~18 screens, and the pinned section plus a masonry wall of fifteen quotes push the final CTA very far down. Grey-on-off-white secondary text and tiny mono labels trade legibility for restraint. Canvas and marquee motion keeps running under reduced-motion, and the measurement record found no reduced-motion rule.

limitations: Tablet widths not inspected; no interaction tested on the 390 viewport beyond rendering and measurement.
The headless full-page capture does not reproduce the pinned section as a user scrolls it; its behaviour was sampled at five scroll offsets only.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Moda
summary: A short white page whose hero is a clickable, HTML-built replica of the product dashboard, framed by blurred colour blocks instead of illustration.

observations.hero: White ground, centred two-line h1 and a two-line grey subtitle, then a wide product dashboard (sidebar with Observe/Harness/Validate groups, three stat tiles, a 'Needs Attention' list, a line chart) that is cut off by the fold, with a 'Results' pass/fail card overlapping its lower right. Blurred rectangles in orange, yellow, blue and mint float in the margins on both sides. The nav has 'Book a demo' (outlined) and 'Sign in' (black) at right; no hero button below the subtitle.
observations.typography: One sans family throughout, measured 'GT Standard L' with a mono companion 'gtStandardMono' for the prompt snippet. The h1 is small for a hero: 32px, weight 600, line-height 1.3, tracking -0.02em (26px, tracking 0 on mobile). Body measured 20px/1.4 at ~55ch (17px on mobile). Section headings ('Monitor every trace', 'Tailored to your workflow') are about the same size as the h1, so the hierarchy is flat and the dashboard carries the weight.
observations.visual_system: Pure white ground with hairline-bordered cards and light grey panels. Accent is a hot orange-red (nav dot, FAQ plus signs, 'Run comparison' button, 'High priority' labels) with yellow, sky-blue and mint used as soft radial gradients behind feature mockups. The repeated motif is the blurred colour block scattered around headlines, echoed on mobile. All imagery is rendered product UI; no photography, no illustration beyond integration logos on a thin orbit ring.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → h1 + interactive dashboard hero → 'For teams running agents in production' logo marquee → 'The loop' headline with 'Book a demo' → three alternating feature rows (Monitor every trace / Find the mistakes they keep repeating / Test every change before it ships), each text left and gradient-backed UI card right → 'Tailored to your workflow' bento: Custom signals, Monitors, Right where you work (orbiting integration icons) → FAQ accordion (seven questions) → closing headline + 'Book a demo' → footer.
observations.interaction: Operated: clicked the 'Problems' item in the hero dashboard's sidebar; the highlight moved from 'Home' to 'Problems' and nothing else in the panel changed, so the hero is live HTML with a selectable sidebar rather than an image. On load four CSS animations were running: a sideways logo marquee and three 'orbit' animations on the integration ring; the monitors mockup also exposes real selects, a number input and checkboxes. With reducedMotion: 'reduce' no animations were running and the scrolled screen was static, though two first-screen frames still differed.
observations.accessibility: The dashboard mockup's text is very small on desktop and unreadable on mobile (sidebar buttons measured 51 × 11px; 31 links or buttons under 32px at 390). Grey subtitle and feature body copy sit at mid-grey on white. The hero dashboard is a cluster of real buttons and inputs that are decorative, so they appear in the tab order without a page-level purpose. No horizontal overflow at either width.
observations.mobile: The h1 wraps to three lines at 26px; the dashboard shrinks to a 350px-wide image-like block with illegible text, and the floating colour blocks bunch below the logo row. Feature rows stack text-above-card; the bento becomes three stacked cards; the FAQ keeps its full-width rows. Nav collapses to logo plus hamburger with the two buttons hidden. Page height 5,516px versus 5,831px on desktop.
observations.copy: h1: "Your agents should never make the same mistake twice."; the first action is the nav's "Book a demo" (there is no button in the hero body), repeated under 'The loop' and in the closing section. The first-screen proof is the dashboard itself with plausible numbers (109K conversations, 14.8% signal rate, 94% pass); customer logos (Final Round AI, Kanu, Brief, Corelayer, Autumn, CodeWisp) sit just under the fold.

principles: If the product is a dashboard, build the hero as working HTML and let it be clicked; a 32px headline is enough when the artefact underneath is the argument.
Keep one accent colour for every interactive cue (nav dot, plus signs, primary button) and push the rest of the palette into soft gradients behind mockups.
Alternate text-left/UI-right rows with one verb-led heading each ('Monitor', 'Find', 'Test') so a feature list reads as a loop.
Put the FAQ on the homepage when the category is crowded; naming competitors in a question answers positioning cheaply.
interpretation.fit: Suits developer and ops tools whose UI is dense and legible at a glance, especially pre-launch teams without customer photos; wrong for consumer or brand-led products and for any product whose UI is not yet presentable.
interpretation.risks: The dashboard dominates the first screen but its text is small on desktop and lost on mobile. The hero has no in-body call to action, and the two nav buttons disappear on mobile, so the only visible CTA at 390 is below the logo row. Decorative buttons and inputs in the mockups add keyboard noise. The blurred colour blocks are the only brand gesture and read as placeholders.

limitations: Which element changed between two first-screen frames under reduced motion was not isolated.
Tablet widths not inspected; no interaction tested at 390 beyond rendering and measurement.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Idilio
archetype_note: Dark consumer app-store launch page: gradient headline, phone mockup, poster grid, numbered how-it-works, team, FAQ, contact form.
summary: A black, app-store-style page that stacks every persuasion device (badge, stars, download counts, posters, five-step walkthrough, team bios, FAQ) and gates entry behind a QR download modal.

observations.hero: Black ground with a faint purple glow. Left column: a pill badge ('#1 Microdrama app in Latin America · 1.3M+ downloads'), a two-line h1 whose second line is a pink-orange-yellow-green gradient, a paragraph, a purple-ruled second paragraph repeating the pitch, a 4.8-star row, white App Store and Google Play buttons and a dim 'Be the first to know →' link. Right: a large phone frame holding an autoplay video (black here) with a mute icon. On load a 'Download our app' QR modal covers the page and a Spanish cookie bar sits along the bottom.
observations.typography: Everything renders in measured 'Arial' (a second family, 'Sofia Pro Zone', appears in the list and shows in the nav and logo). h1 72px, weight 700, line-height 1, tracking -0.025em (48px on mobile). Body 18px/1.6 at ~64ch, mostly light grey on black. Section eyebrows are small, letter-spaced caps in purple, teal, orange or green; step numbers are very large numerals coloured per step; team names are large and bold.
observations.visual_system: Near-black ground throughout with per-section coloured glows (purple, teal, green, orange). Accent purple for the primary button and pulse dot; a five-hue gradient recurs on display lines and the nav underline. Surfaces are charcoal cards with 1px white/10% borders and rounded corners. Imagery: four telenovela-style show posters, five phone screenshots of the app, three portrait photos. Icons sit in small tinted squares.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → hero with phone video → five-stat strip (1.3M+ downloads, 50+ countries, 3M+ monthly views, 29+ series, 400K+ followers) → 'What is a microdrama?' four cards → 'Latest releases' poster row + 'See all shows' → 'How it works' five numbered steps with alternating phone screenshots → 'Made in Latin America' gradient headline, three stats, awards card → 'Built different' six cards → 'We're not just a studio' tech list → creators banner + 'Submit Your Story' → team: three portrait bios → FAQ (six collapsibles) → 'Let's talk' name/email/message form → footer.
observations.interaction: Operated: after dismissing the download modal with 'Not now', clicked the first FAQ summary ('What are microdramas?'); the question turned purple, the plus icon became an ×, and a four-line answer expanded beneath. On load the only running animation was a 'pulse' on the badge's purple dot; the hero video element was autoplay+muted but never left readyState 0 in this browser. With reducedMotion: 'reduce' the pulse animation still ran and the video stayed paused. Header is sticky at 100px; the cookie bar is fixed at the bottom.
observations.accessibility: Secondary copy is grey (~40-60% white) on black, and the 'Be the first to know →' and 'Not now' links are set at 25-40% white. Nav language buttons measured 16 × 16px on desktop and 18 × 20px on mobile; footer social icons are 20px; 19 targets under 32px at 390. The download modal and cookie bar both overlay the first screen, and the modal's close is a 15px × glyph. No horizontal overflow. The h1 gradient line's green word ('With') sits low-contrast on black.
observations.mobile: The hero stacks: badge, three-line h1, paragraph, store buttons, then the phone frame (which is empty) below, pushing the first real content past 1,500px. The stat strip becomes a two-column grid with the fifth stat alone; format cards, how-it-works steps and team bios stack one column; posters become a 2 × 2 grid. The cookie bar covers about a fifth of the viewport and the QR modal still appears. Page height 18,486px.
observations.copy: h1: "Latin Microdramas You'll Fall in Love With"; primary actions are the store badges "App Store" / "Google Play" plus the nav's "Be the first to know". First-screen proof is numeric and ratings-based: the '#1 … 1.3M+ downloads' badge, '4.8 · 1.3M+ downloads on iOS and Android' with five stars, and 'Over 1 million people are already watching'.

principles: For a consumer app, put the store badges and a rating line in the first screen and repeat the download count in the badge, the stars and the body copy; redundancy is the point.
Show the product's actual content (posters, in-app screenshots) rather than abstractions; a numbered walkthrough with real screens explains a monetisation model without a diagram.
Pick one accent and one gradient and reuse them on every eyebrow, underline and display line so a long dark page stays one brand.
Do not stack a modal and a cookie bar on the first screen; one interrupt is already a cost.
interpretation.fit: Suits mobile-first consumer media and games with an existing audience and app-store presence; wrong for B2B, for anything without downloadable proof, and for a product whose first screen needs to be scannable without dismissing overlays.
interpretation.risks: Two overlays on load hide the hero. The page is 15 sections and ~13,500px, with investor, creator and viewer audiences all served on one homepage, so the hero copy repeats itself and the CTA shifts between 'download', 'be the first to know', 'submit your story' and 'let's talk'. Grey-on-black secondary text and tiny language/social controls hurt legibility and tap accuracy. The empty phone frame on mobile is a large blank gap if the video fails.

limitations: The hero video never loaded in headless Chromium (readyState 0), so the phone-frame content was not seen.
Tablet widths not inspected; no interaction tested at 390 beyond rendering and measurement.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: SketchPro.ai
summary: A full-bleed architectural video hero with a 96px light-weight four-word headline, followed by a quiet off-white page of demo videos, a stats band and one quote carousel.

observations.hero: The whole first screen is a blue-grey photograph (the poster of a 1440px-wide autoplay video) of a curved glass facade shot from below. Centred white text: a one-line h1 'Design more. Document less.', a two-line subtitle, a white pill 'Request a demo' and an outlined pill 'See how it works →'. A row of white customer logos (RAMSA, SOM, Ware Malcomb, dar, FFKR, Devcon, Premier) scrolls along the bottom edge of the image. The nav is transparent over the image with a moon icon for dark mode.
observations.typography: Single grotesque, measured family 'fkGrotesk' (Plus Jakarta Sans also listed). h1 96px, weight 300, line-height 1, tracking -0.035em; 40px on mobile at the same weight and tracking. Body 20px/1.4 at a narrow ~31ch measure (18px/1.6 on mobile). Section headlines are roughly half the h1 size at regular weight; eyebrows are small letter-spaced grey caps ('PLATFORM', 'FIRM STANDARDS', 'SECURITY'); ampersands in headings are set in a serif italic. Stats use large light numerals. The closing headline returns to near the hero's size and weight.
observations.visual_system: After the photographic hero, the ground is off-white/near-white with hairline rules dividing sections and a 1px-bordered stat band. There is no accent colour: buttons are black or white pills, links are grey, the only colour is the hero photograph and the logo's blue-green mark. Imagery is two large white-framed demo video panels (blank in headless) and a mock 'AI Knowledge Base' card with a text cursor. The page ships a dark-mode toggle.
observations.page_sequence: Transparent nav over video hero + logo marquee → two-tone positioning statement ('SketchPro is AI designed for architecture & engineering firms…') → large demo video panel with expand/mute controls → 'Platform' split: headline left, six-row feature list right (Automated dimensioning, Tagging, Views & sheets, Schedules, QA/QC checks, Firm standards) → second demo video panel → three-stat band (15 mins, 20+ hrs, 50+) → 'Firm standards' split with typing knowledge-base card and three benefit rows → quote carousel (4 quotes) → 'Security' four-point grid → closing headline + 'Request a demo' → one-line footer.
observations.interaction: Operated: clicked the 'Next quote' arrow; the quote changed from a Dar engineer's airport-scale quote to a RAMSA associate's 'SketchPro isn't about replacing…', the attribution updated, and the active dot moved from first to second. On load two 'logo-scroll' CSS animations ran (the logo marquee); on scroll, the knowledge-base card's text typed itself out (character count rose from 332 to 424). The hero and demo videos were autoplay+muted but stayed at readyState 0 in this browser. With reducedMotion: 'reduce' the two logo-scroll animations still ran; the measurement record found a reduced-motion rule.
observations.accessibility: White 300-weight text over a mid-tone photograph; subtitle contrast depends on the frame behind it. Mobile quote dots measured 6 × 6px (24 × 6px when active) and the mobile menu button is 24px; 10 targets under 32px at 390. Demo-video panels are large transparent 'Play demo video' buttons covering the whole frame with an unmute button inside. Feature-list descriptions are light grey on off-white. No horizontal overflow at either width.
observations.mobile: Hero stays full-bleed with the headline on two lines at 40px and both pills stacked full-width; the logo marquee shows two logos at a time. The positioning statement runs seven lines. Feature list keeps its two-column name/description rows at reduced width; stat band and security grid stack to one column; the knowledge-base card goes above the 'Firm standards' copy. Page height 7,615px versus 6,183px on desktop.
observations.copy: h1: "Design more. Document less."; primary action: "Request a demo" (nav button reads "Request a Demo"). First-screen proof is the logo marquee of named architecture firms and the subtitle's claim 'The world's leading architecture and engineering firms trust SketchPro'; numeric proof ('15 mins', '20+ hrs', '50+') arrives three screens later.

principles: A four-word, two-sentence headline at light weight over a single evocative image can replace a product shot in the first screen when the logos beneath it do the proving.
Keep the body of the page colourless and let one photograph carry all the hue; black and white pills then read as the only interactive elements.
Put a feature list in a name/description two-column table with hairlines instead of cards; it scans faster and scales to mobile without re-composition.
Pair a stats band with the demo video it summarises so the number has a visible referent.
interpretation.fit: Suits tools sold to design, architecture or engineering professionals where the customer logos are recognisable and a cinematic image signals taste; wrong for products that need the UI visible in the first screen, or for teams without a loadable video, since the page's two largest panels are then empty.
interpretation.risks: Two large video panels failed to load here and rendered as blank white frames, leaving roughly 1,250px of empty space; the page depends on media that may not play. Light-weight white type over a photograph is contrast-fragile. The logo marquee ignores reduced motion. Quote-carousel dots are too small to tap on mobile. Proof is logo- and claim-based; no customer numbers appear until the stats band.

limitations: Hero and demo videos never loaded in headless Chromium (readyState 0), so their motion and content were not seen; the hero image described is the video poster frame.
Tablet widths not inspected; no interaction tested at 390 beyond rendering and measurement; dark-mode toggle not operated.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Agency
archetype_note: Post-acquisition wind-down notice: one signed letter, no product content; not a marketing homepage in any of the seven families.
summary: The homepage has been replaced by a four-paragraph wind-down letter under an acquisition banner; there is no headline, product, proof or call to action.

observations.hero: A 40px purple-to-black banner across the top reads 'Agency has been acquired by Klaviyo on August 5th, 2026. Read about it here.' Below it, on an off-white ground, sits the Agency wordmark with four text links (Security, Blog, Press, Privacy) and then a centred ~760px column of body text: four paragraphs explaining the acquisition and the August 31, 2026 wind-down, signed 'Elias, Luke & the Agency team'. A cookie-consent dialog covers the top of this column on load. There is no h1, no image and no button.
observations.typography: No h1 was measured. Display and body are the same measured family, 'ABC Normal', at 22px with line-height 1.6 and a ~73ch measure on desktop (18px/1.5, ~36ch on mobile). The letter is set in regular weight, dark grey on off-white, with one underlined inline link ('Agency is being acquired by Klaviyo'). The banner and nav links are small and semibold. Other listed families (Lato, Eina 01, helvetica) appear only in the cookie dialog and footer.
observations.visual_system: Off-white page ground, a near-black footer-less layout with a white footer band. The only colour is the banner's purple gradient and the teal 'Accept' button of the third-party cookie dialog. Footer shows AICPA SOC and ISO 27001 badges, a 'Subscribe to Our Newsletter' input with a black 'Submit' pill, and LinkedIn/X icons. No illustration, screenshot or photograph anywhere.
observations.page_sequence: Acquisition banner → nav (logo + four links) → wind-down letter (four paragraphs + signature) → footer: logo, compliance badges, 'Company' links (Security, Press), newsletter form, legal links and social icons. Page height 1,221px on desktop, 1,520px on mobile.
observations.interaction: Operated: clicked the cookie dialog's '×' ('Dismiss cookie banner'); the dialog disappeared and the full letter became readable, with no other change. Nothing animated on load (zero running animations) and nothing moved on scroll; the nav sits in a fixed-position wrapper but the page is only ~1.3 screens tall. With reducedMotion: 'reduce' nothing ran and two frames 1.5s apart were identical.
observations.accessibility: The page has no heading elements at all, so the letter is unstructured for screen readers. The cookie dialog's dismiss control measured 14 × 25px on mobile; footer legal links are 17-20px tall. On mobile the dialog covers most of the first screen and the nav collapses to a hamburger. Banner text is small white type on dark purple. No horizontal overflow at either width.
observations.mobile: Banner text truncates at the right edge ('…on August 5th,'). The letter becomes a single full-width column at 18px; the cookie dialog stacks its Accept/Decline buttons full-width and hides the first two paragraphs until dismissed. Footer stacks logo, Company links, badges, newsletter form and centred legal links.
observations.copy: There is no h1; the first line of content is the banner 'Agency has been acquired by Klaviyo on August 5th, 2026. Read about it here.' and the letter opens 'As announced on August 5, 2026, Agency is being acquired by Klaviyo…'. There is no primary action; the only interactive elements are the banner link to a TechCrunch article, the nav links and the footer newsletter 'Submit'. First-screen proof: none.

principles: When a company winds down, a short signed letter at reading size with one dated banner is a complete homepage; dropping the marketing shell avoids promising a product that will not exist.
Keep the compliance badges and the Security link in the footer through a shutdown; existing customers still need them while data is migrated.
A single-column, 22px, ~73ch letter is readable, but even one page of prose needs a heading element so assistive tech can find the start.
interpretation.fit: Suits a sunset or acquisition notice, a maintenance page or a one-announcement microsite; wrong as a reference for any live product homepage, since it demonstrates nothing about hero, proof or conversion design.
interpretation.risks: No heading structure, no primary action and a third-party cookie dialog that hides the message on first paint, especially on mobile. The banner truncates at 390px, cutting off the date. The newsletter form in the footer invites sign-ups for a company that is closing. For dataset purposes the page carries no transferable landing-page pattern beyond the wind-down letter itself.

limitations: The page is a post-acquisition notice, not the product homepage that existed before August 2026; the earlier design was not inspected.
No candidate location in the record, so no geography evidence.
Tablet widths not inspected; no interaction tested at 390 beyond rendering and measurement.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Pravah
summary: A one-and-a-half-screen research-lab page: a canvas glyph of a transformer symbol, one 52px headline, four hairline-ruled use cases, an affiliations row, and nothing to click but 'Get in touch'.

observations.hero: Warm off-white ground. A thin nav (wordmark 'Pravāh' left; 'Research', 'Team', 'Get in touch' right) above a 660 × 198px canvas drawing of an electrical transformer symbol (two overlapping circles between two bus lines), rendered either as hairline strokes or as rows of 0/1 digits depending on when it was captured. Below it, left-aligned in a ~660px column: a two-line h1 and a five-line paragraph. No button, image or logo row in the first screen; the first screen is otherwise empty space.
observations.typography: One family throughout, measured 'Switzer'. h1 52px, weight 400, line-height 1.1, tracking -0.025em (30px on mobile). Body 16px/1.5 at ~56ch (~40ch on mobile). Use-case blocks use tiny letter-spaced grey caps for the audience label, a slightly-larger-than-body regular title and smaller grey description text. The canvas glyph's digits are set in a tiny monospace. Footer links are small.
observations.visual_system: No colour: off-white ground (rgb 253,252,249), near-black text, mid-grey secondary text and 1px hairline rules; a 'Dark' footer toggle inverts to rgb(26,26,26) with light text. The only graphic is the canvas transformer glyph, which doubles as the brand motif. Affiliation marks (Stanford, MIT, Google, IIT, University of Chicago, Octopus Energy) are rendered in grey. Research and Team exist as hidden views swapped in by the nav rather than as sections below.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → canvas glyph → h1 + paragraph → four hairline-separated use cases, each with an audience eyebrow (Hyperscalers & Neoclouds / Data center developers / Chip companies / Power traders), a title and two lines → 'Built by engineers, scientists and researchers from' + six grey marks → footer (© Pravāh 2026 · Dark · Open roles). Research (six papers) and Team (four people, six advisors) are separate hidden views reached from the nav.
observations.interaction: Operated: clicked the footer 'Dark' button (aria-label 'Switch to dark'); the page inverted to a near-black ground, the label changed to 'Light', and the glyph re-rendered in light digits. On load the page was blank at t=0 and content had faded in by 1.5s (the CSS fades [data-in] blocks in); the canvas glyph was seen in two states (line drawing and binary digits) across captures. No CSS/WAAPI animations ran after load. With reducedMotion: 'reduce' nothing ran, two frames 2s apart were identical, and the CSS disables the fade-in under that query.
observations.accessibility: The markup has no viewport meta tag: with mobile device emulation the document laid out at 980px wide (scrollWidth 980 at a 390px viewport), so a real phone would see a zoomed-out desktop layout; the non-emulated 390 capture shows a clean single column. Use-case eyebrows are tiny and descriptions are mid-grey on off-white. Nav and footer links measured 20px tall. Headings are well structured (h1 then h2s). The glyph canvas is aria-hidden.
observations.mobile: In the 390 capture (no device emulation) the column fills the width: glyph shrinks with its binary rows, h1 wraps to three lines at 30px, the four use cases stack with the same hairlines, and the affiliation marks reflow to two rows of three. Nav stays a single row with all three links. Page height 1,823px. Under true mobile emulation the page did not adapt (see accessibility).
observations.copy: h1: "Agents and machine learning for power systems."; the only primary action is the nav link "Get in touch", which is a mailto. First-screen proof: none; the affiliations row ('Built by engineers, scientists and researchers from' Stanford, MIT, Google, IIT, Chicago, Octopus Energy) sits at the bottom of the page, and research papers are one click away in a hidden view.

principles: A deep-tech company can run a homepage as a single column of plain statements: one headline, four audience-labelled use cases, one affiliations line, and no buttons.
Use a schematic of the domain (here a transformer symbol) as the only graphic so the glyph carries both brand and subject.
Label each use case by who it is for before what it does; audience eyebrows let four buyers find their row in one scan.
If proof is academic (papers, affiliations), put it on the page body rather than behind a nav view, so a first-time visitor sees it without clicking.
interpretation.fit: Suits research-led infrastructure or ML companies in a recruiting or partnership phase where credibility comes from people and papers; wrong for anything self-serve, for a product with a UI to show, or for a sales motion that needs a form rather than a mailto.
interpretation.risks: The missing viewport meta means phones render a 980px desktop layout, undercutting an otherwise simple page. There is no call to action beyond an email link, no product evidence, and the strongest proof (papers, team, advisors) is hidden until the nav is used. The fade-in leaves the first second blank. Tiny eyebrow caps and grey descriptions are at the edge of legibility.

limitations: The canvas glyph's transition between line drawing and binary digits was inferred from two captures in different states; its trigger was not observed.
No candidate location in the record, so no geography evidence.
Tablet widths not inspected; no interaction tested at 390 beyond rendering and measurement.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Acely
archetype_note: Consumer conversion page: lifestyle photo, proof ticker, pricing and FAQ in one scroll.
summary: A navy consumer landing page that puts a student photo with a score overlay beside a serif promise and repeats one free-trial button through pricing and FAQ.
round: Pear portfolio, Seed → Series A (year not shown)

observations.hero: A light-green promo bar and a white sticky nav sit above a full-width navy hero. Left column: three-line serif h1, a one-line sans subhead, a green pill button and a small 'No credit card required' note. Right column: a rounded photo of a student at a laptop with a large green '1480' overlaid and a caption about a 110-point gain. A cookie notice overlaps the bottom-right corner.
observations.typography: Measured h1 64px (40px mobile), weight 400, tracking -0.02em, line-height 1.1, family Lora (a serif). Body 18px/1.5 (16px mobile) in measured DM Sans; DM Mono appears in small uppercase labels ('STUDENTS AT TOP SCHOOLS LOVE ACELY', 'SAT 1410 → 1520', 'BEST VALUE'). Section headings reuse the serif at smaller sizes; feature titles use the bold sans.
observations.visual_system: Navy ground for hero and footer, warm off-white elsewhere; accents are a light green (promo bar, primary button, score chips), a blue (plan highlight, numbered steps) and a lavender panel. Surfaces are rounded cards with soft shadows; small pixel-dot textures decorate plan-card headers. Imagery: one lifestyle photo, product screenshots, four illustrated feature tiles, avatar chips, and a line-art character near the final call to action.
observations.page_sequence: Promo bar → nav → hero (serif h1 + photo) → university logo marquee → '20 minutes a day' three-step with product screenshot → blue score-change ticker (name, SAT/ACT before→after) → four feature tiles → three testimonial cards → 'Know what you need' checklist + question-card image → three pricing cards + button → FAQ accordion (15 items) → illustration + final CTA → dark footer.
observations.interaction: Operated the FAQ item 'What is Acely?': aria-expanded turned true, the chevron flipped and two paragraphs of answer text appeared inline; no URL change. On load the university logo row and the score ticker scroll sideways continuously (swiper slides moved ~70px in 1.5s). With reducedMotion 'reduce' no visible element moved at the logo row; the measurement record notes a reduced-motion rule is present.
observations.accessibility: A persistent cookie notice covers the bottom-right of the hero on desktop. Small mono labels (~12px) sit on green and blue chips. Pricing cards are whole-card buttons (each 324×400px) whose selected state is a checkbox icon. The score ticker has no visible pause control. No horizontal overflow measured at either width.
observations.mobile: Hero stacks: centred h1, subhead, button, then the photo below. Logo row and ticker keep scrolling horizontally; the three steps move above the screenshot; feature tiles become icon-left rows; testimonials and pricing cards become one-at-a-time swipeable carousels with arrow buttons and a progress bar; FAQ items stay full-width; footer columns stack to two per row.
observations.copy: h1: "Your personal study trainer for the SAT & ACT." Primary action: "Try for free" (with a 'No credit card required' line beneath). First-screen proof is the photo overlay '1480 — Ava increased her SAT score by 110 points in 2 months'; university logos sit just below the fold.

principles: Put one concrete outcome number inside the hero image so the proof is read before the copy.
Pair a warm serif headline with a plain sans body to make a tutoring product feel personal rather than corporate.
Repeat the same low-friction action label at every section boundary instead of introducing new asks.
Turn social proof into a compact ticker of before→after results rather than long quotes.
interpretation.fit: Suits consumer subscriptions with a free trial and measurable outcomes (test prep, fitness, language apps); wrong for developer tools or infrastructure where a lifestyle photo and pricing-first flow would feel off-register.
interpretation.risks: Two auto-scrolling marquees and a cookie notice compete with the hero; three plan cards and 15 FAQ items make a long page (8,000+px) that leans on the reader scrolling; the serif at weight 400 reads light on navy at mobile size.

limitations: Could not verify animation timing or whether the ticker pauses on hover.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Listen Labs
summary: A two-colour editorial page (cream ground, one saturated blue) that runs an 88px headline over a strip of art-directed portraits, then a long numbered product walkthrough.

observations.hero: Thin nav (logo, five menu items, a moon icon, Sign in, Demo) over a cream field. A small outlined pill ('Join us at an event'), a two-line blue headline spanning about three-quarters of the width, a two-line subhead, and an inline email field joined to a 'Book a demo' button. Below, a full-width row of five colour-graded portraits on green and blue backdrops; one carries a small 'Insight Quote' card. A cookie dialog covers the lower right.
observations.typography: Measured h1 88px at both widths, weight 400, tracking -0.04em, line-height 1, family Inter; the same family carries everything (single measured family). Desktop body measured 12px/1.3 (the small section labels and card captions); mobile body 16px/1.4. Section titles are regular-weight blue sans well below h1 size; step numbers ('01'–'05') are large blue numerals; small sentence-case labels ('Trusted Partners', 'How it Works') sit at both ends of hairline rules at section tops.
observations.visual_system: Two colours do almost all the work: a warm cream ground and one saturated blue for headline, text, numerals, rules and the footer block; a second cream-on-blue inversion is available via the moon toggle. Surfaces are flat; the logo wall is a beige tile grid mixing logos with big stats. Imagery is heavily art-directed: colour-graded studio portraits, retro office scenes, team photos run through a blue duotone, and light product screenshots of a chat-style study builder.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → h1 + email/demo field → portrait strip → 'Trusted Partners' logo/stat tile grid → 'How it Works' five numbered steps, each with a product screenshot → 'Case Studies' three video cards with stat and quote → 'Use cases' six-row list beside a photo → 'See Listen in action' video with 3x/120+/50m+ stats → 'Research Partners' team grid (duotone portraits with prior employers) → 'Book a Demo' form over an office photo → blue footer with seven link columns.
observations.interaction: Operated the nav moon button ('Toggle dark mode'): body background switched from cream to the brand blue and headline/text from blue to cream; the portrait strip and layout were unchanged. On load the portrait strip filled in after the text (one capture showed it still empty) and the hero form re-laid itself out; the four videos stayed paused until played. With reducedMotion 'reduce', no visible element moved after load; the measurement record found no reduced-motion rule.
observations.accessibility: Measured desktop body text is 12px (section labels, captions, form legal copy); the outlined 'Join us at an event' pill is similarly small. Cookie dialog overlaps the hero portraits on both widths. The moon toggle is a 16×16px icon whose aria-pressed stayed 'false' after the colours switched. Four videos sit behind 'Play video' buttons and stayed paused.
observations.mobile: The h1 keeps its 88px measurement but the rendered hero shows the headline at a smaller visual size over two lines; the nav collapses to logo, a 'Book a Demo' button and a grid icon. The email field and button stay side by side in one full-width row; the portrait strip shows one portrait; the tile grid becomes two columns; each step's screenshot sits above its number and text; case-study cards show one at a time with the next peeking in; the use-case photos appear as a cropped two-image strip; footer columns go two-up.
observations.copy: h1: "Customer Understanding, Loud and Clear". Primary action: "Book a demo" next to a 'What's your work email?' field. The first screen offers no logos or numbers; its proof is the strip of interviewee portraits with a sample 'Insight Quote' card, and the logo/stat grid arrives one scroll down.

principles: Commit to one brand colour and one neutral so that photography can carry the mood without competing palettes.
Let a single oversized headline and a joined email-plus-button pair do the whole first-screen job, with proof one scroll below.
Number the product walkthrough and pair each step with a real screenshot so a long page reads as a sequence rather than a feature list.
Show the humans behind the service (team grid with prior employers) as a trust section for a services-heavy product.
interpretation.fit: Suits research, agency-like or insight products sold to marketing and product teams where tone and taste matter; wrong for a developer tool or utility where a 12,500px page and portrait-led hero would delay the concrete demonstration.
interpretation.risks: A very long page (12,500px desktop) with only one h1 and no h2 until far down; 12px measured body copy on desktop; 61 animations on load at 390 wide with no reduced-motion rule; a cookie dialog sits on the hero at both widths.

limitations: The nav bar did not render in this session's headless captures (visible in the earlier screenshots), so the toggle was triggered programmatically.
The use-case list's active row changed between captures but neither click nor hover changed it; its driver was not identified.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Scope
summary: An industrial-mood page that alternates near-black and cream bands, uses a grainy amber gradient as its only colour, and sets every label in mono caps.

observations.hero: A cream nav (logo, a grey pill holding three mono-caps links, 'LOG IN' and a black 'BOOK A DEMO') sits over a full-bleed near-black hero. Centre-aligned: a two-line h1, a two-line subhead and one cream 'BOOK A DEMO' button. Diagonal grainy amber-to-yellow stripes rise from the lower-left and upper-right corners; there is no product image in the first screen.
observations.typography: Measured h1 68px (36px mobile), weight 400, tracking -0.02em, line-height 1, family Archivo (a grotesque sans). Body measured 20px/1.5 (16.8px mobile) in Manrope. Geist Mono carries nav links, buttons, eyebrow labels ('HOW IT'S DONE', 'JOIN US'), image captions, security card titles and footer links, all in caps. Three oversized slashed-zero numerals ('10X', '55%', '0') act as display elements mid-page.
observations.visual_system: Alternating bands: black hero, cream industries section, black workflow grid, cream/black split stat tiles, cream testimonials, black security block, amber-gradient closing CTA, black footer. Colour is restricted to the grainy amber gradient and a small orange square bullet; photographs are orange-duotoned industrial scenes. Motifs: faint grid lines behind product mocks, a thin line-drawn part outline, wireframe polygons, hairline-bordered cards.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → black hero (h1, subhead, button) → 'Trusted by 7 of the top 10' orange eyebrow + 'Accelerate report writing' + horizontal strip of five duotone industry photos → black 'HOW IT'S DONE' four-step grid with dark UI mocks → split tile: line-drawing with 'More field time…' beside stacked 10X / 55% / 0 → 'JOIN US' (black) and 'FOR BUSINESSES' (cream) panels with wireframe shapes → three testimonials → black 'Data security' four-card row + SOC/ISO/GDPR badges → amber 'See Scope run on your own reports' CTA → footer.
observations.interaction: Operated the horizontal industries strip by dragging it: it scrolled 800px, revealing 'Energy' and 'Infrastructure' after 'Chemical'; no arrows or dots are provided. Nothing continued moving after load (four animations counted then zero); the measurement record counted seven animations after scroll at 1440, which I did not see as sustained motion. With reducedMotion 'reduce' nothing moved; no reduced-motion rule was observed in the measurement record.
observations.accessibility: Mono caps labels and captions appear small by eye (not measured) on black and cream. The closing 'BOOK A DEMO' button is dark brown text on a dark translucent panel over the amber gradient, with low contrast at both widths. The industries strip has no visible affordance that it scrolls. All four 'BOOK A DEMO' buttons leave the site for the same external scheduling page.
observations.mobile: Hero keeps the centred stack; the nav shows logo, 'BOOK A DEMO' and a hamburger. The industries strip shows one photo at a time; the four workflow steps stack vertically with their mocks; the 10X/55%/0 tiles become full-width black bands; 'JOIN US' and 'FOR BUSINESSES' panels stack; testimonials stack; security cards stack in one column. Page height grows to 10,614px.
observations.copy: h1: "Supercharge your inspection team". Primary action: "BOOK A DEMO". The first screen offers no logos, numbers or demo; the subhead claims '10x faster inspections' and the first proof ('Trusted by 7 of the top 10 largest inspection providers') appears one scroll down.

principles: Build an industrial identity from one textured gradient and mono-caps labels instead of a multi-colour palette.
Alternate dark and light full-width bands so each section reads as a distinct room rather than a list.
Let three giant numerals carry the outcome claims, with the explanation in small type beside them.
Duotone all photography to one hue so stock imagery looks owned.
interpretation.fit: Suits field-operations, hardware-adjacent or heavy-industry software selling to buyers who book demos; wrong for self-serve products that need the product visible in the first screen or a sign-up path.
interpretation.risks: No product or proof in the first screen; an unlabelled horizontal scroller hides two of five industries; the closing CTA button has weak contrast; mono caps at small sizes reduce readability; section_count measured as 0, suggesting no semantic sectioning.

limitations: Could not verify what the seven post-scroll animations in the measurement record were.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Socratix AI
summary: A blue-and-black enterprise page that stages the product as animated panels (agent run, before/after queue, signal map) revealed section by section on scroll.

observations.hero: Black sticky nav with six links and a blue 'Request a demo' button, then a blue news bar ('NEWS … Money20/20 Money Awards 2026 finalist', 'Read the news →'). The white hero splits left/right: a mono-caps eyebrow 'BUILT FOR THE MAIN STREET', a three-line h1 with three phrases in blue, a grey subhead and a work-email field joined to a blue button; on the right a dark browser-chrome frame labelled 'app.getsocratix.ai' with a 'live' dot holding a demo video. A faint dot grid covers the ground; a cookie bar overlays the bottom.
observations.typography: Measured h1 60.8px (38.4px mobile), weight 500, tracking -0.035em, line-height 1.1, family Geist; body 17px/1.7 (16px mobile) in the same family. Geist Mono carries all eyebrows, card tags ('CASE STUDY'), signal labels and link labels ('READ CASE STUDY →', 'VIEW TRUST CENTER →') in letter-spaced caps. Headline keywords are coloured blue; one h2 greys its first words ('Benefits that' grey, 'redefine your operations' black).
observations.visual_system: White and near-black bands alternate, both carrying a dot-grid texture; one saturated blue is the only accent apart from pale tinted card headers (peach, blue, pink, green) on the story cards. Surfaces are hairline-bordered cards and dark app frames; a hairline logo grid holds integration marks in grey. Motifs: a particle sphere with callout lines (signal map), a striped half-tone globe near the footer, a SOC 2 badge.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → news bar → hero (h1 + email field + app video frame) → 'BUILT BY AI AND FRAUD EXPERTS FROM' logo grid → 'Selected stories' four cards with stat headers → dark 'One command center' particle sphere with signal labels → 'Fewer losses. Cleaner exams.' three use-case panels → dark 'AI that understands' agent panel (GATHER/ASSESS/RECOMMEND/LEARN) → 'Benefits' tab list beside a before/after queue panel → integrations logo grid → dark SOC 2 + 'Ready to see what Socratix can do?' email field → footer.
observations.interaction: Operated the Benefits list item 'Improve customer experience': the highlight moved to it and the right panel swapped from 'BEFORE — MANUAL REVIEW / WITH SOCRATIX AGENTS' queues to a 'CUSTOMER UPDATES' feed ('Onboarding approved', 'Check deposit cleared', 'All clear'). On load ~50 CSS animations ran (named cta-shine-pass, ping, sigLine) and sections fade in on scroll, leaving full-page captures mostly blank. Under reducedMotion 'reduce' the shine pass stopped but ping and sigLine animations still ran (43 counted) while far fewer elements moved; the hero video stayed paused in headless.
observations.accessibility: Cookie bar persists across the whole page at both widths. Mono eyebrows and card tags are small letter-spaced caps (not measured). Benefits list items are clickable without tab roles or aria-selected. Large regions of the page are empty until scroll-triggered reveals fire. The hero video frame rendered black in this session. No horizontal overflow measured.
observations.mobile: Nav collapses to logo plus hamburger; the news bar shortens its text. Hero stacks eyebrow, h1 (38px), subhead, email field, then the app frame. The founders' logo grid becomes two columns with ten visible marks (including 'Y Combinator', 'DoorDash', 'MIT', 'UCLA'); story cards become a horizontal swipe showing one card; later sections rendered blank in the full-page capture because their content reveals on scroll.
observations.copy: h1: "AI coworkers for fraud, financial crimes and compliance teams." Primary action: "Request a demo" (with a 'Work email' field). First-screen proof is the news bar award line and the 'live' app frame; the 'BUILT BY AI AND FRAUD EXPERTS FROM' logo grid starts at the bottom edge of the first screen.

principles: Stage each capability as a small animated panel that changes when a sidebar item is chosen, so the page demonstrates rather than describes.
Alternate light and dark bands with a shared dot-grid texture to keep a long enterprise page feeling like one surface.
Lead with an award or news line in a bar above the hero when the company lacks customer logos it can show in the first screen.
Colour only the keywords in headlines to point the eye without adding a second accent.
interpretation.fit: Suits enterprise workflow software sold by demo to risk, compliance or ops teams where a believable product scene matters more than a sign-up; wrong for a page that must be scannable in one pass or read well without JavaScript, since content appears only on scroll reveal.
interpretation.risks: Roughly 50 running animations on load at both widths, several surviving reduced motion; scroll-gated reveals leave the page blank in captures and for readers who jump; a persistent cookie bar; the hero's product frame depends on a video that may not play.

limitations: The hero demo video did not play in headless Chromium, so its content was not seen.
Mobile sections below the stories carousel were blank in the capture (scroll reveal) and were not re-rendered live at 390.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Tutor Intelligence
summary: A graph-paper hardware page that lets an oversized robot-head render break out of the hero under a light serif headline, with mono-caps navigation and one yellow accent.

observations.hero: An amber announcement bar in mono caps, then a sticky nav (logo, '+ ROBOTS', '+ SOLUTIONS', 'PRICING', '+ COMPANY', 'CAREERS', 'GET IN TOUCH', 'SIGN IN', black 'SIGN UP'). The hero sits on a graph-paper grid: a centred two-line serif h1 in a pale panel, below it a large white robot sensor-head render on a column that extends past the fold. Bottom-left a grey panel holds the one-sentence description with '$14 an hour'; bottom-right a video thumbnail with play control, a yellow 'GET IN TOUCH' and a white 'DISCOVER OUR RESEARCH' button.
observations.typography: Measured h1 72px (32px mobile), weight 300, tracking -0.05em, line-height 1, family Sentient (a serif). Body 16px/1.4 (14px mobile) in Manrope. Roboto Mono carries the announcement bar, nav items, buttons and footer links in caps. Mid-page h2s reuse the serif in blue at roughly 36px in a left column; the 'Get in touch' form title is the same serif in black.
observations.visual_system: Light grey graph-paper grid behind the hero, plain white for the rest, with hairline blue rules separating the three solution rows. Accents: an amber bar, a yellow button and form panel (the panel repeats the grid motif in darker yellow), one green button for Sonny, and blue for the solutions text. Imagery is product-led: a CG render of the robot head, two photographs of robots in warehouses, a frosted-glass office photo. Nav items carry '+' prefixes that turn to '−' when open.
observations.page_sequence: Announcement bar → nav → hero (h1, robot render, blurb, video thumb, two buttons) → 'A robotics research and deployment company' photo + text + button → 'Meet Cassie' text + warehouse photo + yellow button → 'Meet Sonny' photo + text + green button → three blue-ruled rows: palletizing, fleet picking, usage-based pricing, each with a short paragraph and underlined links → yellow 'Get in touch' form (first name, last name, work email, mobile phone) → footer with mono link columns.
observations.interaction: Operated the '+ ROBOTS' nav button: a full-width white panel dropped over the hero with a photo of the Cassie robot, the links 'Cassie' and 'Sonny', and a small grid tile graphic; the '+' became '−' and the label turned blue. Nothing ran on load; sections fade in as they scroll into view (8 transitions and ~285 elements moved after a scroll). With reducedMotion 'reduce' all heading text was present on load and nothing moved after scrolling. The two videos stayed paused in headless.
observations.accessibility: Without reduced motion, the h1 and h2 elements still had empty text about four seconds after load (they were populated under 'reduce'), and lower sections stay blank until their reveal fires. Mono caps nav and footer links are small (not measured). The three nav menu buttons exposed no text name and no aria-expanded value after opening. Measured mobile body is 14px. The announcement bar plus nav takes 111px of sticky height on desktop.
observations.mobile: Announcement bar wraps to two lines; nav collapses to logo and hamburger. Hero stacks h1 (32px), the robot render cropped at the right edge, the blurb, the video thumbnail, then the yellow and white buttons full-width. Company, Cassie and Sonny sections become text-then-photo stacks; the blue-ruled rows stack heading over paragraph; the form sits in a full-width yellow panel; footer links become one long column.
observations.copy: h1: "Intelligent robot workers for industry". Primary action: "GET IN TOUCH" (yellow), with "DISCOVER OUR RESEARCH" beside it. First-screen proof is the video thumbnail of a robot palletizing and the price claim 'from $14 an hour'; no logos or counts appear.

principles: Let a single product render break the hero's frame so the hardware, not the copy, is the first thing read.
Use mono caps for all wayfinding and a serif only for statements, so hierarchy survives without colour.
State price in the first screen when the business model ('from $14 an hour') is itself the differentiator.
Keep one accent for action (yellow) and a second (blue) for reading, so buttons never compete with headings.
interpretation.fit: Suits hardware and robotics companies with a photogenic product and a sales-led motion; wrong for software without a physical object to render, or for any page that must be readable before scroll-reveal scripts run.
interpretation.risks: Scroll-gated reveals leave text absent for assistive tech and captures until motion fires; the hero spends its right column on a paused video thumbnail; mobile body at 14px and small mono caps reduce readability; the announcement bar plus sticky nav consume a large share of the mobile screen.

limitations: Videos did not play in headless Chromium, so the reel content was not seen.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Reflection AI
summary: A warm-neutral research-lab page whose hero is a slowly drifting dot-matrix canvas with a light serif announcement headline centred inside it.

observations.hero: A floating rounded nav bar (logo, five text items, an outlined 'Get in touch' pill with a dot) sits over an off-white field. The whole first screen is a canvas of olive-grey dots forming nested rings and arcs; centred in it are a three-line serif h1, a one-line sans subhead, and two pill buttons, dark 'Try it now' and outlined 'Learn more', each ending in a small dot. No image, product or logos appear in the first screen.
observations.typography: Measured h1 57px (36.5px mobile), weight 350, tracking -0.045em, line-height 1.1, family 'NaN Serf B' (a serif with moderate contrast). Body 16px/1.5 at both widths in measured 'NaN Serf Sans'. Section h2s reuse the serif at roughly 40px; card titles are the serif at about 20px; small uppercase tags ('Solutions', 'Open intelligence') sit in beige chips. Buttons use the sans at about 14px.
observations.visual_system: Off-white ground with beige card surfaces and a dark olive used for primary buttons and one full-width panel; a chartreuse appears on icon chips and two buttons ('Our mission', 'Join us'). Dot-matrix motifs recur: the hero canvas, a second dotted-ring figure beside 'Build with Beam', a stippled green-and-white landscape image, and three circular photo crops in the olive panel. Corners are large radii throughout; a ○● logo mark is repeated as a divider.
observations.page_sequence: Nav → dot canvas hero (h1, subhead, two buttons) → dot figures descending to the ○● mark → 'We're making intelligence open' + 'Our mission' button → 'Solutions' four beige cards (Open-weight models, Open source software, Infrastructure, Solutions) → 'Build with Beam' text + 'Weights'/'API' buttons beside dotted figure → 'Our Partners' logo rows → stippled image with 'The most important technology…' overlay → 'Our convictions' three icon cards → olive 'Build the future of open intelligence' panel with 'Join us' → newsletter form + footer columns.
observations.interaction: Operated the 'Beam' nav item: a click only toggled a small dot before the label (aria-expanded stayed false); hovering set aria-expanded true and dropped a full-width panel with five links (Model card, API, Documentation hub, Weights, Learn more) and a 'Try Beam today' card. The hero dot canvas drifts continuously (about 46k pixels changed in 1.5s). With reducedMotion 'reduce' the canvas was static between captures but still re-drew when the pointer moved; the measurement record notes a reduced-motion rule.
observations.accessibility: Nav labels are small sans text and the mobile menu control is a small four-dot icon. Menu panels open on hover but a click does not open them. Dot canvas sits behind the headline with low contrast between dots and ground, so text remains readable. Partner logos are rendered in a muted olive at low contrast. Newsletter form in the footer; no cookie banner observed.
observations.mobile: The floating nav keeps its rounded bar with logo and a dot-grid icon; the canvas persists behind a three-line 36.5px h1 and stacked full-width pill buttons. Solution cards stack one per row; 'Build with Beam' places the dotted figure above the text; partner logos drop to two columns; the stippled image becomes a tall card with the quote overlaid; conviction cards become icon-left rows; the olive panel keeps its three photo circles below the 'Join us' button; footer columns collapse into accordion rows ('Company' open, 'Connect with us' and 'Legal' closed).
observations.copy: h1: "Introducing Beam: Reflection's 501B open-weight model". Primary action: "Try it now" with "Learn more" beside it. The first screen offers no proof beyond the parameter count in the headline; partner logos (AWS, NVIDIA, Modal, Nebius and others) appear several screens down.

principles: Use a generative canvas as the hero's only image when the product is abstract, but keep text contrast independent of it.
Lead the homepage with the current release as the headline so the page doubles as the announcement.
Build the palette from one warm neutral, one dark and one bright accent, and let repeated motifs (dots, circles) do the branding.
Put secondary actions (weights, API, docs) in the nav menu panel rather than crowding the hero.
interpretation.fit: Suits research labs, model providers and infrastructure companies whose audience already knows what the product is; wrong for a product that needs a screenshot or concrete outcome in the first screen, or for a hero that must be read fast on slow devices where canvas rendering lags.
interpretation.risks: No product or proof in the first screen; menus require hover; the dot canvas keeps moving unless reduced motion is set; partner logos are muted to near-invisibility; the page's section labels ('Solutions' used for both a section and a card) repeat.

limitations: The measurement record counts 4 animations on load that my getAnimations sampling did not capture; motion was confirmed only by pixel difference on the canvas.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Remuner
summary: A conventional SaaS hero is followed by tabbed panels of product UI where an AI assistant drafts plans and answers questions, carrying the argument through screens.

observations.hero: A dark promo bar ('Remu AI vs Excel: we put it to the test') sits above a white nav. On a deep indigo ground, the left column holds the h1 with a green underline stroke under 'drive results', a green subhead, a grey paragraph and two pill buttons; the right column holds a dashboard screenshot with a play button. Capterra and G2 ratings and three G2 badges follow, with a client-logo strip at the fold.
observations.typography: Measured h1: IBM Plex Sans, 43px, weight 600, tracking -0.047em, line-height 1.2. Measured body: Montserrat, 14px, line-height 1.4, measure 93ch on desktop. Section headings use the same semibold sans and appear larger than the h1 in the captures (e.g. 'Everything you need to run compensation, end to end'). Small spaced uppercase green labels ('PLAN DESIGN', 'DATA & CLOSE') introduce tab panels.
observations.visual_system: Indigo-to-violet gradient bands alternate with white and pale lavender sections; teal-green is the action and accent colour. Product evidence is cropped UI cards (plan builder, issue table, chat replies) floated on pale panels. Illustrated 3D-style icons sit on the role cards. A dark indigo footer closes the page.
observations.page_sequence: Promo bar → hero with ratings → client logos → 'Meet Remu' AI section with three feature tabs and sample prompts → 'Everything you need' Design/Automate/Motivate tabs → stats band (15%, 95%, +2) → savings calculator with blurred results → six role cards → integrations and security → video testimonial carousel → resources → newsletter → closing CTA → footer with competitor-comparison links.
observations.interaction: Operated the 'Automate' tab: the panel swapped from 'Any plan structure, live in minutes with Remu AI' to 'From CRM data to approved payouts, on autopilot' with an issue-table and chat mockup. A HubSpot email-capture modal ('Wonder how Sales Directors manage variable pay?') appeared on load and blocked clicks until closed. The client-logo strip moves on load; with reducedMotion 'reduce' that strip still moved.
observations.accessibility: On load a cookie banner and an email-capture modal cover the hero at both widths; the modal intercepted pointer events. Body copy is 14px. Inactive tab labels and hero paragraph are light grey on light and indigo grounds respectively. The logo strip keeps moving under reduced motion. No horizontal overflow at 1440 or 390.
observations.mobile: At 390 the nav collapses to the logo mark, a 'Book a Meeting' pill and a menu icon. The modal fills most of the first screen. Feature tabs stack as full-width cards, the stats band stacks its three numbers vertically, and the calculator stacks inputs above results. Measured h1 drops to 32px; the page grows to 14,128px.
observations.copy: H1: "The sales compensation software to drive results"; primary action "Book a demo" (nav: "Book a Meeting"). First-screen proof is a dashboard screenshot, Capterra 5/5 and G2 4.9/5 ratings, three G2 badges and a client-logo strip.

principles: When the product's value is a calculation people distrust, show the calculation surface itself (plan builder, payout table) rather than describing it.
Put the AI assistant inside real product mockups with concrete sample questions so the AI claim is tied to a recognisable workflow.
Use one tab set per job-to-be-done (Design, Automate, Motivate) to keep a broad platform scannable in a single section.
interpretation.fit: Suits mid-market B2B tools sold to operations buyers who compare vendors on features and reviews. It would be wrong for a developer tool or consumer product where a gated calculator and modal interruptions read as sales friction.
interpretation.risks: The load-time modal and cookie banner bury the hero and block interaction, and the calculator withholds results behind 'Unlock full report'. Thirteen-plus sections, small body text and many mixed accents make the page long and visually busy, and the stats band gives percentages without stated sources.

limitations: The modal was removed programmatically after Escape to operate the tab; its intended close behaviour was not tested.
The hero video behind the play button was not played; its content is unverified.
Stats (15%, 95%, +2) and review scores were not independently verified.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Rex
summary: A light-weight serif headline over a warm off-white ground leads into a blurred-photo panel carrying three outcome metrics, so an AI back-office service reads as calm and enterprise-grade.

observations.hero: A thin framed nav with a ruled content column sits on an off-white ground. The left column holds a customer pill ('synthesia AI-native order-to-cash with Rex') and a two-line serif h1; the right column holds a two-sentence pitch and an inline email field joined to a dark 'Book a demo' button plus a sparkle icon button. Below, a wide blurred-photo panel shows '12d', '90%+' and '30m' metrics over a row of seven process chips, then a ticker of running counters.
observations.typography: Measured h1: family 'tid', 54px, weight 300, tracking -0.022em, line-height 1.0 - a light high-contrast serif. Measured body: 'gdGaio', 16px, line-height 1.5, 41ch measure. Families also include 'geist' and 'chivoMono'; small monospaced uppercase labels caption metrics ('FASTER DSO') and section kickers ('SECURITY', 'COMPARISON'). Section headings pair a dark serif phrase with a grey continuation ('Built for enterprise.').
observations.visual_system: Warm off-white ground with hairline rules and dot terminals marking the column edges. Media panels are soft-focus office photography with grain and thin curved line overlays, holding small white UI cards (agent list, DSO chart, credit-memo approval). One near-black integrations band breaks the light ground. Accent colour is restrained: a dark teal button and small status dots.
observations.page_sequence: Hero with metrics panel and counter ticker → Synthesia case-study card → logo row (Y, Vercel, Forbes, NVIDIA) → 'Finance operations now run on agents' launch-film poster → eight capability tiles (Agents, Mission Control, SLAs...) → three tall solution cards → dark integrations band → 'Built for enterprise' SOC2/GDPR/SSO cards → 'How Rex works' four-step selector → comparison table vs outsourcing → FAQ → footer.
observations.interaction: Operated step '03 Run' in 'How Rex works': the left list expanded Run's description and collapsed Scope, and the right panel swapped from a 'REX EXTRACTED' account card to a 'NEEDS APPROVAL' card ('Apply $44K credit memo to INV-2847', Approve/Edit). On load the hero media panel changed between frames and the counter row scrolls with changing values. With reducedMotion 'reduce' the first screen showed no change between frames.
observations.accessibility: Metric captions and counter labels are very small monospaced grey text on light or photographic grounds. The grey second half of headings is low contrast against off-white. The sparkle icon button beside 'Book a demo' has no visible text label. No horizontal overflow at either width; mobile email field and button appear about 44px tall.
observations.mobile: At 390 the nav reduces to the logo and a menu icon. The h1 wraps to three lines at a measured 42px; the pitch and email form stack beneath it. The metrics panel stacks the three numbers vertically and wraps process chips into a two-column grid. Capability tiles become a single column of square images with captions, and the page grows to 18,863px.
observations.copy: H1: "AI operations partner for order to cash"; primary action "Book a demo" (inline with an email field). First-screen proof is a named customer pill (Synthesia), three outcome metrics (12d faster DSO, 90%+ touchless communications, 30m average response time) and live-looking activity counters.

principles: For a service that replaces headcount, lead with two or three outcome metrics in the first screen rather than a product screenshot.
Embed small, specific UI cards (an approval with an invoice number, an agent queue) inside atmospheric imagery so evidence and mood share one surface.
A light-weight serif display on a warm ground can signal enterprise calm without resorting to dark-mode tech tropes.
Put the demo request inline with an email field next to the pitch so the first action needs no navigation.
interpretation.fit: Suits AI-native services and back-office automation sold to finance or operations executives who value restraint and credibility. It would be wrong for a self-serve developer tool where visitors need to try the product immediately.
interpretation.risks: Blurred photography and tiny monospaced captions lower legibility, and the metrics carry no stated basis or sample. The counter ticker implies live data that a visitor cannot verify. The page is long on mobile (about 18,900px) and the launch film and many tiles repeat the same agent story.

limitations: The launch film and the 'Explore with AI' sparkle control were not opened.
Whether the counter values reflect live data could not be verified.
Outcome metrics were not independently verified.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Spore.Bio
summary: A pixel-bitmap display face over pixelated greyscale imagery turns a lab-instrument company into a sparse sequence of full-screen statements with very little body copy.

observations.hero: A full-bleed greyscale image of large blurred pixel squares fades to black at the bottom. Centred over it: a two-line h1 in a pixel display face ('MICROBIOLOGY,' in white, 'REINVENTED.' in mint green) and a one-line sans subhead. A floating dark pill nav (Mission, Technology, Product, Team, Resources) sits at the bottom of the viewport; the top bar holds only the logo, 'Request a discovery call' and 'Join us'.
observations.typography: Measured h1: Offbit 101, 112px, weight 700, tracking 0, line-height 1.1, set in capitals. Measured body: Archivo Variablefont Wdth Wght, 20px, line-height 1.3, 31ch measure; Poppins also present. The pixel face recurs for the mission statement and the industries list; small grey uppercase sans labels ('APPLICATION', 'JOIN THE EARLY ADOPTERS') act as kickers.
observations.visual_system: Black and white grounds alternate with one saturated royal-blue contact band; mint green highlights key words. Imagery is pixelated or soft-focus: the hero pixel grid, a glowing teal ring for the 'TMSI' technology section, a pixel-edged cut-out of the instrument and pixel-edged pill drops. Press cards use pale lavender tiles with publication logos.
observations.page_sequence: Pixel hero → black mission statement ('The first direct method that can detect, quantify, and identify micro-organisms...') → 'TMSI' technology teaser with glowing ring and 'Discover our technology' → white industries list (water, beverages, cosmetics, pharma, cell/gene, food) → blue 'Join the early adopters' contact form beside the instrument → 'Hungry for more?' press and news list → dark blue footer repeating the pixel headline.
observations.interaction: Operated 'Technology' in the floating pill nav: it navigated to a separate page (/tech-science) with a dark radial-glow statement ('Pasteur began with a microscope...') and the pill now highlighting Technology. During scroll the industries list highlighted one word in blue at a time and the adjacent image changed. With reducedMotion 'reduce', the h1 still assembled on load (letters partly drawn in one frame, complete later).
observations.accessibility: Grey kicker and subhead text on near-white ('APPLICATION', 'Designed for seamless integration...') is low contrast, especially at 390. The pixel display face in capitals reduces letter distinction for long statements. The headline entrance still runs under reduced motion. Full-page captures show long empty black and white stretches where content appears only on scroll. No horizontal overflow.
observations.mobile: At 390 the top bar becomes a translucent logo chip and a square menu button; the floating pill nav is not shown in the first screen. The h1 drops to a measured 48px on two lines and the subhead wraps to two lines. The industries list becomes one item per line, the instrument image moves above the contact form, and the page is 9,827px.
observations.copy: H1: "Microbiology, reinvented." (rendered in capitals); primary action "Request a discovery call". The first screen offers no proof beyond the one-line claim 'The new, ultra fast, AI-based microbiology testing technology'; press coverage appears near the end.

principles: Derive the display type and imagery from one product-specific motif (here, the pixel as the unit of imaging) so the identity explains the technology.
When the technology is hard to show, let one declarative capability sentence carry a full screen instead of diagrams.
Let press and announcements serve as the proof section when the buyer is regulated and slow to buy, rather than inventing metrics.
interpretation.fit: Suits deep-tech or hardware companies at pre-commercial stage, recruiting partners and talent more than selling. It would be wrong for a product with self-serve purchase or many SKUs, where visitors need specifications and pricing fast.
interpretation.risks: Very little copy (about 48 visible words in the candidate check) and no first-screen proof leave regulated buyers without detail on validation or throughput. Scroll-gated content leaves blank stretches, low-contrast grey labels hurt legibility, and the headline animation ignores reduced motion.

limitations: Nine product and sector videos were present but paused with autoplay off; their content and triggers were not verified.
The pill nav links to separate pages, so no in-page control was operated; the contact form was not submitted.
Measurement reports no sticky nav, while the pill appeared fixed at the bottom during the live scroll; the discrepancy was not resolved.
Single browser, single inspection date; homepage content can change.

name: Ambiguous AI
summary: Full-fidelity app mockups switched by task tabs, plus a split 'what your team sees / what your agent runs' panel, stage the human-and-agent workspace claim.

observations.hero: A floating rounded white nav bar sits over a pale ground with a blue haze at the top right. Centred: a 'Backed by a16z Speedrun' line, a two-line h1 with 'Human-AI Collaboration' in blue, a one-line subhead, a 'Works with' row of six agent-tool logos, an orange 'Create a workspace' button beside a grey 'Invite your agent' button, and three check-marked terms. Colourful app icons (docs, chat, calendar, mail) float at both edges.
observations.typography: Measured h1: Inter, 72px, weight 700, tracking -0.02em, line-height 1.1, set in Title Case. Measured body: Google Sans Flex, 16px, line-height 1.5, 88ch measure. JetBrains Mono is present and used in the agent code panel ('agent.ts'). Section headings are bold sans at a smaller size, centred.
observations.visual_system: Near-white and very pale grey bands with a soft blue gradient at hero and closing CTA. Orange is the single action colour; blue marks the h1 accent. Product evidence is full-width light-theme app chrome (Docs, Sheets, Mail) with a left rail of coloured app icons. Glossy 3D-style app icons are the recurring motif; customer-employer logos (Uber, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta, Google) appear greyed.
observations.page_sequence: Hero → 'Brought to you by AI professionals from' logo row → '18 AI-Native Applications in One Place' app directory beside a Docs preview → 'An AI coworker that actually does the work' with four scenario tabs and app mockup → 'One workspace, two ways in' app tabs with UI and code side by side → pricing comparison ($465/mo vs $0) → testimonial carousel → FAQ accordion → 'Start free. 18 apps included.' CTA with MCP/CLI/REST links → footer.
observations.interaction: Operated the 'Fill a column from a doc' tab: the mockup switched from a Docs NDA with a comment thread to a Sheets 'Prospect Research' table with an 'Ambi' assistant side panel (empty at the moment of capture).
